eras.label: Unification and the early Shah kings

events.title: Paleo-Kathmandu Lake Dried
events.detail: Buddhist Account: Manjushri traveled from China saw the lake and recognized its potential for human civilization. With one strike of his mighty sword he open the Chobhar hill allowing the water to drain away and creating habitable land. Hindu account: Nepalese version of the Bhagavat Puran says that Banasura captured Krishna's grandson Aniruddha who secretly married Banasura's daughter Usha. Krishna and the Yadavas set off with their army and eventually defeated Banasura who was living in Nepal/Assam region. Lord Krishna used Sudarshan Chakra to cut Chobhar so his clan members i.e. gopalbanshi could settle down in the lush pastures.

events.title: Indo-Aryan Migration
events.detail: Indo-Aryan tribes moved into the north-west of India from Central Asia in several waves of migration.

events.title: Vedic Period
events.detail: The Vedas and epics (Ramayana Mahabharata) establish the shared Hindu cultural framework. Rise of Janapadas which are realms republics and kingdoms notably the Iron Age Kingdoms of Kuru Panchala Kosala and Videha respectively one after another located in North-Western Indian Sub-Continent. During the late Vedic Period the kingdom of Videha emerged as a new centre of Vedic culture situated even farther to the East (in what is today Nepal and Bihar state) reaching its prominence under the King Janak.

events.title: Pashupatinath Discovered
events.detail: A cow everyday went to a certain place and gave milk under excavating that land Pashupati Jortirlinga was discovered Ne Muni came and established Bhuktaman from the cowheard as their King as protector of the land.

events.title: Gopalbanshi Rule
events.detail: Ne Muni declared Bhuktaman as king and then they ruled from Mata Tirtha

events.title: Mahispal Rule
events.detail: The childless king Yakshya Gupta died creating power vacuum meanwhile Mahispals attacked and accended the throne establishing Bar Singh as their first king

events.title: Kirat Rule
events.detail: Mahispal grew weak over time Yalambar attacked the valley as Battle of Chitlang was fought in which Kirat killed king Bhuwan Singh. They ruled from Gokarna jungle. After being defeated they lived in Ollo Majh and Pallo kirat region in the east

events.title: Kipat Land Tenure
events.detail: In the eastern hills the Kirat clans (Rais and Limbus) entirely rejected central state land claims. They formalized the Kipat system where land belongs strictly to the clan/community. An individual inherits land rights purely by birth. The central crown couldn't tax or arbitrarily seize Kipat land preserving tribal sovereignty.

events.title: Second Urbanization
events.detail: Started with new urban settlements arising at the Ganges plain forming the base of the Maurya Empire. Started with formation of 16 great rival kingdoms (Mahajanapadas). One of 16 Mahajanapadas Magadha used iron weapons war elephants and brilliant kings to defeat all the other 15 kingdoms. A military leader of low birth Mahapadma Nanda launched an internal coup killed the king and stole the entire Magadha prize for himself establishing Nanda Empire. Rise of Buddhism/Jainism. Chandragupta Maurya under strategy of Chanakya overthrow the corrupt Nanda dynasty to establish Maurya Empire. Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) was born in Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) in 563 BCE linking Nepal indelibly to the roots of Indian spiritual history.

events.title: Indo-Aryan Khas Migrated to Western Hill
events.detail: They brought with them masto culture i.e. kul puja and Khas language present day Nepali. They were the Mallapuri that Manadev exerted control over. Khas society assimilated later migrants including Rajputs and Brahmins fleeing from the Indian plains following the Muslim invasions. This intermixing led to the creation of modern Nepali caste groups like the Khas Bahuns (Brahmins) and Chhetris (Kshatriyas).

events.title: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
events.detail: Alexander the Great's Indian campaign was the easternmost expansion of his empire. It pushed into the Indian subcontinent culminating in the famous Battle of the Hydaspes. Upon reaching the Beas River the Macedonian army homesick exhausted and terrified of the rumored vast armies of the Nanda Empire further east mutinied and refused to march any further. Later Chandragupta Maurya fought a major war against Seleucus I Nicator (the Greek general who inherited Alexander the Great's Asian empire). Chandragupta won securing vast territories in modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan.

events.title: The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka visited Nepal
events.detail: He converted to Buddhism after witnessing the horrors of the Kalinga War. He made Buddhism the state religion built thousands of stupas and sent missionaries across Asia He visited Lumbini and erecetd Ashoka Pillar and stupas in Patan. He also married his daughter Charumati to a local prince

events.title: Licchavis from Vaishali Migrate to Nepal while Kirat Ruled the Country
events.detail: They were living in Vrijji confederation of Vaishali kingdom who got displaced due to expansion of Magadha and Gupta Empire. At first the Somabansi (Lunar) Rajputs invaded Nepal and defeated Kirat kings and seized throne. They ruled from Gokarna

events.title: Sombansi to Suryabansi
events.detail: Sombansi king Bhaskar Varma was too busy in expansion and died without a male heir. This created internal strife. Suryabansi Rajputs came from India and captured that power vacuum. Bhumi Varma became first Suryabansi king. They shifted capital from Gokarna to Baneshwor. They heavily championed orthodox Vedic Hinduism

events.title: Gupta Empire in India
events.detail: Following the collapse of the Mauryan Empire in 185 BCE the Indian subcontinent fragmented into multiple regional kingdoms foreign empires and trade-driven dynasties rather than a single unified state. The rise of the Gupta Empire marked the end of centuries of political fragmentation following the fall of the Mauryas. It initiated what historians call the "Golden Age of India" characterized by unprecedented advancements in science mathematics literature and art under a highly decentralized but powerful central authority. The Gupta dynasty actually grew in power by marrying a princess from the Licchavi clan who went on to rule Nepal. Nepal acknowledged the nominal over-lordship of the Gupta Empire at its peak. It heavily influenced Nepalese art temple architecture (Shikhar style) and administrative structures which were adopted by the Licchavi dynasty in Nepal. During this time Indian scholars artists and the Sanskrit language migrated into Nepal building the foundation of Nepal's architecture and literature.

events.title: Gosthi/Guthi and Jagir Land Tenure
events.detail: Gosthi or Guthi were established as autonomous self-perpetuating civil trusts formed by groups of citizens for specific civil and religious duty. Licchavi kings established temporary land assignments to military and civil officers in lieu of salaries giving birth to the Jagir system.

events.title: Panchali System of Administration
events.detail: Licchavi kings delegated specific state rights to these village bodies including local tax collection and minor judicial enforcement to Panchali which later became Panchayat. The members of each village Panchali were the heads of each household. Its heads were Panchalikas or Prajapanchas. These Panchalikas used to do local social work. In some places, the Panchalikas became strong and even transformed into small separate states.

events.title: Mandev
events.detail: Exeretd control over kirat and mallapuri erected first stone inscription built grand palace called Managriha issued Manaka coin

events.title: First Epigraph in Changunarayan Temple
events.detail: Talks about Mandev being king at young age after father died his mother not going sati he going to east to reclaim influence over kirat feudals and to west to reclain influence over mallapuri

events.title: The Age of Fractured Kingdoms in India
events.detail: The fall of the Guptas fractures India into rival regional powers that rule different zones simultaneously. The Rajput clans dominate western and northern India while Chola Dynasty dominated the south. During the later part of this period Nepal's local rulers (the Malla Kings) heavily adopted the lifestyle court customs and temple art styles seen in the Indian Rajput and Chola kingdoms.

events.title: Amshuvarma
events.detail: Was a feudal lord who rose to prominence being assistant to king Shivadev I rising through the ranks of samanta mahasamanta and later establishing himself the title of Maharajadhiraja for the first time turning Shivadev and his sons Udayadev and Dhurvadev to just figureheads. Historians also believe that he married Shivadev's daughter. He built Kailashkut bhawan which became the seat of the administration. Opened Kuti (aka Yakrushong La not that disputed kuti) and Kerung pass in the north

events.title: Bhrikuti Married to King Songtsen Gampo the founder of Tibetian Empire
events.detail: She introduced Mahayana Buddhism in Tibet seen as the first step towards establishing real ties with China. Prior to her arrival the Tibetian plateau was entirely dominated by Bön the indigenous spiritual tradition. She brought Nepali master-artisans architects painters and sacred Buddhist statues to Lhasa. Notably she commissioned the famous Jokhang Temple and the Red Palace (later Potala Palace) using Newar craftsmen from Nepal. She introduced devotional practices centered around Arya Tara and Avalokiteshwara. Tibetan Buddhists recognize Princess Bhrikuti as a literal human incarnation of Green Tara. She is celebrated for bringing the light of the bodhisattva ideal to Tibet.

events.title: Udayadev
events.detail: He lost the throne in coup after Amshuverma's death he along with his daughter Bhrikuti and son Narendradev fled to Lhasa for asylum he offered marriage proposal of Bhrikuti to Songtsen Gampo along with highly advanced artistic religious and architectural intellectual property to Tibet. He died in exile

events.title: King Songtsen Gampo founded The Tibetan Empire
events.detail: Pre-unification Tibetean Pleateu was a loose collection of nomadic pastoralists and horse-based warrior clans. The Western Plateu was dominated by the Yarlung Dynasty while Zhang Zhung Dynasty dominated Western Tibet. The immediate shift toward unification began with Songtsen Gampo’s father Namri Songtsen. In the late 6th century he formed alliances with disgruntled rival clans to overthrow a powerful regional prince. This military alliance expanded Yarlung territory significantly laying the exact geostrategic foundation that allowed his son Songtsen Gampo to conquer the rest of the plateau.

events.title: Narendradev
events.detail: He grew while in exile in Tibet. The emperor provided him with Tibetan cavalry and infantry. He attacked Kathmandu while the Abhira-Gupta (Jishnugupta/Vishnugupta) rulers and Amshuverma's thakuri clan had infighting for legitimacy and reclaimed the throne. He built the Bhadradhivasa Bhawan palace formally opened diplomatic relations with the Tang Dynasty of China

events.title: Rato Macchindranath Jatra
events.detail: During Narendradev's reign rishi Gorakhnath visited Kathmandu but felt disrespected by the locals. He then captured all the cloud-routing Nagas and sat on them to meditate causing 12 years of drought. To end his meditation king went to Assam and brought the sage's spiritual master (Macchindranath) to the valley. The sage stood up out of respect for his teacher freeing the serpents and bringing rain. Festival concludes with Bhoto Jatra. Legend states that a farmer cured the eye disease of the Naag Raja's wife and was gifted a magical jewel-studded vest. The farmer later had his vest stolen by a ghost. They took their argument to the King who was unable to determine the true owner. The King ruled that the vest should remain under the care of Rato Machhindranath. Since then the vest has been publicly displayed once a year in Jawalakhel giving the rightful owner a chance to claim it with proof.

events.title: Fall of Licchavi
events.detail: local village councils (Panchalis) and regional feudal barons (Samantas) autonomous governing powers backfired as they stopped paying taxes as the rulers became weaker powerful Thakuri clan within administration sidelined the Licchavi rulers trade with north disrupted as both Tang Dynasty in China and Tibetan Empire collapsed

events.title: The Dark Age
events.detail: This period marks most turbulent chaotic and poorly documented history competing capitals between Patan and Bhaktapur among Thakuri kings

events.title: Adi Shankaracharya visited Nepal
events.detail: Vrishadeva Verma was the king. Shankaracharya came and challenged Buddhist religious leaders using Shastrartha and won them which under-cut their intellectual legitimacy burnt ancient Buddhist scriptures chaityas and monasteries were demolished or turned to hindu shrines forced monks to marry and kill animals introduced caste system re-organized the worship at Pashupatinath instituted a rule that the chief priests (Bhattas) of Pashupatinath must always be recruited from South India.

events.title: Collapse of Tibetean Empire and Era of Fragmentation and & Buddhist Renaissance Begin
events.detail: Langdarma who converted to Bon from Buddhism in 838 killed his brother King Ralpachen and became the King. Following this he widely persecuted Tibetan monks nuns and destroyed their monasteries. Later he was assassinated by a Buddhist monk triggering a total collapse of the centralized empire. Tibet fractures into tiny independent regional kingdoms ruled by local warlords. The arrival of Indian master Atisha in 1042 CE marks the "Second Diffusion" of Buddhism sparking a massive cultural renaissance and the creation of various Tibetan Buddhist schools. In 1244 CE Mongol ruler Godan Khan invaded Tibet establishing a unique "Priest-Patron" (Cho-Yon) relationship where Tibetan lamas provide spiritual guidance in exchange for political protection from Mongol Khans. With the fall of the Mongol Yuan dynasty and establishment of Ming Dynasty in 1368 CE Tibet breaks free and is ruled by successive native secular dynasties (Phagmodrupa Rinpungpa and Tsangpa) (1354–1642 CE) which began as a golden age of independence but ultimately descended into an intense bloody sectarian civil war.

events.title: Thakuri Takeover of Kathmandu
events.detail: Thakuris capitalized on this vacuum after Licchavi's fall and systematically hijacked the palace machinery stopped paying taxes to the Licchavi king. King Raghavadeva ascended the throne

events.title: Nepal Sambat Started
events.detail: Newar merchant Sankhadhar Sakhwa discovered sand of the Bishnumati River had miraculously turned to gold. He used this wealth to entirely pay debts of every citizen in the Kathmandu Valley. King Raghavadeva inagurated Nepal Sambat to celebrate.

events.title: Gunakama Dev
events.detail: Believed to have founded present day Kathmandu. He transitioned ktm from agricultural to urban society. He Started Indra Jatra to commemorate foundation of Kathmandu and renovated Pashupatinath temple

events.title: Indra Jatra
events.detail: Lord Indra came to earth disguised as a peasant to steal Parijat flowers for his mother Dakini Locals caught him red-handed didn't recognize him and tied him up as a thief. His mother came looking for him revealed their identities and promised the valley winter rain and mist in exchange for his release. We celebrate to thank Indra's arrival to earth and for the monsoon rains and to ensure a good harvest. Later it also also featured the Kumari Jatra procession started in 1756 by King Jaya Prakash Malla

events.title: The Two Capitals System in Kathmandu
events.detail: Thakuri rule was its lack of a strict centralized line of succession the rule fractured in to two courts. One Thakuri faction established its royal seat and court in Patan (Lalitpur). A rival Thakuri faction established a competing capital in Bhaktapur (Bhadgaon).

events.title: Nagaraja the First Khas Malla King
events.detail: Coinciding with Licchavi's fall Nagaraja unified the scattered Khas clans and founded the Khasa Malla Empire in the Karnali region. Eestablished his winter capital at Dullu (Dailekh) and his summer capital at Sinja Valley (Jumla).

events.title: Establshment of Simraongadh Kingdom aka Tirhut or Karnat Kingdom
events.detail: Western Chalukya Empire of the Deccan led by Prince Vikramaditya VI invaded Bengal and replaced ruling Pala Empire. Nanyadeva who was army official established himself as Mahashamantadhipati of Simraongadh Kingdom Later when Chalukyas focused their army back in Deccan he declared independence

events.title: Magarat Kingdoms
events.detail: These Barha Magarat i.e. east of the Kali Gandaki including Gulmi Argha Khanchi Musikot and Rising and Athara Magarat i.e. west of the Kali Gandaki in name of tribes such as Pun Buda Gharti Roka Thapa etc.Magar came into prominence as independent kingdoms coinciding the fall of Licchavi. They ruled through hilltop strongholds called Kots

events.title: Loot and Influence over Kathmandu by Nanyadeva
events.detail: He backed one of the sideliend Thakuri Prince Shivadeva to make him king and exerted influence and drew massive wealth. He used his political leverage to extract heavy tribute and launch military raids specifically designed for plunder and loot rather than territorial conquest. This constant siphoning of gold and resources significantly bolstered the economy of his own kingdom in Mithila. Malla kings later created myth of him permanently ruling Kathmandu as they desperately wanted to claim a direct bloodline descent from him since he was highly influencial.

events.title: Beginning of Malla Era
events.detail: Powerful military aristocrat named Arideva during Thakuri era launched a final political and masterfully coordinated takeover of the palace and later merging two capitals into Kathmandu. He dropped the older Thakuri and Licchavi royal suffixes (-deva or -verma) and created a brand-new dynastic identity around the warrior suffix Malla.

events.title: Sen Migrated to Western Nepal
events.detail: Sens were Suryavanshi Rajputs from Rajastan during Delhi Sultanate's invasion of Rajasthan. They used strategic diplomacy marrying into the families of powerful local indigenous Magar chieftains

events.title: Islamic Empires & The Mughals in India
events.detail: Ghurid Empire of Afghanistan expanded to India winning over Rajput king Prithviraj Chauhan. This monumental victory allowed his slave-generals to sweep across northern India into Bihar and Bengal establishing the foundation for centuries of Muslim rule under the Delhi Sultanate. They even fought against the Mongol invasion which made India one of the rare major civilizations to successfully withstand the height of Mongol. Over three centuries it evolved from a small regional power into a vast and expanded deep into the Deccan Plateau. Babur from kingdom of Kabul using revolutionary gunpowder warfare and strategic political alliances defeated Delhi Sultanate. Using field artillery he expanded the empire rapidly as his grandson Akbar secured the northern heartland by allying with regional Hindu Rajput rulers. Successive emperors pushed south and east into Bengal and the Deccan with expansion peaking under Aurangzeb who united nearly all of India into a global economic superpower through relentless military conquest. When Islamic rulers took over northern India many Hindu priests scholars and royal Rajput families fled north into the safety of the Nepali hills strengthening Nepal's identity as a robust Hindu kingdom.

events.title: First Recorded Massive Earthquake of Nepal
events.detail: The vamsavalis (chronicles) composed in the Kathmandu Valley provided a record of this major tremor. However, the extent of damage caused by the 1223 earthquake is not found in historical records.

events.title: 7.8 Mag. Kathmandu Earthquake
events.detail: Historical records mentioned that many houses and temples in Nepal collapsed and that one-third of the population of the Kathmandu Valley was killed. King Abhaya Malla was also killed due to the same earthquake.

events.title: 7.1 Mag. Sagarmatha Earthquake
events.detail: The earthquke resulted in significant casualties, widespread epidemics, and famines. While local historical diaries (thyasphu) focus heavily on the physical destruction within the Kathmandu Valley, modern geological studies indicate that these major 13th-century seismic ruptures occurred along the main Himalayan thrust fault line extending toward the Sagarmatha region.

events.title: Taleju Bhawani Temple
events.detail: Islamic armies of the Delhi Sultanate attacked Simraongadh the king Harisimhadeva fled to Kathmandu with their ancesteral relic Shri Yantra of Goddess Taleju Bhawani. While the king died on the way Queen Devaladevi came to Kathmandu with her son Prince Jagatsimha and married him to Bhaktapur heiress Princess Nayakadevi. From that union Princess Rajalladevi was born and she was married to a rising highly ambitious local noble named Jayasthiti Malla. After merging leinage with Nanyadeva, Malla kings regarded Nanyadeva as their supreme founding ancestor and Taleju Bhawani as the absolute tutelary deity of the state. This also helped introduce Mithila culture and language in Kathmandu. The actual temple structure was built in 1564 CE by King Mahendra Malla

events.title: Sultan of Bengal Attacked Kathmandu
events.detail: Sultan Shamshuddin Ilyas Shah set fire to the cities of Bhaktapur and Patan completely destroyed wood-and-thatch palaces and broke the sacred Shiva linga of Pashupatinath into three pieces also ransacked the Swayambhunath stupa to extract gold and relics before retreating back to Bengal. Lowest point of the Dark Age

events.title: Inviolability of Birta i.e. Maphi Birta
events.detail: In the far-western Khas Malla Empire King Prithvi Malla of Dullu codified the sacred private nature of tax-free land grants to Brahmans (Vritti/Birta). Stone inscriptions introduce severe spiritual laws warning future rulers that confiscating private land will doom them to reborn as worms in human waste.

events.title: Dashain Celebration Started
events.detail: Durga/Shakti worship predates all the medieval Nepali states. The Kathmandu Valley was already a religiously plural society before the Licchavis. Licchavi inscriptions provide evidence of Shiva worship, Vishnu worship, Bhagavati/Durga worship, Harihara, Surya worship, Buddhist monasteries and institutions. The Licchavis, who ruled the Valley from roughly the 4th/5th century onward, came from the broader North Indian cultural sphere. They brought or reinforced Sanskritic political and religious traditions. An inscription records that Vijayaswamini, associated with King Manadeva's royal family, installed an image of Bhagavati at Palanchok around 505 CE. By at least the 14th century, we have strong evidence that the autumnal Navaratri festival was a major part of Kathmandu Valley royal religion. Malla Kings developed a distinctively Newar ritual system around the goddess Taleju, a manifestation of Goddess Durga and tutelary goddess of Malla Kings. Her worship became intimately connected with the royal Dashain/Mohani rituals. When Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered Kathmandu Valley, he inherited this sophisticated royal ritual culture. The Gorkhali rulers adopted and incorporated elements of the Malla-Newar religious system while simultaneously associating the worship of Durga with the authority, military power and legitimacy of the Shah monarchy. As the Gorkhali state expanded across the territories of numerous ethnic, linguistic and religious communities, Dashain increasingly became a common ritual through which loyalty to the king and the state could be expressed. The state used its administrative and military institutions to extend the festival across the kingdom. Local authorities and traditional intermediaries such as Subbas, Mukhiya, Jimidar and other headmen could function as representatives of the central state in local Dashain rituals. When the state appointed lthem, their administrative authority, tax-collecting privileges, and ancestral communal land rights (Kipat) were tied directly to state obedience For instance, Subbas were legally mandated to establish a Dashain Ghar (sacred festival room), slaughter animals, and collect a festival tax called Dashain Kharcha to fund state celebrations. Refusing to host these rituals or pay the tax was treated as a rejection of the King’s authority. This frequently resulted in the state stripping the Subba of their title and reallocating their communal lands to Hindu settlers. PN Shah elevated traditional Phulpati tradition by bringing flower procession from Gorakhkali, the Shah dynasty's ancestral deity at Gorkha, to Dasain Ghar at Hanuman Dhoka. The Phulpati procession was synchronized with the royal military parade, gun salutes and the king's arrival at the old palace. The king then personally received and worshipped the Phulpati. Still today, Nepal Army carries that tradition of Phulpati procession from Gorkha and gun salutes (Harshabadhai). The process intensified under the Rana regime. The Hindu character of the state was reinforced through centralized administration, social classification and the Muluki Ain of 1854. They would sometimes even send police to learn if the indigenous people really observed Dashain as per the diktat. People were ordered to place hand marks of the blood of the sacrificed animal at the main gate of their houses as evidence that they conducted Durga pooja duly. Some Kirat historical accounts have often cited that, in 1885 Rana administration executed Kirat individuals such as Ramlihang Aathpahariya and Ridama Aathpahariya from Dhankuta for defying royal decrees mandating the observance of the Dashain. The abolition of Kipat in the 1960s, weakened an important foundation of Limbu communal autonomy. Later Dashain-boycott movements were sought to reclaim indigenous festivals and identities that activists believed had been marginalized by the state. Moreover, Kirat people observing Dashain started putting white tika as an expression of their own ritual tradition and identity, rather than the victory symbolism associated with the red tika of Dashain.

events.title: Formation of Baise/Chaubise Rajya
events.detail: The last Khas Malla king Prithvi Malla died without a strong direct male heir causing rebellion among the ministers which led to the feudal lords declaring themselves independent forming 22 kingdoms. Meantime the migrated Sen from Rajasthan used Magar/Gurung military alliances to from new kingdoms giving rise to 24 kingdoms in Magarat region.

events.title: Jayasthiti Malla
events.detail: He was of Maithil or regional Kshatriya origin he fused his identity with Queen Devaladevi’s lineage by marrying Bhaktapur Princess Rajalladevi gaining undisputed dynastic legitimacy. He formed alliances with the noblemen of Patan and arranged a coup against the weak king Jayarjunadeva. He formally institutionalized Taleju Bhawani as the absolute protective state deity to further prove his leinage with Mithila-Karnat. He promulgates the Manav Nyayashastra (Human Legal Code) which structurally categorized entire population into rigid Hindu caste system reorganized property/land laws and standardizes weights and measures.

events.title: First Sen Kingdom in Palpa
events.detail: The Kham Sen aka Rudra Sen was the first king

events.title: Mag. 7.6-8.2 Nepal –Tibet Border Earthquake
events.detail: This earthquake occured in northern border of nepal reported extensive destruction and large loss of life. One important consequence was damage to religious architecture, including the Machhindranath temple according to historical earthquake compilations.

events.title: Gelug (Yellow Hat) School of Tibetan Buddhism Established
events.detail: Founded by the great Tibetan scholar Je Tsongkhapa. During the Phagmodrupa era Je Tsongkhapa traveled to Central Tibet instituted his monastic reforms and founded the Gelug school. It is today the newest and largest school of Tibetan Buddhism. It emphasizes strict adherence to monastic rules (Vinaya) and rigorous philosophical study. Practitioners thoroughly study traditional Buddhist texts (sutras) before advancing to complex esoteric practices (tantras). Tsongkhapa's deciple Gendun Drub founded the great Tashi Lhunpo Monastery. After his death his disciples identified a young boy Gendun Gyatso as his deliberate spiritual reincarnation. This cycle of reincarnation continued to Sonam Gyatso who ultimately established the Dalai Lama tradition.

events.title: Seto Macchindranath Jatra
events.detail: People who bathed in a sacred river and visited the Swayambhu stupa were granted direct entry into heaven. King Yaksha Malla and his high tantric priest recognized Yamaraj and using powerful tantric spells they captured him demanded immortality in exchange for his freedom. Yamaraj prayed desperately to Avalokiteshvara (Seto Macchindranath) for help. The white-faced deity emerged from the water ordered the King to release Yamaraj and promised that anyone who visited his own temple and took part in his annual chariot procession would be blessed with longevity health and protection from untimely deaths.

events.title: Yakshya Malla and Partition of the Kathmandu Valley
events.detail: After death of Yaksha Malla his sons refused to co-rule. They fractured the Malla Empire into independent city-states: Kathmandu Patan and Bhaktapur. This rivalry caused a structural military weakness that allowed Mukunda and later PN Shahto easily target the valley.

events.title: Mag. 8.2–8.8 Lo Mustang Earthquake
events.detail: The earthquake occurred on 6 June 1505 and had an estimated magnitude between 8.2 and 8.8 making it one of the largest earthquakes in Nepalese history. It hit western/northern Nepal, around Mustang/Karnali and the Nepal–Tibet region. Some estimates reported that the earthquake killed an approximate 30 percent of the Nepalese population at the time.

events.title: Mukunda Sen I aka Mani Mukunda Sen
events.detail: He expanded the Palpa Kingdom dramatically conquering till Koshi River in the east and Gorakhpur (India) in the south

events.title: Expansion of Sen Kingdom
events.detail: Mukunda Sen immediately after ascending the throne launched campaigns against the neighboring Bhure-Takure (petty chieftains) including Argha and Gulmi he then allied with indigenous Magar chieftains to exert control over the fertile Terai plains including the Butwal and Gorakhpur regions. Then he attacked Kathmandu and was able to extract immense wealth gold and political tribute. Towards the east he reached till Koshi River. He established a grand winter palace at Jit Gadhi/Butwal Fort and a summer capital at Tansen Palpa

events.title: Mukunda Sen Attacked Kathamndu
events.detail: He lead a massive invasion into the Kathmandu Valley as it became weak after division continuously for 3 years 1525 1526 and 1527. His army brutally plundered the valley cut down crops and stole immense wealth while returning. He also stole image of Bhairav

events.title: Structural Birth of the "Shah" Title
events.detail: Khas-Thakuri rulers of Kaski and Lamjung dropped their old titles Khan or Khand and formally granted Shah title by Mughal Emperor of India (traditionally Babur or Humayun) to elevate their political status in exchange of diplomatic goodwill and allegiance to Mughal rulers

events.title: Division of Sen Kingdom
events.detail: After he renounced the throne he partitioned his massive empire into four independent sister-kingdoms i.e. Palpa Butwal Tanahaun and Makwanpur and gave each of them to his sons

events.title: The Birth of Gorkha Kingdom
events.detail: Drabya Shah the prince of Lamjung overthrew the indigenous Khadka Magar/Ghale kings and establishesd the Gorkha Kingdom

events.title: Dalai Lama Tradition Began
events.detail: The native secular dynasties Phagmodrupa Rinpungpa and Tsangpa took sides in a massive religious rivalry. The Rinpungpa (and later the Tsangpa kings who overthrew them in 1565) chose to fiercely patronize the older dominant Karma Kagyu (Red Hat) school. The older fading Phagmodrupa dynasty chose to sponsor the rising Gelug school. As the Tsangpa kings grew into a dominant military force they viewed the rapid expansion of the nearby Gelug monasteries around Lhasa as a direct existential threat. The third lama of Gelung tradition Sonam Gyatso traveled to Mongolia to meet the powerful leader Altan Khan to forge a fresh alliance. Impressed by the lama's wisdom Altan Khan bestowed upon him the Mongolian title "Dalai" which translates to "Ocean". This move effectively resurrected the old Priest-Patron (Cho-Yon) relationship providing the Gelug sect with a powerful foreign military insurance policy. Sonam Gyatso became the 3rd Dalai Lama. His two predecessors were retroactively given the title posthumously thus formally starting the lineage.

events.title: Ram Shah of Gorkha
events.detail: He brought Nanda Mishra a prominent Brahmin scholar and priest from Benares in his council and with his help introduced system of justice issuing 26 Thitis that included standard measurement interest rate cap to 10% for cash and 25% for kind conservation laws to prohibit cutting trees near roads encouraged communities to resolve minor conflicts etc. Built Gorkha Durbar Expanded kingdom to Sanyankot Barpak and Dhading. Forged strong diplomatic relations with King Siddhi Narsingh Malla of Patan and brought Newar traders artisans and coin-minting experts

events.title: British East India Company's Entry to India
events.detail: Starting in 1608 the company established factories (trading posts) in regions like Surat Madras Bombay and Calcutta exporting Indian textiles spices and indigo to Europe. Untill the death of Aurangzeb they only remained as trading company and were very submisive. In 1690 the East India Company sought a firman (an official royal decree) from Emperor Aurangzeb to grant them a complete monopoly and tax-free trading rights across India. When negotiations broke down Sir Josiah Child ordered a naval blockade of Mughal ports. Aurangzeb easily crushed the EIC militarily seized their factories and only let them return after the British begged for forgiveness and paid a massive fine.

events.title: Bisket Jatra
events.detail: Princess of Bhaktapur was cursed: every man who married her was found mysteriously dead in the royal bedchamber the morning after the wedding. Nobody wnated to marry her. A brave prince stayed awake and saw two deadly serpents crawl out of the sleeping princess's nostrils. He chopped the snakes to pieces ending the curse; King Jagat Jyoti Malla of Bhaktapur ordered the dead snakes to be hung on a 55-foot-tall wooden pole for all to see. The jatra is accompanied with rituals like chariot striking of Bhairab and Bhadrakali symbolizing their mating Sindur Jatra as a welcome to Basanta ritu and Tongue Piercing as a sacrifice for the town's prosperity.

events.title: Siddhi Narasimha Malla of Lalitpur
events.detail: He built Krishna Mandir did alternate trade agreements with parts of Tibet initiated the Kartik Naach festival first playwriter in Newar language in 1652 he undertook a two-year pilgrimage to India entrusting son Srinivasa known as Saint king for renouncing throne and abdicating in Varanasi

events.title: Kaji Bhim Malla’s Travel and First Trade Treaty with Tibet
events.detail: He ensured that Kathmandu and Tibet gained shared administrative authority over the vital border towns of Kuti and Kerong. Newari merchants from the Kathmandu Valley were granted permission to establish 32 trading houses in Lhasa. The Kathmandu was allowed to appoint a representative (Nayo) in Lhasa to protect their citizens' interests. Nepal also got to establish its own court in Lhasa to oversee cases of Nepalese in Tibet. Tibet agreed to exempt Newari merchants from customs duties and charges. Nepal was granted the monopoly to mint silver coins (Mahendramalli) for Tibet’s internal use cementing substantial financial benefits. His rising popularity and influence deeply threatened other royal court ministers. They lied to King Lakshmi Narasimha Malla claiming Bhim Malla was planning a coup to overthrow the King using his newfound power. King belived it without investigation and instantly ordered Bhim Malla to be executed upon his return. Before burning alive Bhim Malla's wife cursed the royal court and the entire country saying यो दरबारमा कहिल्यै विवेक नआओस्. Later it had cultural impact as people started using "Sati le sarapeko desh".The King later discovered Bhim Malla was completely innocent driving the King into severe mental illness and madness from guilt.

events.title: Pratap Malla of Kathmandu
events.detail: After father's severe mental breakdown he took the reign. He was ambitious and hyper-educated. He inherited treasury that was overflowing due to Bhim Malla’s currency monopoly and duties collected from Indian merchants moving up from the south. That wealth funded an unprecedented architectural intellectual and religious renaissance. He expanded Hanuman Dhoka Palace Installed famous Hanuman statues in palace gates named as Hanuman Dhoka erected a massive stone pillar called Pratap Dhvaja built Rani Pokhari to console queen after youngest son's death Krishna Temple in durbar square architectural updates to Taleju Bhawani mandir institutionalized Kumari tradition by building the permanent grand structural protocols Kathmandu became cosmopolitan trade hub Kashmiri Muslim merchants used Kathmandu as trade hub to import Tibetan musk wool yak tails and Chinese silk to Mugal empire he welcomed first European Jesuit missionaries (such as Father Grueber and Father D'Orville whom he met while they passed through the valley on their way back from Lhasa) mysterious stone inscription onto the walls of his palace containing words written in 15 different foreign scripts (including French English Persian and Greek) arrogantly challenging his rival brother-kings in Patan and Bhaktapur.

events.title: Dalai Lama Consolidated Political Power
events.detail: By the early 1600s the Tsangpa Dynasty had conquered almost all of central Tibet. The Tsangpa king Karma Tenkyong Wangpo launched a brutal campaign against the Yellow Hats surrounding Lhasa and heavily persecuting Gelug monks. Facing complete annihilation the prime minister of the young 5th Dalai Lama secretly sent an urgent plea to Güshi Khan the fierce military chieftain of the Khoshut Mongols. In 1642 the Mongols laid siege to the Tsangpa capital at Shigatse captured the Tsang king and completely executed the anti-Gelug leadership. Instead of absorbing Tibet into Mongolia Güshi Khan handed absolute sovereign political authority over the unified nation to his spiritual teacher the 5th Dalai Lama. The 5th Dalai Lama builds the Potala Palace and consolidates the theocratic rule.

events.title: Srinivasa Malla of Lalitpur
events.detail: He expanded the Patan Durbar Square Diplomatic in mediateding disputes among the kingdoms partnering with neighboring states for collective defencehis own son Yoga Narendra Malla partnered with rebellious ministers to force him to abdicate

events.title: Jitamitra Malla of Bhaktapur
events.detail: He built Thanthu Darbar Hiti miles-long state canal infrastructure that brought fresh clean water directly from the hills to dhunge dharas and and agricultural fields began construction of 55 Jhyale Durbar when Kathmandu and Patan allied against Bhaktapur he formed secret military alliances with the rising Gorkha Kingdom and Chaubise hill states to maintain balance

events.title: 8 Mag. Northern Koshi Earthquake
events.detail: The earthquake triggered severe ground shaking throughout the Kathmandu Valley and eastern Nepal. It caused a heavy loss of lives and livestock, and it completely destroyed or critically damaged numerous residential buildings, palaces, and historic temples. It is also linked with the Bhim Kali Dhunga of PN Campus. Researchers discovered that the massive Bhim Kali boulder (a 10-meter-wide rock weighing roughly 300 tons) was moved or deposited as a result of the intense shaking from this 1681 earthquake. However, there are other theories too. Large stones like Bhim Kali Dhunga and Chipledhunga are believed to be transported to a lowland plain by glacial movement and fluvio-glacial forces during the Ice Age as normal river current cannot transport such mass. Later, over the years massive earthquakes that triggered collapse of mountain peaks in the Annapurna range might have transported them to their present location.

events.title: Yoga Narendra Malla of Lalitpur
events.detail: He built his famous stone pillar statue topped with a golden bird declaring he is alive as long as the bird stays poisoned by political enemies he had no legitimate heirs when he died and thus a period of political instability began

events.title: Bhupatindra Malla of Bhaktapur
events.detail: He commissioned and completed the Nyatapola Temple in an astonishingly short six-month period which is tallest pagoda temple in all of Nepal surviving both earthquakes To guard temple he built stone statues of legendary Rajput wrestlers Jayamal and Phatat followed by elephants lions griffins and goddesses in the side of stairs. He completed 55 Jhyale Durbar. Like others he erected his stone pillar statue. Unlike others he joined hands and a bowing head without weapons as a sign of respect towards Taleju.

events.title: The Dictatorship of the Patan Pradhanas
events.detail: Following Yoga Narendra Malla's heirless death a council of six powerful noble ministers (The Pradhanas) hijacked Patan's state machinery. They turn the Malla crown into a puppet office deposing blinding or assassinating kings at will. Administrative collapse left Patan completely defenseless against future outside annexation.

events.title: Rise of Regional Powers in India
events.detail: The central Mughal authority collapsed after the death of Emperor Aurangzeb in 1707. The fall of the Mughal Empire fractured India into competing regional powers and ultimately paved the way for absolute British colonial rule. The Hindu Maratha Confederacy in central and northern India and Sikh Empire in Punjab region became the dominant military power in India conquering vast Mughal territories. Wealthy Mughal provinces like Bengal Awadh and Hyderabad broke away becoming de facto independent kingdoms ruled by local Nawabs and Nizams.

events.title: Capuchin Missionaries First Arrived in The Kathmandu Valley
events.detail: Historically Capuchin missionaries entered the Kathmandu valley using it as a pass-way to Tibet. Their mission (first Jesuit and then Capuchin) failed in Tibet as Tibetan government viewed it as subversive to both Buddhist spiritual and political authority resulting in the expulsion of the Capuchins in 1742 and 1760. While Capuchins were first welcomed by King Jagajjaya Malla in 1715 to establish permanent mission their work expanded rapidly after their expulsion from Tibet. He allowed them to use Kathmandu as a critical transit station for their journeys into Tibet. However due to rising societal friction he briefly expelled them in 1722. Following their expulsion from Kathmandu in 1722 King Ranajit Malla warmly welcomed the Capuchin friars into his kingdom of Bhaktapur. He became their greatest royal patron in the valley. Ranajit Malla provided them with land heavily subsidized their work and famously issued a decree explicitly permitting them to preach teach and convert his subjects to Christianity. As the final Malla ruler of Kathmandu King Jaya Prakash Malla initially treated the Capuchins coldly. However as geopolitical pressures from the advancing Gorkhas mounted he aggressively tried to win their favor to secure Western alliances. He granted the Capuchin mission a formal royal charter gifted them land to build a small Catholic church in 1760 and actively sought to please them. With the Malla rulers Capuchin missionaries enjoyed good ties. While Capuchin were second batxh of missionaries after Jesuit they cared more about helping those in need while Jesuit missionaries were more concerned with their adherents. Medical care was one of prominent social activities of Capuchin missionaries. During the devastating smallpox epidemic of 1716 and 1735 missionaries worked to alleviate suffering using Western medical knowledge. They also organized medical service during the war of Gorkha and Kritipur in 1766. Even the chief-commander of Gorkha soldiers Surapratap Shah brother of Prithivi Narayan Shahwas wounded and was cured by the treatment of missionaries. They also contributed in the areas of history geography ethnology and religion. One of the missionaries Joseph Rovato wrote on ‘The Decline and Fall of the Malla Dyasty’ and 'The Rising power of Prithivi Narayan Shah'. Missionaries helped to prevent some cases of wives immolating themselves on the funeral pyres (Sati) of their dead husband. They spoke against this system of the community. They helped to reconcile many broken families especially when husband and wives were separated. They provided counseling for those families and helped restore broken relationships. Many times missionaries even admonished the kings nobles and common people for their unjust deeds cruelty and sin. They asked them to repent for their unjust deeds and to seek God’s forgiveness. Prithvi Narayan Shah after the unification expelled the Capuchin missionaries because he suspected them of acting as foreign spies and political conspirators who had secretly aided his Malla enemies and invited British military intervention against his Gorkha conquest.

events.title: Smallpox And King Vira Mahendra Malla
events.detail: One of the earliest known episode of smallpox causing estimated death of 20000 people. King Vira Mahendra Mall of Patan died of smallpox.

events.title: Tibet Became Qing's Protectorate
events.detail: Lhazang Khan grandson of Güshi Khan acquired effective power as ruler of Tibet by eliminating the 6th Dalai Lama. Dzungars the rivals of Güshi Khan's clan invaded Tibet under the pretext of liberating the Tibetan people from an unpopular ruler. Though initially welcomed by some locals the Dzungars quickly alienated the population. They plundered the sacred Potala Palace looted Lhasa and executed monks from rival Buddhist sects. Local Tibetan groups began fighting a guerilla war against them. The Qing Emperor Kangxi viewed the Dzungar occupation of Tibet as a massive national security threat. Qing forces allied with local Tibetan partisans and defeated the outnumbered Dzungars. Tibet then came under the rule of the Qing dynasty of China in 1720 after the Qing expelled the forces of the Dzungar Khanate. Qing escorted and installed the 7th Dalai Lama onto the throne and recognized Tibet as its protectorate state where the Dalai Lama retained internal cultural and religious autonomy but China managed its foreign policy and defense.

events.title: Smallpox And King Bhaskar Malla
events.detail: One of the earliest known episode of smallpox in Nepal. The epidemic lasted for two years and accounted for 18,714 deaths. King Bhaskar Malla and his two wives isolated themselves away from the city in Kindol Bihar near Swayambhu. After six months of isolation king became restless. Upon the advice of a farmer who told the king that the epidemic had subsided the king in excitement is said to have immediately galloped to his palace. While living with his concubines he contracted the disease and died soon after. In the same year the Living Goddess Kumari also succumbed to the disease.

events.title: Paranoia of Jaya Prakash Malla
events.detail: Fiercely independent but deeply paranoid Kathmandu's final king Jaya Prakash Malla faced constant coups from his own nobility. He removed his local Newar generals and hires foreign mercenaries from India to guard the palace. The deep betrayal and fragmentation between the king and his subjects completely crippled Kathmandu's military cohesion.

events.title: The Gorkhali Infiltration
events.detail: Young Gorkhali Prince PN Shah lived inside the Bhaktapur palace as a guest of King Ranjit Malla. He formed a ritual brotherhood (Mijju) with the crown prince Bir Narsingh Malla. PN Shah spends three years observing the valley's political vulnerabilities geographical layouts and fractured defense frameworks using Bhaktapur’s hospitality to blueprint his future unification campaign.

events.title: The First Disaster at Nuwakot
events.detail: PN Shah rushes into an invasion of Nuwakot and is completely routed by Jaya Prakash Malla's forces. He had his reality check from that battle.

events.title: PN Shah Ascends the Gorkha Throne
events.detail: Following the death of his father Nara Bhupal Shah 20-year-old Prithvi Narayan Shah officially takes the crown.

events.title: The Banaras Military Overhaul
events.detail: PN Shah travels incognito to Banaras to purchase modern flintlock muskets and hires Muslim gunsmiths to establish domestic weapons factories in Gorkha. He institutes a strict military meritocracy uniting Khas Magar Gurung and Thakuri soldiers.

events.title: Capture of Nuwakot
events.detail: Armed with modern muskets and a tactical night-ambush strategy Gorkha crushes the Malla garrison seizing the lucrative Kerung trade pass to Tibet.

events.title: Thapathali Durbar Built
events.detail: Built by Kaji Nain Singh Thapa was the son of Amar Singh Thapa father of PM Mathabarsingh Thapa and maternal grandfather of Jung Bahadur Rana. After the fall of Thapa aristocracy Jung Bahadur Rana began to live in his grandfather's Thapathali durbar. Following Bhandarkhal Parva in 1848 he was able to seize all of the immediate property of his maternal uncle PM Mathabarsingh Thapa and PM Bhimsen Thapa. During this acquisition Jung also acquired Thapathali durbar complex. The palace was later confiscated from Jagat Jung. Chandra Sumsher stayed there for 18 years until 1904. After Chandra Shumsher's death his son Singha Shumsher JBR inherited the Thapathali Durbar Complex and named it Singha Mahal. In 1965 Nepal Rastra Bank sifted to Singha Mahal. It suffered severe structural damage during the 2015 which was completely reconstructed in its original design

events.title: Economy Before Unification
events.detail: Trade: Eastern Terai exported rice timber elephants to Bihar and Bengal; due to transport facility same rice couldn't reach Kathmandu in lack of transport facility. Butwal was trade center in the west. Exported iron brass copper ores in exchange of cotton goods of hills. In mountain region they exchanged rice ghee paper with Tibet for salt and wool. Kathmandu continued to be entreport for India and Tibet. However trade consisted limited processed goods such as metal-ware ivory goods wooden vessels and coarse variety of clothes. Newari merchants were competed with Indian traders and in many cases Nepali traders only became middlemen between trades of India and Tibet. Manufacturing: Cotton clothes sugar and paper manufactured in Kathmandu and hill area mostly for domestic consumption. Copper Iron Lead ores extracted in hilly region around Baglung. Monetization: Signs of monetized economy eg. wages for labors working to built royal palace in Jumla were paid in cash. Coin minted in Kathmandu valley (esp. patan) were only in circulation. Occupational Castes as Info for Economic Activity: In hill occupational castes only limited to tailors leather-workers black-smith gold-smith. Larger list in terai such as dairyman gardener washermen oilmen carpenter shopkeeper etc. In Kathmandu Newar community even more diverse such as painters land-surveyors incense-makers brick-makers confectioners ginger and radish cultivator etc. and more. Kathmandu was well known for handicraft in India and China. Land Tenure and Taxation: Raikar Birta Guthi Kipat Sera (appropriated for meething royal palace needs); Birta and Guthi represent alienation of state ownership right and it was profitable for the landowner as they enjoyed hight rent by tenent and unpaid labor service. In Eastern and Central Hills raikar landlords only enjoyed occupancy rights that could be inherited and subdivided but sale and mortgage is not allowed. Post-unification rents were based on Adhiya system i.e. half of gross produce. The tenants (mohi) were encouraged to use waste lands but eventually they were taken up converting to Raikar or Birta. So no matter the type of land tenure peasants were always exploited. In Karnali and Terai landholding rights appear to be in a form of property right by allowing landlords (Chuni ryots/raiti) the re-deemable or non-redeemable mortgages for land and permitting tax payment in money and in Terai only 5 crops rice mustard cotton/jute tobacco and sugarcane were eligible to collect tax in cash per unit of cultivation. In western Terai the measurement was ox-team i.e. hal syatem. So in Karnali and Terai land could be held without engaging in agriculture if taxes are paid in cash as compared to Central and Eastern Hills resulting in occupation of large waste lands making themselves Jamindars. Local Administration and Tax Collection: In Terai it pollower Mughal era system of local hierarchy. Local Jamindars from many villages choose among themself a Chaudhari who collects revenue. Each village is represented by senior ryot called Jetharaiyat representing the peseantry. In kathmandu Valley government was represented by Dware who collected revenue in help of 4 Pradhans the substantial landlords of the village. In hills each villages similarly functioned under head-men called Thani Mukhiya Jimmawal. In Kirat region it had head-men like Subba Mijhars and Rais exercising judicial authority colleceted tax fees fines etc.

events.title: Economic Blockade of Kathmandu Valley
events.detail: PN Shah begins capturing the high mountain ridges surrounding the Kathmandu Valley (including Makwanpur to the south and Sindupalchowk to the east) imposing a brutal economic blockade. Anyone caught smuggling grain salt or cotton is instantly executed causing hyperinflation and starvation inside the Malla capital.

events.title: First Battle of Kirtipur
events.detail: Gorkha assaults Patan’s shield fortress Kirtipur. A combined valley army routs the Gorkhalis. Gorkha's brilliant military mastermind Kalu Pande is killed. PN Shah narrowly escapes death.

events.title: Battle of Plassey & Start of East India Company Rule
events.detail: It occurred because the British abused trade privileges fortified Calcutta without permission and captured the city in response to local resistance. Despite commanding 50000 troops against just 3000 British soldiers the Nawab of Bengal lost due to internal treachery. His commander Mir Jafar secretly defected to Robert Clive in exchange for the throne. Jafar's troops refused to fight allowing the British to win install him as a puppet ruler and gain total control over Bengal. Through military power and alliances the British systematically defeat the Marathas and the Sikhs conquering the entire subcontinent.

events.title: Smallpox and King Jagat Prakash Malla
events.detail: The smallpox erupted in Bhaktapur but no epidemic was reported in Kathmandu. King Jagat Prakash Malla of Bhaktapur died.

events.title: Annexation of Makwanpur and the Defeat of Mir Qasim
events.detail: Gorkha annexes the southern Sen kingdom of Makwanpur. The Malla kings beg the Nawab of Bengal Mir Qasim to intervene. Gorkhali forces ambush the Nawab’s 2500-man army in the ridges capturing advanced European cannons and rifles.

events.title: Second Battle of Kirtipur
events.detail: A second failed assault on Kirtipur. PN Shah’s brother Surpratap Shah is permanently blinded in one eye by a defensive arrow.

events.title: Fall and Mutilation of Kirtipur
events.detail: On their third attempt the Gorkhalis infiltrate Kirtipur at night through betrayal. Furious over the deaths of Kalu Pande and his brother's eye PN Shah infamously orders his troops to cut off the noses and lips of every single male citizen in the town over the age of twelve leaving a psychological scar of terror across the remaining valley cities.

events.title: Kinloch Expedition Defeated
events.detail: Realizing total doom is near Kathmandu's Jaya Prakash Malla sends a desperate plea for help to the British East India Company. The British sends a heavily armed expeditionary force of 2400 soldiers under Captain Kinloch to march north and crush Gorkha. PN Shah plays the climate and geography perfectly. He lets the British forces enter the malaria-ridden dense jungles of Sindhuli Garhi then launches a brutal pincer ambush. The British are decimated by disease and Gorkhali kukris fleeing back to the plains. Gorkha captures British military technology.

events.title: 7.9 Mag. Northern Bagmati Earthquake
events.detail: The earthquake caused massive structural destruction, resulting in the collapse of over 18,000 houses across the country. Numerous ancient buildings and medieval temples were severely damaged or destroyed. There was a swarm of tremors (21 shocks in 24 hours) in this earthquake. The seismic shaking triggered or coincided with severe weather. Heavy monsoon rains heavily complicated the aftermath. The Bagmati River suffered catastrophic flooding, which swept away vital crops along its banks and entirely destroyed a major bridge spanning the river.

events.title: Conquest of Kathmandu
events.detail: During the annual Indra Jatra festival while Kathmandu’s soldiers are heavily intoxicated Gorkhali troops launch a silent three-sided assault. They capture Hanuman Dhoka palace without a major battle. JP Malla flees to Patan; PN Shah claims the throne.

events.title: Bloodless Fall of Patan
events.detail: Terrified by Kathmandu's sudden capture the corrupt noble ministers of Patan (the Pradhanas) instantly surrender the city. King Tej Narsingh Malla flees with JP Malla to Bhaktapur.

events.title: Jajarkot as First Vassal State
events.detail: Jajarkot was the first principality out of many to accept the status of a vassal under the Gorkhalis. In a letter to the Raja of Jajarkot Prithvi Naryan Shah wrote: "We confirm your ancestral authority within your territory including your authority to award capital punishment upgrade or degrade caste collect levies to finance the sacred thread investiture ceremonies and weddings of royal princes and princesses and fees for the expiation of caste offenses. We also confirm your authority to grant or confiscate Birta lands and to collcet judicial fines escheats and fees for stamping weights and measu-res. You shall pay only Rs. 701 whenevct a new King ascends our throne. When a new King ascends your throne you shall have authority to collect customary payments from your people."

events.title: Forced Labor and Slavery
events.detail: To fulfill labor requirement of the government every adult above 12 years of age was obilged to render compulsary unpaid labor called Jhara to state in activities such as temple construction transportation etc. also included service in army druing Ango-Nepal War. Also used to reclaim waste land construct irrigation canal capture wild elephants and supply fodder supply food and fruits to royal palace supply construction materials in some cases depending on their occupation. Beyond gov requirements revenue officials and landhords in many Terai districts were permitted to extract unpaid labor. Raiker lands got depopulated as labor for agriculture went to Jhara in 1790s government ordered to band forced labor in Terai districts. Morever it required the forced labor to be extracted only from inhabitants of Birta land and not Raikar. Also in Hills Jhara got banned for non-governmental jobs. In addition Slavery was widely practiced as a result of indebtness rebellion to Gorkha Kingdom violation of caste and cow-slaughter rules adultery etc. Later to stop emigrating slaves governmnet ordered release of slaves in few regions but they were rarely efective.

events.title: Land Revenue Collection
events.detail: In Hills land tax was mostly collected by Amanat System in which salaried government official called Dware collect taxes in corrdination to village head and landlords.It was less extractive and fairer. In Terai both Amana and Ijara System was practiced. In Ijara private contractor (Ijaradar) collects taxes providing fixed contract amount to government. It was highly extractive. Mostly government prefered this for easiness of the government.

events.title: Non-Land Tax Sources
events.detail: Royal Palace Levies or Walak: Progressive levy paid by each housestead village head landlords high-ranking officials according to their land area or economic status to fund special occasions in royal palace like bartabanda marriage funeral of royal family members. In some cases used to pay military expenses and loan incurred by Rana Bahadur Shah; Governmental Levies: Paid to cover governmental expenses. Darshan-Bhet was levy paid during appointment of military or civil employee. Salami was paid annually by different occupational members eg. Hunters had to supply one hide or skin annually for military use leather-workers paid two hides or skin. Fees were paid for copper inscription issued in record of birta land and transaction of Birta Guthi Kipat. Local Levies: Paid to village heads after new crop is harvested local Kotwal or police chief were paid in cash or kind Zamindars were paid taxes on marriages and use of communal facilities like water and forest. Commercial Taxes: Government gave contract for collection of costumes on exports and imports government had monopoly on cotton transit. Sales tax was collected at 1% on both buyer and seller in eastern Terai. Abolished in 1798 likely due to collecting difficulty and reintroduced in 1805 to more newly annexed terrotories simplifying it by collecting only from seller for sepecific luxury goods like jewelry textiles falcons horses elephants yarn blanckets wax copper iron paper tobacco herbs drugs salt musk sheep goat etc; Mines and Minting: Mining activities of copper iron and lead in Baglung and surrounding hills yielded revenues through exports which reduced later due to internal consumption on coin minting and weapon making. Minting of coin was charged 4% in coinage and 8% profit on mixing alloy; Forests: Duties were collected on exports of timber herbs musks elephants etc. in Terai. Falcons in north-western hills also contributed to exports. Judicial Fines: In absence of judicial courts military officers landlords and revenue collectors acted as judges and in many cases they acted as extractve instituion imposing heavy fines. Religious and caste related fines were also imposed eg. fines on slaughter of cows. Regressive Tax System: Most taxes were collecetd on economic activities on which the peasants and workers relied on. Property taxes were rear only one existing was Pota Tax whose effect was only in valley which too was burdened only on small landlords.

events.title: Major Socio-Economic Policies
events.detail: Land Reclaimation and Settlement: Before the Anglo-Nepal War government tried to reclaim waste lands directly through forced labor but it soon failed in absence of tenants to cultivate land in such a policy. It also resorted to giving waste lands and virgin forests to civil and millitray officials nobility chieftans etc. in the form of Birta. Another instrument was Jagir lands that were allotted to government employees and military. Often Jagirs were assigned for military consideration such as area of strategic importance like Makwanpur. The Birta and Jagir holders then recruited tenents for the development of such land. To increase revenue and finance military government also took policy of encouraging locals and Indians to reclain waste lands and settle in Terai. From time after 1793 officers were sent every year to Terai to arrange irrigation and incourage the reclaimation and settlement. Towards the end of 18th century large area of waste and virgin lands were given on contracts to individuals that had resources to promote land settlements. Rents for first few years were exempt and credit facilities were provided by governemt for an year at a low 12.5% rate. Post Anglo-Nepal war the Jhara needs declined and government started paying wages in certain cases. Nepal also faced sortage of labor as many slaves had fled to India. The government asked them and criminals who fled to return and settle in the waste lands and pay their due whenever they can. In the 1920s forests in the Rapti Valley and Morang were cleared for Hill settlers who were allocated land according to “the chronological order of their application”. In this scheme settlers could receive “as much land as they could reclaim”. However the initiative failed to establish permanent resettlement likely because of virulent malaria. Trade and Commerce: Government wanted foreigners not to interfere in trade with Tibet. Though Nepal and East India Company signed trade treaty in 1792 with aim of expanding trade to Tiber for India and with aim to increase export for Nepal it never got realized as Nepal didnt let Indian good pass Tibet except few commodities like wax timber ghee etc. In the period Nepal exported good worth 364000 and imported worth 71000. This surplus is result of Nepal limiting import only for royal needs. State was also involved in trading at that time opening market towns in Makwanpur (1806) and Saptari(1809) with the aim of capturing the trade with Tibetian. Gov thought that if Tibetians and foreigners meet then Nepali traders would lose their market. Market Regulation: Government banned use of foreign clothes solocal weavers sold the local clothes at prices fixed by government. As it was not economicaly viable cases of violation was seen which was punishable. Prices of curd milk and the grains in time of shortage were also fixed. Domestic Defence Production: With increase in demand of weapons Nepal started production of rifles and gunpowders in 1793 procuring technicians from India. Nepal couldn't fulfil the need of steel in the industries and had to export it from India. Incase of gunpowder the saltpetre was locally produced allowing smooth production. The ryots in Terai were given contract of extracting saltpetre for which 50% of price was given to them. Nationalization of Mining Industries: Before 1800 mines in the hills were privately maintained paying certain quantity if metal to gioernment. Due to large number of contractors the procurement of metals became difficult so in 1800 government brought all the mining industries into its supervision but it got soon reverted to contractors as the procurement became difficult due to distant terroteries. However governemnt maintaied monopoly over buying the metals at its fixed rate. Transportation and Communication: Government took policy of expanding communication to westward for military needs Kumaon and Gadhwal while isolating Kathmandu to South as a defence strategy against British. Large Scale Exodus: As the rent payment for tenants transioned to cash (Adhiya to Kut) many tenants couldn't get cash to pay for resnt they couldn't sell their crop timely resulting in burrowing money to pay rent and if crop failure occurs they couldn't pay rent and had to be enslaved. Many such slaves fled to India due to pressure from lenders and slave masters. Isolation: Soon after PN Shah took over Kathmandu Christian missionaries like Jesuit and Capuchin were expelled all foreign traders were banned no mountain trails linking Kathamndu to India was built. This policy remained unchanged untill 1950.

events.title: Fall of Bhaktapur and End of Malla Era
events.detail: Gorkhali forces scale the walls of Bhaktapur. The last three Malla kings Jaya Prakash Tej Narsingh and the elderly Ranjit Malla make a desperate final stand inside the Durbar Square. JP Malla is shot in the leg later spend his final days in area of Pashupatinath Tej Narsingh captured and kept in chains until his death and the elderly Ranjit Malla surrenders accepting peaceful exile to Varanasi. The 568-year Malla Era officially ends.

events.title: Birta Guthi and Kipat Confiscation
events.detail: Military requirement grew exponentially and land to allot for Jagir were not enough. Therefore PN Shah confiscated Birta and Guthi without royal sanctions and lack of evidences in the Kathmandu valley. Initially PN shah wrote to allow Kirats to enjoy their Kipat right but being skeptic many of them migrated to India and Sikkim. The lands of those fugitive Kirat were confiscated by the government. During Nepal-Tibet war this backfired as such Kirat joined the Tibetian forces against Nepal. Post-war the government invited the Kirats assuring their traditional land and customs were restored. Later in 1976 the regime came with idea of encouraging migration of non-Kirat communities from other part of Nepala and TIbet and India to Kirat region ensuring that they would get non-Kipat land as Raikar land. This broke the Kirat hegemony and their control over waste lands despite protest. Later ceilings were also imposed on Kipat holdings held without documentary devidences and excess holdings were confiscated. Taxes on homestead lands started to be collecetd after 1993 regardless of it being Kipat.SInce the Birta and Jagir land were not taxed government revenue shrunk transferring fiscal burden to the peasant workers and small trader class.

events.title: Pota Birta Introduced
events.detail: PN Shah's extensive ongoing military campaigns required a continuous flow of cash but a staggering amount of the valley's most fertile agricultural land was locked away as tax-exempt Birta holdings owned by religious institutions nobility and priests. To rescue his military treasury from starvation he introduced the Pota Tax. It established that state's sovereign right to revenue superceded religious and private immunities and was only property tax at the moment. Another type was Bekh birta which is temporary tax-exempt birta

events.title: Jagir Tenure and Rakam Formalized
events.detail: Royal treasury lacked the hard cash to pay thousands of soldiers and civil administrators the state assigned them right of taxable state land (Raikar) as their salaries temporarily so that they can collect taxes from land alloted to them. The Jagir tenure system was divided into Khuwa Jagir (dry land) tax paid on cash and Khangi Jagir (wet land) tax paid on kind or goods. Later due to inflation Khangi Jagirdars profited by collecting high-value in-kind revenue exploiting both the government and landholders compared to the stagnant cash value of Khuwa assignments. Rakam was a variant of Raikar where insted of cash it was paid by labor services or the delivery of specific goods to the state.

events.title: Rajya Tenure Introduced in Vassal States
events.detail: During expansion to avoid costly prolonged military battles it allowed states to act as vassal alloting chieftains (Rajautas) to collect and appropriate land revenues within their autonomous domains. Sirto Rajya: These states maintained substantial autonomy by paying a fixed annual tribute called sirto eg. Mustang Jajarkot Salyan. Thek/Thekka Rajya: These states operated on a fixed-revenue contract system acting as revenue-collecting intermediaries for the central government eg. Achham Dullu. Sarbangamaphi Rajya: These were rare highly privileged principalities typically bound to the central ruling family by strategic matrimonial alliances or exceptional loyalty eg. Bajhang.

events.title: War Economy and High Taxation
events.detail: During expansion era lacking sufficient cash reserves the state relied extensively on the Jagir system. Crown also pushed the Pota Tax onto traditionally tax-exempt private Birta estates and attempts to tax autonomous communal Kipat lands. Emergency wartime levies mainly the compulsory Jhura tax was collected to fund ammunition weapons manufacturing and foreign arms.

events.title: Death of PN Shah
events.detail: PN Shah dies at age 52 at Devghat. On his deathbed he delivers his geopolitical manifesto the Divya Upadesh

events.title: Pratap Singh Shah Dev
events.detail: Dies at age 26 of smallpox

events.title: Rana Bahadur Shah
events.detail: Dies at age 30

events.title: The Regency Blitzkrieg Under Bahadur Shah
events.detail: Under the aggressive regencies of mother Queen Rajendra Laxmi PN Shah's youngest son Bahadur Shah expands on a multi-front imperial blitz. Annexes Sen kingdoms of Chaudandi and Vijayapur pushing the border to the Teesta River (Sikkim). Conquers all 24 Chaubise and 22 Baise Rajyas crosses the Mahakali River and swallows the Indian hill states of Kumaon and Garhwal till Sutlej river.

events.title: Kausahi-Bisahi Levy Introduced
events.detail: Collected from Birta owning Brahmin and Sanyashis in annexed western hills for consideration of their land. Provision also mad ethe Brita owning Brhamins could relinquish their land as payment of Kausahi-Bisahi levy.

events.title: First Invasion of Tibet and Kerung Treaty
events.detail: Nepalese merchants had been circulating coins of a lower-alloy silver in Tibet leading to severe economic friction and Tibet halting trade with Nepal. The Shamarpa Lama a high-ranking Tibetan religious figure fled to Nepal due to a dispute over his inheritance and urged the Nepalese court to intervene. The Army under Damodar Pande won the batle and forced TIbet to sign Kerung Treaty making them pay tribute to Nepal a sum of Rs. 50001 every year in return for giving back to Tibet all the territories acquired during the war. Also ensured all trades go through Nepal and the routes through Sikkim and Bhutan remain closed.

events.title: Lack of National Integration
events.detail: Nepal got politically unified but nation-building din't happen in same manner. In western and far-western hills PN Shah and successors subjugated states as its vassal. Annexation only happened where the ruler revolted. Rulers were overly focused on expansion which gave no time for administrative divisions. Limbus of eastern hills and Tharus and Rajputs of Terai couldn't relate to new political authority at center. Even no Limbu or Rajput fought from Gorkha Army. Country was not connecetd geographically too. Only road and rope-ways were built for military purpose not trade and commerce.

events.title: Second Invasion of Tibet and Treaty of Betrawati
events.detail: When Tibet defaulted on their tribute payments Nepal launched a second highly aggressive invasion capturing Digarcha monastry and arresteing the minister of Lhasa Dhoren Kazi. Chinese Emperor Qianlong sent a massive Manchu-Tibetan army commanded by General Fuk'anggan which forced the Nepalese forces to retreat all the way back to Nuwakot. Nepali Army could stop them at Betrawati river and under the terms of Qianlong the treaty was signed. Most humiliating that Nepal had to to subordinate to Qing dynasty terms by presenting tribute to China every 5 year acting as a tributary state to the Qing Empire. Over the time it became less frequent taking even 14 years of gap. The last mission was in year 1906. Nepal also lost its right to isse silver coins and 32 Newar merchant lost their special tax-exempt status.

events.title: Land Tenurial Insecurity
events.detail: Before 1793 Jagirdars in hills could evict their tenant in yearly basis and in terai ryots were evicted if they reclaimed waste lands. This resulted in lower cultivation in Birta and Jagir lands and government in 1793 came up with tenurial security by allowing eviction only if the rents were not paid or some serious offence were made. This also extended to Birta Guthi and Kipat saying that eviction are not generally allowed but din't dictate the conditions on which they could be evicted. This in absence of central supervision gave the landlords enough room to exploit the tenants. The tenants were also obliged to supply loan to their landlords at 5% interest rate befor ethe harvest to cover expenses of the landlord otherwise landlord can evict their land. The burden of finding money to loan and the low intrest rate compared to general 25% in cash put massive cost to the peasants.

events.title: Revenue Estimate 1793
events.detail: Approx 5 Lakh. Revenue from Eastern Terai districts only totaled Rs. 244104. Western Terai was not annexed at the moment. Major sources were: duties on salt proft on saltpetre copper and iron land taxes; coin minting and duties on trade with Tibet; sale of elephants. Even after western terai annexation revenue didn't increase all collecetd revenue from west was spent on military needs.

events.title: Abdication of a Mad King Rana Bahadur Shah and Exile
events.detail: King Rana Bahadur Shah grandson of PN Shah abdicates the throne to crown his infant son Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah. He does this to legitimize his marriage to a beautiful Brahmin widow Kantipavati promising her child the succession against orthodox Hindu laws. Kantavati dies of smallpox. Driven insane by grief Rana Bahadur desecrates temples smashes the deity of Harati Ajima (Shitaladevi for Hindu worshiped as goddes of smallpox) at Syambhunath and executes the royal doctors. The terrified nobility led by Mulkaji Damodar Pande unites to force the mad king into exile in British-controlled Banaras.

events.title: Smallpox And King Rana Bahadur Shah
events.detail: A severe smallpox epidemic swept the valley and the queen of King Rana Bahadur Shah got infected. Seeing his wife gravely ill Rana Bahadur dedicated himself to prayers for her paid homage to the Goddess of smallpox Sitala Devi at Swayambhu and donated money for her speedy recovery. He even abdicated the throne in favour of his two-year old son Girvan. He also ordered children with the disease to be removed outside the Valley all the way across the Tama Kosi in the East or the Marsyandi in the West. Because of the Valley's demographics these were Newar children. Despite all efforts Kantivati succumbed to the disease making King mad and leading to his exile.

events.title: Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah
events.detail: Rules under the regency of Queen Tripurasundari dies of chickenpox at the age of 19

events.title: Ex King's Return and Execution of Damodar Pande
events.detail: In Banaras Bhimsen who was his millitary assistant acts as the exiled king's strategic brain plotting the return Meanwhile Nepal and East India Company signed a treaty that led to the establishment of the first British Resident Captain Knox In fight between Regents Subarnaprabha and Rajarajeshwari Knox sided with Subarnaprabha which Rajarajeshwari didn't like and treated him like persona non grata. After this British broke diplomatic ties with Nepal and allowed the ex-King Rana Bahadur to return to Nepal. Backed by Bhimsen's maneuvering Rana Bahadur marches back to Nepal. The state troops sent to stop him defect to his side. Rana Bahadur re-claims power as Mukhtiyar (Regent) and instantly orders the arrest and brutal decapitation of his chief rival war hero Damodar Pande at Thankot. Pandes were stripped of their ancestral lands exiled or reduced to poverty. During the exile Rana Bahadur borrowed large sums from East India Company and Indian merchants which were paid through revenue of Siraha Mahottari and Morang. Situation worsened so much that government was forced to borrow money from Indian merchants to run internal expenses.

events.title: Anglo-Nepalese Treaty
