events.detail: Trade and defense alliance to standardized customs duties and opened borders promise mutual military aid against common enemies and establish the first British Resident in Kathmandu

events.title: First British Resident Captain William O. Knox
Great Birta Confiscation (62 Haran)
events.detail: On top of high taxation citing the legal basis that many landholders lack proper documentary evidence the government launched a ruthless national survey. Bhimsen Thapa the then Mukhtiyar systematically confiscates the Birta and Guthi lands of thousands of religious priests and Brahmans. It was done to fund the military of ongoing unification campaign.

events.title: Killing of Rana Bahadur Shah
events.detail: To gain absolute power Bhimsen Thapa sought to destroy his rivals Sher Bahadur Shah and Tribhuvan Pradhan who were previously with Damodar Pande. He manipulated King Rana Bahadur into investigating Pradhan knowing it would drag Sher Bahadur Shah as well given their ties arguing that pardoning him was mistake and he was doing financial mishaldeling in wartime. Being unable to show the accounts he was sentenced to death.Terrified by an abrupt death sentence Khawas broke down in prison. He confessed and framed Sher Bahadur Shah as the mastermind behind the British collusion. During a tense late-night court tribunal called to investigate financial corruption a bitter argument breaks out between Rana Bahadur and his hot-headed half-brother Sher Bahadur Shah. In a flash of rage Sher Bahadur draws his sword and slashes King Rana Bahadur Shah down killing him on the spot.

events.title: Bhandarkhal Parva and Rise of Bhimsen Thapa
events.detail: With the King dead and the assassin killed Bhimsen Thapa locks down the city gates. He weaponizes the tragedy falsely blaming the entire anti-Thapa nobility for a grand conspiracy to kill the monarch. His troops surround the Bhandarkhal palace gardens. Bhimsen orders the systematic slaughter of 77 high-ranking noblemen ministers and rival military officers in a single night. He forces Rana Bahadur's senior queen to go Sati to eliminate royal opposition. With his enemies entirely wiped off the map Bhimsen Thapa appoints himself Mukhtiyar (Prime Minister) launching 31 years of absolute undisputed dictatorial control over Nepal.

events.title: Bhimsen Thapa
events.detail: Over Militrization: Reorganized the Gorkhali army along western lines introducing standardized uniforms European drilling and modern military ranks. Established Nepal's first major state-run arsenals gunpowder factories and artillery foundries constructed permanent military barracks. Architecture: Built the original eleven-story twin Dharahara one in at his residence Janarala Bagh, Bhotebahal and another at Sundhara. Upgraded the Basantapur Palace with western-influenced architecture. Isolation: Introduced passport policy through militarized border-control strategy designed to protect Nepal from British infiltration utilizing the Churia hills as a primary defense line. The policy required travel documents and imposed rigorous searches with severe death penalties for officials allowing anyone through without proper authorization

events.title: Kut System Replacing Adhiya System
events.detail: The Adhiya system in hill region limited the landlords to benefit from the competition among the cultivators. Kut system was introduced which fixed the rates ie. pre-determined volume of grain to the landlord based on the category of land.

events.title: Anglo-Nepal War
events.detail: British claimed Butwal belonged to them because they had recently taken over the territory of the Nawab of Oudh who previously claimed suzerainty over Butwal. In May 1814 Nepalese forces attacked a British police post in Butwal killing a British officer which beacme immediate cause.

events.title: Balbhadra Kunwar at Battle of Nalapani
events.detail: Balbhadra Kunwar defended the Khalanga Fort with just 600 people (including women and children) against 3500 British troops. They inflicted heavy casualties and killed British General Gillespie. When the British cut off their water supply the 70 survivors refused to surrender. After days of drinking polluted water and blood they drew their kukris and fought their way out.

events.title: Amar Singh Thapa at Siege of Malaun
events.detail: After Bhakti Thapa's death Amar Singh Thapa was surrounded by British forces at Malaun and was forced to surrender the western territories.

events.title: Smallpox and First Vaccine Drive
events.detail: The disease appeared first in the west of the country but found its way to Kathmandu by July. Officials requested vaccinations from the British who had been trying to spread the new practice in India for over a decade. The British organised vaccinations around the Valley beginning in Banepa. It is hard to say how many people actually got vaccinated. But one thing we do know: the king was not among them. In late October both of the king's children showed fever and then rash. One perished on 2 November. Two weeks later on 18 November Gardner learned that 'the Raja had unfortunately taken the smallpox'. He died two days later. Despite regular resurgence of disease vaccination use was sporadic and government efforts weak. Several reasons explain why Nepalis did not use vaccination. Some people particularly some Newars and Tarai groups disliked the vaccine. But a far greater problem was that the Rana governments did little to make it widely available or to promote it. They never set up a health system to promote sound practices across Nepal.

events.title: Thapas vs. Pandes
events.detail: Pandes the decendents of Damodar Pande utilized lingering public humiliation of the Sugauli Treaty labeling Bhimsen Thapa a coward who had surrendered holy Nepalese soil to the British. They had support of Senior Queen Samrajya Laxmi who was fed up of Bhimsen Thapa's monopoly in state. Junior Queen Rajya Laxmi was supporting Bhimsen Thapa's nephew Mathabar Singh Thapa to counter Pande faction.

events.title: Sugauli Treaty
events.detail: Nepal is stripped of nearly one-third of its imperial territory surrendering Sikkim in the east Kumaon and Garhwal in the west and major chunks of the fertile Terai. The borders of Greater Nepal are permanently fixed to the Mechi River in the east and the Mahakali River in the west. A British Resident is permanently stationed in Kathmandu to monitor the court. Impressed from the fight of Nepali soldiers in the war the forces of Kumaon and Garwal were recruited in the British-Indian army for the first time. By 1857 Indian Mutiny there were five Gurkha regiments in the army.

events.title: First Permanent British Resident Edward Gardner
Rajendra Bikram Shah Dev
events.detail: Dies at the age of 67 under confinement in the Bhaktapur palace

events.title: 7.8 Mag. Gorkha Earthquake
events.detail:
It struck on 25 April 2015 at 11:56 a.m., with a magnitude of about Mw 7.8–7.9, along the Main Himalayan Thrust, at a shallow depth of about 8.2 km. Human loss: About 8,857 people died in Nepal and more than 22,000 were injured; nearly 3.5 million people were left homeless. Including deaths in India, China and Bangladesh, the total death toll was about 8,964. Cultural heritage: Numerous historic monuments and UNESCO World Heritage sites were destroyed or severely damaged, including parts of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur Durbar Squares, Changu Narayan and major temples. Dharahara collapsed, killing at least 180 people. Immediate Response: The Nepal Army launched Operation Sankat Mochan. Around 90% of Nepal Army soldiers were mobilized for rescue and relief. Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force were also heavily deployed. According to PDNA, 65,059 Nepal Army personnel, 41,776 Nepal Police personnel, 24,775 Armed Police Force personnel, 22,500 civil servants, around 4,000 government and private health workers were involved in rescue and relief. International Response: A major assessment found that 34 countries physically sent personnel around 76 urban search-and-rescue team approximately 2,242 personnel, 135 search-and-rescue dogs, around 141 foreign medical teams, roughly 1,858 medical professionals and 18 foreign military teams participated in the emergency response. India's Operation Maitri involved the Indian Army, Indian Air Force and National Disaster Response Force. Indian aircraft began operating within hours sending its NDRF search-and-rescue teams. The Indian government subsequently reported 2,223 sorties, evacuation/rescue of approximately 11,200 people, transportation of around 1,700 tonnes of relief material, and medical assistance to 4,762 injured people. China, the United States, United Kingdom, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Japan, Israel, Australia, Canada, Spain, Singapore, Malaysia, Poland, Thailand and others contributed rescue personnel, medical teams, aircraft and supplies. The United States deployed military personnel and aircraft. One tragic episode occurred on May 12 when a US Marine Corps UH-1Y helicopter delivering relief supplies crashed near Charikot, killing six US Marines and two Nepali soldiers. Nepal's infrastructure could not easily absorb the sudden arrival of thousands of foreign personnel, aircraft and tonnes of relief material. Problems included congestion at Kathmandu airport, customs delays, insufficient helicopters, difficulty reaching remote areas, duplication of some forms of aid, inappropriate or unnecessary relief materials, concerns about distribution, coordination problems, political disputes over who controlled aid. There was also tension over whether international NGOs should route assistance through the government's official disaster-relief mechanisms or distribute it directly. Kathmandu airport itself became a bottleneck, and restrictions were placed on heavy aircraft after cracks appeared on the runway.PDNA and Aid: The Post-Disaster Needs Assessment estimated approximately $7 billion in recovery and reconstruction needs, while later estimates put total economic damage at around $10 billion. The housing problem was particularly enormous. On June 25, 2015, government organized an international donors' conference in Kathmandu. At the conference, international donors pledged approximately $4.4 billion for Nepal's recovery and reconstruction covering 66% of the estimated $6.7 billion recovery and reconstruction requirement. The conference was therefore a diplomatic success for Nepal. India made one of the largest commitments. India pledged approximately $1 billion in cash and materials for reconstruction, with approximately one-quarter of the pledge being a grant. This is particularly significant because India had already spent heavily on the immediate rescue operation through Operation Maitri. Reconstruction:

A major Rural Housing Reconstruction Program was established for earthquake-affected districts.

Damage was estimated at around US$10 billion, roughly half of Nepal’s GDP at the time. Reconstruction therefore became a major national economic challenge. Long-term social consequences: The disaster affected housing, migration, urbanization, debt, tourism, healthcare and social inequality. Vulnerable groups, particularly poor and marginalized communities, faced greater difficulty accessing relief and reconstruction assistance. International response: Nepal received massive international assistance. Around US$3 billion was pledged, with India launching Operation Maitri and numerous countries sending rescue teams, medical personnel, supplies and financial assistance.

events.title: British Resident Brian Houghton Hodgson
events.detail: He previously served as assistent resident and took over the position after retirement of Gardner

events.title: Bihar-Nepal Earthquake
events.detail: Magnitude of 7.6–7.9 epicentred in Phaplu, Solukhumbu. At least 30% or more of all homes in northern Nepal were destroyed death toll remained under 500. The Dharaha built in Janarala Bagh was torn in half and was never rebuilt. The Dharaha at Sundhara was newly built a year later for Queen Lalit TripuraSundari Devi. It caused heavy pressure on national reserve due to relief and reconstruction tasks.

events.title: Darjeeling Established a Hill Station and Nepalese Migration
events.detail: Darjeeling was established as a hill station in 1835 when the Raja of Sikkim gifted the ridge to the British East India Company as a health camp. British officials wanted a cool mountain escape from the hot summer weather in the plains of India. Dr. Archibald Campbell took charge in 1839. He built roads and brought people to the area and subsequent growth of tea estates, covering 700,000 acres by 1871, also created a huge demand for labour. One estimate is that 12 to 15 per cent of the Kiranti population in the eastern hills of Nepal moved across the border between 1840 and 1860. Ironically enough, in mixing here with other ethnic groups from Nepal, the emigrants’ need for Nepali as a lingua franca was higher than at home; this in turn affected their own languages. A sample of the Thangmi language collected by Brian Hodgson in Darjeeling in 1847 shows more Nepali influence than is found in the Thangmi spoken today in the Dolakha and Sindhupalchok districts of Nepal itself.

events.title: Second Dharahara Built
events.detail: Queen Lalit Tripura Sundari Devi was actually Bhimsen Thapa's niece. Seeing his amazing tall building, she wanted a tower of her own next to Bhimshen's Dharahara. Because of her royal request, Bhimsen Thapa built the second, slightly shorter tower at Sundhara. After the original Bhimsen Tower was destroyed, Queen Lalit Tripurasundari's tower came to be known as Bhimsen Stambha.

events.title: Diplomatic Blow to Bhimsen Thapa
events.detail: Hodgson wanted Nepal to sign trade treaty so that Britain can use Kathmandu as a commercial highway to open trade with Tibet and China. But Bhimsen Thapa resisted on this in line of this isolationist policy. Later when Bhimsen thapa sent his nephew Mathbarsingh Thapa on a high-profile diplomatic mission to London via Calcutta Hodgson sent secret communications to the acting British Governor-General in Calcutta. He refused Mathbarsingh travel permits and took the gifts and official letters meant for King William IV in Calcutta promising to forward them himself. Sabotaging the mission Hodgson exposed that Bhimsen actually had no influence over the British. This public humiliation ruined Bhimsen’s credibility.

events.title: Fall of Bhimsen Thapa
events.detail: After the diplomatic blow his position continuously weakened. Mathbarsingh wasted 150000 rupees of state funds in Calcutta on dancers and luxury while country was facing cash crunch. Bhimsen Thapa faced massive criticism and cost him personal treasury to compensate it after Queen complained. To fix the cash crunch the palace cut army salaries destroying the military's loyalty to Bhimsen Thapa. Same year Mathbarsingh's illicit affair with his widowed sister-in-law resulting in a child. Bhimsen’s bitter rival Ranajung Pande exposed this publicly. The scandal disgraced the Thapa family forcing Mathbarsingh to flee the capital into exile. palace stripped Mathbarsingh of his military command. The senior queen was able to convince King Rajendra Bikram Shah to use Pajani to replace Thapa governers with Pande. July 1837 when the Senior Queen's youngest infant son suddenly and mysteriously died Pandes immediately rumored that the royal vaidya put poison into the prince's medicine on orders of Bhimsen Thapa. This led to Bhimsen’s immediate arrest and imprisonment in chains setting off the chaotic series of bloody massacres and counter-coups that ultimately cleared the path for Jung Bahadur Rana in 1846.

events.title: Tyranny of the Pandes
events.detail: Following Bhimsen Thapa's death Rana Jang Pande became Mukhtiyar. His faction seized absolute control of the administration. Thapa witch-hunting started and Bhimsen Thapa’s nephew Mathabar Singh Thapa fled to India.

events.title: Brian Hodgson's Intervention
events.detail: Pande coming to power runied the treasury state failed to pay the army Jagir lands. The army soon marched on the palace and demanded pay British Resident Brian Hodgson intervened decisively calling Rana Jang Pande's resignation warning British would attack otherwise. Terrified of losing crown King Rajendra dismissed Rana Jang Pande.

events.title: Lord Ellenborough and British Shift to Strict Non-Interference
events.detail: Ellenborough became the Governor-General of India detested "politicals" (civilian diplomats) who meddled in native states. He ordered Hodgson to withdraw entirely from Nepalese court affairs and maintain strict neutrality. Believing he knew Nepal better than his superior Hodgson largely ignored these instructions. Hodgson directly violated Nepalese sovereignty by giving refuge inside the British Residency to an Indian merchant who was actively being hunted by King Rajendra Shah. In a bizarre move to protect his own position Hodgson conspired with King Rajendra. They attempted to secretly mail a joint appeal directly to the high authorities in London completely bypassing and undermining Ellenborough’s command in India. Furious at this insubordination Ellenborough summarily dismissed Hodgson in late 1843. To humiliate him he demoted Hodgson to a minor clerk position in Simla prompting Hodgson to resign from the service completely.

events.title: British Resident Sir Henry Montgomery Lawrence
events.detail: He practiced non-interference. He famously stated that the Nepalese court was a "volcano" and that British interference would only trigger an explosion. Lawrence spent his time studying Nepalese culture writing essays and helping his wife Honoria recover her health in the hills. During his stay he took note of a sharp ambitious young military officer named Jung Bahadur Kunwar (later Rana). Lawrence wrote in his journals that Jung Bahadur was the most capable dangerous and ruthless man in Nepal predicting he would eventually seize the country.

events.title: Mathabar Singh Thapa Becomes Prime Minister
events.detail: Senior Queen Samrajya Laxmi died of sudden fever in 1841 further weakening Pandes. Junior Queen Rajya Laxmi forced king to issue royal decree granting her Joint-Sovereignty. King then appointed a weak neutral coalition Prime Minister Chautariya Fateh Jung Shah. Fearing rise of Pande under him the queen and Brian Hodgson concluded that they needed a strongman from the Thapa bloodline to restore order. Mathabar Singh Thapa was called from India and made the Prime Minister.

events.title: Assassination of Mathabar Singh Thapa
events.detail: He firmly refused to help the Queen strip Crown Prince Surendra of his birthright she found hyper-ambitious 28-year-old army colonel named Jang Bahadur Kunwar the nephew of Mathwar to kill him. On the midnight of May 17 1845 Mathabar was summoned to the royal palace under the emergency pretext that the King had fallen critically ill. As Mathabar rushed into the dark royal bedchamber his nephew Jang Bahadur emerged from behind a screen and shot him dead in the back. Fateh Jung Shah was made Prime Minister

events.title: Acting British Resident Captain George O.B. Ottley
events.detail: Permanent resident John Russell Colvin fell overly sick leaving Captain Ottley as the Acting Resident

events.title: Kot Massacre
events.detail: Though Fateh Jung was PM the true de facto ruler of Kathmandu was Gagan Singh Bhandari the Junior Queen's handsome favorite courtier political ally and clandestine lover. On the evening of September 13 1846 at around 10 pm Gagansingh was mysteriously shot dead. Knowing Gagansingh’s death Rajya Laxmi went insane with grief and rage demanding immediate blood-soaked vengeance she ordered the entire nobility military officer corps and civil ministers of Nepal to assemble immediately unarmed at the kot. Jung Bahadur already had 500 loyal soldiers at the Chhauni Barracks just near the palace commanded by his brothers. They were instructed not to let anyone except court members inside not even king. Courtiers filled Queens ear that Birkeshar was the culprit and Jung Bahadur also agreed. Abhimansingh Rana suspected that the murderer was Jung Bahadur also agreed. Knowing that Queen and Jung Bahadur are about to kill Birkeshar he then dashed to inform King Rajendra about the situation in kot. King went to the Kot right away despite Abhimansingh's warning. Even Jung Bahadur's army couldn't dare to stop the king. Queen ordered Abhimansingh to cut down Birkeshar. King intervenes saying that we cannot cut somebody down just for the heck of it. Fattejung Shah was not there king said we would do necessary once he comes. After a while KIng himself goes to Fattejung's residence to fetch him. Fattejung suggests that they may return from the Kot safely only if they take the British envoy along with them; otherwise they might fall into the ambush of Junge. King orders that everyone to keep going to Kot while he would bring the envoy. Queen stepped down the stairs ordered to kill Birkeshar otherwise she would kill him. Three wise men Fateh Jung Abhimansingh and Dalbhanjan Pande suggested that anecssary action be taken only after finding truth yet Queen was not satisfied with the answers of Birkeshar. To console her he was chained then she returned to the hall climbing back up the stair. Fattejung Abhimansingh and Dalbhanjan stood at the foot of the stairs hoping that the queen would summon them. But no sooner had the queen entered the sitting room than gunfire burst out all of a sudden—all the three ministers were shot from behind with the bullets passing through their bodies. Fattejung and Dalbhanjan fell immediately while Abhimansingh who was shot in the leg. Before he was stabbed by the watchman he screamed "Gagan Singh was killed by Jung Bahadur! I am being murdered for knowing the secret!". After that Jung Bahadur and his borthers surrounded the kot and caused absolute slaughter in which Pande and Thapa nobles were kileld and 55 top-ranking ministers were slaughtered in a single night. King Rajendra appoint Jung Bahadur as Prime Minister in the morning.

events.title: King Rajendra's Plea to British Resident
events.detail: While everyone assembeled in the kot King Rajendra went to call British envoy the assistant resident Ottley in Lajimpat at 1 am. At the gate the king was told that the acting Resident was suffering from severe rheumatism and ‘does not see people at night’. Thus the King was turned back by a junior officer at the behest of the envoy. A disappointed and disheartened King Rajendra returned home. While returning the King out of fear avoided the Kot courtyard and went directly to his palace.

events.title: Jung Bahadur Rana
events.detail: Initially started as Mukhtiyar later after the Sanad became Prime Minister. Died naturally at age 59.

events.title: Government Employees Data 1846
events.detail: Beureaucrats-2997 Army-18971 Elite Force 212

events.title: Bhandarkhal Massacre
events.detail: Queen demanded Jung Bahadur to execute Crown Prince Surendra to clear the path for her son but he refused stating he would protect the rightful heir. Queen organized a secret counter-coup allying with Basnyat clan. Planning to ambush Jung Bahadur in Bhandarkhal garden. Bir Dhoj who had been sent to bring him was killed. Bahadur marched his armed soldiers to the Bhandarkhal gardens caught the conspirators completely by surprise and slaughtered 23 of them on the spot. Queen Rajya Laxm and King were sent to exile in Varanasi. Fragile Prince Surendra was put on the throne as a puppet prisoner-king.

events.title: Surendra Bikram Shah Dev
events.detail: Dies naturally at age 51

events.title: Alau Parva
events.detail: Fearing exlied King's plot to return Jung Bahadur officially declared him unfit to rule and dethroned on May 1847 crowing Surendra as new King. Infuriated by his dethronement King Rajendra raised a small ragtag army of loyalists and exiled anti-Rana courtiers in India. In July 1847 he crossed the border back into Nepal setting up a military camp at a small village named Alau (in Parsa). Jung Bahadur’s forces easily ambushed and routed King’s troops at Alau. The KIng was captured and brought back to the Kathmandu as a prisoner.

events.title: Pretext of JBR's Europe Trip
events.detail: Towards the end of 1848 a fierce battle erupted between the British and the Sikhs in Punjab. JBR wanted to help the British side offering troops. However his offer was declined twice. Being humiliated he marched to Bisauli of Bara district with large entourage including 32000 foot soldiers 52 cannons etc. for hunting and showcasing his power. However the spread of cholera and malaria which began killing the soldiers forced them to return. At the beginning of his rule he confiscated vast Jagir holdings in Terai of nobles died during Kot Massacre and kept them to himself. However the revenue collection didn't go as expected since the Chaudharies who were given contract to collect taxes they used to abscond the fund and flea to India. He made an agreement with British administration in Calcutta for extradition of such criminals.However British officers didn't cooperate which frustrated JBR. He then decided to establish direct relationship with the crown inGreat Britain bypassing generals in India. Hence he expressed his desire to the then Resident Colonel Thorsby. Thorsby suggested to write a letter which he did and sent it to Calcutta. The Governor-General forwarded the message to Britain where the request was accepted. The British also asked the Governor-General to arrange the necessary provisions. Subsequently James Broun-Ramsay sent a letter of acceptance to Kathmandu. The visit was to be diplomatic in nature with Jung Bahadur visiting as a Royal Ambassador. After appointing his brother Bam Bahadur Kunwar as interim prime minister and Badri Narsingh as interim Commander-in-Chief Jung Bahadur left Kathmandu for Calcutta.

events.title: Charburja Durbar/ Bahadur Bhawan Built
events.detail: It was built as a residence for Maharani Jind Kaur the youngest queen consort of the Sikh Empire’s Maharaja Ranjit Singh who fled British imprisonment and sought political asylum in Nepal. The original structure was heavily damaged by a massive fire in 1905. The palace was initially occupied by Commander-in-Chief Rudra Shumsher Rana. However in 1934 the powerful Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher Rana launched a political purge stripping Rudra Shumsher of his power and exiling him to Palpa. Juddha Shumsher seized the grand property and handed it over to his own son General Bahadur Shumsher Rana. From that point forward the estate was renamed Bahadur Bhawan in his honor. In 1954 Boris Lissanevitch a charismatic former Russian ballet dancer chef and Calcutta club Club 300 owner established Nepal's first international-standard luxury hotel the Royal Hotel inside Bahadur Bhawan. When King Tribhuvan was in exile he became a regular at Boris's club and formed a close personal friendship. Later King personally invited Boris to relocate to Kathmandu. Coming to Nepal he formed partnership with Prince Basundhara and negotiated a lease for a massive vacant wing of Bahadur Bhawan to open the Royal Hotel. It was Nepal’s first luxury hotel and a place fit for western dignitaries and tourists. With opening of other hotels like Soaltee and Annapurna and growing competition the famous hotel closed in 1969.

events.title: JBR's Europe Trip
events.detail:
He took with him 16 officials including his brothers Jagat Shumser and Dhir Shumser childhood friend and confidant Senior Captain Ran Mehar Adhikari and kaji Karbir Khatri a physician an artist 4 cooks and 22 servants. Among all Dhir Shumser could make most favorable impression to British because of his charm and tact. Karbir Khatri was veteran of several diplomatic mission like one to Peking. He was caught in two occasions: while carrying secret letetst to Lahore proposing anti-british alliance with Sikhs and in embezzelment of state treasury. Jung Bahadur wished to keep him under survillience. He was religious bigot too and was not liking the idea of going to beef-eating country but had no choice. The team spent 15 days of hunting in Terai and reached Calcutta in 7 weeks. He was well-received in Calcutta with 19-gun salutes civic receptions and grand balls. On 7 April the team boarded a P&O steamer for 6 week voyage to England. The ship traveled through Madras Sri Lanka and Aden before reaching the Suez Canal. In Egypt Jung Bahadur and his team visited Cairo and Alexandria where he met with Abbas Helmi. On 15 May the team arrived in Southampton.

Brought in manual press from England and named it Gidde Press.

events.title: Muluki Ain
events.detail: Within a month of return from Britain he appointed a 230 member Law Council i.e. Ain Kausal to codify law. Finally after 3 years of deliberation the 1400 page of Muluki Ain was promulgated. It replaced fragmented local customs and arbitrary royal decrees with a single written code applicable across the whole kingdom and left no descretionary power to the implementing officer. It covered major issues such as crime murder violation of caste law religious endowments charitable trusts land tenure land measurement division of inheritance purchase and sales of slaves welfare of widows and orphans marriage regulations practice of sati etc. It had provison of punishing the complainant if the allegation turned out false. The legal code also reduced the intensity of punishment compared to practiced customs. Treason rebellion homicide and cow killing remained capital offence but punishment for manslaughter and killing of cow were reduced to life imprisonment. The Muluki AIn's principle was that loss of life was to be paid by loss of life. Initially it imposed complete ban on gambling but was later allowed in special occasions. Legal minimum age of female for marriage was five. Only few exceptions were granted for sati system while the system largely remained. JBR feared social opposition from Hindu establishment for any such reforms. It had interesting privision to convert prision term with fine of Rs 5 for each month. No court fee but winner of money related cases had to pay 20% to government as jitauri. Codified Caste Hierarchy: Muluki Ain was based on Manusmriti scruitures and local customs. The code divided the entire population of Nepal into five distinct hierarchical groups: Tagadhari (Wearers of the Holy Cord) i.e. Hill Brahmins and Chhetris, Namasinya Matwali (Non-enslavable Alcohol Drinkers) i.e. high-status indigenous ethnic groups such as Magar, Gurung, Rai, and Limbu, etc, Masinya Matwali (Enslavable Alcohol Drinkers) i.e. marginalized indegenous groups such as Tamang, Chepang, and Thami, etc., Pani Nachalne Tara Choichhito Halnu Naparne (Impure, but Touchable) i.e. Muslims, foreigners, and specific Newar occupational groups, and Pani Nachalne Choichhito Halnu Parne (Impure and Untouchable) i.e. Dalits such as Kami, Damai, and Sarki, etc. Criminal punishments, court fees and legal rights were heavily determined by an individual's caste status. High-caste Tagadharis were immune to the death penalty or enslavement, facing only fines or shaving of the head (mundan). For instance, Brahmin and women were never put to death. Conversely, lower-caste individuals faced brutal corporal punishment, enslavement, or execution for minor offenses against upper castes. The code strictly regulated endogamy to prevent the mixing of castes. Hypergamy was strictly regulated through complex sub-caste assignments for offspring and Hypogamy was treated as a severe capital offense, resulting in execution, life imprisonment, or asset forfeiture. bhat or water with whom. Committing a violation—such as a Brahmin drinking water touched by someone in a Pani Nachalne caste—resulted in legal prosecution, state-mandated fines, and forced ritual penance to restore purity. The code legally locked generations into hereditary professions. It banned lower castes from owning property in certain areas, entering specific temples, or pursuing occupations reserved for the ruling elites. This mechanism systemically blocked social and economic mobility.)

events.title: Second Nepal–Tibet War
events.detail: Tibetians started occupying and collecting tax from the regions Nepal sold the grazing rights 10 years back. When Nepal sent its tax collectors in that region the mission was ill-treated and obstructed while some also died enroute. Nepali traders in Lhasa were persistently violated and the resident of Nepal Gorvernment was expelled. Nepal had 3 demands: payment of RS 1 Crore as compensation for loses of Nepalese merchants restoration of Kuti and Kerong districts cession of district of Taklakot in western Tibet. When no response came from Tibet Dhir Shumsher and Khadga Shumsher attacked through Kuti General Krishna Dhoj attacked through Mustang and Jung Bahadur attacked from Kerong totaling 27000 troops. Initially Nepal captured Kuti Kerong and Jhunga districts bringing Tibetians to negotiating table however the talks dragged on till winter. Snow disconnecetd Nepal's communication and meantime Tibet attacked with 60000 soldiers recapturing Kuti and Jhunga. Nepal brought another 14000 troops in counter attack recapturing Kuti Jhunga and Taklakot. By Januray 1856 both siides were desperate to end the war Tibet faced revolt in Kham province while peasants became hostile as about 4 lakh of them were involved in this war insted of their farming duty. A treaty was signed in which Tibetans agreed to make annual payment of Rs 10000 refrain from imposing custom duties on nepali goods and allow Nepalese merchants in Lhasa. In return Nepal withdrew occupied districts of Kuti kerong and Jhunga. It was indeed a Pyrrhic victory as the gains from treat could hardly offset Rs 30 lakh spent on war effort.

events.title: Terai Exploitation
events.detail: Terai was heavily forested malaria-ridden and used as a natural defensive barrier against British India. Jung Bahadur radically shifted this policy to maximize revenue. Mass Deforestation happened and cleared land was transformed into farmland to grow cash crops like grain tobacco and opium. Ranas brought in landless peasants from India and the hills to cultivate the land. These farmers were heavily exploited by Zamindars (landlords) and intermediaries through exorbitant rents forced labor and arbitrary evictions. extraction pipeline exporting high-value Sal timber and grain to British India while paying zero taxes to the state exchequer.

events.title: Bam Bahadur Rana
events.detail: Served till natural death

events.title: Lal Mohar/ Sanad
events.detail: Till 1856 he had consolidated power but was a normal PM who could be replaced by King. To eliminate this vulnerability Jung Bahadur orchestrated a brilliant realpolitik trap. He suddenly resigned from the premiership citing exhaustion and mental burnout. It created chaos in the country. Bam Bahadur became the PM. Relinquishing PM title he was actually eying to return as something more than an ordinary prime minister. Within 5 days of his resignation he conferred himself the sovereignty of Kaski and Lamjung after King Surendra was issued Lal Mohar to a document drafted by Jung Bahadur himself. He became the Maharaja which granted full de jure sovereignty of part of Nepal and partial de jure sovereignty over whole of Nepal. It also decided of their lineage using surname of Rajput Rana the 14th century rulers of Chittor who were known for heroic defence against Muslim invators. He created his own Roll of Succession and ensured that King could not deploy a single soldier spend a single rupee of state revenue or meet with foreign diplomats without the written consent of him.

events.title: Jung Bahadur's Dilemma
events.detail: Though he became the Maharaja British administration refused of recognizing dual sovereignty because of which his title became meaningless. Britain thought recognition of two Maharaj will create civil war and continued engaging with KIng and and PM bypassing Jung Bahadur. After the death of Bam bahadur and while Britain was engaged in fighting Indian Rebellion Jung bahadur reinstated himself as the new Prime Minister of Nepal. King Surendra also handed the power of Pajani to Jung Bahadur

events.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857 and Start of British Raj
events.detail: Triggered by the use of animal-fat greased cartridges that offended Hindu and Muslim sepoys/soldiers the revolt quickly spread across northern and central India fueled by deep-seated resentment over heavy taxation forced land annexations if a ruler died without a direct male heir and religious interference. Led by figures like Rani Lakshmibai aka Jhasi ki Rani and Bahadur Shah Zafar the rebellion ultimately failed due to a lack of centralized leadership and unity. However it marked a major turning point in history by permanently dissolving company rule and transferring direct control of India to the British Crown establishing the British Raj.

events.title: Nepal's Assistance in Indian Mutiny
events.detail: Jung Bahadur's led a force from Kathmandu to help British troops recapture Lucknow. Jung Bahadur made conscious choice of supporting Britan instead of the rebels knowing the military might of Britain during his Europe trip. Rewarding Nepal's service British Government restored Nepal's 300-kilometer land of Terai called Naya Muluk (Present day Banke Bardiya Kailali Kanchanpur). Nepal also got 6 lakh 80 thousand as salary for the troops 4000 bullock carts laden with plunder and Lucknow's Begum rebel leader Nana Saheb and 3000 soldier's wealth as they had come to Dang and Butwal during the war

events.title: Diffusal of Tibetain Problem
events.detail: Nepalese residnet in Tibet was assaulted at a formal state darbar. Jung Bahadur called him back and started preparing for a war. However the army has grown weak and unprofessional by the time. Country maintained active force of 25000 army troops which could be stretched up to 60000 if trained arm personels and retired ones were included. After 1855 war with Tibet army came into inexperienced hand especially due to appointment of under-age Rana family members into top ranking military positions. Average pay was also unattractive as their salaray remained unchanged since 1870s earning just Rs 70 per annum. Even though country was on war footing Jung Bahadur opened negotiation channel and the resident was restored.

events.title: Albert Edward the Prince of Wales' (later King Edward VII) Hunting Trip to Terai
events.detail: After knowing the Edward's trip to India Jung Bahadur sent letter through Ranaudip Singh to Calcutta to extend and invitation for the prince. He accepetd the invitaion and visisted Nepal for 2 weeks of hunting in Terai.

events.title: Ram Lakhan Thapa Uprising
events.detail: An ex-Gorkha soldier proclaimed himself as incarnation of Ram lakhan Thapa a traditional hero of Magar people comissioned by goddess Manakamana to overthrow Rana rule. For that he established a revolutionary camp in Bungkot Gorkha of 1500 men. The local population also united behind them declaring Thapa as the alternative Prime Minister. He was arrested along with his 6 deputies. He was hanged to death in-front of Manakamana temple.

events.title: Ranodip Singh Kunwar
events.detail: Assasinated at age 60

events.title: Ranodip's Dilemma
events.detail: Jung Bahadur's order of succession for PM position was to be run over brothers. However the order of succession for Maharaja of Kaski and Lamjung was to be run over sons. Given that the Maharaja had power to instruct the PM it became incompatible for Ranodip Singh to declare JBR's son Jagat Jung as the Maharaja. Therefore he assumed both the titles.

events.title: Crown Prince Trailokya's Mysterious Death
events.detail: Jagat Jung and Trailokya conspired to kill those ahead in succession of Jagat Jung. However Trailokya died mysteriously by poisoning. Jagat Jung allied with Trailokya's brother Narendra in a primise of making his son the King after Rajendra's death instead of Prithvi.

events.title: Nepal's Loosing Grip on Trade with Tibet
events.detail: Nepal's trade with India and Tibet was one of the major source of government revenue. From 1850s opium emerged as new export item as demand for Chinese opium rose following Opium War of 1840-42. To grab the profits Nepalese farmers grew opium and sold to governmnet which then was deported to India. It peaked in 1883. Towards the end of 19th century Indian railway system extended to southern border of Nepal which assisted in development of Butwal and Nepalgunj as entrepot centers. Kathmandu's monopoly started to suffer when in 1888 railway was constructed from Calcutta to Darjeeling on permission from King of Sikkim. This route led up to Chumbi Valley of Tibet which was a gateway to Lhasa. This reduced travel date to 20 days from Calcutta-Lhasa less than half time compared to Calcutta-Kathmandu-Lhasa.

events.title: Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah Becomes the King
events.detail: After Surendra's natural death Ranodip and Dhir Shumser concealed the news so that house-arrested ex-King Rajendra couldn't claim the throne. On the same day they declared his 5-year-old grandson as the King. Jagat Jung becomes weak as his plans with Narendra is wiped up.

events.title: Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah
events.detail: Died suspeciously at age 36

events.title: Return of Confiscated Land to Brahmins
events.detail: In Septmeber 1846 JBR announced to return back the confiscated land to win support for his newly established authority but the work couldn't be carried out until Ranodip set 3 year deadline establishing office and sending officers to districts through the mix of land return and compensation.

events.title: Failed Conspiracy Against Ranodip Singh
events.detail: The Thapa Pande and Bansyat who were removed from power by JBR planned to kill Dhir Shumsher who was kacting PM while Ranodip was hunting in Terai. The plan failed as grandson of Gagansingh betrayed and informed Dhir Shumser. Dhir Shumser cleared off the real conspirors but he also used it to remove Jagat Jung Prince Narendra and Bam Bikram Rana his previous conspirors by blaming them. Jagat Jung was in India during the time his titles were removed while other two were imprisoned. After this event Ranodip created a special force for the PM's defence called Bijuli Garath.

events.title: Loss of Commercial Supremacy in Tibet
events.detail: Argument broke between a Nepalese trader ans Tibetian women who was accused of stealing jewellery from the shop. It escelated leading to looting and burning of Nepalese shops. Both sides prepared for war while Nepal demanded Rs 15 Lakh as compensation. There were 45000 men in the army at that time. Later both wanted to avoid the war and settled the fight with Tibet paying 10 Lakh in compensation. However this incident led to Nepali traders losing their business supremacy to Kashmiri and Muslim traders.

events.title: Internal Division and Ranodip's Benaras Trip
events.detail: After Dhir Shumser died in 1884 Ranodip's position weakened. It presented Jagat Jung a chance to plead for return. In influence of his wife Ranodip took all charges off Jagat Jung though denied his entry because the senior Rana committee refused it. Regardless of the warning Jagat Jung returned and was sent to Kathmandu in chains. In such a turmoil to strenthen his position Ranodip visited Banaras and agreed to allow four new Gurkha regiments to be recruited in exchange of one rifle per each recruitment in a total of 5600 and grant him Grand Cross of the Order of the Bath position upon the request is met.

events.title: Cholera Episodes And Earliest Efforts on Sanitation
events.detail: Cholera had struck Kathmandu valley in 1823 1831 1843 1856 1862 1867 1872 1874 and 1875. The 1856 and 1872 outbreaks killed large numbers. In 1872 200 to 250 people perished each day. 1885 Episode: G H Gimlette the doctor at the British Residency had shared the earliest account of the Cholera outbreak in Nepal of year 1885. In 1885 Nepal had seen lots of rain and extremely hot weather. The first ugly symptoms of cholera manifested themselves in mid May. Soon five or six people were dying each day. By the end of May 10-12 people were dying. The British doctor tried to spur the palace into action making ‘frequent and urgent’ calls for temporary clinics to treat the sick. But his pleas went ‘entirely disregarded’ by the Rana rulers at the time. Eventually the government gave a space for a small dispensary but that fell far short of the what Gimlette really wanted -- a ‘place into which patients could be admitted and treated continuously’. Another poor decision added fuel to the fire. Over 15000 troops were gathered in Kathmandu for a possible deployment in India. Some soldiers got sick and others were not dispatched home immediately. Only after a colorful parade two weeks later on 1 June 1885 were soldiers sent home. But it was too late. The disease followed them around the country. Kathmandu saw ‘a sudden increase’ in cases the death rate now topping 50 per day. Cases appeared in Patan and then Bhaktapur. Cholera spread into the mountains. By 14 June cholera had invaded the palace. Of the over 300 people who lived there 25 were dead by evening chiefly slave-girls and servants. A panic ensued and the Durbar was quickly emptied. On June 29th after alternating days of heavy rain and high temperatures the daily death toll climbed over 100. As temperatre started to go down outbreak finally coming to an end in early September. Records show that 909 people received treatment at the British Residency dispensary and estimates suggest that as many as 10000 people perished in a city of 50000. Bir Hospital: In November that year Bir Shumsher seized power in a coup. He inherited not only a premiership but a Valley ridden with disease. Cholera was endemic and it was accompanied by typhoid smallpox goitre syphilis and chronic dyspepsia. The The British Residency dispensary at Lainchaur was inadequate. “In a poor country like ours wealth means health” Bir Shumsher remarked an unusually pragmatic admission that epidemics were not divine punishment but structural afflictions of urban life. He soon pledged to expand health care. In 1889 he opened Bir Hospital and staffed it with Indian doctors to treat cholera typhoid smallpox and other prevalent illnesses. Piped Water: Bir Shumsher also realized the need for safe drinking water. By the late 19th century the British had developed a technological ecosystem for water supply intakes pipes fittings reservoirs and trained engineers. Bir Shumsher appealed to the British Government in India for engineering assistance. A British engineer named Mr Feigneur surveyed Kathmandu to prepare maps and estimated the volume of water that could be brought from the Rudramati River. In 1889 a more experienced engineer Lockhart Matthew Sinclair arrived. Sinclair reviewed Feigneur’s plans updated them and chose the Bishnumati River as the source of the city’s drinking water. The system was designed to serve about 70000 residents through both private connections and public standpipes. The project involved some 40km of imported cast-iron pipes weighing 1.866 million kg. Construction required 620000 man-days of labour and cost over 6 Lakhs. Transport costs inflated prices: a load of cement costing Rs 10 in Calcutta was worth Rs 33 by the time it reached Kathmandu. Finally Bir Dhara Works was inaugurated in September 1891 six years after the cholera epidemic. Water flowed out of 131 taps including eight in Lainchaur six in the royal palace eleven in the prime minister’s palace sixteen around Tundikhel thirteen in Thapathali seven in Thamel and two in Naxal. The Bir Dhara system marked Kathmandu’s transition from reliance on wells rivers springs and hiti to piped water operating for several decades and laying the foundation for the expansion of drinking water services across the country in the late twentieth century. Extensions followed in Patan under Chandra Shumsher and Bhim Shumsher later added the Tri Bhim Dhara. Basic Hygiene Measures: Bir Shumsher also attempted to introduce basic hygiene measures such as pit latrines with squatting slabs. However there is no record of these facilities being built in his palaces later built palaces or elsewhere.

events.title: 42-Saal ko Parva
events.detail: Sons of Dhir Shamsher led by Bir Shamsher launch a bloody palace coup assassinating Prime Minister Ranodip Singh. Jagat Jung was killed shortly and his supporters fled including Prince Narendra and Ranodip's senior wife. Roll of Succession was revised to exclude the families of other Jung Bahadur's brothers. Before the coup Shumser borthers were poor 17 of whom had to live in just one house of their father. Bir Shumsher appropriated the entire property of the Jung family and the late Ranodip. The Ranodip Singh's wealth valued at about Rs. 70 Lakh at that time. British recognized his government after two months though they were dissatisfied with such a bloody transition. To secure the loyalty of the army influential priests and family factions the newly installed Prime Minister Bir Shamsher weaponized state land. Massive birta grants were given state gave these landlords absolute authority over the local population. The tenant farmers living on these newly granted Birta lands were stripped of rights. They were forced to pay exorbitant rents and subjected to Vethi i.e. compulsory unpaid forced labor for the landlord's personal projects palaces and farms.

events.title: Bir Shumsher
events.detail: Died naturally at age of 48

events.title: Bhaubhakta's Ramayan Published
events.detail: Bhanubhakta Acharya despite any fromal education started a linguistic revolution that shifted literature away from exclusive Sanskrit rituals into accessible common folk language. By translating Ramayana into everyday Nepali poetry he bridged regional dialects and unified the country’s linguistic identity. He was jailed once due to his father's mishandlling of accounts as he handled revenue collection in the Terai. Bhanubhakta was held legally responsible for the missing funds and was sent to prision. Frustrated by the bureaucratic delays and his deteriorating health he wrote a famous petition in verse form to Prime Minister Jung Bahadur Rana. Deeply impressed by the beauty of the poetry the Prime Minister cleared his charges ordered his release and gifted him a cash reward. Motiram Bhatta who spent his 25 years of life in Benaras returned to Kathmandu and established a publishing business. He gathered a circle of poets who composed and performed songs for Rana court. He rediscovered Bhanubhakta's lost manuscripts and printed the complete Ramayana in Benaras. He died at age of 30.

events.title: Conspiracy Aganist Bir Shumsher
events.detail: Khadga Shumsher conspired against his own brother but pre-informed of the intention Khadga Shumsher was arrested and was banished in Palpa. He was succeeded by another brother in line Rana Shumsher as Commander-In-Chief. He too died within three months and was succeeded by his brother Dev Shumsher. Ranbir Jung Jung Bahadur's illegitimate son who was military officer in British-India as vakil in Calcutta. He planned another military attack with about 3000 men through Ilam Dhankuta and Palpa however failed ending the attempt of Jung family to reclaim the throne forever.

events.title: Close Relation with British-India
events.detail: British only wanted Magars and Gurungs in the recruitment but the government rejected. Also offered to allow families to accompany that was rejected too. It created discomfort in relationship. Bir Shumsher was suspecious of the British resident Charles Girdlestone's sympathy towards Jung Rana. In Feb 1888 Bir Shumsher visited Calcutta. In exchange of British non-interference in Nepal's domestic politics and strict survelience of exiled Jung Ranas Bir Shumsher agreed to continue sending recruits allow recruiting depots at different points and high caste men be not recruited. in March of 1892 Lord Roberts visited Kthmandu which was first for any high-ranking British official. Roberts was greatly impressed by the welcome and built a very good rapport with Bir Shumsher. In February 1893 Bir Shumsher again visited Calcutta and made agreement of buying 8000 Martini-Henry rifles. He also wished to visit England in similar capacity as Jung Bahadur. If allowed it would be sth like recognition of Nepal's independent status while British wanted to maintain it as semi-soverign protected states of India. Fearing the denial would distance Nepal and the military needs in British India wouldn't be met the trip was approved but it never happened later citing Bir Shumsher's business with Tibetian affairs.

events.title: Bir Shumsher's Faceoff with King Prithvi
events.detail: Ranodip has moved King Prithvi's residence from Human Dhoka to Narayanhiti under close survelience. Prithvi used to invite his four half-brothers who lived in Hanuman Dhoka in palace to socialize. However Bir Shumsher didn't like this thiking that public grievances would reach the KIng through these half-brothers. Therefore he accused them of encouraging King to drink and debauchery and banished them to remote hills. King being furious wanted to assert his power and promoted one of the half-brothers to colonel but Bir Shumsher refused to recognize it. King Prithvi then forcefully moved to Hanuman Dhoka with his wives and slaves however he was not supported by his mother as well as she insisted that he is nominal and has no right to act against the will of the Prime Minister. At the end after a month King returned back to Narayanhiti Palace.

events.title: Bir Hospital Established
events.detail: Nepal's first hospital

events.title: Gurkha Remittance Economy and Agrarian Drain
events.detail: Ranas fulfilled British Empire’s insatiable demand for soldiers to police its colonies which guaranteed British protection for their autocracy against domestic revolutions or democratic movements exporting potential young rebels. It also drained manpower for agriculture sector farming declined. The cash raised living standard turning Nepal into export economy but remittance did not transform into domestic capital accumulation or industrial investment. Even though retired soldiers had money feudal land system prevented him from climbing the economic ladder because most fertile lands were locked under the tax-free Birta monopolies of the Rana family.

events.title: Lal Durbar was Built
events.detail: Built by Bir Shumsher 1890 for his youngest wife. In 1901 Tej Shumsher Bir Shumsher JBRs fourth son inherited this palace. In 1934 March by Juddha Shumsher JBR exiled Tej Shumsher to Narayani Zone and captured all his property along with Lal Durbar. In 1951 by end of Rana rule Lal Durbar was reclaimed by Tej Shumsher's sons. When Boris' Royal Hotel closed in 1969 he partnered with prominent Indian businessman Radhe Shyam Saraf. Looking to expand they acquired portions of the recently reclaimed Lal Durbar palace to open an upscale standalone version of the Yak & Yeti restaurant. Later in 1977 they acquired whole Lal Durbar and opened a full fledge hotel.

events.title: Bir Dhara Built
events.detail: First piped water system in Nepal was introduced first in Kathmandu and later in Bhadgaon in 1895. It was only available to the elite and one of the first efforts for the defence against cholera.

events.title: Seto Durbar Built
events.detail: It was built by Rana Prime Minister Bir Shumsher JBR in 1893 as a grand private residence and a technological showcase for his family. It was heavily utilized by his son Gehendra Shumsher Rana who was a famous engineer scientist and inventor. During the earthquake of 1934 fire broke out and most of Seto Durbar was destroyed leaving only a small wing intact which was occupied by NIDC Development Bank Head Office later merged with Rastriya Banijya Bank.

events.title: Arya Samaj
events.detail: Arya Samaj a vigorous Hindu reform movement was founded in 1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati. Its core mission was to promote physical spiritual and social progress by returning to the infallible authority of the ancient Vedas and rejecting idolatry the hereditary caste system and irrational superstitions. Madhav Raj Joshi started preaching his agnedas in Kathmandu and Pokhara in 1893. It got no reaction from government at the time. Later an Arya Samaj centre was set in Kathamandu. It soon got traction of religious leaders. In 1905 a scholarly debate took place in presence of Chandra Shumsher where he defended himself against the best theologists. But that debate ended up with Madhav Raj Joshi begin beten up for blasphemy against the deities of Nepal. He was then sent to prision for two years and his followers were harrashed. Upon his released he moved to Darjeeling continuing his Arya Samaj.

events.title: Lazimpat Durbar aka Agni Bhawan Built
events.detail: It was built by General Jit Shumsher Rana brother of Jung Bahadur Rana. In due time it became the property of General Agni Shumsher Rana son of Juddha Shumsher. General Agni Shumsher was the grandfather of several prominent royal figures. His granddaughters Queen Aishwarya Queen Komal and Princess Prekshya were all born inside this very palace before marrying into the Shah royal family of Nepal. In 1964 the palace was purchased by a hospitality entrepreneur named Ram Shanker Shrestha turning it into Hotel Shanker.

events.title: Ghanta Ghar Built
events.detail: Designed by Kumar and Kishor Narsingh Rana it blended European neoclassical elements with local architectural styles. It was destroyed by 1934 earthquake and was reconstructed later in simple and more functional style. It was damaged during 2015 earthquake too which was soon renovated.

events.title: Administrative Reorganization
events.detail: Before administrative reorganization Nepal had 10 districts the country was divided into 4 different regions or Gaunda headed by the Governors or Bada Hakim. One was in terai one was in the east headquartered in Dhankuta one was in the center headquartered in Palpa and one was in the west headquartered in Doti. The governors of Terai and Center were more powerful having pajani power too. They were to supervise the district governors or kaji/sardar. The district governers had responsibility of maintaining rule and order revenue collection through the village heads maintainenece of infrastructures and also supervisisons of rajas/rajautas. The raja/rajautas in the west and the communal heads or Subbas of kirat in the east were given authority of holding judicial courts upholding the tradition since the time of PN Shah. The Chief governors recieved statements of income and expenditure from the revenue collectors and used to forward the funds to national treasurery or Muluki Khana as soon as it reached 10000. In 1895 Bir Shumsher carried our major reorganization where Hill was divided into 23 and Terai was divided into 12 districts. All hill district offices or goswara were headed by Bada Hakim while 12 terai districts were grouped into four circles centered on Hanumannagar Birgung Tauliwawa and Nepalgunj each circle headed by Bada Hakim. Their major task was maintaining rule and order through Judicial Court (Amini) and collect revenues through Revenue Office (Mal Adda).

events.title: Phora Durbar Built
events.detail: Built by Bir Shumsher featuring extensive water fountains and gardens right in front of the Narayanhiti Palace. In 1966 the property was sold to the United States government which houses American Embassy today.

events.title: Kaiser Mahal Built
events.detail: Purchased an old palace from Jeet Shumsher by Chandra Shumsher who then destroyed it and built a new one and gifted his son as a wedding present to his son Kesher Shumsher. After death of Kaiser Shumsher his wife and two sons officially donated the palace the surrounding grounds and his massive personal book collection to the Government of Nepal. Under the reign of King Mahendra the government formally established the space as the Kaiser Library. The palace has also housed parts of the Ministry of Education. After significant damage to government buildings it served as temporary office space for the Ministry of Education. The garden of the palace has been lovingly renovated into what is now called the ‘Garden of Dreams’

events.title: Jawalakhel Durbar Built
events.detail: Constructed by Bir Shumsher Rana for his brother Juddha Shumsher and mother Juhar Kumari. It was designed by Jogbir Sthapit. Partially damaged in the 1934 earthquake it has been used since 1982 as the Nepal Administrative Staff College.

events.title: Forest Deterioration
events.detail: Forest exports were the second highest rouse of revenue for government after land revenue. Official establishments taking care of timber export were known as kathmahals. They either employed own labors to cut and transport to the place from where where timber merchants exported them or auctioned the whole right to a contractor. The kathmahals mismanaged the first system because of which government incurred huge loss. In 1897 Bir Shumsher abolished this kathmahal system. Hence state took no part in the operation instead the whole industry was contracted to private operators. Because of this forests were highly exploited beyond sustainable regrowth as the contractors carted out only one-tenth of the trees they cut leaving out trees that even had slightest of defect. The British India had its own contract with Nepal for the supply of Sal timber for railway sleepers. Nepal didn't have technology to send ready-made sleepers by then. Later in 1901 Nepal invested heavily in construction of saw mills in Nepalgunj and Nawalpur. In the succeeding decades Nepal's forests deteriorated rapidly.

events.title: Durbar High School Built
events.detail: School started in 1854 inside Thapathali Durbar by Jung Bahadur Rana after his return from England. The school had to shift constantly from Thapathali Durbar to Charburja Durbar Seto Durbar and Narayanhiti Durbar before being located in a small shed in Jamal. Bir Shumsher built the permanent building for the school. In 1900 Prime Minister Dev Shumsher made the school totally public and in 1967 its name was changed to Bhanu Madhyamik Vidyalaya. It has been a co-educational school since 1973 A.D.

events.title: Trade 1900
events.detail: Between 1880-1900 Nepal's total export increased by 64% to Rs. 2.5 Crore while imports doubled to Rs. 1.6 Crore i.e. Import-Export Ratio of 0.64. According to figures for the year 1899–1900 British Indian imports into Nepal amounted to Rs. 13374745 and exports from Nepal to Rs. 20934021. Of the total export of food grains amounted to Rs. 3442890 timber Rs. 699206 and ghee Rs. 349636 for the same year

events.title: Dev Shumsher
events.detail: Forced to abdicate within 114 days

events.title: Reforms of Dev Shumsher
events.detail: He was adoped by his childless uncle as a godson who left him a modest fortune upon death He did not have to face the hardships his other brothers faced. He was well educated and fluent in english. He had learned how public administration parliamentray system of government functioned in Britain from his English teacher. Here are the reforms he tried to bring: Liberation of Female Slaves: Dev Shumsher issued a proclamation liberating all femake slaves of Kaski Lamjung and Kathmandu. The freed number did not exceed 100. It was highly opposed at that time which forced him to abandon his plans. A salve was purchased for Rs. 20 which equaled a worth of 500kg of rice at that time. Participatory Governance: Called a British constitutional expert to advise him on representative government. As a start he called army officers senior civil servants religious leaders trading communities peasants and townspeople. He asked people to discuss anything except the crown succession and religion. Debate lasted for six hours that came up with several suggestions like promoting cottage industries. PM also installed suggestion boxes around Kathmandu ensuring anonymity of the person. But the concept was so alien that the response was negligible. He also founded Gorkhapatra newspaper which formally transitioned into an autonomous public corporation under the Gorkhapatra Corporation Act in 1963. Human Capital Development: At the time of Dev Shumsher the enrollment of Durbar High School was just 17. He proclaimed a scheme for universal primary education and 57 Nepali language elementary schools were established throughout the country. Judicial Reform: There were four principle seats of justice Char Adalat at capital: Ita Chapali (most powerful only could issue death sentence) Koti Ling Taksar and Dhansar headed by a dittha and assisted by 2 bicharis. The "vice royalties" of Palpa and Doti had their own judicial establishments but beyond that there were only 8 bicharis in western hills and 4 in eastern hills. Terai was divided into 8 divisions each headed by subba while Patan and Bhaktapur had its own court. All verdicts of these courts could be appealed in Char Adalat. And all decisions of the Char Adalat could be appealed to Bhardari Sabha. Bir Shumsher introduced 5 levels of courts and fixed the limits of their juridiction. 21 lower courts were established at administrative centres in Hills Terai as well as Patan and Bhaktapur. Above these courts at 4th level three courts of appeal were established at Palpa Dhankuta and Doti. At the third level were the Char Adalats. Now appeals from them were taken to newly formed 3rd level court Adalat Goswara. Above it in 2nd level the justic was dispensed by Commander-in-Chief in consulattion with Muluki Adda the Home Officeand panel of bhardars. The final court was Dev Shumsher himself. At village level an amali was assigned the duty of tax collection and act as judge for minor cases.

events.title: Fall of Dev Shumsher
events.detail: Annoyed by the reforms of Dev Shumsher Chandra Shumsher planned to sack him. In doing so he won over Hajuria General Fateh Shumsher Gehendra Shumsher officer incharge of Bijuli Garath and even informed the British Viceory Lord Curzon. Dev Shumsher was returning from a prize distribution in Durbar High School and was proceeding to Seto Durbar where he was met by Chandra Shumsher and others who soon overpowered he PM. The King was in the next room who then reluctantly confirmed Chandra's appointment. Dev was sent to exile in British India.

events.title: Chandra Shumsher
events.detail: Died naturally at age of 66

events.title: Singha Durbar Built
events.detail: The lavish private residence boasting 1700 rooms was ordered to be built by Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher and was designed by Nepali architects Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana. Most of the people worked as unpaid forced labor under the Jhara system that was in practice. At that time the structure cost 50 Lakhs. Immediately after construction Chandra Shumsher sold this property to the Government of Nepal for 2 Crore Nepali rupees as the official residence of the Prime Minister.

events.title: 32 Kothi Mahajan
events.detail: Marwadi families were brought from Rajasthan into Nepal starting the time of Jung Bahadur giving them citizenship and security. They were mostly active in textie trading. During the time of Chandra Shumsher 32 shops were established in Indrachowk and Makhan Tole and those Marwadi shop owners were given title of 32 Kothi Mahajan. Those were the prominent business houses that still rule Nepal's business sphere. Bhuramull Chaudhary whose family grew into CG Global Ram Lal Golchha who built Biratnagar Jute Mill Chand Mal Dugar who have become player in Nepal's hydropower sector and banking Radhe Shyam Saraf who founded institutions like Yak & Yeti Hotel and the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu Shiv Narayan Mittal who diversified investment later forming Mittal Group Chiranji Lal Agrawal laying groundwork for Vishal Group Kam Kumar Kedia whose heirs later went on founding first private sugar mill Brij cement Siddhartha Bank Mayaram Bholaram who founded first petrol pump were some of those.

events.title: British Expedition to Tibet aka Younghusband Expedition
events.detail: British-India feared that Russia was establishing a secret alliance with the 13th Dalai Lama to extend its influence into Tibet. British launched a military expedition in December 1903. Led by Colonel Francis Younghusband British and Indian soldiers fought their way successfully captured Lhasa in August 1904 and signed Convention of Lhasa in September 1904. This allowed British to trade in Yatung Gyantse and Gartok. It opened Chumbi Valley for direct trade between Lhasa and Kolkata. Kalimpong emerged as the main entrepot for trans-Himalayan trade eroding Kathmandu's position in trade. Ironically Chandra Shumsher’s offered Nepali troops for the expedition though it was declined. But Calcutta did accept the loan of several thousand yaks and porters for transportation purposes.

events.title: Lakshmi Niwas Built
events.detail: Built by Chandra Shumsher for his son Mohan Shumsher. It is named after Mohan Shumsher's wife Laxmi. This building was designed by Mr. Kumar Narshingha Rana and Mr. Kishore Narsingha Rana. It was returned to Nepal governemnt in 1953 which remains as Nepal Army camp likely Bhairavnath Gadh today near Sital Niwas.

events.title: Gaddi Baithak Built
events.detail: Built by Chandra Shumsher in 1908 and it was used for to coronations and to welcome head of states from other countries.

events.title: Chandra Shumsher's Europe Visit
events.detail: He hoped to discuss international status of Nepal and unrestricted importation of arms from Britain. However the visit got approved only on the basis that such issues won't be raised. It remained as a goodwill visit only. He took his nephew Padma Shumsher and his eldest son Mohan Shumsher with him. He toured industrial areas militray establishments etc. He visited Oxford University to receive an honorary Doctorate in Civil Law from the hands of Chancellor Lord Curzon.

events.title: Baber Mahal Built
events.detail: Chandra Shumsher commissioned it as a luxurious residence and gifted it to his son Field-Marshal Baber Shumsher. The heirs of Baber Shumsher faced immense financial pressure trying to pay for the upkeep of a sprawling multi-acre palace so they sold it to the government. They retained old stables guard quarters and rear courtyard structure on which Gautam Rana opened Baber Mahal Vilas. The main palace complex now host multiple departments including Department of Road and Kathmandu District Court.
