events.title: Pharping Hydropower
events.detail: Opened the first hydro-power project of Nepal and second of South Asia providing electricity to Rana nobles.

events.title: Xinhai Revolution in China
events.detail: Wuchang District of Wuhan

events.title: Tribhuvan Bir Bikram Shah
events.detail: He ascended to the throne at the age of five upon the death of his father. He died naturally at age 48.

events.title: King Georve V's Hunting Trip in Terai
events.detail: Chandra Shumsher wanted to invite Georve V since he was the Prince of Wales but had to cancel due to outbreak of Cholera in hunting site. Later when Georve V came to British India for a coronation darbar he was invited to Terai for sikar. He spent 5 whole days out of 10 in hunting in Kasara Chitwan. He also offered Royal Victorian Order inspected four Nepalese regiments and met two Gurkha veterans.

events.title: Trade 1912
events.detail: The year 1912/13 witnessed the total exports of 4 Crore 65 Lakhs and imports of rupees 2 Crore 22 Lakhs. The import-export ratio for the year was 0.47

events.title: Tibet Declared Independent
events.detail: Following the collapse of the Qing Dynasty the 13th Dalai Lama expels Chinese forces and issues a formal declaration of independence. Tibet operates as a de facto independent state for nearly four decades.

events.title: First Nepali Pastor Ganga Prasad Pradhan Arrived Nepal
events.detail: Ganga Prasad Pradhan was a Newar raised in Darjeeling who is known as the first ordained Nepali pastor. Pradhan converted to Christianity while studying at a school run by Church of Scotland missionaries in Darjeeling. After forty years of ministry to the Nepali-speaking community in northern India, focused mainly on producing a Bible translation and other evangelistic materials in Nepali, he decided in 1914 to return with his family to Kathmandu to establish a Christian presence in Nepal. Travelling with a group of around forty people, Pradhan and his colleagues' presence was discovered by the authorities soon after they arrived in Kathmandu. They were firmly instructed to leave, being told: "there is no room for Christians in Nepal".

events.title: Nepal and the First World War
events.detail: In Merch 1915 7500 men were sent under General Baber Shumsher deployed in North-West (Punjab) frontier and United Provinces (UP). The second contingest of 4000 troops were sent in December 1915 followed by another 4000 a year later. At the time 26000 Gurkhas were already serving regular Indian Army. And forces were sent regularly to recover the losses. The total number of men who actually left the country for military purposes exceeded 2 Lakhs out of 50 Lakhs population. Nepal also contributed financially. In September 1914 government contributed Rs. 3 Lakhs to the war fund and to this PM personally added contribution of 2 Lakhs 25 Thousands. In Januray 1916 a further Rs. 3 Lakhs was donated and in Januray 1917 additional Rs. 3 Lakhs. In 1918 to mark silver wedding ceremony of the Emperor and Empress of India another donation of 2 Lakhs was made to the war efforts. Moreover 18144 kg of cardamoms 38420 kg of tea and sufficient timber for 200000 broad gauge railway sleepers 31 machine guns along with 71 mechanics from the arms factories were also sent to India. Bribery: While Nepal fully supported to Britain Kala Singh one of Indian revolutionaries came to nepal incognito to pursuade Chandra Shumsher to support them being only Hindu Kingdom and also bribed of territorial concession and making him Pm of one of an independent Indian Republic. This proposal was rejected and the guy was arrested later by British. Religious Problem: Nepali soldiers had to fight in European and Middle Eastern front crossing ocean and it was dreaded as kalo pani and believed that they lost caste on crossing ocean and an expensive ritual had to be done called pani patia to be re-adimitted to the caste. In the World War despite resistance from the dharma gurus Chandra Shumsher reached a compromise with them to re-admit the soldiers without such expensive rituals if they didn't overstay in their mission and they go certificate from British officer that they had observed the regulation of their caste during the mission. The tradition of pani patia ended after Second World War as more Nepali started travelling to Europe. This was actually used as a political weapon of ruling class to retain a hold on the Gurkha troops. After the war was over Nepal celebrated the victory with public holiday fireworks parade of troops and religious ceremonies. But the political benefit to Nepal i.e. unequivocal acknowledgemnet of Nepal's independence by British got threatened by large-scale migration to India. Of more than 11000 Gurkha soldiers discharged from regular Indian Army at the end of war only 4000 returned. Rest remained in India hoping for better future. To stem outflow of people Chandra Shumsher increased salary of Nepal Army and imposed total ban on employment in Indian Army. Reward: Britain granted Nepal an annual peacetime subsidy of 10 Lakh Indian Rupees in perpetuity and permitted the country to freely import modern arms and ammunition through British India for the very first time.

events.title: Lekhnath Paudyal's Early Breakthrough in Nepali Literature
events.detail: One of the Great Literary Trio. Early Nepali poetry was written in straightforward language so the average often uneducated citizen could easily understand it. Lekhnath Paudyal believed that for the Nepali language to be respected on a global scale its literature needed academic weight. He introduced flawless grammar elevated vocabulary complex metaphors and mastered incredibly difficult rigid classical Sanskrit poetic meters (such as Shardulvikridita and Shikharini). He proved that Nepali could be just as beautiful and mathematically precise as ancient Sanskrit. To bypass strict state censors Lekhnath Paudyal masterfully used allegorical double meanings; on the surface Pinjada Ko Suga ("The Parrot in the Cage") appeared to be a harmless spiritual poem about a captive bird longing for nature. However the oppressed public immediately decoded the true message: the trapped parrot represented the silenced citizens of Nepal and the cage symbolized the tyrannical Rana regime.

events.title: 7.1-7.7 Mag. Nepal–Tibet Earthquake
events.detail: 7.1-7.7 magnitude earthquake, epicenter near Mt Api in western Nepal. Damage in Darchula and Indian Kumaon.

events.title: Administrative Reforms
events.detail: Prime Minister kept four departments directly under him. Khadga Nishana Adda or PM's office was established in 1917 Bintipatra Niksari Adda was established which was highest court of appeal headed by PM. Munsi Khana or Foreign Office which dated from time of Bhimsen Thapa and Gharkaj Adda or Public Works Office for design maintenence and repair works of PM's residence and palaces were also under PM. Below the four departments were eight other departments under the supervision of the head of civil administration the Commander-in-Chief. The most important of all was Muluki Bandobast Adda the Home Office which was formerly just Muluki Adda. The reformed office consisted of seven sections: Ain Sawal Phant(old Ain Causal continued functioning as Law Council formulating ammending and codifying law.) Purju Phant (authorized projects and activities of government on the basis of purji from PM) Report Niksari Phant (received reports from districts on law and order revenue movement of foreigners and general administration) Nepal Pahad Bandobasta (revenue administration of hill and Kathmandu valley) Madesh Bandobast Phant (revenue administration of Terai) Rakam Bandobast Phant (dealt with government contracts) and Kath Niksari Phant (management and administration of forests and sales of timber and forest products). There were other major offices too. Hazari Goswara or Government Personnel Office was set up by Bir Shumsher to record attendance and leaves of employees and was known as the most corrupt office. A new posiiton of Director General was created to supervise the introduction and implemnetation of education. Some offices were replaced too. Kumari Chowk was replaced by Shresta Office for keeping accounts and audits in 1917. Jung Bahadur's Kitab Khana the civil and military registry was reorganized and renamed as Commandari Kitab Khana under which each appointments had to be done after sitting in interview with PM and Commander-in-Chief. Jangi Adda the defence office created by JBR on return from England was reorganized and renamed as Jangi Bandobast Adda. The Muluki Khana (treasury) and Kausi Tosakhana (office of public expenditure) remained unchanged. In addition to 13 major departments large number of small offices were established to deal with specialized government task such as Goswara Tahvil (central records office) Municipal Goswara (municipal office) Jail Khana (prison administration) Taksal Adda (minting office) Bijuli Goswara (office to supply electricity) Census Goswara (to keep general census) etc. All these departments were housed in Singha Durbar.

events.title: District Administration
events.detail: Districts boundaries were altered to make 20 hill districts and 12 Terai districts. Postal offices were opened aayur vedic dispensaries appeared in few districts. Regular police forces were introduced in Terai however in terai law and order was still maintained through village heads. New revenue system was introduced in Terai by replacing tax collecting amali by mal subbas who headed district revenue offices or mal addas. The actual revenue collection was in the hand of jimadar who recieved commission of 25 paisa for every rupee collected. In the hill the mal adda was headed by mal hakim who has a contractual obligation to deliver a stipulated amount of revenue to the district treasury. If collection fell short it was to be fulfilled from his salary. The actual task of tax collection was in the hand of a local men called talukdars. Chandra Shumsher also reformed daudaha the inspection team to be sent from Kathmandu who would report to the Muluki Bandobast Adda. The Kathmandu valley was directly administered under Hajuria Geberal through the office Sadar Jangi Kotwali. In Lalitpur and Bhaktapur administration ran through Brigadier Generals. The law and order of three districts was rested upon Sadar Police Goswara. Anyone needed to leave the valley required permit from Sadar Jangi Kotwali and anyone needed to enter the valley needed permit from their district governor.

events.title: Connectivity Projects
events.detail: A walking and porter trail connecting Raksaul to Bhimphedi was constructed along with a 500m Churiya Tunnel in 1917. It was closed in 1956 after construction of Tribhuvan highway. A 20 km ropeway was constructed from Bhimphedi to Kathmandu in 1924. It was upgraded in 1959 and closed in later 1990s. A metre gauge railway was opened from Raxaul to Amlekhgunj in 1927. It was closed down in 1965 as it became redundant after Tribhuvan Highway linking southern border was buit. Chandra Shumsher started building modern Scottish trail bridges and by the Rana Regime there were 30 bridges in Nepal. A telephone line was also laid from Kathmandu to Raxaul, Birgunj to connect with India in 1914. It took another two decades before the system was upgraded to be used for ‘administration commerce and diplomacy. In 1935 twenty-five automatic telephone lines were installed in Kathmandu followed by a line connecting Kathmandu and Dhankuta in 1936. In 1948 Mohan Akashwani wireless system was established under Prime Minister Mohan Shamsher. By 1951 Palpa District was linked to Kathmandu and Bhairahawa followed in 1953. In 1950 Kathmandu received a “Central Battery” telephone exchange marking the start of public telecommunications services.

events.title: Russian Revolution
events.detail: The Russian Revolution of 1917 was not a single event, but a pair of massive explosions of public anger that destroyed the 300-year-old Romanov monarchy and created the world’s first communist state. It unfolded in two distinct phases: the February Revolution (which overthrew the Tsar) and the October Revolution (which brought the Bolsheviks to power). February Revolution(March 1917): Russia suffered staggering military losses against Germany. Millions of peasants were drafted, leaving farms empty and triggering mass food shortages in cities. Tsar Nicholas II went to the military front lines to command troops personally. He left his wife, Tsarina Alexandra, in charge. She was heavily influenced by the erratic mystic Grigori Rasputin, which completely ruined the royal family's reputation. Inflation soared, factories ran out of fuel, and working-class citizens in the capital city of Petrograd (now St. Petersburg) faced freezing winters without bread. On International Women's Day, thousands of female factory workers poured into the streets of Petrograd demanding bread and peace. Industrial workers quickly joined them, paralyzing the city. When the Tsar ordered the army to shoot the crowds, the soldiers refused. Instead, the military mutinied, joining the protesters and supplying them with weapons. Realizing he had lost all authority, Tsar Nicholas II abdicated the throne on March 15, ending centuries of imperial rule. Dual Power: After the February Revolution, Russia developed a situation of “dual power” between the Provisional Government, which formally held state authority, and the Petrograd Soviet, which represented workers and soldiers and could mobilize them. The government struggled with continuing the war, military defeats, food shortages, economic disruption, and growing unrest among workers, soldiers, and peasants. Alexander Kerensky became its central figure but failed to resolve these problems. Lenin returned from exile in April and issued the April Theses, calling for “all power to the Soviets,” an end to cooperation with the Provisional Government, and an end to the war. Bolshevik influence grew rapidly. The government's failed June offensive triggered the July Days, when soldiers, sailors, and workers demonstrated for Soviet power. The uprising collapsed, as the revolt was premature because the provinces did not yet support a full seizure of power. Vladimir Lenin fled to Finland, while figures like Leon Trotsky were jailed. The decisive turning point came with the Kornilov Affair in August, when General Kornilov appeared to threaten Petrograd. Kerensky armed the Bolsheviks and relied on the Soviet to defend the revolution. The Bolsheviks' role in defeating the attempted coup greatly increased their credibility and influence. By September, Trotsky had become chairman of the Petrograd Soviet, and the Bolsheviks had gained majorities in both Petrograd and Moscow. With the Provisional Government increasingly discredited and the Bolsheviks now the strongest organized radical force, Lenin returned to Petrograd and pressed for an immediate seizure of power. In October, the Bolshevik Central Committee voted 10–2 to overthrow the Provisional Government in favor of Soviet power, setting the stage for the October Revolution. October Revolution (November 1917): On 24 October [N.S. 6 November], the government closed numerous newspapers, and closed Petrograd, attempting to forestall the revolution; minor armed skirmishes ensued. The next day, a full-scale uprising erupted as a fleet of Bolshevik sailors entered the harbor and tens of thousands of soldiers rose up in support of the Bolsheviks. Bolshevik Red Guards under the Military-Revolutionary Committee began to occupy government buildings. In the early morning of 26 October [N.S. 8 November], they captured the Winter Palace, the seat of the Provisional government located in Petrograd, then capital of Russia. Russian Civil War: The Bolshevik seizure of power was contested by multiple groups, leading to full-scale war by 1918. The main sides were the Red Army, fighting to establish a Bolshevik socialist state under Lenin, and the White movement, largely composed of former imperial officers and conservatives led by figures such as Alexander Kolchak. They were joined by socialist opponents of the Bolsheviks, nationalist movements, peasant “Green” armies, and 13 foreign powers that intervened against the Bolsheviks. The Bolsheviks initially lost large territories but gradually defeated White offensives from the east, south, and west. By 1920, the major White armies had been defeated, although fighting and anti-Bolshevik resistance continued for several years. The Bolsheviks also fought nationalist movements across the former empire, successfully incorporating Ukraine, the Caucasus, and much of Central Asia, while Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania retained independence. The Peace of Riga (1921) settled the Polish-Soviet conflict. The war effectively ended with the capture of Vladivostok in October 1922 and consolidated Bolshevik control over most of the former Russian Empire, paving the way for the formation of the Soviet Union. The conflict caused an estimated 7–12 million deaths, mostly civilians, and permanently transformed Russia's political and territorial order.

events.title: First Ever Women's Committee Formed
events.detail: BP's mother Divya Koirala wrote a letter to Chandrashamsher's Maharani Balkumari Devi. In that she pointed out the need to open an association to encourage women to work for the benefit of the country. She also informed that women will be encouraged when the queen is the patron or chairperson. Accordingly in June 1974 a Women's Committee was formed with Balkumari Devi as president and Divya Koirala as secretary. That was the first organization established for women's rights and welfare in Nepal.

events.title: Krishna Prashad's Parcel to Chandra Shumsher & Exile
events.detail: BP's father staged a symbolic protest by gathering the tattered rags of poor peasants and sending them as a package directly to Chandra Shumsher. Enraged by this open act of defiance Prime Minister Chandra Shamsher ordered the seizure of the Koirala family's properties and sent the family into a long political exile in India

events.title: Tri-Chandra Campus
events.detail: The Tri-Chandra college was first institution of higher education. It introduced science at the Intermediate level a year later marking the genesis of formal science education in the country. In 1924 it became a full four year institution with an enrollment of just 30. However up until the advent of democracy in 1951 it was the only college in entire country. It was not accessible to the general public but only to a handful of noble members of Rana regime. Untill the end of Rana-rule it had less than 200 students.

events.title: Yugoslavia's Precursor Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes Formed
events.detail: Before World War I, the South Slavs were divided among several empires and kingdoms. Serbia was an independent kingdom, ruled by the Serbian Karađorđević dynasty. Slovenes, Croats and many other South Slavs lived inside Austria-Hungary. Bosnia and Herzegovina was also part of Austria-Hungary. Montenegro was an independent kingdom but closely connected to Serbia. The Austria-Hungary was a dual monarchy created in 1867. It was essentially one empire with two major political centers. But the empire contained many other peoples: Czechs, Slovaks, Poles, Ukrainians, Croats, Slovenes, Serbs, Romanians, Italians, Bosnians, etc. Austria-Hungary fought alongside Germany and the Ottoman Empire in World War I. When Germany and the Central Powers began losing in 1918, Austria-Hungary began to fall apart. Two important political entities emerged: Kingdom of Serbia — already an independent South Slavic state. State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs — created in October 1918 from South Slavic territories that had belonged to Austria-Hungary. The leaders of these territories decided to unite with Serbia. So, on 1 December 1918, they created the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (SHS). The new country was not created as an equal federation of Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia, Montenegro, etc. Instead, the Kingdom of Serbia's existing monarchy, army, bureaucracy and political institutions became the foundation of the new state which largely centralized the political system in Belgrade. The political hostility turned violent on June 20, 1928. During a heated debate in the Belgrade parliament, Puniša Račić, a nationalist Serbian deputy, pulled out a revolver and opened fire on the opposition benches. He killed two Croatian deputies on the spot. The assassination caused outrage across Croatia, triggering mass protests, riots, and violent clashes with police. Croatian deputies pulled out of the parliament entirely, leaving the government completely broken. Realizing the democratic system had utterly collapsed, King Alexander I launched a royal coup on January 6, 1929. He abolished the constitution, dissolved parliament, and seized absolute power. Later that year, he officially renamed the country the Kingdom of Yugoslavia in a desperate attempt to ban all separate ethnic identities and force everyone to be just "Yugoslavs"

events.title: Harihar Bhawan Built
events.detail: Built by Chandra Shumsher as a residence for his second son Shankar Shumsher. It was designed by the famous engineer-architect brothers Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana. After Shankar Shumsher stayed in the UK post-democracy the Government of Nepal nationalized all his properties along with Harihar Bhawan. Currently this palace is occupied by the Department of Agriculture National Library of Nepal and National Human Rights Commission.

events.title: A B C Rana Classification
events.detail: He shortened the succession line to guarantee his own sons would become Prime Minister. The official royal roll was overpopulated; stripping titles from B and C classes saved the state immense wealth. He feared a military uprising and used caste purity as an excuse to disarm ambitious illegitimate relatives. A class Rana were Born from legitimate high-caste wives. These Ranas held exclusive rights to become Prime Minister and hold the highest military and administrative posts. B class were born to legitimate wives from secondary high-caste backgrounds or through marriage with royal family members. They could rise to the level of Colonel but were excluded from the premiership. C class were born to wives from lower castes or those deemed illegitimate. Like B Class their administrative and military promotions were capped at the level of Colonel. The wealthy educated and heavily marginalized C-Class Ranas felt deeply insulted. Decades later excluded C-class figures like Subarna Shumsher used their immense wealth to fund and form the Nepali Congress.

events.title: Makai ko Kheti
events.detail: Subba Krishna Lal Adhikari Adhikari was inspired to write a book about maize cultivation after reading an Indian book that a friend had given him. In the book he used double meaning to satire to the Rana regime. He wrote about "red-headed and black-headed insects" destroying crops which the rulers took as a direct mockery because Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher and his brother wore red and black caps. He also compared local and foreign dogs pointing to British influence over the Ranas. On 2 August 1920 Adhikari was sentenced to nine years in prison; his sentence would be reduced to six years if he handed over all 1000 copies of the book to the government. Adhikari tried to return all the copies but one had gone missing and he was unable to locate it. All of the 999 copies were burnt. No surviving copies of the book have been found. He died in prision.

events.title: All-India Gorkha League
events.detail: Ex-Gurkha living in Dehradun founded an organization which remained apolitical for first six years but later when Thakur Chandan Singh a fromer Indian Congress activist and Gurkha veteran became its president in 1926. It advocated religious and political reforms in Nepal through its mouthpiece Gorkha Samsar. In 1927 a new branch was opened in Assam. Bahadur Shumsher Rana a son of deposed Dev Shumsher was the president that year. Later Chandra Shumsher brought off some of its leaders turning the organization conciliatory towards the regime.

events.title: The Prince of Wales' (later King Edward VIII) Hunting Trip in Terai
events.detail: Third Britsh royal to visit Nepal General Baber and Keshar Shumsher were responsible for the trip. Prince was accompanied by Lord Mountbatten along with 49 Europeana nd 243 Indians.

events.title: USSR Formed
events.detail: After Bolsheviks won the Russian Civil War, instead of formally maintaining the old Russian Empire, they organized territories into separate Soviet socialist republics. By 1922, the four principal republics were: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR), Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic, and Transcaucasian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (covering Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia). These republics agreed to create a federation called the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR). The Treaty on the Creation of the USSR was signed on December 29, 1922, and the union was formally proclaimed on December 30. The first Soviet constitution formally established the institutional structure of the USSR. The Transcaucasian SFSR was later dissolved in 1936, splitting its components—the Armenian SSR, Azerbaijani SSR, and Georgian SSR—into individual, direct union republics of the USSR. Although the republics theoretically retained certain rights, real political power was increasingly concentrated in the Communist Party leadership in Moscow. Through subsequent border shifts, annexations, and the creation of new union-level republics (such as the Baltic and Central Asian SSRs), the total number of constituent republics reached 15 by 1940, remaining at that count until the dissolution of the USSR in December 1991. They were: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, and Uzbekistan.

events.title: Sital Niwas Built
events.detail: Chandra Shumsher built it as a private residence for his youngest son Krishna Shumsher. It was designed by Kumar Narsingh and Kishor Narsingh. Damaged in the 1934 earthquake it was later restored. Amidst anti-rana political pressure Krishna Shumsher decided to leave the country and later handed over Sital Niwas to the Government of Nepal. Temporarily it was leased to Indian Embassy. Later it became the state guest house under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It transitioned to the Presidential Palace in 2008.

events.title: Anglo-Nepal Treaty of Friendship
events.detail: British had long avoided recognition of Nepal as independent nation for the reason that it didn't want Nepal to have relation with other nations and to ahve unrestricted possession of arms. But amid Nepal's favor in WW I due rapidly dterriorating security situation in sub-continent such as Third Anglo-Afghan War and increasing Japanese influence over north of Mongolia Britain came to gove Nepal what it expected of Britain. The treaty was signed in kathamndu between Chandra Shumsher and British envoy to Nepal Lieutenant-Colonel W.F.T. O'Connor recognizing Nepal as an independent and sovereign state. This treaty stood as testament of the protection of the independence of Nepal and the increment of the status of Nepal among the other nations of the world. After the treaty British resident remained as envoy and Nepal got unrestricted right to possess arms.

events.title: Stopped Granting Jagir
events.detail: To improve the the performance of civil service he introduced cash salaraies and aboilished the system of granting Jagirs.

events.title: Abolition of Slavery
events.detail: He did it step by stem gradually from prohibiting enslavement of any person who was not born to that consition to giving option of paying Rs. 25 to 120 any slave had right to buy their freedom if master decided to sell them. Finally all slaves owned by government were set free and invited all salves to become free settler on land in the Chitwan. The final appeal came from PM on Nov 28 which set timeline for the liberation of all slaves. At the time there were 51419 slaves out of 56 Lakh population. Slave owners were compensated at current market rates. Government paid out large amount of Rs. 36 Lakhs and 70 Thousands (i.e. 15% of anual revenue) in compensation of 15719 slave owners.

events.title: Revenue Estimate 1924
events.detail: Approx 2 Crore 44 Lakhs

events.title: Shree Durbar Built
events.detail: Built by Chandra Shumsher for his young wife Bal Kumari Devi. It was designed by Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana. It was passed to Chandra Shumsher's son Madan Shumsher. After Madan Shumsher passed away in 1955 his widow Rani Jagadamba recalled Kamal Mani Dixit who served as trusted advisor and legal caretaker of Madan Shumsher to manage her massive estate and philanthropic endeavors. Because of this immense trust Rani Jagadamba appointed Kamal Mani Dixit as a primary board member secretary and caretaker of her trusts including the Madan Puraskar Guthi and the Jagadamba Databya Aushadhalaya. Large portions of the Shumsher family's sprawling Shree Durbar estate were converted into public educational and literary institutions managed by the Dixits. Today it houses Madan Puraskar Pustakalaya Sajha Yatayat and Rato Bangala School.

events.title: Balkrishna Sama's Theater Revolution
events.detail: One of the Great Literaty Trio. Sama completely reinvented storytelling in Nepal by shifting the focus from gods to humans. He published Mutuko Byatha the very first modern tragedy in Nepali literature. It moved local theater completely away from traditional religious mythological reenactments and introduced audiences to Shakespearean psychological realism. In rapid succession he wrote socio-political dramas like Mukunda Indira and Prahlad. He even dropped his aristocratic family name ("Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana") to stand with the common people. His epic Chiso Chuhlo directly challenged caste discrimination by highlighting a tragic love story across caste lines. This was his most potent era because he boldly used theater to criticize caste discrimination fatalism and social inequality. He effectively dragged Nepali society into the era of intellectual realism.

events.title: Bhim Shumsher
events.detail: Died naturally at the age of 67

events.title: Sita Bhawan/Tangal Durbar
events.detail: Sita Bhawan was built by Bhim Shamsher for his wife SIta. She lived in this palace until its nationalisation in 1969. Today it houses Nepal Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and Nepal Children's Organization (NCO) aka Bal Mandir. Top officials of the Bal Mandir illegally leased out large portions of the valuable land to private business entities which is called Bal Mandir kanda.

events.title: Tulsi Mehar Arrested
events.detail: After spending four years living and working alongside Mahatma Gandhi at the Sabarmati Ashram in India Shrestha returned to Nepal. Backed by the previous PM Chandra Shumsher he founded Chandra Kamdhenu Charkha Pracharak Mahaguthi the first social non-governmental organisation in Nepal to promote the spinning wheel. When Bhim Shumsher came to power he viewed the Charkha movement with deep suspicion. He feared that the movement was a disguised extension of India's anti-colonial freedom struggle. Therefore Mehar was arrested and thrown into prison. When released during Juddha Shumsher's regime he continuously fought for democratic causes.

events.title: Office Hour Reform
events.detail: Bhim Shamsher introduced the official 10:00 to 4:00 pm office hours and formal weekly Saturday holiday

events.title: Panchayats Formed
events.detail: The Panchayat was established during the time of Bhim Shumsher. Outside the valley, panchayats were established merging 4-5 villages in goswara (big administrative office) where goswaras were opened, and in mauja (tax office) where goswaras were not opened. To be a Pancha, of any area the person should have been a housekeeper in that place or should have been a jimindar or talukdar in that place. They should have good intentions and conduct. Men who are qualified to do the work of the Panchayat. However, they should not be under the age of 25, guilty of bribery, theft, dacoity, forgery, or forgery. To select the Panchayat, men who have reached the age of 16 in the village or mauja should gather, select and send properly stamped approval paper. In the case of the Pradhan Pancha, the person must be Talukdar or Jimindar of the village. If it was not possible, there was a provision that the Raiti could be chosen by the Badahakim and appointed as the Pradhan Pancha.

events.title: Library/Pustakalaya Parva
events.detail: After the death of Chandra Shumsher Bhim Shumsher allowed Krisha Prasad Koirala to come to Nepal. Krishna Prasad Koirala Chittadhar Upasaka (Hridaya) Jogveer Singh Kansakar and Harshadas Tuladhar among others decided to open a public library at Machendra Baaash. An application form was prepared to seek permission from Bhim Shamsher. It was signed by 45 people. But shortly before submitting the application to Bhim Shamsher Ramchandra Adhikari said that it was motivated by the intention to carry out activities against the Rana Tantra. 45 people who signed the application were arrested. And one hundred per person was fined. Krishna Prasad Koirala Chittadhar Hriday Lakshmi Prasad Devkota Siddhicharan Shrestha and others were fined.

events.title: Lalita Niwas aka Subarna Mahal Built
events.detail: Bhim Shumsher forcefully acquired 300 ropanis of land from hundreds of civilians and built a Subarna Mahal palace for his grandson Subarna Shamsher Rana. The palace was later renamed Lalita Niwas after goddes Lalita Devi. After King Mahendra conducted coup then Finance Minister Subarna Shamsher fled to India. In 1961 Land Acquisition Act was enacted under which state paid out due financial compensation to the private owners of land to officially convert the property into government-owned public land to establish administrative headquarters and residences for top state officials. Under the act Mahabir Bhawan Harihar Bhawan Sita Bhawan Lakshmi Niwas Baber Mahal and 284 Ropani out of 299 Ropani of Lalita Niwas was acquired by governemnt paying due compensation. the government provided a fair market compensation of Rs 45000 per ropani. The remaining 14 Ropani of Lalita Niwas was forcefully confiscated by the then Panchayat government as political punishment to Subarna Shumsher. Records show that the government decided to sell Lalita Niwas’ 8 ropani land to Kanak Shumsher for Rs 45882 upon his request. In 1979 King Birendra gave 12 ropani of the land to his favourites using his special order (hukum prabhagi). The post-panchayat Krishna Prasad Bhattarai-led interim government issued a cabinet decision intended as a restorative justice measure: land that had been confiscated from political activists by the Panchayat regime for opposing the monarchy was to be returned to its original owners. This noble intent was hijacked by a syndicate operating within the Dillibazar Land Revenue Office. In 1992 the heirs of Subarna Shumsher in collusion with corrupt officials submitted applications claiming that 112 ropanis of Lalita Niwas had been “confiscated” without compensation. To support this lie the conspirators ensured that the original 1964 compensation records and the Gazette notifications “disappeared” from the government archives. Within few months the Land Revenue Officer without informing the government transferred 112 ropani land which was under the supervision of Sumer Jung Adda (a ceremonial unit of the Nepali Army) to Subarna Shumsher’s son Rukma Shumsher and grandson Hemdary Sumsher in four installments. 12 ropani out of that 112 ropani was gifted to the officers in Land Revenue Office. Shobhakant Dhakal and Ram Kumar Maharjan created fake tenants of those lands which was itself illegal that on government land no tenancy (mohi) rights can be claimed. The then head of Land Reform Department Umanath Gyawali decided that the mohi claims hold. The Rana family went to High Court against this decision but the decision came on behalf of the tenants. Dhakal and Maharjan carved out 30 ropani land from those tenants. In 2003 a case was filed in CIAA against those private-turned land but the CIAA under Surya Nath Upadhaya said that land are private lawfully and dismissed the case. When another case was filed in 2007 CIAA under Lalit Limbu decided to bring those lands under the government. Against that decision Dhakal and Maharjan went to Supreme Court. The hearing of Balaram KC and Rajendra Prasad Koirala decided in favor of the mafia. In 2008 CIAA went to Appeal the decision and the full bench of Khilaraj Regmi Min Bahadur Rayamaji and Anup Raj Sharma made verdict again in favor of the mafia. In 2010 Madhav Nepal's government brought 27 ropani land in the perifery of PM residence in the name of PM residence. There as well fake tenents were created and in the name of compensation 13 ropani was distributed to tenants. The tenants again sold their land to same mafias. The tenant related decision was to be legally done throguh Land Reform Department but this time it was done through Land Revenue Office. The government opened a road for PM's convenince which actually opened road for the same land that the mafias captured. In 2012 during Baburan government The Land Revenue Department transferred 3 Ropani land to made-up Pashupati Tikinchha Guthi. Once the land was categorized as Guthi property the “fake tenants” (proxies for the land mafia) were once again used to claim ownership rights. In 2019 KP Oli government formed a probe committee under Sharada Prasad Trital which concluded that the land had been stolen through institutionalized forgery. In 2023 CIAA and CIB jointly led the investigation following the conclusion of Trital committee. In 2024 CIAA filed another case in special court and the bench of Khusi Prasad Tharu Ram Bahadur and Ritendra Thapa convicted the mafias and many government officials however acquiting political leadership on the name of policy decision. The court also ordered the cancellation of all private ownership certificates. The secondary buyers of the land such as Min Bahadur Gurung Bishnu Poudel etc. were not directly convicted howveer their holding were turned void while they have right to go to court against the sellers of that land.

events.title: Abolition of the Death Penalty
events.detail: He practically abolished capital punishment in Nepal restricting the death penalty exclusively to cases of severe state rebellion or treason.

events.title: Custom Reforms
events.detail: Bhim Shumsher encouraged cotton cultivation and reduce custom of the imports of cotton and salt.

events.title: Kathmandu Municipality Established
events.detail: Kathmandu was first declared as a municipality in 1932 after the formulation of the Kathmandu Municipality Sabal act. It was founded as a waste management department and Singha Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana was appointed as the first 'Mayor Man' of Kathmandu municipality in the same year by the government of Chandra Shumsher.

events.title: Juddha Shumsher
events.detail: Abdicated the throne. Died naturally at age of 77 in Dehradun

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate 1933
events.detail: NPR 145= INR 100

events.title: International Recognition of Nepal's Independence
events.detail: AFter the Treaty of Friendship with Britain Chandra Shumsher and later Juddha Shumsher wanted to open embassy in London insted of Calcutta to which Britain rejected. However after much pressue from Juddha in 1934 the position of Nepalese vakil in Delhi was raised to that of Consul-General which was actually agreed in 1816 Sugauli Treaty. Likewise the British Envoy in Kathmandu was raised to that of a Minister and British Legation was raised to the status of Embassy. Juddha Shumsher visited Delhi in 1935 first time as a PM of independent nation. In May 1933 Italian Consul-General in Calcutta visited Nepal which was first of its kind from a country other than Britain and China. In May 1934 French mission also visited followed by Chinese Consul-General in Calcutta the next month sent by President Chiang Kai-shek. It made clear that China had abandoned claims to suzerainty over Nepal which the Qing Empire had maintained. In 1935 Belgian delegation arrived offering Grand Order of King Leopold on behalf of Leopold III for sacrifices made by Gurkhas against Germany. Ironically next delegation was of German in 1937 which invested Juddha Shumsher with Red Cross on behalf of Chancellor Adolf Hitler. Just three years later Gurkha troops were again fighting Germans.

events.title: SLC Board Formed
events.detail: A Board of Education was formed to make arrangements for conducting School Leaving Certificate in nepal under the sponsorship of Patna University.

events.title: 90 Saal ko Mahabhukampa
events.detail: Earthquake struck at 2:13 pm of magnitude 8.3 epicentered in Okhaldhunga. 8,519 people died and 15,000 were injured. Over 2,00,000 homes devastated. One wing of royal palace collapsed killing two of King Tribhuvan's daughters. The government's reaction was immediate and surprisingly effective. Night curfeu was imposed to deter theft. Fair foodgrain and basic commodities market was setup by government in Tudikhel. Within water supply was restored and within four days electricity was restored. Judda Shumsher was in a hunting trip in Terai riding Eleplant who didn't even know when earthquake struck. He was only informed after three days after which he immediately rode for Kathmandu. The railway line in the Terai was devasted because of which it took him further 17 days to get back to Kathmandu. Juddha Shumsher immediately ordered distribution of free food and clothing. Bamboo was made available for construction of shelters and permisison was granted to cut down trees from government protected forests. Arrangements were made to import 250000 roofing iron sheets free of custom and ropeway charges. PM authorized four months of salary in adavnce for government employees. He allocated 50 Lakh for earthquake relief fund. Interest-free loans were distributed to victims and each house household could borrow up to Rs. 1500. Shortly after another 50 Lakhs was authorized to the relief fund. In September 1938 when bulk of loan fell due for repayment PM wrote off all outstanding loans and refunded those who had already made repayments. Post-earthquake first planned streets in Nepal were created. The resources were ploughed into building a straight street from what is now New Road Gate to Gaddhi Baithak. Damaged houses that stood along the way were demolished and a wide street replaced the winding alleys of the old town. The façade design of each building was planned and the new buildings laid out in such a way that they either faced an existing road courtyard or a backyard. Whatever the size of the plot they all had to have the same façade whereas the internal space could be designed according to the plot owner’s will. In Sukra Path new buildings could not be higher than 9.2m. The windows on the first floor were stipulated to be bigger in size compared to second floor with about 1m in width and 1.7m in height. The windows on the second floor were 0.85m in width and 1.3m in height much bigger than in traditional Newa homes.The houses could be only three stories the ground floors had wooden door panels for shops and they all had 0.7m thick cornices and 1m high parapet walls. Along Dharma Path the houses could be as high as four stories again maintaining the same details as on the adjacent street. Hence over time the intersection of New Road (formerly Juddha Sadak) Sukra Path and Dharma Path was turned into the city centre which housed offices of Gorkhapatra Sansthan the municipal office Nepal’s first movie theatre Jana Sewa Hall (Bishal Bazar today) Utpatti Kendra textile shop Juddhodaya Public School Bhugol Park to commemorate the earthquake etc. After completing New Road the government started work on Putali Sadak cutting through fields and houses. At the time these were one of the few straight roads in the Valley and the goal of this ‘reconstruction’ was to recover the function of society in affected areas including restoring livelihoods and reviving economic activity.

events.title: Sharada Magazine
events.detail: Started by poet Subba Riddhi Bahadur Malla. It was the first registered magazine in Nepal. Due to the strict censorship during Rana regime the magazine faced multiple obstacles. The writings needed to be attested by censorship department of Nepali Language Publication Committee. Several times the articles stories and poems needed to be edited in compliance with the government which used to frustrate the writers. Sharada magazine played the first role in introducing modernity in Nepali literature. The writings of many popular writers used to be published in the magazines among them were Laxmi Prasad Devkota Balakrishna Sama Lekhnath Poudyal Siddhicharan Shrestha Ram Krishna Sharma Hriday Chandra Singh Pradhan Bhawani Bhikshu Pushkar Shamsher Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala and Shiva Kumar Rai. It was closed in 1962 due to lack of funding.

events.title: Removed C-Class Ranas From The Line of Succession
events.detail: Illigitimate son of Bir Shumsher Rudra Shumsher was next in line of succession. Chandra Shumsher's legitimate sons pressed to remove him from the role. Juddha Shumsher finally stripped Rudrs Shumsher off the role of Commander-in-Chief and sent him to Palpa. Hiranya Shumsher (Subarna Shumsher's father) was sent to Dhankuta. Similarly Pratap Shumsher and Ram Shumsher were also cut off the role. Later those wealthy C-class Ranas established industries and business in India and teamed up wuth revolutionaries to overthrow the regime. Even the revised roll of succession didn't solve the internal tension. It soon surfaced again when Juddha Shumsher started giving important roles to his son Bahadur Shumsher while he was 6th in the line. Bhim Shumsher's son Padma Shumsher and Chandra Shumsher's sons were unhappy.

events.title: Nepal Chhatra Sangh
events.detail: The Nepali student movement began organizing in 1935 with the establishment of the 'Nepali Chhatra Sangh' by Nepali students in Banaras India. Later in 1951 the organization was opened in Nepal under the presidency of Ganesh Bahadur Gurung and Krishna Prasad Bhattarai as vice-president which later went to become the Nepal Bidyarthi Sangh.

events.title: Laxmi Prasad Devkota's Romantic Explosion
events.detail: One of the Great Literaty Trio. While Lekhnath was about discipline and Sama was about intellect Devkota (Mahakavi) was about unbridled imagination and heart. He rejected the elite Sanskrit styles favored by Lekhnath and wrote in common musical patterns (Jhyaure) ensuring everyday citizens could enjoy poetry. In 1936 he published Muna Madan. This short narrative poem shattered the literary landscape by choosing a folk rhythm (Jhyaure meter) and exploring the themes of labor migration human grief and true love over caste. It went on to become the best-selling book in Nepali history. In 1945 Devkota wrote and published his masterpiece epic poem Shakuntala in a staggering sprint of just three months. In the same year he published Kunjini. This decade established him as an unstoppable hyper-prolific force of nature permanently changing the syntax emotional boundaries and speed of modern Nepali writing.

events.title: 63 Industries Opened
events.detail: Throughout the reign of Juddha Shumsher 63 industries were opened with an estimated total capital investment of Rs. 7.2 Crore of which only Rs. 20 Lakhs was invested by Nepalese businessmen. Most of the industries at that time were opened on investment from Indian Marwari financiers. For instance on initial capital of INR 1.6 Lakhs Biratnagar Jute Mills (1936) was established with 75 percent investment of Indian investor Krishna Chimariya and 25 percent shares of Nepali investors. Nepal government had 8 percent shares. Likewise Ramlal Golchha initiated Raghupati Jute Mills (1946) J.P. Singhania initiated Nepal Rice Mill (1937) Morang Cotton Mills (1942) and Morang Sugar Mills (1946) Gauri Narayan Giri initiated rice mill in Janakpur (1838) etc. During World War II Nepalese factories mushroomed to exploit supply shortages in British India but they were instantly priced out when advanced Indian corporations returned to commercial production post-1945. This crisis proved fatal because the ruling Rana elite and Indian investors had aggressively extracted wartime profits as personal dividends rather than reinvesting in modern machinery leaving the under-capitalized Nepal Bank Limited unable to bail them out. Finally the 1950 Indo-Nepal trade agreement stripped away protective customs barriers just as India restricted raw material exports following its 1947 independence completely starving and bankrupting a domestic manufacturing sector already crippled by a lack of internal transportation networks.

events.title: Foundational Industrial Laws and Institutions
events.detail: First ever company Act was introduced in 1936. was a groundbreaking piece of legislation that shifted Nepal from a medieval family-run economic structure into a regulated western-style corporate system influenced from British Companies Act of 1929. Udyog Parishad (Industrial Council) was established in 1934 to promote industrial development and provide a platform to extend financial loans and monopoly in production and sales to incipient industrial ventures in cotton jute mines paper bobbin plywood frames sugar dairy soap and oil. In 1939 Gharelu Adda (Cottage Industry Office) was established whose charter was to promote cottage industries. In 1941 he founded Nepal Beureau of Mines to systematically survey and exploit the country's mineral resources.

events.title: Sundarijal Small Hydropower Station Inagurated
events.detail: The Nepal's second oldest hydroelectric plant was built in 1936 under Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher to alleviate increasing urban power demand with significant British technical assistance. It is located in the Kathmandu District and generates power using the flow from the Sundarijal River with a capacity of 640 kW. It is still active and operating in regular mode.

events.title: Connectivity Projects
events.detail: Janakpur to Jaynagar railway was opened in 1937 by British India. Initially it was used by Britishers to carry timber from the then heavily forested areas of Janakpur. When all the timber in the area had been cut down the owners gave the railway to the Nepali Government and the carrying of passengers began. Telephone lines were extended into eastern Terai. Juddha Shumsher restructured the Samarjung Comapany in 1941 formerly used to organize prison labor to road construction tasks as a Department of Main Roads. Marshy lands in Terai were given rent-free to retired Gurkha soldiers. The annual contribution of Rs. 2 Lakhs from British India for postwar military reconstruction fund was used to open two centres in Dharan and Pokhara where they could be given training in improved methods of agriculture animal husbandry and cottage industries. PM also added Rs. 2 Lakhs from his private purse. It was also done so that anti-rana activity of ex-Gurkha in India is contained.

events.title: Nepal Bank Limited Established
events.detail: NBL is the first commercial bank of Nepal established in 1937. It was as joint venture between the government and the private sector in which 60% was subscribed by the government and the balanced 40% was offered for the sale to private sector.

events.title: Shukra Raj Shastri Jailed
events.detail: Shukra Raj Shastri son of Madhav Raj Joshi set up Nepal Civil Rights Committee (Nepal Nagrik Adhikar Samiti) in 1937 to create awareness for socil reforms through writing and discussions on Hindu texts. Other founding members were Kedar Man Byathit Muralidhar Sharma Dharma Ratna Yami (Hisila Yami's father) and Ganga Lal Shrestha (Pushpa Lal Shrestha's brother). In November 1938 Shukra Raj Shastri was arrested and jailed for 6 years for giving public discourse on Bhagvad Gita in Indrachowk.

events.title: Nepal in Second World War
events.detail: Following the Munich crisis of September 1938 Juddha Shumsher wrote to London offering military support. It was politely declined at first but when war officially began Nepal offered 8000 troops. This trend continued reaching 160000 Nepali soldiers. At first Nepali were used for garrison in India but as war progressed they were sent to Middle East north Africa Burma and western Europe. Of 182 Victoria Crosses distributed 10 were awarded to Nepali. Nepal also contributed 3000 wallnut trees 800 sal trees 192 service revolvers 144 pairs of binaculars and 95 machine guns. Juddha Shumsher personally donated Rs. 77000 to the war funds. In return of the support Britain doubled Nepal’s annual subsidy to 20 Lakhs Indian Rupees and gifted the Rana regime a massive one-time post-war victory lump sum of 3.75 Crore Indian Rupees. Nepal also received advanced British military hardware to modernize its army British technical assistance to build vital infrastructure like ropeways and mills and elevated global diplomatic status with the upgrading of the British Residency in Kathmandu to a full independent embassy.

events.title: Judicial Reform
events.detail: Before Juddha Chandra Shumsher had tried some reforms such as authorizing bada hakims in terai to hear appeals against village level amini courts. He also established lower courts in remote areas such as Taplejung Dadeldhura Humla and Darchula. Ilam and Doti got the status of Gaundas. Chandra SHumsher also abolished Taksar and Dhansar courts designating Ita Chapali as a criminal court and restricting Koti Ling to hearing civil cases. The 2nd tier court under Commander-in-Chief was converted to Sadar Bhardari Adda. The 1st tier court was called the Bintipatra Niksari Adda directly answerable to Prime Minister. He aboilished the Bintipatra Niksari Adda and replaced it with three Bhardari Courts. The 2nd tier bhardari court was split into Sadar Appeal Pahila (First Appeal) and Sadar Appeal Dosra (Second Appeal). In 1940 he replaced bada hakims from Terai and created new courts with appellate juridication. Finally Pradhan Nyayalaya was established as the supreme court with power to supervise all courts and to review the decisions of the bhardari courts. In 1946 he abolished the bhardari courts. At the end of Rana rule there were 56 district courts and 13 regional appeal courts.

events.title: Great Four Martyrs
events.detail: In 1936 Nepal Praja Parishad was formed with an aim to overthrow Rana regime. In May 1940 they distributed leaflets in Kathmandu blaming Ranas for country's backwardness. In October 1940 the 43 members of the party were arrested along with Tanka Prasad Acharya. It got revealed that along with Praja Parishad another organization called Raktapat Mandal was formed which had planned mass assasination of top Rana family members. It also revealed that the group was under the direct command of King Tribhuvan. Revealing it would be very dangerous at the moment as Rana's own legitimacy was tied with the King so nothing was done at the moment. However in the night of 24 January 1941 one of the founder members of the Parishad Dharma Bhakta Mathema was hanged from a tree by road to Pashupatinath at Siphal. Shukra Raj Shastri who was serving his prision sentence was also dragged from prison and hanged on the side of the road at Pachali Teku. His body was left hanging with placard saying that such would be the fate of any man attempting to mislead people. Large crowds gathered to view the dead bodies and it only helped to intensify people's hate towards the regime.Three nights later another two founding members Dasarath Chand and Ganga Lal Shrestha were executed by firing squad. Tank Prasad Acharya being Brahman was shaved and marched through streets to prison. The 14 members of the party were life sentenced inclusing Ganesh Man Singh and remaining members were sentenced to prision.

events.title: Mass Suicide by Yogmaya And Her Disciples
events.detail: Yogmaya Neupane founded one of Nepal's earliest women's organizations the Nari Samiti and used her poems (Sarvartha Yogbani) to challenge social injustice caste discrimination and Rana oppression. During a meeting with the wife of Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher Rana she was offered gold coins which she refused saying that the establishment of a just and moral (Dharma Rajya) state was more important. After repeated appeals for reform were ignored Yogmaya and dozens of her disciples performed Jal Samadhi by jumping into the Arun River in 1941 making it one of the most significant acts of protest against the Rana regime. Yogmaya's suicide did not create the immediate political shockwave that followed the martyrdom of the Four Martyrs largely because the Rana regime suppressed information about it. However it became a powerful long-term symbol of resistance to injustice social reform and women's activism in Nepal.

events.title: Quit India Movement
events.detail: Cripps Mission to secure full Indian cooperation in World II in exchange of its Dominion status. However rejecting the terms All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India resolution where Congress would resort to civil disobedience and call the people to resist and violate government authority. In response the British imprisoned Congress' leadership for the duration of the war. Jinnah to whom Cripps had offered the right to opt out of a future union with India supported the war effort with his fellow Muslims and gained in status in British eyes. Nepali Leaders like BP Koirala Matrika Koirala Ganesh Man Singh Krishna Prasad Bhattarai Dilli Raman Regmi etc. also participated in the movement and were jailed.

events.title: Krishna Prasad Koirala Arrested
events.detail: Returning to Nepal Krishna Prashad started the trade of a type of herb called Chandamduwa which was very profitable at that time. Using his social network he opened many school hospitals postal offices etc. During the Indian independence movement many leaders fled to Nepal for security. Krishna Prashad Koirala turned his rice mill in Janakpur into a refugee camp. Arrangements were made to give food accommodation and training. That was not acceptable to the Rana government. As a result he was arrested and kept in prison till his death in 1945.

events.title: Judda Shumser Announced National Development Plan by Prime Ministerial decree
events.detail: Did not come to reality

events.title: Hanuman Nagar Jail Break
events.detail: Socialist Leaders Jayaprakash Narayan fled Hazaribagh Central Jail and along with underground leaders Ram Manohar Lohia Kartik Prasad Singh Dr. Baijnath Jha Brajkishore Shastri and Shyam Nandan Singh. They formed Azad Dasta and fled across the border into Koiladi-Barsain of Saptari. In Koiladi-Barsain they met with Nepali leaders Rameshwar Prasad Singh Chaturanand Singh and Jaimangal Prasad Singh (Ramraja Prasad Singh's father) and decided set up an underground base and a military training camp at Haldibari to train youths in guerrilla warfare. The British administration found the location and pressed Nepal government to arrest them. In May 1943 Nepalese police successfully arrested Jayaprakash Narayan Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia and several other key leaders detaining them at the Hanumannagar Jail. The Indian leaders and the leaders of Koiladi-Barsain in Nepal including Rameshwar Prasad Singh Jaimangal Prasad Singh Chaturanand Singh Meen Bahadur Singh planned to drive them out of jail. On the night of May 23 1943 a joint force launched a surprise raid on the Hanumannagar jail and freed the leaders. JP and Dr. Lohia were escorted very tactfully to India which brought a ray of hope for revolutionaries in India. Around 200 people including Rameshwar Prasad Singh Jaimangal Prasad Singh Chaturanand Singh were arrested by the Rana regime from Saptari and taken to the Central Jail.

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 92= INR 100) 1943
events.detail: Due to large wartime inflow of Indian rupees from the remittances of Gurkha soldiers in the British Army and from rice exports sold at high price

events.title: Soviet Expansion Into Eastern Europe
events.detail: The Soviet expansion in Eastern Europe occurred between 1945 and 1949 as they established political control over the region following World War II. This geopolitical shift transformed Poland, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Czechoslovakia, and East Germany into Soviet satellite states, effectively creating the Eastern Bloc and initiating the Cold War. Poland: Communists used police terror, disqualified opposition candidates from voting lists, and massive ballot box stuffing during the 1947 elections to force out the democratic Peasant Party. Hungary: The Soviet military arrested key anti-communist politicians, while local communists used "salami tactics" to blackmail, divide, and disqualify opposition MPs until only communists remained. Romania: Soviet leadership forced the reigning King to appoint a communist Prime Minister in 1945, followed by rigged elections in 1946 and a final ultimatum in 1947 that forced the King to abdicate at gunpoint. Bulgaria: The country was a wartime monarchy that transitioned into a fragile multi-party coalition republic under the "Fatherland Front" after a 1944 coup. Communist factions later took control of the police, executed the top democratic opposition leaders for "treason," and systematically banned all rival political parties by 1947. Czechoslovakia: In February 1948, communists staged a coup over a parliamentary democracy by deploying armed workers' militias, seizing government buildings, and threatening a civil war, forcing the president to accept an all-communist cabinet. East Germany: Soviet authorities forced the dominant Social Democratic Party to merge into the Communist Party in 1946, building a puppet police state that officially declared itself the German Democratic Republic in 1949.

events.title: First Paper Currency Notes Issued
events.detail: Released currency notes were of denominations 1510 and Rs.100 and the notes had the Picture of late King Tribhuvan’s crown. The notes of King Tribhuvan were not signed by a bank governor but by a Khajanchi (head of the treasury) who was a high Hindu priest in the same time. Nepal’s early paper currency probably includes the only notes of the world which were signed by a high priest.

events.title: Juddha Shumsher Renounced the Throne and Went for Syanyas
Padma Shumsher
events.detail: Resigned from the position and died naturally at age 78 in Calcutta

events.title: Inherited Empty Treasury
events.detail: Juddha Shumsher had requisitioned large area of lands and spent immense sum to provide for his 20 sons and about equal daughters. Upon appointment he was shocked to find out that the exchequer virtually depleted. Padma Shumsher himself was estranged from his father Bhim Shumsher thus had no share of wealth from his father. He hed very ceremony for his inaguration and also didn't move to official residence of PM and insisted on living in his own modest residence at Bishalnagar.

events.title: Yugoslavia Became a Socialist Republic
events.detail: During World War II, Yugoslavia was invaded and occupied by Germany and its allies in April 1941. After the Axis invasion of Yugoslavia, Josip Broz Tito, the General Secretary of Communist Party of Yugoslavia, led the Yugoslav guerrilla movement, the Partisans, often regarded as the most effective resistance movement in German-occupied Europe. By the end of 1943, the Partisans, with the Allies' backing, took power in Yugoslavia. After the war, elections were held in November 1945. The Communist-led People's Front won essentially all seats because opposition forces had been excluded from meaningful participation. On 29 November 1945, the Constituent Assembly formally abolished the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, ended the monarchy, and proclaimed the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia (FPRY). King Peter II, who had been in exile during the war, never returned to power. The new Yugoslavia nationalized much of the economy, introduced socialist economic planning, and established a one-party communist political system. By 1963, Yugoslavia had firmly established itself as a socialist state. After the 1948 split with Stalin, Tito had developed a distinct Yugoslav model of socialism based on workers' self-management, social ownership of enterprises, decentralization, a leading role for the Communist Party, and rejection of Soviet-style centralized planning. By the 1960s, Yugoslavia wanted to emphasize that it had moved beyond the initial revolutionary/postwar phase toward a more developed socialist system therefore changed its name to Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in 1963. The name change accompanied a broader constitutional restructuring. Yugoslavia was moving away from the highly centralized model of the immediate postwar period toward greater decentralization and workers' self-management. The six republics increasingly received greater responsibilities, while the federal system was designed around the idea that power should be exercised not only by the central state but also by workers, municipalities, republics and other self-governing institutions.

events.title: Lord and Lady Mountbatten Visited Nepal
events.detail: first Governor-General of independent India

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 72= INR 100) 1946
events.detail: Continued effect of wartime money

events.title: Nepal Malchalani Tatha Beema Company Founded
events.detail: There were no Nepali insurance companies before 1947, so Nepal Bank Limited established the first non-life insurance company titled 'Nepal Malchalani Tatha Beema Company'. It became 'Nepal Insurance and Transportation Company Limited' in 1959. It transformed into 'Nepal Insurance Company Limited' in 1991 to operate as non-life insurance. Nepal Bank Limited and Asian Life Insurance Company Limited remain the dominant major institutional shareholders controlling the company today with 51% of shares.

events.title: Nepali Congress Party Formed and First General Convention
events.detail: On 18 Asoj 2003 BS after publishing an appeal in a newspaper called “The Searchlight” in Patna on 15 Katik 2003 BS a meeting held at Narendra Regmi’s house in Dugdha Binayak Banaras decided to establish the “All India Nepali National Congress” and formed an ad-hoc committee for it. B.P. Koirala was the coordinator of the committee with Subba Devi Prasad Sapkota as the chairman Balchandra Sharma as the vice-chairman Krishna Prasad Upadhyay Bhattarai as the general secretary Gopal Prasad Bhattarai as the publicity minister and Dinanath Sapkota and Laxmi Prasad Sapkota as the members and Lila Nateshwar (Ishwar) Baral as the office minister. The First Party Convention held at Bhawanipur Khalsa in Kolkata on 12 and 13 Magh 2003 merged the party with All India Nepali Gorkha Congress of Dharma Narayan Pradhan and changed its name and formed the "Nepali National Congress". It expressed respect for the struggle and bravery of the Praja Parishad against the Rana regime in the country and made its leader Tanka Prasad Acharya (who was imprisoned in a Kathmandu jail at that time) its honorary president and BP Koirala its acting president. Similarly Balchandra Sharma was a minister Krishna Prasad Upadhyay Bhattarai was the organization minister Dr. Dilli Raman Regmi was the head of the Publication Department Leela Nateshwar (Ishwar) Baral was the office head Devi Prasad Sapkota D.N. Pradhan Devvrat Pariyar Krishna Bahadur Pradhan (pseudonym of Ganeshman Singh) Gopal Prasad Upadhyay Bhattarai Lakpa Tshiring Sherpa and Rudra Prasad Giri were members.

events.title: Biratnagar Jute Mill Strike
events.detail: The demonstration started on March 4 1947 under the leadership of Girija Prasad Koirala along with Tarini Prasad Koirala Man Mohan Adhikari and Yuvaraj Adhikari as employees in the mill. The strike was launched with initial demands purely based on labor rights but later the workers also demanded political trade union rights. The Nepali Congress supported the strike at Biratnagar. On March 9 Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala joined the strike with his supporters and the strike grew in number. Padma Shumsher sent state troops to Biratnagar to put down the strike. The strike ended when the troops reached Biratnagar after they arrested the leaders. Some of these leaders escaped capture by fleeing to India. Six National Congress leaders (Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala Girija Prasad Koirala Tarini Prasad Koirala Gehendrahari Sharma Manmohan Adhikari and Yubaraj Adhikari) were walked to Kathmandu as prisoners. The Nepali Congress held a conference in Jogbani India and resolved to initiate a nationwide Satyagraha or civil disobedience movement if the prisioners were not released. Thus the countrywide anti-Rana demonstration started which only grew bigger on using force. On May Padma Shumsher announced several reforms to appease the protestors such as introduction of female education calling experts to discuss civil rights establishment of elected municipals and publication of annual budget. On 2 June 1947 he also released all the leaders. Within a month of announcement municipal elections were held in Kathmandu with 77% voter turnout. The city was divided into 21 wards and among all elected counsellors seven were from business community seven from teaching profession and tem were nominated members.

events.title: Nepal-America Agreement of Commerce and Friendship
events.detail: As a last stretch to anchor the sinking boat Ranas tried to neutralizing the challenges posed by the political opposition through the expansion of the diplomatic relations and and seeking the financial and technical assistance. An Agreement of Commerce and Friendship was signed in Kathmandu recognising each other's sovereignty and establishing formal diplomatic relation

events.title: Jayatu Sanskritam Movement
events.detail: On 1 June 1947 the students of Tin Dhara Pakshala submitted a written demand to Prime Minister Padma Shumsher requesting courses in geography history economics and political science. When the government ignored the students went on strike waving anti-Rana flags. The strike lasted until 15 June when the government agreed to expand the curriculum offered to the students. Although the protests were placated by promises from Prime Minister Padma Shumsher his military commander-in-chief Mohan Shumsher ordered arrests and imprisonments and forcefully deported forty-two students who were identified as leaders of the movement. Most of those deported student leaders like Shree Bhadra Sharma (Tanahaun) joined NC in due course. He had previously come into contact with Nepali Congress in 2003 when he went to Banaras to take part in the intermediate level examination.

events.title: First Kathmandu Municipality Election
events.detail: Four forts of Kathmandu Municipality were determined for the election and 21 wards were established within them. In the east, Bishalnagar, Tangal, Gyaneshwor, Naxal and Dillibazar were located, while in the west, Bishnumati Wari, Bhimsensthan, Kankeshwari, and Kaldhara were located. In the north, Bishnumati Pari Paknajol, Thamel, Lazimpat, and Ghaihridhara were located. Also in the south it was extended to Bagmati Wari, Kuriya Gaun, Bagbazar, Tripureshwor and Pachali. The area within this was declared Kathmandu Municipality. There was a system of electing one person from each ward and only deputy Mayor was to be voted by people. Only males were included in the voter list. Finally, the voter list was prepared including the names of males who had reached the age of 21. A total of 68,118 voters were determined from 13,553 households. Ballot papers were delivered to every house based on the number of men who had reached the age of 21 a day earlier. It was estimated that 60 to 65 percent of the votes were cast in the election. Wards 5, 9, 10 and 11 out of 21 wards were unopposed. There were 22 polling stations in the remaining 17 wards. Voting was allowed only from 11 am to 3 pm. Since the candidates were given colors without any symbols, they had to cast their votes in the same color. Since the polling stations were open, everyone could see who voted for whom. A municipal board of 31 members was formed, 21 elected and 10 nominated. However, due to differences in working style, 16 elected members resigned within ten months. A month later, 6 of the remaining nominated members also resigned. Gehendra Shumsher Thapa was appointed as the chairman of Kathmandu by the Rana regime and Shankar Dev Pant was elected as his deputy from the common people.

events.title: NC's Expansion in Pokhara
events.detail: Nepali Rastriya Congress: After the Jayatu Sanskritam Movement Nepali Rastriya Congress felt necessity in expansion of its organization in Nepal. Shree Bhadra Sharma was asked to work in the west no. 3 region which included today’s Lamjung, Tanahu (Sharma’s home district) and Kaski district. When he first arrived in Pokhara from Banaras with some pamphlets and Congress documents, he did not have any contacts in Pokhara. After secretly disseminating some pamphlets he headed to his area, Bandipur. Kadam Kumar Piya, a merchant of Bandipur, knew Prem Raj Mulmi, the son of a Pokhareli trader, Harsha Kumar, who had studied in the Juddhodaya Public High School, in Kathmandu. Harsha Kumar ahd migrated to Pokhara from Patan in 1919. Piya came all the way to Pokhara and introduced Sharma to Mulmi, a young lad in his twenties. Though young, Mulmi had already found a place in a loose network of seniors like Rishi Keshav Parajuli, Dharma Shila, Mukti Nath Timisina, Sundar Prasad Marsani, Daya Shankar Palikhe, Shri Kant Adhikari, etc. These people were in their thirties. They were educated to an extent, had some knowledge of the outside world, and were eager to do something for the society they were in. They met regularly either at Mulmi’s shop/residence or at the Dharmashila Buddha Bihar at Nadipur where the Buddhist nun Dharma Shila (born as Setimaya Tamrakar) resided. When Shri Bhadra Sharma explained the rationale of his coming, and sought support, the first person Mulmi turned to was Rishi Keshav Parajuli, a young man in his early thirties, who, influenced by Gandhi, wore homespun clothes. Within a few days some ten locals—friends of Parajuli and Mulmi—were ready to be part of this underground initiative, to be part of the Congress. They gathered in front of the Bindhyabasini temple at midnight and took a vow, and signed the membership card with their blood to become members of the party. Present that day in this secret meeting, according to Shri Bhadra Sharma, were Rishi Keshav Parajuli, Bhakta Raj Mulmi, Mathura Prasad Bajimaya, Dil Bahadur Bhari, Govinda Bahadur Vaidya, Jhapat Bahadur Bhattachan, Ram or Chin Bahadur Badgami (one of the two), and probably Daya Shankar Palikhe. Not only was the member selection procedure different, but also the members came from different caste groups—from Brahman purohit (priest) to Newar and Thakali youths from trading families. In this new social formation aimed for modern system of governance, old symbols were used, but they were raised to a higher level by invoking god, and the contract, in the form of membership, was signed by their own blood. Nepali Prajatantrik Congress: Around the same time, Hari Prasad Sharma of the Nepali Prajatantrik Congress also arrived in Pokhara in order to expand the party organization. Since Hari Prasad was not student like Shree Bhadra, his movement was not easy. He entered Pokhara with the party documents (pamphlets, etc.) in the disguise of a sadhu known as Kana-Baba. Two youths of Masbar namely Tek Nath Baral and Hom Nath Baral were returning from their hang out place i.e., Prem Raj Mulmi’s shop when Hari Prasad saw two “educated-sounding” young men. Prem Raj Mulmi’s businesses was to exchange Indian currency brought by Gurkha soldiers with Nepali currency. He would use the Indian currency to purchase and import goods from India. After a brief conversation, the two took baba along to their house, and later they even built him a thatched hut in a nearby hill, a kilometre away from their residences. Tek Nath Baral was also among the students expelled during the Jayatu Sanskritam movement, and was already in contact with the Congress during his stay at Banaras. Initially local youths like Purna Bhadra Adhikari, Hom Nath Baral, Tek Nath Baral, Agni Prasad Baral, etc., became members. Unlike Shree Bhadra who left recruitment largely to local activists, Hari Prasad personally coordinated the recruitment effort. When badahakim Dhan Shumsher Rana, the son of Palpa's badahakim Rudra Shumsher, discovered his activities and ordered his arrest, local activists secretly moved him to Mukti Nath Timisina's (a teacher at basic school in Batulechaur) house in Batulechaur and eventually helped him escape Pokhara.

events.title: Nepal Woman Association Formed
events.detail: Mangala Devi Singh led the founding of the Nepal Women’s Association the first organized women’s political movement in Nepal. It demanded women’s education political participation and an end to legal and social discrimination under Rana rule. The movement linked women’s rights directly with the broader anti-Rana democratic struggle and helped bring women into organized political activism for the first time.

events.title: India got Independence
events.detail: As British left the India Ranas felt the insecurity as Britan was providing security to the regime. Therefore it reversed its isolationist policy. It sent goodwill mission to Washington on October 1946. As a result diplomatic relation was established in April 1947. Though Rana feared of liberated India that it might invalidate the Anglo-Nepal Treaty but it turned out fine. Nepal agreed to render military assistence to India in crisis situation in exchange of support to the Rana regime. India was also eager to continue recruitment of Gurkhas into its militray as they were handy in coercing princely States. Hence on Nov 1 1947 Britain–India–Nepal Tripartite Agreement was signed that divided the existing 10 Gurkha regiments alloting 6 to India and 4 to British. Agreement to Gurkha recruitment was set to be renewed every five years with British while with India it was set to be operative unless one side formally requests abrogation.

events.title: India-Pakistan war of 1947–1948
events.detail: Fought between India and Pakistan over the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. Maharaja Hari Singh was a Hindu monarch while vast majority of his subjects were Muslim. Hoping to maintain sovereignty the Maharaja chose not to join either nation immediately and sought independence. In late summer pro-Pakistani rebellions broke out among Muslim subjects along Kashmir's western borders. On October 22 1947 thousands of armed Pashtun tribesmen from Pakistan's North-West Frontier Province invaded Kashmir. Realizing his state forces were vastly outnumbered Maharaja Hari Singh appealed to the Indian government for military assistance to repel the invaders. India agreed to send troops but on one strict condition: the Maharaja had to legally join India. On October 26 1947 Hari Singh signed the ⁠Instrument of Accession formally making Jammu and Kashmir a part of India.
