Pakistan refused to recognize the validity of the Instrument of Accession viewing it as a move forced upon a population that largely favored Pakistan. The Pakistani military entered the fray shortly after to back the tribal forces. This turned a localized conflict into a full-scale war between the newly independent regular armies of India and Pakistan which raged until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire took effect on January 1 1949. Military representatives from both countries met under UN mediation and signed the Karachi Agreement on July 27 1949. This line left roughly 65% of Jammu and Kashmir's territory and population under Indian control while the remaining 35% (consisting of Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan) fell under Pakistani control. However neither India nor Pakistan trusted the other enough to withdraw their militaries as the UN resolution required. Because the troop withdrawals never happened the proposed democratic vote to let Kashmiris decide their own future was never held.

events.title: NC Second General Convention
events.detail: BP Koirala; Nepali Rastriya Congress held its second convention in Banaras in Magh 2004 which elected BP Koirala as its president.

events.title: The Nepal Government Act 1948
events.detail: Following the announcement of May 2047 Mohan Shumsher called a three-man team from India to advice him on political reforms. They drafted a constitution which was promulgated despite reservation from the hardliners. It envisioned the establishment of Council of Ministers tenured four years a bicameral parliament (Rajya Sabha and Bhardari Sabha) and a High Court. PM and Maharaja of Kaski and Lamjung were to be heriditary who was to choose three members and two were to be chosen by the legislature. It envisioned village and town panchayat elected from universal suffrage and the district panchayat to be elected by the members of village and town panchayat. It ensured fundamental rights to speech and assemble. Padma Shumsher resigned even before the constitution came into effect on 14 April 1948 therefore this constitution died even before it could be implemented.

events.title: Padma Shumsher's Resignation
events.detail: Padma Shumsher was relatively liberal who stood with the constitutional reform. However Mohan Shumsher vehemently opposed these changes. To escape the immediate danger from the anti-reform camp he moved to India resigning from his position.

events.title: Mohan Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana
events.detail: End of regime

events.title: Mohan's Appeasement vs Nehru's Push for Reform
events.detail: Mohan Shumsher was certain that for his regime to continue he needs unequivocal support from India. However Nehru was firm in his resolve that the Rana regime cannot continue without visible political reform. Along the line of appeasement policy in mid-1948 Nepal offered a loan of ten battalions of Nepal Army to assist in Hydrabad and Kashmir crisis which was gracefully accepted. In Februaru 1950 Mohan Shumsher travelled to New Delhi for discussion with PM Nehru on treaties of friendship and trade. Just before the visit to deflect Indian criticism he announced his plans for formation of a constituent assembly to draft a constitution for Nepal. However India made it clear that the conclusions of the treaties should be linked to the introduction of political reform. Mohan Shumsher reluctant for the reform he delayed it and hoped that China's recent occupation of Tibet would force Delhi to come to his terms. It actually worked India wanted to conclude the treaty of friendship as soon as possible dropping the linkage with political reforms. The treaty ensured that Nepal would not tolerate any threat to security of India by a foreign aggressor obviously China in this case. This compromise between Rana and Nehru came as a discomfort to Nepali Congress. While Indian Government was willing to use Nepali Congress insurgency to pressure Ranas into accepting political reforms it did not want the regime toppled. New Delhi supported the struggle as log as it didn't threaten the regime but it would not give and material support to arm struggle. At lease NC got green signal from India.

events.title: Nepal Prajatantrik Congress Formed
events.detail: While BP was released from jail on August 2047 Dilli Raman Regmi who was was made the acting president refused to leave the position for BP. He further dismissed Tanka Prasad Acharya and declared himself president. This led to split in which Dilli Raman Regmi continued his activity maintaining the party name Nepali Rastriya Congress. The BP led Nepali Rastriya Congress also went some internal differences on non-violent vs violent means of revolution. Leaders especially related to Rana family prioritized on voilent struggle this led to fromation of Nepal Prajatantrik Congress by Subarna Shamsher's Mahabir Shamsher Mahendra Bikram Shah and Rishikesh Shah in Calcutta.

events.title: BP Koirala Arrested
events.detail: In Septemebr 1948 Nepal Praja Panchayat was opened with aim to cooperating with Rana governement in implementing 1948 constitution. However when the government showed no interest in doing so the party decided to launch a satyagraha. As it gained momentum BP koirala traveled incognito to Kathmandu with a proposal to Nepal Praja Panchayat to coordinate its activities with Nepali Congress but it was rejected. To add to his woes BP Koirala was arrested and thrown into prision. After six months he went on hunger strike which triggered widespread anti-Rana protests in India and several politicians including PM Nehru wrote to Mohan Shumsher on BP's behalf. With growing political pressue and BP's deteriorating health BP was released after 29 days of hunger strike.

events.title: NC Third General Convention
events.detail: Matrika Prasad Koirala; The convention was held in Darbhanga and Matrika Prasad Koirala became the president. Meanwhile Rastriya Prajatantrik Congress made Mahendra Bikram Shah its president.

events.title: Nepal Communist Party Founded
events.detail: Founded under Puspalal Shrestha's leadership by Niranjan Govinda Vaidya, Nara Bahadur Karmacharya, Narayan Vilas Joshi and Moti Devi Shrestha was not established within Nepal itself. The CPN (Communist Party of Nepal) was founded in a house on the second floor of 28 Nabin Sarkar Lane Shyambazar area Kolkata India. Moti Devi was not physically present in Shyambazar. After the establishment of this party leaders including Manmohan Adhikari, Tulsilal Amatya, and Keshar Jang Rayamajhi also joined. Mohan Bikram Singh also joind the party later in 1953.

events.title: 15-Year Development Plan
events.detail: Mohan Shumsher thought the people's discontent is due to economic hardship rather than political. Therefore he inagurated National Economic Planning Committee that drew up a 15-year development plan to improve transport agriculture mines industry education health etc. However the committee rarely met and effectively existed only on paper.

events.title: Mao Zedong declared the founding of the People’s Republic of China Chiang Kai-shek of KMT fled to Taiwan
Pokhara's First "Modern" School as Political Aerna For NC
events.detail: On Dec 6, 1949, Pokhara established its first modern English school, Pokhara Public Middle School PPMS in a few pauwas (resting places for pilgrims/travellers) of Narayansthan. After discussing among themselves for more than a year, the activists pushed the idea of establishing the English/modern school further. When, on one occasion, the regional education director Ram Singh Thakuri, based in Tansen, came to Pokhara to inspect the Basic school, the activists—Mukti Nath Timisina, Rishi Keshav Parajuli, Dharma Shila, Sundar Prasad Marsani, and the likes—voiced their concern. Thakuri agreed to write a supportive report on their petition to the Rana PM. He also advised them to collect five to seven thousand rupees for the purpose, and to mention this fact in the letter, which, according to him, would help their bid. Elated by the encouraging discussion, they began to collect signatures for the petition as well as seek donations to finance the school (because if the government were to be asked for finances, it was more likely that they wouldn’t receive the permission). If we look at the profile of the activists involved in the opening the PPMS, we find that they had been separately involved in propagating different types of education—from voluntarily teaching children in their neighbourhood to running a Bihàr, or Brahmacaryàshram, as well as the Basic school. But their collective activism was centred on promoting what they called modern education i.e. primacy of English, and group involvement. Such a crave for English education resulted from people believing that English epitomized prosperity, and advancement like in the West. The initiative also challenged conservative caste and religious attitudes, which dismissed English education as “cow-eaters’ education.” By promoting English education, activists challenged the Ranas’ monopoly over knowledge and sought to close the social gap between rulers and subjects. More importantly, the school was politically significant. Activists used it as a legitimate public institution where they could meet, organize, build networks, identify supporters, and discuss politics without openly confronting the Rana regime. The government granted the permission but the teachers were not available who could teach English, because except the badahakim, his son, and a couple of others, nobody knew English. Badahakim, who was chairperson of the school managing committee, was unco-coperative. He even sacked secretary Rishi Keshav Parajuli on suspesion of being a Congress member. The school gave activists a legitimate space to organize, build networks, and participate in public affairs, gradually transforming themselves from subjects into citizens with claims to influence their own destiny. Its management committee was also politically significant: the Rana governor formally chaired it, but most other positions were occupied by local political activists such as Rishi Keshav Parajuli (Secretary), Mukti Nath Timisina(Advisor), Prem Raj Mulmi, Sundar Prasad Marasaini, Daya Shankar Palikhe, etc. Bringing rulers and activists into the same institution symbolically challenged the traditional hierarchy between the governed and the governor.

events.title: Dr. Toni Hagen travels across Nepal in 1950 as part of a first Swiss development assistance mission.
Bindhyabasini Fire And Arrests
events.detail: The Incident: In 1950, a fire broke in Bindhyabasini temple during an yagya that spread and burnt 300 houses and killed no less than two dozen people. It turned out to be an opportunity for the political workers to expand their role and reach into the public. The social actors did capitalize the moment by spending their time and energy in helping the victims in various ways. Along with protests, handwritten pamphlets were distributed demanding compensation and support from the government. Had it been only a natural calamity, the people would not perhaps have planned to come out in the street. But the locals tied it up with badahakim Dhan Shamsher Rana. Under Rana's insistance, for the first time a black goat was sacrificed in the yagya. There already was resentment against the idea but when fire broke on the last day of yagya, anger was geared against the badahakim. A major public procession in Pokhara marked a shift from subjects to citizens: people who had traditionally only petitioned rulers now collectively demanded relief and challenged government decisions, asserting rights even when such action was technically illegal. The NC leaders and the social activists actively participated in the protests. After the protests the political activities were strictly banned and survelience was increased. The Compensation: To control the situation, Mohan Shumsher sent Fatte Bahadur Pande to assess the condition along with the relief material. Mohan Shumsher couldn't fully trust Dhan Shumsher since his father Rudra Shumsher, badahakim of Palpaa had already defected to NC. After the assessment, poor familes were given foodgrains and others were given interest free loan. Later through a radio message Padma Shumsher announced that money will be given to rebuild the house. Accordingly, within two months funds were disburshed. This incident made Ranas to bow to the demands of Pokhreli which filled people with confidence and sense of empowerment. NC Merger: A major development came in April 1950, when the two Congress parties merged into Nepali Congress. The news excited the Pokhara activists because they anticipated a larger nationwide movement against the Rana regime. Until this point, Pokhara's activists had largely operated independently, taking initiatives based on their own understanding rather than following instructions from a central political organization. Two activists, Ram Bahadur Badgami and Bhakta Raj Mulmi, were therefore sent to Banaras, the major center of the Nepali Congress's political activity in India. Ram Bahadur Badgami began working at the Congress secretariat. He regularly sent political materials back to Pokhara, including party documents, circulars and pamphlets. A Congress rubber stamp and party flag were also brought to Pokhara, helping formalize the local organization and connect it with the national movement. Hari Prasad Sharma Arrested: The expanding political network suffered a major setback when Hari Prasad Sharma, who had been involved in organizing underground political activities in Pokhara, was arrested. Authorities discovered a notebook containing the names of people Sharma had met in Pokhara. Sensing the threat of arrests Muktinath Timisina, Ram Bahadur Badgami, Bhakta Raj Mulmi, etc fled form Pokhara and reached Banaras to join NC leaders. Based on this information some one and half dozen people, including Dharma Shila, Shrikant Adhikari, Sundar Prasad Marsani, Min Bahadur Gurung (later won 1959 election from Kaski and became Deputy Minister of Defence), Mohnath Baral, Bishnu Hari, Shree Prasad Upadhaya, Khadananda Sharma, Madhav Prasad Ghimire (the poet, wasn't politically involved but just due to having name in the diary), were arrested. Dharma Shila became the first woman political prisoner in Pokhara after being imprisoned for nine days. However, interestingly, some “big fishes” like Rishi Keshav Parajuli, Mukti Nath Timisina, and Prem Raj Mulmi were spared. Though Timisina was not locally arrested he was asked to report to the centre, Kathmandu. When he reached Kathmandu he learned from his sources that he would immediately be arrested, so he chose to flee to India. Later when the government learned this, it asked the local authority to confiscate the belongings of Timisina, but since Rishi Keshav Parajuli and Prem Raj Mulmi also got to learn this, they shifted “important things” from Timisina’s house. Even though Parajuli was not arrested, he was stripped of his post as the PPM School secretary. It seems that the government did not want to annoy the traders for no business person was arrested.

events.title: NC Fourth General Convention of Unity
events.detail: Matrika Prasad Koirala; Nepali Rastriya Congress and Nepali Prajatantrik Congress merged to form the Nepali Congress party in the convention held at Tiger Hall in Calcutta. The Nepali Prajatantrik found Matrika to be accomodative one so under general agreement he was chosen the president. Mahendra Bikram Shah was elected General Secretary and Subarna Shumsher was Treasurer. Even after the merger he continued his faction as Nepali Rastriya Congress along with Rishikesh Shah.

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 103= INR 100) 1950
events.detail: Due to increasing volume of imports from India

events.title: Symbolic Revolt in Pokhara
events.detail: Khaddar and Kurtha-Suruwal: After NC's influence in Pokhara there was a gradual increase in the number of people who wore homespun cloth called khaddar. And, instead of traditional lavedà-suruwàl, new kurthà-suruwàl or kurthà-paijàmà became popular. People were also seen sporting what is called Jawàhar kot. These attires were associated with the Congress party of India, or basically with the activists of the independence movement there, and eventually became sartorial choice/symbol of the Nepali Congress leaders. Meanwhile for wearing kurta-suruwl and carrying political books teacher Rishi Keshav Parajuli was forcefully removed from Pokhara Public Middle School. A low level worker in local court, Netra Pani Gautam, who unknowingly wore kurtha-suruwal as a fashion and went to reciveve dashain tika from badahakim was slapped, made to remove clothes and walk back home naked. Namaste and Clapping: At a school visit by the badahakim in Batulechaur, students and local Dalits deliberately greeted him with namaste instead of the customary swasti, which symbolized submission to the Rana rulers. They also clapped after his speech, another break from protocol. Both acts (namaste as well as clapping) were unacceptable as per the existing norms. All this was concocted by Mukti Nath Timisina, a teacher at the school and former chakaridar in Rana court, who had stood up against the practice of swasti. The Rana administration objected and ordered students not to use namaste, but took no further action. Mukti Nath Timisina also held a translator’s job at the Nepali Bhasha Prakashini Samiti, which earned him the pandit title. Hukka Sharing and Ploughing: After becoming members of NC, they started sharing hukka, breaking caste rules between groups that traditionally could not share it. Around 15 activists collectively ploughed a field near Fewa Lake, a task traditionally associated with lower castes. This publicly demonstrated their rejection of caste boundaries. The actions had serious social consequences. Some activists, such as Dil Bahadur Bhari, were beaten up by their families, while their families were ostracized and even denied access to communal water sources.

events.title: Korean War of 1950-1953
events.detail: polarization between the US and USSR started Cold War

events.title: India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship
events.detail: Open Economic Relationship: Nepal was free to import goods from or through India. National Treatment: Citizens of both countries received reciprocal privileges regarding residence property business and movement. Security Consultation Clause: Both governments agreed to inform and consult each other regarding serious security threats. Strategic Dependence: Nepal agreed to obtain arms and military equipment through India or with India's consent.

events.title: India–Nepal Treaty of Trade and Commerce
events.detail: Free Trade with India: Goods moving between Nepal and India generally faced no customs barriers. Third-Country Tariff Constraint: Nepal could not impose higher tariffs on Indian goods than on goods imported from third countries. It also ensured that Nepal would impose tariff on its exports to ensure that the good wouldn't be cheaper than identical goods produced in India. Transit Rights: Nepal obtained access to overseas trade through Indian territory and ports. Revenue Protection: The treaty sought to prevent third-country goods from entering India through Nepal to evade Indian customs duties.

events.title: Bairgania Conference and NC's First Armed Struggle
events.detail: A huge conference was held in Bairgania Bihar on 27 September 1950 where Nepali Congress announced an armed revolution against the Rana regime. While most leaders were in favor of armed revolution while Girija Prasad Koirala and few leaders were against violent way of struggle. Party also announced the liquidation of operations in India and declared that the party would operate only inside Nepal. Leaders like Bhadrakali Mishra were ideologically against the armed struggle. He was a Gandhian, who even served as a personal assistant to Gandhi, travelled with him and spent some time at his ashram

events.title: Pokhara's Revolution and Counter Revolution
events.detail: Bairgania Conference: Two Pokharelis, namely Mukti Nath Timisina and Ram Bahadur Badgami attended the Bairgania Conference. Timisina, who had fled after the kana baba incident was given the responsibility to prepare for the uprising in Pokhara. When the NC decided to immediately launch an armed attack after Tribhuvan flew to India, Timisina was asked to go to Pokhara. But he did not do that citing personal reasons. Because of his absence, there wasn’t anybody who would convey the decisions of the party and act accordingly in Pokhara. Thus, in Pokhara, neither did the local activists have arms nor were there any other militant groups. Whatever organization the local activists had built had been dismantled to a large extent because of their arrests. The government’s prohibitory notices—the criminal elements are engaged in disturbing peace and tranquillity, but the government is determined to book them to justice and bring peace and harmony back; do not participate in any such activities that is against the law; inform the government of any criminal activities and get rewarded, etc.—also would give the people indication of the graveness of the situation. And the activists would have been able to read between the lines. Not many people however had any idea of what Congress was, or what it was up to, but they seemed to be aware of the imminent threat. Some in Pokhara even had sent their children to other places for their safety. Tej Nath Ghimire, literary figure and founding president of Nepal Sikshyak Sangh, Kaski, was one of them. He, along with his sister, was sent to a nearby village, Bhalam. When he returned after some days, he was again sent to his maternal uncle’s house at Ghachok. Preparations For Revolution: It was already more than a month since the armed struggle had started and mostly good news had started reaching Pokhara. A secret meeting was called at Rishi Keshav Parajuli’s residence on January 6, 1951 to take a collective decision on the matter. Some 50–60 people participated; many of whom, by then, had already been members of the party. In the meeting Parajuli proposed the idea of organizing continuous peaceful demonstrations against the Rana regime in Pokhara. First Day: Though most agreed with the idea, not many were enthused to take part in them, especially on the first day. Prem Bahadur Pradhan (Haran), an India returnee, was not invited to the meeting but had found about it and he became the first person to volunteer for the job. After some cajoling eight more were ready to demonstrate on the first day, which was scheduled for the same day in the afternoon. But by the time the meeting ended, three individuals had changed their mind. The demonstration was to commence from the southern end of the market, Simalchaur. But at the last minute, another three changed their mind and backed out. Only three—namely, Haran, Uttar Kumar Shrestha, and Khem Raj Bharati—were left to take up the task. As decided, Rishi Keshav Parajuli, along with two other friends, arrived on the scene with the party flag, which he handed over to the participants and taught them the slogans as well as the “way” of chanting them. Seeing three men carrying a flag, which was never seen before, and chanting slogans which was unheard of (and also incomprehensible), common people were both frightened and at the same time curious. Congress was an enigma of which many had heard (negative) rumours but none had actually seen its members. Even though people were frightened, they were peeping from behind the doors. They were surprised to see familiar faces in the Congress. When they reached near Ranipauwa, a constable approached and told them that they were called by the governor and tried to snatch the flag. In the scuffle the flag got torn up. On their way to the badahakim office, they kept on chanting slogans. Contrary to their expectations, badahakim Dhan Shumsher Rana appeared not enraged, and was in conciliatory mood; rather than chastising the demonstrators, he “suggested” to them not to get involved in such activities. In the meantime, while Rana was speaking, Haran lit a cigarette in front of him, which already was a crime to put him behind the bars. The bodyguard of the governor Rana snatched the cigarette and scolded him for smoking in front of the “General.” Unfazed, Haran shouted back, “Does only your Jersàheb (general sahib) have mouth, don’t I have one?” and even pulled the mat that the governor was standing on. This act alone, unimaginable prior to the movement, illustrates the transformation that would be seen in the entire country in the coming days. Haran was taken into custody, and the other two were released. In the evening, the authorities issued a notice asking the public not to participate in any demonstration or organize any such programs that create problem in maintaining peace and tranquillity in the city. Second Day: Encouraged by the day’s accomplishments, Rishi Keshav Parajuli and friends sat together to plan for the next day. None of the nine demonstrators selected for the next day’s program backed out. New flags were made and the demonstration began from the same place and took the same route. The difference this time was that there were some more people, some more flags, and the onlookers who initially were frightened and had even closed their shops, did not do so. The agitators were arrested and the governor again assuaged them to not get involved, but later released them all. Among the demonstrators was also a sixteen year old Jagannath Sigdel, who would a decade later become the editor/publisher of the first newspaper Himdåt of Pokhara. he was there to protest the arrest of his màmà (maternal uncle) Shri Kant Adhikari. Adhikari was a teacher at the Basic school that Mukti Nath Timisina had established and was arrested from the school itself. Third Day: When the second day’s demonstration too went well, they decided to take out a huge demonstration by mobilising more people. Preparations were afoot to make a big show. The shopkeepers donated clothes and the tailors worked overnight and prepared party flags in large numbers. People flocked in great numbers—around five hundred flags that they had prepared were all gone. But there was another alternative, làlupàte—a flowering plant with long stem and red leafy flower—that those without flags could carry. And they were chanting slogans, which most had heard for the first time—Ranasahi Murdabad (down with Ranaarchy), Nepali Congress Jindàbàd (long live NC), Inquilab Jindàbàd (long live/hail to revolution). Inquilab, Jindàbàd, Murdàbàd were all Urdu words so not many understood the actual meaning, but perhaps that did not matter much for they knew that they were protesting against the Rana regime. The first thing the demonstrators did on that day was to take control of the telephone office, which was just a few hundred meters away. It was not difficult at all, for the chief of the office had already sneaked out sensing the situation. Afterwards, the demonstrators moved towards the (militia) barrack which was also nearby. The officer at the barrack did try to stop them for a while but gave up after some time without much fuss. Parajuli hoisted the party flag there, and released the three political prisoners, namely, Shri Kant Adhikari, Shri Prasad Ghimire (another prominent political figure of the area) and Khadananda Sharma. They then proceeded towards Nalakomukh where three other major offices—the post office, court and jail—were located. On the way, the number of demonstrators swelled to a great extent. They easily took control of these offices as there was no significant resistance. Now only two but very important offices were left. One was the general administration office (goswara) or badahakim office, and the other was land revenue office. Besides, the major obstacle was the army contingent stationed at Bindhyabasini temple premises with more than a hundred army personnel. This contingent was sent from Kathmandu a few months after the infamous fire to quell any possible insurrection. By the time the jubilant crowd reached the governor’s residence cum office it was becoming dark, and cold, as it was winter. The establishment had the arms but the crowd was too big to be fired upon. The “rebels” kept on chanting slogans and asked the authorities to give up, but they did not budge. When it became dark, only the core group of fifty-sixty people remained outside the governor’s office whereas others were sent back home. The authorities’ plan to arrest the group in the wee hours was leaked and the rebels sent words and called back the people, thus foiling the plan. Fourth Day: It was not a surprise that the next day people flocked in even greater numbers given the previous day’s victory. When the crowd swelled, the rebels pressed the governor to surrender but he was unrelenting. In the afternoon a few demonstrators forcibly entered the governor’s residence and took him out; there was not much of a resistance. The governor was forced to tender his resignation, and to chant the same slogans that the agitators were chanting. The governor wept, pledged loyalty to the Congress and chanted “Nepali Congress Jindàbàd.” After taking controlof the office, the activists turned their attention to the land revenue office which was at the temple premises, where the army contingent was also stationed. Here also the activists succeeded in pursuing the army to give up. By the evening the Congress activists had total control over Pokhara—all the offices and arms were locked and the keys were in the rebels’ hand. Counter-Revolution: But the victory or the “revolution” as the local actors fondly called it, lasted less than 24 hours. Even before they could organize the victory rally, a “counter-revolution” occurred. The next day some Chhetris from the suburbs, and the army of the erstwhile government under the aegis of the Rana lieutenants attacked the NC activists who were busy making preparations for the victory rally. Though none died, they got a severe beating. The old regime again took control of the town and the treasury Most of the able-bodied men who participated in the demonstrations fled, and the “reactionaries” created mayhem in the town. Support From Syangja And Palpa: The main actors regrouped in the southern part of the city and from there they went to the neighbouring district Syangja, which was already under the control of the “revolutionaries.” With the help of the “liberation army” of Syangja and of Palpa, the NC activists encircled Pokhara and asked the people not to recognize the old regime. Many of the local people came forward in helping the army contingent by providing food and logistics, some however sided with the old regime. This “counter revolution” thus led to a polarization between the groups which supported the old regime, and which backed the progressive forces or the rebels. And because of the participation of dalits, women and others in the movement, the traditional caste-ethnic boundaries were also weakened to an extent, for the movement brought them together in a single platform. This became more evident in the immediate post-Rana period, during which we observed somewhat conscious efforts to break the traditional hierarchical caste boundaries. In the meantime a compromise was reached between the Rana rulers and the king in exile, orchestrated by the India government, and later the NC leadership too was coaxed to call off the armed struggle. Ceasefire: The news and the order for ceasefire also reached Pokhara. A sort of compromise was also reached locally thus ending the stand-off. Even after the formation of a coalition government in Kathmandu, Dhan Shamsher Rana remained the governor of the region for some time. However, his authority had largely deteriorated. Since there existed a parallel sort of government, the badahakim or the authorities were no more feared as in the past. In fact, the governor became an object of fun and mockery, for the people got to see his vulnerability, his helplessness, and his moist eyes at the time of the rebels’ takeover. This coming of world upside down brought a sea-change in the peoples’ worldview and attitude, as would become clear during the post-Rana years. Pokhreli NC Leaders Post Revolution: Active NC leaders like Prem Raj Mulmi withdrew from political life after the 1960 imposition of Panchayat. Other prominenet leaders like Pandit Muktinath Timisina and Shrikant Adhikari published an article in Himdoot newspaper supporting the coup.

events.title: Annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China
events.detail: After the fall of Qing Dynasty Tibet operated as an independent nation with its own government currency and army for nearly 40 years. However Tibet failed to secure formal international recognition or UN membership leaving its legal status weak. In 1949 when the Chinese Communist Party won the civil war Mao vowed to reclaim all historical Qing territories. In October 1950 Mao's People's Liberation Army (PLA) attacked from eastern Tibetan region of Kham. They secured rich natural resources established a military buffer zone along the Indian border and restored historical borders claimed by the former Qing Dynasty. In 1951 facing 40000 Chinese troops within its borders the Tibetan government—led by a 15-year-old Dalai Lama—was forced to negotiate. He was forced to sign the Seventeen Point Agreement which officially yielded Tibetan sovereignty to China in exchange for religious and political freedom. Violating the terms of agreement Beijing enforced aggressive communist land reforms and suppressed religious practices in eastern Tibetan provinces. On March 10 1959 fears that Chinese forces intended to kidnap the Dalai Lama triggered a massive ⁠uprising in Lhasa. The PLA crushed the protests with heavy artillery shelling the Dalai Lama's summer palace and killing thousands of protesters. The Dalai Lama fled across the Himalayas into India where he established the ⁠Central Tibetan Administration. Newly independent India and a withdrawing Britain refused to intervene leaving Tibet geopolitically isolated against a powerful Chinese military.

events.title: King Tribhuvan Takes Asylum of India
events.detail: The was Nepali Congress planned to seize King Tribhuvan during Indra Jatra and take him to Palpa where they would set up a parallel government. But unfortunately the somebody leaked the plan and on 24 September 1950 a group of armed Nepali Congress volunteers and several serving army officers were arrested. Under interrogation the detainees implicated King Tribhuvan in the planned coup. King faced an immediate threat to his life and freedom after the Ranas discovered his secret alliance with anti-Rana revolutionaries. So one day he took approval from Rana to take his family on a picnic. When the motorcade of his family left the palace it entered the Indian Embassy on the way. Rana immediately called the Bhardari Sabha and declared Birendra as King insted of Mahendra. However when emissaries were sent to Embassy King rejecetd their decisions and said that he has no intention of abdicating and Birendra wouldn't go to palace. Within hours the Bhardari Sabha deposed King Tribhuvan and declared his four-year-old grandson Gyanendra as the new King whom they found in the royal palace. On 10 November two Indian planes landed at Gauchar Airport (now called Tribhuvan International Airport) and the royal family fled to New Delhi excluding the infant King Gyanendra. Tribhuvan was formally welcomed by Indian prime minister Jawahar Lal Nehru and other high officials.

events.title: The Armed Revolution
events.detail: King's move put all revolutionaries in a state of hurry. Nepali Congress did not want to miss the momentous opportunity and decided to take immediate action. Party president MP Koirala BP Koirala and Subarna Shamsher (the Supreme Command Council) immediately flew to Purnea a border town of Bihar. Commanders posted at different points inside Nepal were immediately called there and ordered to prepare for armed strikes at the same zero hour throughout selected posts of the country like Birgunj Bhairahawa Biratnagar Ilam and other points. Central Front (Birgunj): It was commanded by Thirbam Malla and Purna Singh Khawas. When Birgunj surrendered to the revolutionary forces the first people’s ‘provisional government’ was declared. The forces successfully captured the treasury with fifty lakhs rupees silver coins 250 rifles and ammunitions. However Thirbam Malla died in the operation. The captured money drew the attention of all as to how to preserve it. Despite an acute shortage of resources they tried to hand the funds over to the exiled King in Delhi. However the revolutionaries were arrested at the Safdarjung airport in Delhi by Indian authorities who confiscated the cash (though it was later returned to the government of Nepal after the political change). Eastern Front (Biratnagar Udayapur Bhojpur): In the east BP Koirala led the Biratnagar operation alongside Keshav Koirala Girija Prasad Koirala and GB Yakthumba. After fierce fighting by turnning tractor to tank to break down wall of the Governor's residence the Rana governor surrendered. During the capture the governor’s son was killed while trying to escape with valuables. BP intervened to protect the surrendered governor and his family even stopping Yakthumba from attacking him. The incident highlighted both the dangers of wartime excesses and the leadership’s efforts to maintain discipline and prevent abuses of power. Krishna Prasad Bhatatrai commanded forces in Udayapur. His contribution was more organizational and political than military compared to figures like BP or K.I. Singh. Narad Muni Thulung commanded Bhojpur front. Western Front (Nepalgunj Dang Pyuthan Palpa): K.I. Singh led the western front. His forces achieved several successes in western Nepal but communication with the Congress high command was poor and discipline was weaker. General Rudra Shumsher's Defection: Rudra Shumsher who was stripped off from the role of succession and sent to Palpa as Western Commander of Palpa refused to strongly suppress rising pro-revolution sentiment in his area. He withdrew effective resistance instead of launching full military action against insurgents and took away well-armed garrison of Rana government. It came as a final blow to the regime which forced them to come in compromise for the Delhi Agreement.

events.title: Socio-Economic Indicators 1951
events.detail: Literacy at 2%; less than 5000 children in school; 200 doctors; 300 had college degree; 1000 were high school graduates; 321 primary schools 11 secondary and 2 higher secondary; less than 1% engaged in modern industrial occupations; 85% of all employment and income based on traditional agriculture; per capital income $45; total length of metalled road reached 376 km.

events.title: Public Works Department Established
events.detail: A new department was established to carry out varous public constructin works including road construction. Kul Ratna Tuladhar was the first chief engineer of Nepal's Public Works Department where he served since its establishment in 1951 till 1957. Under his tenure Tribhuvan Highway Kanti Highway and Hetauda-Narayanghat roads were constructed. Later in 1961 Department of Roads was establsihed to carry out road construction works.

events.title: Nepal Terai Congress Formed
events.detail: On 27th August 1951, Mahottari President of the Nepali Congress Rama Kanta Jha, Munsi Daya Shankar Gupta of Taulihawa, and Raghunath Prasad Gupta, who was a journalist living in Kathmandu at the time, met the then Home Minister BP Koirala and submitted a letter of appeal to end the discrimination against the Madhesis, reminding them that democracy had come to the country. However, Koirala only assured that the country was in an unstable state due to the recent political changes and that all discrimination would gradually end. He could not convince them to implement the letter of appeal. Soon after, the Terai Congress Party was established on the initiative of Gupta. Baldev Das Yadav, Jha and others became members of the party headed by Kulananda Jha. The party was reportedly founded in 1951 at Kalyanpur in present-day Siraha, with Kulananda Jha as founding president. Vedananda Jha, then a journalist in Patna and brother of Kulananda Jha, was subsequently brought in because of his education and intellectual reputation and became its president. After that, Mahottari President of the Nepali Congress Mahendra Narayan Nidhi met the then party president and Prime Minister Matrika Prasad Koirala and submitted a 14-point written letter of appeal to end the discrimination against the Madhesis and guarantee jobs according to qualifications. That too was not listened to. When Nepal National Education Plannning Commission report was published recommending Nepali to be only recognizied langugae and medium of education to be only Nepali, Terai Congress led the Hindi Bachao Andolan. The Tarai Congress also demanded that the government create two provinces in Madhesh and similar provinces in hills as needed. In 1959, when the first parliamentary elections were held in Nepal, the Tarai Congress fielded 21 candidates. None of them won the election, but four came as close rivals. Unfortunately, less than two years later, the king staged a 'coup' and imposed the Panchayat system, and the Tarai Congress faded away. In 1961, the Madhesh Mukti Morcha was formed in Taulihawa. The president of the morcha, Raghunath Raya, vice-president Ramji Mishra, and secretary Satyadev Tripathi were shot dead by the regime. The morcha itself disappeared with that incident. Vedananda Jha was also arrested after the royal coup. However, he was released from jail within a few months and entered the panchayat later becoming ambassador to India. A party meeting of Terai Congress held in the border town of Raxaul under the leadership of the then general secretary, Ramjanam Tiwari. In 1961, at the call of Subarna Shamsher, Terai Congress merged with NC and joined the struggle to restore democracy. The leaders of Terai Congress who joined NC at that time were believed to be ignored by the NC establishment after a few years. Around 1975, Gajendra Narayan Singh, along with the same group of leaders, formed a Madhesi faction within the Congress, which later (around 1985) emerged under the name of the Sadbhavana Parishad, giving a new path to Madhesi politics.

events.title: Four Point General Agreement for Technical Cooperation with US
events.detail: President Truman through his second inaugural address of January 20 1949 announced and listed four major themes that would guide American foreign policy in the post-war period. U.S. government was to provide support to underdeveloped countries so that these countries would be able to protect themselves from the expansion of communism. The treaty came as a need for Ranas to get the assistance to save his sinking boat while for Truman Nepal became most suitable country to watch developments in China. Hence the first economic cooperation started which provided lump sum of $ 300000. USOM Office (later USAID) was etablished at Rabi Bhavan. The first priority was in areas of agriculture Village Development Program in 10 districts health and education; later on capital assistance projects focusing on industrial development transportation and communication. United States became the first country to formally establish an economic assistance program in the country.

events.title: Tripartite Delhi Agreement
events.detail: Mohan's son Vijaya Shumsher and Keshar Shumsher the Foreign and defence ministers respectively travelled to New Delhi on 27th November to discuss the succession issue with India. Ranas were ready to accept political reforms of limited extent but not the re-recognition of King Tribhuvan. However India proposed election of constituenct assembly to draft new constitution formation of joint inetrim government of Rana and Nepali Congress and recognition of King Tribhuvan. Ranas were deeply divided on the proposal but due to Nepali Congress's increasing control over major cities and Rudra Shumsher's defection they had no other options but accept the terms. On 8 January Mohan Shumsher announced that King Tribhuvan would be restored and cabinet with popular representation would be formed. Negotiations started between three parties: Congress King and Ranas in New Delhi. Nepali Congress leaders were only invited to New Delhi in time to ratify the Indian proposals after these had been accepted by the Rana regime. Thus Nepali Congress viewed the coalition as a temporary truce and accepted it with the intention of fighting the Ranas from within government. A compromise was reached to form a 10-membered cabinet equally divided between Ranas and Nepali Congress with Mohan Shumsher as PM. On 15th February King and Nepali Congress leaders flew back to kathmandu with a grand public welcome. On 18th February King issued a lal mohar revoking all heriditary powers and privileges that was bistowed upon the Rana family.

events.title: School Library and Cultural Boom
events.detail: The overthrow of Rana autocracy encouragement for education by sections of the new ruling elite (ex-Ranas) and initiatives by educated youths—many of whom had studied in India—created a favorable environment for rapid educational expansion after 1950. Despite the country lacking educational infrastructure trained teachers administrative systems and financial resources local communities—especially in urban areas and the Terai—began establishing schools through their own initiatives. These schools relied heavily on community resources and often charged tuition fees which meant they largely catered to relatively better-off social groups. To regulate this rapid growth the government gradually established educational institutions during the mid-1950s including the Ministry of Education Board of Education school inspection system and Nepal National Education Planning Commission (NNEPC). Following NNEPC recommendations school administration was largely decentralized. Communities were entrusted with responsibilities such as establishing schools selecting teachers raising funds approving courses and managing school administration through school management committees composed of parents and local leaders. This reflected the growing belief that education was closely linked with community development. Libraries and cultural organizations also expanded rapidly during this period. Community libraries reading rooms literary circles and youth organizations became important centers for education public discussion and cultural activities. Nepal Sanskritik Parishad (NSP): It was a cultural organization launched in 1951 by Bal Chandra Sharma and Kedar Man Vyathit. It was chaired by BP Koirala and funded by Kaiser Shumsher. The NSP organized seminars awarded fellowships published critically edited texts and released Nepal's first social science journal called the NSP Patrika in April 1952 under editorship of Iswar Baral. The organization died with death of Kaiser Shumsher in 1964. Nepal Sanskritik Sangh: Founded in February 1951 by Shailendra Nath Rimal and youths from Dillibazar area. Its earlier activity was running library organizing sports and publishing. Its one of the early publication Bhimshen Thapa and Tatkalin Nepal by Chittaranjan Nepali won the first Madan Puraskar in social science/philosophy category. It was financially supported by Babar Kaiser and Mohan Shumsher. The organization is still alive though less prominent with a building in Kalikasthan Dillibazar. Madan Purashkar Guthi: Registered in December 1955 by financial support of Madan Shumsher's (Chandra Shumsher's son) widow Rani Jagadamba and management of Dixit family. It initially honored Nepali books for four disciplines of prose poetry social science/philosophy and science. Starting mid-1970s the Guthi decided to honor only one book per year and by late 1980s it started awarding Jagadamba-Shree award for organizations or individuals for their contribution in Nepali language.

events.title: Mohan Shumsher's Interim Government
events.detail: Rana Side (5 Ministers) Mohan Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana – Prime Minister and Foreign Affairs Babar Shamsher Jung Bahadur Rana – Defence Chudraj Shamsher – Forests Nripa Janga Rana – Education (C-Class Rana predisosed to NC) Yagya Bahadur Basnyat – Health and Local Self-Government (C-Class Rana predisosed to NC) Nepali Congress Side (5 Ministers) Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala – Home Affairs Subarna Shamsher Rana – Finance Ganesh Man Singh – Commerce and Industry Bharatmani Sharma – Food and Agriculture (Party-newcomer from Dang) Bhadrakali Mishra – Transport (Result of "poiliticking" at New Delhi. Joined party only after becoming Minister. Gandhian spent time in Gandhi's Ashram. Likely recommended by CPN Sinha the then ambassador to Nepal)

events.title: NC's Secreterait Reform
events.detail: Only after NC came to coliation government government ministries like Home, Finance, etc. were established. BP setup the Ministry, appointed a Home Secretary, who was Nepal's first MA in Philosophy. At that time, the most powerful ministry became the Ministry of Home Affairs. Because this ministry handled all the work of the judiciary and personnel administration. He even brought 2-3 experts from India to modernize the secreteriats of newly formed NC-led ministries. The Ranas brought in military officers as secretaries, while the Congress appointed university professors. At that time, young people like Bhavanath Sharma, Pradyumnalal Rajbhandari, Kulnath Lohani were brought in from the professorships. Rana-era employees remained in the lower ranks. That is why in the administrative field at that time, it was said that 'young general, old soldier'.

events.title: Nepal's First Budget is Published
events.detail: by Finance Minister Subarna Shamsher of Rs. 5 Crore 2 Lakhs and 50 Thousand

events.title: St. Xavier’s and St. Mary’s Schools Established
events.detail: Jesuit missionary Fr. Marshall Moran of Patna visited Nepal in October 1949, and while he was in Kathmandu, the possibility of a Jesuit school in Nepal had been discussed. In November 1950, General Mrigendra Shamsher Rana, the Director of Public Education in Nepal, visited Patna to inform Fr. Moran that the Government of Nepal was interested in a school to be run by the Jesuits at Godavari. Later on recieving approval from the Provincial of Chicago, school was established in Godavari. On July 1, 1951 the first batch of 65 students were admitted into the school at St. Xavier’s Godavari. As a result of the steady growth of the number of students, the Primary Section was shifted to Jawalakhel on September 1954. The purpose was to have the primary section at Jawalakhel and the high school section at Godavari. In the years to come many more changes were adopted to satisfy the growing demands of admissions into the Jesuit school. Eventually St. Xavier’s Jawalakhel became a full-fledged high school and St. Xavier’s Godavari became fully a primary boarding school that accommodated the strength of 280 boarders in the course of time. In 1996 the leadership made strategic reform of admitting girls to promote gender equality, upgrading Godavari back into a full high school, and phasing out the hostel completely by 2002 to transition fully into a local day school. Likewise, Nepal Government, through Fr. Marshall Moran, invited the Sisters of the Institute of the Blessed Virgin Mary (IBMV) in Patna to open a school in Lalitpur. The invitation was graciously accepted, and thus the first St. Mary’s School was opened in Jawalakhel in 1955. Today, there are 5 primary St. Xavier’s schools and 4 primary St. Mary’s schools operating across Nepal. St. Mary's School, Pokhara was established in 1983.

events.title: Nepal Police Headquarter Established
events.detail: Previously the Rana Commander-In-Chief was responsible for the internal law and order in the country. It didn't even have any secretary or police. Police Headquarters was established in 1952 in Kathmandu. Toran Shumsher J.B. Rana was appointed the first Inspector General of Police. NC's pro-democratic paramilitary force, Rakshya Dal was directly appointed into the Nepal Police which was about 6,000 in number but were without any weapons. When there was about to be clash between police and the Gorkha Dal led by Bharat Shumsher, BP appointed some of the Gorkha Dal people into nepal police. BP also requested 1000 guns from Nepal Army to the PM and was granted with big difficulty. In 1955 The Police Act, 2012 BS came into effect legally establishing the institution.

events.title: Radio Nepal Established
events.detail: During the armed sgtruggle of Nepali congress in 1950, Tarini Prasad Koirala established Prajatantra Nepal Radio in Biratnagar to broadcast their activities as well as other information which encouraged the general people to support their movement against the Rana rulers. Tarini Prasad Koirala and Phanishwar Nath Renu were its first two newsreaders. Tarini read the news in Nepali and Phanishwar in Hindi. Ranu Devi Adhikari used to sing revolutionary songs written by Tarini Prasad Koirala. Following the revolution's success, the new democratic government recognized the strategic value of radio. The transmitter was packed up, brought to the capital's palace complex inside Singha Durbar, and officially converted into Radio Nepal on April 2, 1951 chaired by Tarini Prasad Koirala. Ranu Devi went on to become the first female singer of Radio Nepal singing revolutionary songs like Nepali Nepali and Aaja Deshko Kranti.

events.title: Bir Gorkha Dal Revolt
events.detail: It was underground organization formed under green signal of Baber Shumsher and lead by Nati-Jarnel Bharat Shamsher and Randhir Subba to subvert army and overthrow the gorvenment. A heated discussion took place between Baber and NC leaders in the parliament regarding the organization. Since Baber Shumsher refused to obstruct the political activities of his family BP Koirala ordered the arrest of several members of Gorkha Dal including Bharat Shunsher. The next day Gorkha Dal mambers raided the jail and released Bharat Shumsher and then proceeded to attack BP's residence. After his private secretary was wounded BP had to fire a gun and kill his nearest assailant. It has seruous consequences for Ranas. On April 14 King took over the title of Supreme Commander-in-Chief and Gorkha Dal was declared illegal. This also gave Congress excuse to retain the paramilitary police force Rakshya Dal which BP created as the Home Minister. Congress demanded removal of Baber Shumsher and demanded the crisis be resolved in Nepal itself under mediation of King but Mohan Shumsher insisted it to be done by Delhi. An agreement was reached in Delhi that cabinet be resuffeled and an Advisory Assembly be formed to function as little parliament. A new cabinet was formed in June 10 where Baber Shumsher was replaced by Singha Shumsher and Bharat Mani Sharma was replced by Surya Prasad Upadhaya. Mohan Shumsher assumed both Defence and Foreign ministry. On October 2 the Advisory Assembly was announced by the King which had no Rana representation.

events.title: Nepal Interim Government Act 1951
events.detail: Strengthened king introduced Supreme Court and insured fundamental rights like equal protection of the laws to all citizens freedom of speech and expression freedom of assembly without arms freedom to form associations and freedom to move to or reside in any part of the country. Religious freedom was also guaranteed.

events.title: Industrial Regulation Act 1951: Start of industrial licensing.
Public Service Commission Founded
events.detail: The Public Service Comission of Nepal was established on June 15, 1951 under the leadership of its first chairman, Sardar Nagendra Man Singh Pradhan. It was created to replace nepotism and personal favoritism with a fair system of open competitive exams for government jobs. As BP Koirala came to Home Ministry he was responsible for internal governance and restructuring the law-and-order system. To strip away the old Rana tradition of hand-picking loyalists for government jobs, he spearheaded the establishment of Public Service Comission. Koirala strongly advocated for institutionalizing a rule-based, competitive examination system to replace favoritism. His administration invited the Indian Administrative Reorganization Committee (the Butch Commission) to help design a professional, neutral civil service structure for a democratic Nepal. It led to the inaction of The Civil Service Act (1956) which formally institutionalized a professional, neutral, and stable civil service. However, this institution was not effective during the interim period at that time. If there were gazetted posts, the cabinet was given the right to recruit, and if there were others, the secretary or director. Only technical posts like teachers, doctors, engineers and second-class administrative posts were sent to the commission. Although there was a legal provision to send them to the Public Service Commission, they started recruiting in a hurry, saying that it would be done as agreed upon in the reorganization later. Promotions also started to be done in the same way. The Council of Ministers and Royal Advisory Committees formed up to 2015 BS seem to have been competing to get their people into government service. The post of Badahakim was separated from the civil service by the Royal Advisory Committee. 16 Badahakims were dismissed and new appointments were made by the Shah and the Ranas. The elected government of 2016 began the work of administrative reorganization. But the Public Service Commission objected to it in its first report, saying that nepotism and favoritism were prevalent. After that, an agreement was reached between the Prime Minister and the Commission Chairman and the examination began. Only after this was the Commission able to become functional. After King Mahendra Shah took power in a military coup, overthrowing the elected government, he carried out extensive civil service reforms. He issued the 'Public Service Commission Restriction Rules-2017' to recruit and hire according to his own preferences. He suspended the Public Service Commission from 25 Poush 2017 to mid-2018.

events.title: Nehru Visited Nepal
events.detail: Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru made an official three-day state visit to Nepal. He was officially welcomed by King Tribhuvan and held discussions with Rana and Nepali Congress leaders. He visited the sacred Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu alongside his daughter Indira Gandhi.

events.title: Fall of Coliation Government
events.detail: On November 6 police fired on a pocession of student killing one. Mohan Shumsher expressed sympathy and indicated that he would conduct impartial inquiry. BP interpretated this as a refusal of collective responsibility. On November 10 the first anniversary of coaliation BP spoke over Radio Nepal citing the coliation unnatural and demanded homogeneous Cabinet dissolving current one. The Congress bloc resigned from the government the same day. The People's Front consisting of Dilli Raman Regmi's Nepali Rastriya Congress Tanka Prasad Acharya's Praja Parishad and the Communist Party of Nepal demanded all-party government. Despite BP having popular support among party members King Tribhuvan insisted on making Matrika Prasad Koirala the PM. Party reluctantly agreed to it and gave name of eight NC members and six independent for the cabinet.

events.title: Matrika Prasad Koirala (1st Term)
events.detail: MP Koirala was backed by Indian support and even some ministers were chosen for Indian interest. Nepali Congress Side (8 Ministers) Matrika Prasad Koirala – Prime Minister Foreign Affairs and General Administration (First commoner PM). Surya Prasad Upadhyaya – Home and Food (A key intellectual strategist of the party close to Indian leadership). Bhadrakali Mishra – Transport (Retained from the Interim Government; continued to represent the Madhesh region's political leverage). Ganesh Man Singh – Agriculture and Land Management (Shifted from Industry/Commerce represented Newar community). Subarna Shamsher Rana – Finance (Retained his portfolio). Mahabir Shumsher Rana – Planning and Development Mines Forests and Electricity. Narad Muni Thulung – Minister for Local Autonomous Administration (Represented Limbu community). Mahendra Bikram Shah – Industry Commerce and Civil Supplies Independent (6 Ministers) Kaiser Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana – Defence (Former Rana elite retained to placate the royal army and prevent a military coup). Sarda Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana – Education (Appointed to keep traditional aristocratic oversight over the country's developing school system). Nar Bahadur Gurung – Health (Representing Gurung community ek Gurkha). Bhagawati Prasad Singh – Law and Justice (Represented Madhesh community). Khadga Man Singh – Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dharma Ratna Yami – Forests (Represented Saivite and Buddhistic sections).

events.title: Dispute Between BP and MPK
events.detail: MP Koirala had no strict ideological alliance he was more sort of appeaser pragmatic and accomodative. He din't want to stand against the feudal lords and wanted just to restrict his activities to regular administration. BP saw this transition phase to be time for basic social and economic chnages. However MP Koirala kept appointing Rana loyalists in the administrative position much to dislike of BP's faction. The government also doubled the size of King's privy purse. Disturbed with all these on February 1952 BP announched his intention to contend for party president against Matrika arguing same person shouldn't hold two positions. He also called for CPN Sinha's replacement calling his out for trying to balance one leader over another. He also called the ban on Communist Party as unwise and appealed for vital economic policy to prevent Chinese from taking advantage of Nepal with the help of KI Singh. Both borthers were called to Calcutta by Jay Prakash Narayan and an agreement was reached that BP will become the party president and the government would broadly function in party's agenda.

events.title: Inequality of Land Ownership
events.detail: Data on land ownership before 1952 shows Raikar 50% Birta 36.3% Kipat 4% Guthi 2% Rajya Rakam Jagir etc. 7.7%; Gini coefficient for this land distribution in 1952 is 0.56 compared to 0.57 today. Though per household average plot holding declined from approx 1.35 hectares in 1952 to only 0.19 hectares in 2020/21 mostly due to land ceiling and generational division; the persistent inequlaity in land holding comes largely from landless of 26.1% of households
sources: Land Reform in Nepal:A Study of Subsistence Holding and Land Redistribution -Bhumi N. Shrestha*

events.title: Establishment of Police Headquarter
events.detail: Mr. Toran Shamsher J.B. Rana was appointed the first Inspector General of Police. The Police Act 2012 BS (1955 AD) came into effect. The Police Regulation 2015 BS (1959 AD) came into effect.

events.title: Raksha Dal Revolt
events.detail: Nepali Congress's Muktisena led by KI Singh was dissatisfied with Delhi Accord. Therefore he kept launching attacks with his men. Though he was asked to stop the fighting he refused. He launched another unsuccessful attack with 300-500 men on Bhairawa but was soon arrested in February 1951 by Indian and Nepali troops. On the night of 21 January 1952 a segment of the Rakshya Dal who were disatisfied elements ranging from Ranas and political malcontents staged revolt in Kathmandu seizing Singha Durbar and key government offices such as secreteriats prisons radio stations telephone offices etc. Among those released was KI Singh and his associates who were under detention. The rebels acclaimed KI Singh as their leader. On Januray 22 the state army and King's personal bodyguards recaptured most of the building while KI Singh fled to Tibet and eventually Peking. King announced a ban on Rastriya Mahasabha and Communist Party of Nepal for their alleged involvement.

events.title: Indian Military Checkposts in Nepal
events.detail: After the Raksha Dal revolt Nepal realized how vulnerable was its state mechanism and it invited an Indian military mission to Nepal to reorganize the state army along modern lines. Though mission was set to stay for one year it only left in 1958 after staying for six years. Nepal completely lacked the technology and manpower to monitor its own 1400-kilometer Himalayan border with China which had become important for both Nepal and India after Tibet annexation. In later 1952 King Tribhuvan and PM MPK formally permitted the Indian Military Mission to take over strategic border security. India provided the advanced wireless radio technology signaling equipment and trained intelligence officers. Nepal provided local guides and a small contingent of Nepali soldiers to co-staff each post. In total 17 administrative checkposts were setup at that time.

events.title: Nepal Citizenship Act 2009
events.detail: It was the first citizenship act of Nepal. Citizenship by Descent: Granted to individuals whose fathers were citizens of Nepal at the time of the child's birth. Citizenship by Birth: Automatically granted to anyone born within the territory of Nepal. Naturalized Citizenship: Given to any foreign woman married to a male Nepali citizen; to any foreign national living in nepal for at least 5 years.

events.title: Pradhan Nyayalaya Act 2008 Inacted
events.detail: When BP Koirala came to Home MInistry, it oversaw the judicial system of the country. Under his political leadership and recommendations, the blueprint to reform the older Pradhan Nyayalaya structure (originally set up by Juddha Shumsher in 1997 BS) into a truly independent entity began. As the crucial effort to it Pradhan Nyayalaya Act 2008 was prepared in his tenure which formally received the Royal Seal (Lalmohar) on Baisakh 26, 2009 BS (May 8, 1952 CE). It is why Baisakh 26 is celebrated every year as Law Day (Kanoon Diwas) in Nepal. The Act formally introduced the writ system (empowering the court to issue orders like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari) and the precedent system into Nepalese jurisprudence. The Act also provided clear statutory footing and jurisdiction to the apex judicial body, helping separate judicial functions from absolute executive/royal control. Bisheshwor Prasad Koirala v. Kathmandu Commissioner Magistrate: In early 1950s B.P. Koirala had written a personal letter to a friend Dr. Bhawani Bhakta discussing the democratic reforms his party, the Nepali Congress, wanted to establish. The letter was intercepted and handed over to the Kathmandu Magistrate's office. The local administration, still deeply entrenched in old, authoritarian ways, felt politically threatened by the rising democratic consciousness and the public awareness Koirala was generating. To silence him, the Kathmandu Magistrate used a set of old administrative rules called the Kathmandu Valley Commissioners' and Magistrate Sawal, 2009 BS. They issued a restrictive order against Koirala, treating his democratic advocacy as a public safety threat. Koirala challenged this restriction by appealing directly to the newly structured apex court, the Pradhan Nyayalaya. He argued that this order violated Section 30 of the Supreme Court Act which empowered the apex court with Writ Jurisdiction and the power of Judicial Review and the fundamental freedoms of speech and expression guaranteed under the Interim Constitution of Nepal, 2007 BS. The court scrutinized Section 1(sa) of the Magistrate’s Sawal (rules) and explicitly declared it null, void, and unconstitutional. The bench famously stated: "It is the duty of the Supreme Court to declare any act contrary to the constitutional provision as unconstitutional." This was the first time in Nepal's history that a court used the power of judicial review. It drew a sharp line in the sand between the Executive (the Magistrates and government) and the Judiciary. It proved that the courts were no longer a rubber stamp for rulers, but an independent protector of the people. B.P. Koirala had champion-drafted the Pradhan Nyayalaya Act while in office to create an independent judiciary. When he was subsequently targeted by the state after leaving office, that very exact law became the shield that saved his personal liberty.

events.title: NC Fifth General Convention
events.detail: BP Koirala; The party held its fifth general convention in Janakpurdham (First in Nepal). B.P. Koirala was elected as party president and Dhanman Singh Pariyar and Rajeshwar Prasad Upadhyaya were elected as general secretaries. Under the principle of "one person, one post" MPK himself proposed BP to be the party president. However, it was fiercely opposed by 10 to 15 people including Bhadrakali Mishra. The Jay Prakash Narayan's mediation between BP and MPK couldn't last long as Matrika started taking cabinet decisions without consulting ministers from BP's faction. The CWC of the party wrote PM to reshuffle the cabinet dropping the independent members and proposed cabinet with 7 members with five from NC and two from independent. MPK rejecetd the proposal. On recieving letter of MPK, CWC called its ministers to resign by July 22. Only three members Subarna Shumsher Ganeshman and Surya Prasad Upadhaya resigned while rest three sided with MPK. On July 24 MPK along with Narad Muni Thulung Mahabir Shumsher and Mahendra Bikram Shah resigned from the party CWC. Soon after Bhadrakali Mishra formed a new party Jana Congress. Blachandra Sharma, Kedarman Byathit and Bharatmani Shah formed Nepali Congress Left and Matrika himself founded Rastriya Praja Party on April 30 1953

events.title: Low-Grade Employees' Strike and Minimum Salary Set
events.detail: A Union of Low-Grade Government Employees was formed shortly after revolution mostly supported by the Communist Party. On March 2 1951 Home Minister BP Koirala ordered through Gazette asking governemnt employees not to participate in any form of party politics and union activities. But the protest continued to which government paid no serious attention. A year later on May 16 1952 the union presented ultimatum to start strike from June 1. Government ignored again and the strike started. On June 2 MPK-led Government notified all stricking employee of their dismissal. The president of that association was Keshar Bahadur Maskey and the secretary was Maheshwarman Chhonchu Shrestha. The strike, which lasted for seven days, became politicized after the cadres of the then Nepal Communist Party openly participated in the rally. The strike continued unless King intervened with Royal Proclamation on June 6 which announced revised pay scale beginning with a minimum salary of Rs. 30 per month. The association was banned and it's leaders' jobs were not retained. Maheshwarman then joined the Communist Party. This is where the politicization of bureaucracy is believed to have begun in Nepal.

events.title: Matrika Resigned as PM
events.detail: Once the three cabinet members resigned and the union protest deteriorated his position MPK also resigned from the post losing legitimacy of the party and people.

events.title: King Tribhuvan
events.detail: King decised to impose direct rule as temporary provision working with his six Royal Councilors. Keshar Shamsher -- Chief councilor (General Administration; Finance; Defence) (A-class Rana) Mahavir Shamsher -- Councilor (Home; Planning and Development) (Resigned from Congress few hour before becoming memeber of council) Surendra Bahadur Basnyat -- Councilor (Industry Commerce; Food and Civil Supplies) (Rana military oligarch) Manik Lal Rajbhandari -- Councilor (Public Works and Communication Law and Parliamentary Affairs; Health and Local Self-Government) (veteran Rana civil administrator) Khadga Man Singh -- Councilor (FOreign Affairs; Revenue and Forest) (Ex-prisoner for Prachanda Gorkha plot during Rana time) Sharada Shamsher -- Adviser (Edication) (A-class Rana)

events.title: Special Circumstances Power Act
events.detail: The Interim Government Act had no provision of Royal Councilors so King promulgated the new act which suspended all the clauses of previous Act. It vested all executive power in the King. It not only provided legal foundation for the Royal Councelors' regime but also marked the introduction of King's absolute authority in political affairs.

events.title: First Municipality Elections in Lalitpur, Bhaktapur, Biratnagar, and Birgunj
events.detail: Shortly after the elections in Kathmandu in 1947, elections were also held in Bhaktapur and Lalitpur municipalities. There were 10 elected members in Bhaktapur and 12 in Lailitpur. While 4-each were nominated. 2, 5, 7 and 8 of 10 wards of Lalitpur Municipality were elected unopposed. The elections were held in the remainign 6 wards of Lalitpur on Sep 13, 1952. In the election of the mayor here, 1 out of 19 members was absent and there were 3 candidates, and all three received 3 votes each. In the re-election, when only 2 candidates participated, Narendraman Joshi was elected as the mayor with 5 votes against 4 votes. Surendra Shamsher was elected unopposed as the deputy mayor. In the wards of Bhaktapur elections were held on Oct 11, 1952. Similarly, elections were also held in Biratnagar and Birgunj municipalities in 1953.

events.title: International Nepal Fellowship Founded
events.detail: Nepal Evangelistic Band was founded in 1943 by British physician and a missionary in India, Lily O'Hanlon, the NEB worked with ethnically Nepali converts in northern India during the 1940s. In 1952 O'Hanlon and her colleagues Hilda Steele were given permission to undertake medical work in Pokhara. On November 22, 1952, a team of eleven—six expatriate missionaries including O’Hanlon and Steele, along with five Nepali Christians such as David Mukhia and his wife Premi Mukhia—trekked from the India-Nepal border into the mountains to reach Pokhara. Initial operations began as a general clinic at Ramghat, with subsequent activities shifting to land owned by a Nepali Christian at Tundikhel, using temporary thatch-and-bamboo structures for staff quarters to address the area's pressing healthcare needs. In 1954, the team ordered pre-fabricated aluminium huts from India to have safer, more weather-proof buildings. Locals nicknamed the shiny metal huts “Shining Hospital”, a name which the mission officially adopted. The Hospital was western Nepal's first general medical facility. In 1955 the institution began addressing leprosy under the leadership of expatriate staff members Eileen Lodge and Betty Bailey. This early leprosy work marked a pivotal expansion, integrating specialized treatment into the hospital's general services. The NEB later changed its name to the International Nepal Fellowship (INF), and expand its work into a range of medical and social justice activities. By 1957, to better segregate and focus on leprosy care, INF opened Green Pastures Hospital as a dedicated leprosarium branching from Shining Hospital, providing a sanctuary for affected individuals with construction of foundational facilities completed by 1962. The facility transitioned in 1978 when the original Shining Hospital closed, giving way to the Shining Community Health Centre, which incorporated specialized services like nutrition wards and pharmacy support at the nearby Gandaki Zonal Hospital (later Western Regional Hospital). However, Green Pastures further developed with the completion of a 23-bed ward in 1963, incorporating outpatient services, an operating theatre, laboratory, and departments for physiotherapy and occupational therapy. By the 1980s, it underwent a reorientation toward comprehensive disability care. Its rehabilitation programs expanded to include spinal cord injury management and cerebral palsy support, building on the hospital's existing physiotherapy and occupational therapy departments established since 1963. These changes reflected a broader recognition that leprosy cases were declining due to effective treatments like multi-drug therapy introduced in 1982, allowing resources to be redirected toward emerging disability challenges. By the 1990s, it had become Nepal's only dedicated spinal cord injury facility outside Kathmandu, serving as a critical referral center for rehabilitation in Western Nepal. In subsequent decades, expansions continued with the 2015 establishment of an Ear Centre for hearing-related disabilities, the 2021 inauguration of a Palliative Care and Chronic Disease building, and the 2023 opening of the Eileen & Betty Centre, a dedicated leprosy ward honoring early leprosy pioneers Lodge and Bailey. Similarly, Shining Hospital, Surkhet was founded in 1977. It originally began its operations as a specialized leprosy clinic before expanding into a full hospital facility. Later another Shining Hospital was also opened in Nepalgunj.

events.title: Ramghat Church Established
events.detail: Nepal's first modern Protestant church, Ramghat Church (Nepal Christiya Ramghat Church), was established in 1952 in Pokhara. 1952 in Pokhara. It was founded by David Mukhia and his wife Premi, who were ethnic Nepali Christians returning from India along with the INF's Shining Hospital mission. They along with the help of the missionary team built a thatched and bamboo hut for a church in 1952. David Mukhia was born in Christian family in Darjeeling. His parents had immigrated to darjeeling from Ilam before he was born. He went to Duncan Hospital for nursing training in 1933. When Duncan hospital was closed, he joined the Nepal Evangelistic Band and came to Nepal along with the mission. He was forced to leave the country because of baptism in Nepalgunj (1958) and Tansen (1959). A second church was stabilized in Kathmandu called Putalisadak Church on 8th of April 1953 by two missionaries from South India, Mr. Athali and C.G. George. Likewise Gyaneswor Church was established in August 1957 by eleven members, including Rajendra Kumar Rongong and Robert Karthak who went to Bhaktapur later.

events.title: Nepal-UN Technical Assistance Agreement
events.detail: outlined terms of technical assistance provided by the UN to Nepal

events.title: Matrika Forms Rastriya Praja Party
events.detail: The conflict between Koirala brothers resulted in splitting of the party and formation of a new party by MPK's block. The convention held in Burgunj elected MPK as its president and Mahendra Vikram Shah as its general secretary.

events.title: Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary Summit Mt. Everest
events.detail: For three decades British reconnaissance had approached the mountain from North Face Tibet. That changed in 1950 when Nepal opened its borders to foreigners. A British-New Zealand reconnaissance led by Eric Shipton in 1951 they pioneered the southern route through the treacherous Khumbu Icefall and up the Lhotse Face. Recognizing the opportunity the Nepalese government granted the first Everest climbing permit via Nepal to Switzerland in 1952. The expedition was led by Edouard Wyss-Dunant and one of its member was Tenzing Norgay Sherpa. Raymond Lambert and Tenzing Norgay made a bold summit attempt. They pitched a tent at around 8400 meters—the highest camp ever established at that time.
