At approximately 8595 meters just 250 meters below the summit they were forced to turn back due to exhaustion dehydration inadequate oxygen and failing equipment. The Swiss made a second attempt in autumn 1952 the first serious post-monsoon Everest expedition. Battling brutal winter winds and extreme cold they reached 8100 meters before retreating. British team was given permit for year 1953 which recruited Tenzing Norgay in their team given his prior experience. Finally on the third attempt by Tenzing Norgay and Edmud Hillary Everest was summited in 1953.

events.title: Trekking and Hotel Boom of 1950s And 1960s
events.detail: The trekking boom of Nepal began in the 1950s establishing Nepal as an oriental Shangri-la of “spiritual awakenings”. Expeditions: Triggered by the country's opening to the outside world in 1951 it was sparked globally by the historic 1950 French expedition to Annapurna I and the 1953 conquest of Mount Everest turning the region into the premier destination for mountaineers. Boris Lissanevitch Colonel Jimmy Roberts and A.V. Jim Edwards are widely celebrated as the "Holy Trinity" of pioneers who single-handedly built commercialized and shaped the hospitality trekking and wildlife tourism landscapes of modern Nepal. Boris Lissanevitch: Leveraging personal connection with King Tribhuvan and King Mahendra he opened Royal Hotel inside Bahadur Bhawan in 1954. He convinced a King Mahendra in 1955 to grant the country's first official tourist visas to a group of cruise-ship travelers. He introduced European fine dining international spirits and Western sanitation standards to Kathmandu. Boris famously leveraged his deep aristocratic connections in India to partner with Thomas Cook & Sons in Calcutta. High-net-worth Westerners on luxury global cruise ships would dock in India. Thomas Cook would bundle them onto charter flights into Kathmandu and usher them to Royal Hotel. He is considered "Father of Tourism" in Nepal. By the mid-1960s the Nepalese royals realized that Boris a charismatic foreigner completely monopolized the country's wealthiest visitors and elite foreign dignitaries. Wanting to grab the market the royal family entered the market with The Hotel Soaltee (opened in 1966 by Prince Himalaya) and the Hotel Annapurna (opened in 1965 by Princess Helen Shah). By the late 1960s the royals aggressively squeezed him on lease terms eventually refusing to renew it forcing the Royal Hotel to shut its doors permanently in 1969. Historically the King relied on Boris to cater state dinners and house visiting royalty (like Queen Elizabeth II in 1961). Once the Soaltee and Annapurna opened all state-sponsored luxury prestige and foreign diplomatic banquets were immediately diverted to the new royal-owned hotels. In a fascinating twist of elite circles after the royals successfully ran Boris out of business and closed the Royal Hotel the Soaltee group realized they still desperately needed his culinary genius and star power to attract elite Westerners. They hired Boris to run the Ghar-e-Kabab (Nepal's first high-end Indian restaurant) inside the Soaltee effectively turning their former rival into an employee. Colonel Jimmy Roberts: He was a decorated British Army officer who joined the military in India so he could climb mountains. He made the historic first ascent of Mera Peak in 1953 followed by the first ascent of Putha Hiunchuli (23750 ft) in 1954. In 1957 he led the famous expedition that stopped just 150 feet below the summit of the sacred mountain Machhapuchhare (Fishtail) fulfilling the promise to the King of Nepal that no human would ever step on its absolute peak. Towards the end of 1958 he was appointed to the newly created post of Military Attaché at the British Embassy in Kathmandu. After retiring from his regular Army career in May 1962 he stayed in Nepal. he coined the term "trekking" and and legally registered ⁠the first commercial trekking agency called Mountain Travel Nepal in 1964. In 1970 Roberts managed the logistics for Chris Bonington’s historic expedition of Annapurna South Face. The massive global media coverage of this climb single-handedly put the Annapurna Circuit on the global map transforming Mountain Travel Nepal from a niche agency into a massive commercial success. Many elite mountaineering teams arriving with massive budgets relied on Jimmy Roberts' infrastructure to hire hundreds of local porters buy tons of local supplies and manage complex logistics. He mapped out iconic trails—including the classic route to Everest Base Camp and the Annapurna circuit—and revolutionized local employment by systematically hiring and training Sherpas as expert alpine mountain guides. He invented the entire commercial trekking industry. This pipeline poured huge amounts of foreign currency directly into the rural mountain economies long before commercial tea-houses existed. Furthermore he pioneered early "Leave No Trace" rules by strictly forcing his staff to carry kerosene and pack out all glass tin and plastic. He is considered "Father of Trekking" in Nepal. John Coapman & A.V. Jim Edwards: Coapman grew up as a "missionary kid" in late-colonial India. There he developed a deep passion for big-game hunting particularly tiger shooting. In August 1964 John Coapman signed a 15-year lease agreement with Nepal's Ministry of Forests to build a treetops tourist lodge in the Chitwan Forest. He opened the Tiger Top Lodge with his wealthy Texas investors Herb Klein and Toddy Lee Wynne. When wealthy tourists landed in Kathmandu and stayed at Boris’s Royal Hotel Coapman used that elite pipeline to pitch his wild jungle safaris funneling guests straight from Kathmandu down to Chitwan. The lodge faced severe financial strain in its early years leading to intense disagreements over profits expenses and ownership shares. Following the dispute in 1972 John Coapman left Nepal and on behalf of the original Texan owners Jim Edwards stepped in to manage the lodge. Over the years he transformed the business from a struggling hunting-style operation into a globally renowned pioneering model for responsible ecotourism and wildlife conservation. Elizabeth Hawley: Arriving in Kathmandu in 1959 as a journalist she became the ultimate gatekeeper of Himalayan mountaineering.She founded The Himalayan Database what became the definitive record of all expeditions in Nepal. She personally interviewed every single climbing team passing through Kathmandu validating summits and creating the elite intellectual infrastructure that supported the climbing boom. Further Expantion: Department of Toursim was established in 1957 and a Tourism Act was enacted in 1964. In 1960 Swiss pilots brought the Pilatus PC-6 Porter—a legendary Short Takeoff and Landing (STOL) aircraft—to Nepal. Wealthy older tourists who could not physically hike for weeks were loaded into these rugged Swiss aircraft at Kathmandu. They were flown on custom high-priced "mountain flights" to see Everest from the air or dropped directly onto remote dirt strips near the base of the mountains. This single aviation pipeline allowed high-paying luxury travelers to experience the deep Himalayas in a single afternoon. In 1964 Lukla Airport (Tenzing-Hillary Airport) under the supervision of Sir Edmund Hillary. Hillary originally bought the land from local Sherpas for $2650 and had them trample the dirt runway to compact it. In 1966 Royal Nepal Airlies was founded. In 1968 Nepal's first cashino was opened in Soaltee Hotel. The 1960s became the "Golden Age" of elite ultra-high-end aristocracy tourism in Nepal. Wealthy Westerners royal jet-setters and high-society industrialists flew into Kathmandu on a highly exclusive pipeline.

events.title: Matrika Prasad Koirala (2nd Term)
events.detail: While King Tribhuvan was waiting for NC infighting to settle and was parallelly having talks with other political parties it gave no success. Tribhuvan was still not in favor of making BP the PM so she was looking for alternatives. At the end King entrusted Matrika Prasad Koirala as the PM. Matrika Prasad Koirala – Prime Minister Foreign Affairs and General Administration Narad Muni Thulung -- Minister of Defence; Revenue; Forest (NC leader sided with Matrika) Tripurawar Singh -- Minister of Health and Local Self-Government; Education; Public Works; Communications (Ktm political leader and ex organizer of Praja Panchayat NC leader since 1951 who sided with Matrika) Satyanath Das Yadav -- Minister of Law and Parliamentary Affairs (MPK's family friend and landlord from Saptari) Mahavir Shumsher --Minister of Home; Planning and Development; Industry and Commerce; Civil Supplies and Food (King's favourite)

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 162= INR 100) 1953
events.detail: Reached record high making imported goods expensive

events.title: Tribhuvan Gram Bikas Started
events.detail: Village Development Program of USA managed by United States Operations Mission (USOM). Later Government gave it name of Tribhuvan Gram Bikas with strong support and technical assistance from USOM. The programme aimed to improve the socio-economic conditions of rural populations engaged primarily in agriculture by delivering an integrated package of services. These included agricultural extension services irrigation facilities basic health and education services and the construction of rural roads and tracks. To build the required human resources a Village Development Training Centre was established in Kathmandu in 1952 under USOM assistance. Later in the fall of 1956 a Women’s Training Centre was also set up to train female personnel for participation in rural development activities. By June 1957 Village Development Programmes (VDPs) had been extended to ten districts marking the early expansion of structured rural development efforts in Nepal. Over time the programme evolved into a more structured planning framework under Nepal’s First Five-Year Plan (1956–61) which introduced a three-tier development strategy: Nucleus Development Dehat Development and Village Development. Nucleus Development focused on improving basic village infrastructure such as wells roads and school facilities. Dehat Development expanded this approach by introducing agricultural inputs like improved seeds and fertilizers along with basic social services such as primary education drinking water and health facilities. Village Development represented the most intensive level incorporating scientific farming practices soil surveys health and maternity services cooperative institutions and cottage industries with the aim of transforming the rural economy more comprehensively. In the later phase of implementation the Indian model of Block Development was integrated into the system through Indian aid providing an administrative structure to coordinate and implement these programmes more effectively across large rural areas. 6 Nucleus Development 34 Dehat Development and 12 Village Development units were established in that period. During the late 1950s particularly after William O. Thweatt joined USOM as Program Economist in 1959 greater emphasis was placed on capital-intensive projects especially in industrial development transportation and communications. Under his influence a portion of Public Law 480 (PL-480 “Food for Peace”) resources in India was also utilized to support local cost financing for USOM-assisted projects in Nepal.

events.title: Bhim Dutta Panta's Farmers Revolt
events.detail: Bhim Dutta panta was KI Singh influenced communist-oriented leader from Dadeldhura. He along with his large followers attacked police station in Brahmadev Mandi and captured government treasury. His rebelion spread other towns as well and authorities found it problomatic to contain them due to difficulty in transferring forces from kathmandu. MPK visited India and requested for assistance and accordingly UP police crossed into Nepal and joined Nepali forces in encountering the rebels. In the operation two were killed 50 injured and 276 taken in custody. Bhim Dutta himself was killed on August 23 in an accidental shooting.

events.title: Second Kathmandu Municipality Election
events.detail: First since 1951 change which would turn out as political barometer. Though election was not contended on party basis, each party supported their candidates. This time, the number of wards was reduced to 18 from 21 and name of the 'Municipality' had changed to 'Nagarpalika'. The voting age remained at 21 years. This time, women were also allowed to vote and stand as candidates. Also, arrangements were made for the candidates to choose their own election symbols. In this election, ward no. 15 was unopposed, while 56 polling stations were set up in the other 17 wards. In addition, secret balloting was arranged in the election. 73 candidates contested almost all as independents since political parties were not percieved well due to the power struggles. Nearly 53% of total 56,000 voters went to polls and six of Communist-supported candidates won. Four each of NC and Praja Parishad supported candidates won and one of Gorkha Parisahad. Reamaining four were independents. The result clearly showed MPK's Rastriya Praja Party lacked support in Kathmandu. Sadhana Devi Pradhan was elected from Ward No. 8 with 2455 votes out of 4113 votes cast, becoming the first female representative of Nepal. Janak Man Shrestha (CPN-backed) was elected as the mayor and Prayagraj Singh Suwal (NC-backed) as the deputy mayor of the 22-member municipal board, consisting of 18 elected and 4 nominated members.

events.title: Nepal Tarun Dal Formed
events.detail: The youth wing of NC was formed under the main guidance of Nepali Congress’ founding president BP Koirala. Singha Dhwaj Khadka was its founder president. In its earlt days it was mainly formed to dissipate the idea of democratic socialism among the youths.

events.title: Indian Aid Mission Established
events.detail: Indian Aid Mission in Nepal was set up for developing projects in a number of areas including health connectivity education power and government departments. Many infrastructure based programs and Block Devlopment Program was run under the mission.

events.title: Rapti Valley Development Project (RVDP)
events.detail: Motivation: Massive Flood of 1954 and landslides left thousands of Nepali hill farmers impoverished landless and food-insecure. The U.S. and the Nepali monarchy feared that a desperate destitute population would become prime targets for communist recruitment and agrarian rebellion. Resettling these farmers into the fertile Chitwan (Rapti) Valley was heavily backed by the U.S. to ensure political stability. The head of USOM Paul Rose was eager to adopt a New Deal-inspired vision of development that sought to address both concerns and benefit ordinary people rather than just the elite. Nepal's Secretary for Development and Planning Sardar Bhim Bahadur Pande had recommended Chitwan for that purpose. He wanted roads ‘so the burdens of agriculture and industry may roll on wheels rather than to continue to crush the backs and spirits of the people’. He hoped to harness Nepal’s streams to create ‘freedom from floods’ to water crops and to offer ‘tools that will take the drudgery out of daily labour’. Most importantly he wanted ‘the tillers of the soil to become the owners of the soil’. That meant land reform. Elsewhere in his writings he called U.S. programs in Nepal as a ‘prescription for revolutions’. The 1951 revolution for him was only a ‘half revolution.’ In 1953 Rose and his team travelled to Chitwan on foot and concluded that valley could be the place where they could experiment his 'revolution'. The program languished for a couple years without funding untill the 1952 Flood relief projects opened the funding taps for the Rapti Project. Project Detail: In December 1955 the construction of 52-mile double-lane gravel Hetauda-Narayangadh road began. In early 1956 a malaria eradication program was launched using DDT spraying to target the Anopheles minimus mosquito. Heavy machinery including three tractors was introduced to begin breaking "virgin land" for new settlers. In September 1956 a sawmill was established to process timber which accelerated the clearing of forests and grasslands. In 1957 a demonstration farm was launched to introduce improved livestock poultry and crops and to train farmers in modern agricultural methods. Throughout 1957-58 the DDT spraying continued and efforts to build health facilities and schools were implemented. In 1959 the Hetauda-Narayanghat road was inagurated. Throughout late 1950s and 1960s the resettlement and land distribution continued. Consequences: The original objective of the planned settlement in Chitwan Rapti Valley was to settle victims of natural disasters from the hills distribute land to landless settlers and introduce modern agricultural techniques. Despite egalitarian goals wealthy migrants and Kathmandu-based politicians frequently captured the most valuable land reproducing traditional class and caste barriers. The target was to settle 25000 people and to bring 50000 bighas (33860 hectares) of land under cultivation. By 1961 5233 families had been allotted 27000 hectares of land but only 10350 hectares were actually brought under cultivation. Only few Tharu actually obtained land. After Chitwan was opened Tharus uneducated and less worldly lost more and more of their land to the new Bahun and Chhetri migrants of the region. Initially many Tharu tenants avoided land ownership viewing it as a burden of taxes and state visibility which left them vulnerable when land suddenly became a scarce valuable commodity which is termed as the state of "voluntary landlessness". In 1955 nearly 100% of the population were Tharu; in 1970 that figure was only about 14%. Between 1954 and 1959 Rapti's population increased 160% from 25000 to 65000 thousand with “settlers being brought in from all over Nepal”. Prior to RVDP land had been virtually unlimited for Tharu. But eventually immigrants and landlords registered vast portion of land in their name and Tharu lost their their grazing and agricultural land. It was the time family of Puspa Kamal Dahal Prachanda migrated to Chitwan from Kaski in 1962. In case of agricultural modernization Tharu did get training and equipments for agricultural modernization they lacked necessary skills such as how to trade save or use money for modernized economy. RVDP also brought about mass deforestation and loss of natural habitat for animals. As a way to counter this Chitwan National Park was established in 1973.

events.title: Malaria Eradication Program
events.detail: Malaria control project was first initiated in Nepal in 1954 with the support from USAID (then USOM). The objective of the project was to study malaria mainly in Terai belt of central Nepal. In 1958 Government created Nepal Malaria Eradication Organization (NMEO). The NMEO launched National Malaria Eradication Program with the objective of eradicating malaria from the country in coordination with WHO and USOM. All Nepal below four thousand feet was classified malarial but limited personnel infrastructure and geographic knowledge restricted operations to the sixteen IBDC control centers and Pokhara Kathmandu and Rapti valleys. The NMEO organized Nepal into East Center and West zones and accelerated spraying operations in the Center reaching the East in 1962. The West was to be the “final phase of expansion” and spraying was expected to start in July 1963 and finish by 1969. Logistical difficulties however delayed operations in the West until at least 1965. The resettlement programs soon followed after the malaria control elevating Hill settler fortunes and dispossessing Indigenous Tarai peoples of land livelihoods and opportunities.

events.title: NCP's First National Convention
events.detail: Manmohan became General Secretary Keshar Jung started the two-line struggle (The CPN's first general convention began secretly in Patan on January 30 1954 moving to Kathmandu for ten days. It made key decisions to build on the 2007 movement's achievements. Manmohan Adhikari was elected General Secretary. While he was abroad at a Chinese Communist Party congress Dr. Keshar Jung Rayamajhi became acting general secretary and tried to consolidate power. This sparked a "two-line struggle" between Rayamajhi's faction and that of founding General Secretary Pushpa Lal immediately following the convention.)

events.title: Matrika's Cabinet Reshuffle
events.detail: Matrika himself wanted to reshuffle his cabinet after the Kathmandu election so he can broaden his support but he was against including NC ministers therefore he made three-party coliation though King announced for four-party coliation. Matrika Prasad Koirala Mahavir Shumsher (Independent Retained) Narad Muni Thulung (Rastriya Praja Party Retained) Keshar Shumsher (Independent) Dilli Raman Regmi (Nepali Rastriya Congress) Tanka Prasad Acharya (Praja Parishad) Bhadrakali Mishra (All-Nepal Jana Congress a NC splinter)

events.title: United Mission to Nepal Established
events.detail: During the 1951 revolution fighting had taken place just over the border from Raxaul, and wounded combatants from both sides were treated at Duncan Hospital. For providing this service, Dr Trevor Strong and Ernest Oliver were invited to visit Kathmandu after the revolution. They walked for several days and while in Kathmandu had an interview with B.P. Koirala, the Home Minister of the Nepalese government, to explore the possibility of mission work. They were told that medical and educational work would be welcome, but open preaching was not allowed. These discussions dovetailed with a separate approach by the authorities in Tansen to American missionaries Bob and Bethel Fleming and Carl and Betty Friedericks (representing Methodist and Presbyterian missions). Contact had been made as a result of ornithological trips into Nepal in October 1949 and the winter of 1951–52 during which medical assistance had been given to the people of Tansen. Eventually a letter came from S.K. Dikshit in the Department of Foreign Affairs, permitting a hospital in Tansen and clinics in Kathmandu. They started a women’s and children’s clinic as the first mission work in Bhaktapur on 7 January 1954. Methodist Bishop J.W. Pickett circulated an invitation letter from Home Minister of the Nepalese government to the National Christian Council of India. It endorsed this proposal and the United Christian Mission to Nepal was founded in March 1954 as a cooperative endeavor between eight Protestant denominations. Bishop Pickett was the founding President of the Board and Ernest Oliver the first Executive Secretary. The Flemings had already commenced medical work in Kathmandu in January 1954, and the Friedericks began medical work in Tansen in June 1954, but the work quickly expanded and diversified into other areas, such as education and development of hydropower. By 1990 the UMN "comprised 39 member missions, 420 expatriate missionaries, and over 2,000 Nepali staff". From 2002, UMN moved away from directly implementing projects to building partnerships that support local organisations due to which the size of UMN is currently much reduced from this level. Now, UMN has 12 local partners: local and national non-governmental organisations

events.title: Heightened Political Turmoil
events.detail: Advisory Assembly was formed on April 13 1954 with 113 members. NC rejected the nominations as it was only given 11 seats while MPK's party was given 45. The government was not able to pass its resolutions from the assembly at times due to internal rift among the participating parties. King Tribhuvan got ill so Prince Mahendra had to actively engage in order of his father to settle the disputes. NC announded satyagraha demanding general election constituent assembly and independent judiciary. Though all parties were against NC the communist-dominated Jana Adhikar Surakshya Samiti supported. But within two days Prince Mahendra sent letter to BP that those demands would be fulfilled soon. The protest was called off however Jana Adhikar Surakshya Samiti took it was betryal and vandalized NC party office. Tanka Prasad Acharya and Bhadrakali Mishara were sacked by the PM and he himself assumed Finance Ministry. On his budget he proposed 10% surcharge on land tax and exemption on birta land which was widely criticized. Though PM dropped the provisions later seven budget cut motions were table by opposition among with two were passed with some MPK's party mambers voting for it. That evening MPK submitted his resignation. On fourth anniversary of democracy King Tribhuvan gave full royal powers to Mahendra. On the same day Mahendra announced that he would take personal control of the Anti-Corruption Department Public Service Commission Central Intelligence Bureau and Civil Servants' Registration Office. He further pledged to remove within fifteen days any misunderstanding over the independence of the Supreme Court. Here for the first time was a ruler with enough confidence in himself to promise specific accomplishments by a self-imposed deadline and enough determination to back up his words by assuming personal control over the relevant governmental departments. The PM's resignation was accepted on March 2.

events.title: Koshi Treaty
events.detail: A sequence of severe floods during the 1953 monsoon season created an urgent need for flood management infrastructure. India’s parliament approved a plan for a barrage and embankments in December 1953. Nepal shall provide necessary lands; India shall be the owner of all lands acquired from Nepal; no time limit; India shall regulate all the generated power supplied by the Koshi River; Nepal shall utilize up to 50 percent of the hydro-electric power; India shall establish schools hospitals provision of water-supply and electricity drainage tramway lines and other civic amenities in the project territory of Nepal; any maintainence to be done by India; No hydro electricity generated yet!

events.title: Flood as a Means for King's Rise and American Penetration
events.detail: Overview: Nepal's worst flood in history. Bal Chandra Sharma led Advisory Assembly estimated death of 300, displacement of 2 lakh people and monetray loss of 1-1.5 crore rupees. Later, final estimate found that about 1000 people died, and 25,000 families lost their homes. The flood was primarily caused by exceptionally intense, concentrated monsoon downpours combined with the region's fragile mountain geography. It mostly affected eastern Terai while Kathmandu and hilly region also faced significant damage. All means of transportation from the valley to the southern plains particularly the road from the valley to Bhimphedi then to Amlekhganj railway from Amlekhganj to Raxaul and the ropeway were seriously damaged. Government Response: Nepal’s government sent out a worldwide appeal for help. Government formed Special Situation Control Committee (SSCC) focused on controlling food prices preventing black marketeering overseeing the supply of essential goods and inspecting infrastructure damage. Despite these efforts the government's response was largely limited to top-down post-disaster relief distribution with little focus on preparedness or vulnerability. The Advisory Assembly also formed its own relief committees though they were often short-lived or deactivated due to internal political disputes and lack of executive authority. King's Response: Amidst the failure of the government and the Advisory Assembly to create a unified relief effort the King and Crown Prince stepped in establishing the "Royal National Distress Alleviation Fund" which positioned the monarchy as a more effective and stable actor. The Crown Prince Mahendra took an active role later in the year including inspection visits to affected areas and oversight of relief efforts. The persistent political crises combined with the government's failure to address the flood disaster provided the necessary conditions for Mahendra to dissolve the cabinet and the Advisory Assembly in early 1955. US's Response: US was running Village Development Program but it had limited impact to which USOM head Paul Rose wasn't satisfied. Rose’s multiple requests to Washington for more dollars and technicians for Rapti Valley and other projects were repeatedly turned down. After the flood Rose convinced US government for aid stressing that flood relief programs would create ‘significant favorable political impact’. As a result in late 1954 the US announced a $2 million relief package. Due to the total lack of local governmental mechanisms to administer relief large portion of fund remained unused. Later the remaining fund was chanelled towards Rapti Project.

events.title: NNEPC Report And Hindi Bachao Andolan
events.detail: The Report: MPK's government, in partnership with US formed the Nepal National Education Planning Commission (NNEPC) to devise a masterplan for post-democratic national education system. The commission surveyed Nepal's existing schools and gathered public feedback to design a standardized, Western-funded national education system that unified the country under the Nepali language, structured modern school tiers, and established teacher-training infrastructure. The commission was led by Sardar Rudra Raj Pande (as Chairman), Kaisher Bahadur K.C. (Education Secretary), and Dr. Hugh B. Wood (Educational Advisor from Univenity of Oregon via USOM). Sardar Rudra Raj Pande served as the Headmaster of Durbar High School from 1925 to 1938, the Headmaster of Tri-Chandra College from 1938 to 1951 and the Vice Chancellor of Tribhuvan University from 1964 to 1969. NNEPC report explicitly stated: The study of a non-Nepali local tongue would mitigate against the effective development of Nepali for the student would make greater use of it than Nepali - at home and in the community - and thus Nepali would remain a "foreign" language. If the younger generation is taught to use Nepali as the basic language then other languages will gradually disappear and greater national strength and unity will result. The report was made public in 1956 and protests had begun, but when the government led by Prime Minister K.I. Singh issued a directive to all schools in October 1957 to use Nepali as medium of instruction, all hell broke loose, particularly in the Tarai. The Reaction: People from the Tarai opposed this imposition from above, and organized various protests. Supporters of Nepali language too organized various program in support of the government’s decision. Activists, politicians, and educators formed localized Hindi Bachao Samitis (Save Hindi Committees) in major southern border towns. The Nepal Terai Congress, took direct leadership of the movement. They transformed the linguistic grievance into a broader political demand for regional autonomy, federalism, and the recognition of Hindi as a co-official state language. The government, however, could not fully impose its decision for two reasons. First, there were massive protests against this decision particularly in the Tarai. Second, and more importantly, the unavailability of Nepali language textbooks, and Nepali speaking teachers made it difficult for the government to fully impose its decision. However, at the highest level, i.e., in grade 10/SLC, the state’s might prevailed to a large extent, as the SLC exams were centralized.

events.title: King Mahendra's Direct Rule
events.detail: Following MPK's resignation Mahendra imposed the direct rule. He was closely watching the infighting between the political that resulted in much instablity. He believed "real democracy can be realized only when the people shed their narrow outlook and do not contribute to rumor-mongering and unrest but try to arouse feelings of nationalism and national progress. I have seen people interpret democracy as the spread of unrest and useless rumors". Mahendra was strongly critical of the democratic experiment in Nepal. It is also clear from his statement on the first anniversary of Democracy where he said: "Today instead of our golden dreams we have in our country innumerable organizations in none of which can we see a selfless leader....The so-called complete democracy violated every rule and regulation and all around we heard only desperate muddled and panicky voices. And when the opportunists forgot the interests of their country the so-called progressives fell victim to a selfish devilishness and humanity began to spew poison and illusions." On the fourth anniversary it became even more vocal where he said: "it is a matter of great shame that we cannot point to even four important achievements that we have made during this period. If we say that democracy is still in its infancy we have seen such qualities as selfishness greed and jealousy which are not found in an infant." Council of Royal Advisors Gunja Man Singh Lt. Gen. Ananda Shamsher Guruju Bhogendra Raj Purendra Vikram Shah Aniruddha Prasad Singh Nobody had any political background contrary to King Tribhuvan's cabinet. Except for the Gorkha Parishad all parties criticized this setup.

events.title: Bangdung Conference
events.detail: It was the result of the efforts of Indonesian President Sukarno Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser and Burmese Prime Minister U Nu. Nehru successfully used the conference to champion a "third way" in global politics. This directly laid the groundwork for the formal creation of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961. Countering a strict United States containment strategy Zhou Enlai bypassed Western barriers to establish direct diplomatic economic and cultural links with the Afro-Asian world. He successfully calmed the anxieties of anti-communist neighbors. Gamal Abdel Nasser acted as a powerful voice for Arab nationalism and African decolonization.

events.title: King Mahendra's Political Program
events.detail: On May 8 he called all major political parties for a conference with intention to establish a new political system. The four political parties --NC Praja Parishad National NC and Rastriya Praja Party--boycotted the meeting. He also sent 9 tour commissions to districts to survey public opinion. King announcehd the full moon day of October 1957 to be election day. King held multiple negotiations with political parties where he insisted on partisan cabinet while King would preside. Political parties repeatedly rejected it.

events.title: Held conference inviting representatives of political religious and social organizations to discuss country's future
events.detail: major political parties boycotted; showed genuine concern to keep the administration free from party-politics; however the conference was against continuation fo direct rule

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 185= INR 100) 1955
events.detail: Due to increasing volume of imports from India

events.title: Tribhuvan International Airport Inagurated
events.detail: Gaucharan: The formal beginning of aviation in Nepal is generally placed at Gauchaur on 23 April 1949 with the landing of a Beechcraft Bonanza carrying the Indian ambassador. On 20 February 1950 an Indian registered Dakota DC-3 commenced the first ever scheduled service linking Kathmandu to Patna Kolkata and Delhi. On 15 June 1955 the airport was inaugurated by King The airport was again renamed to Tribhuvan International Airport in 1964. US Assistance: In the 1960s the USAID programme shifted its transport infrastructure priorities from road-building to internal air transport systems as road construction in Nepal had proven to be difficult time-consuming and enormously expensive. The US financed runway expansion at the Kathmandu airport to 2013 meters and in 1961 provided three Douglas Commercial (DC)-3 and two Short Takeoff and Landing (STOL) Pilatus Porter aircraft to the newly set-up Royal Nepal Airlines Corporation (RNAC). Between 1959-1974 the US invested over USD 8 million in communication and navigation equipments to the Kathmandu airport and six other airfields ‘financed improvements of nine existing airfields funded training of RNAC officials and operators and the construction of airfield buildings including six terminals and three buildings at the main Kathmandu airport’ and also funded surveys for 36 STOL airfields and built several of them. ADB Loan: Subsequently between the 1970s and 1990s ADB financed an expansion and upgradation of Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu under a USD 29.25 million loan. The project which experienced significant delays was finally completed in 1996 nearly 14 years after its target completion date. In 1985 the extension apron of runway 02/20 was overlaid. The development of the terminal building was commenced in the same year. In 1987 the construction of the Airlines Operation and Control Tower building was completed and the taxiway was overlaid. In the same year on 11 October Nepal witnessed the first ever landing of the Concorde. In 1989 the construction of the terminal building was completed and on 18 February 1990 the newly built TIA complex was officially inaugurated. Radar Installation: In 1997 airport surveillance radar (ASR) and secondary surveillance radar (SSR) came into the operation. The installation of radar surveillance was proposed by Japan in 1994 following the crash of Thai Airways Flight 311 and Pakistan International Airlines Flight 268 in 1992 which together claimed the lives of 280 people including 17 high-level Japanese diplomats. In May 2007 Austrian Airlines discontinued its flight to Vienna Nepal's last direct air link to Europe. The European Union placed all Nepali airlines on its aviation safety blacklist on December 5 2013.

events.title: Nepal publicly endorsed Panchsheel in 1955 while establishing formal relation with China
events.detail: Panchasheel first adopeted in 1954 Sino-Indian Agreement

events.title: Nepal Became Member of UN
events.detail: After once rejected by veto from Soviet Union in 1949 due to Cold War competition between US and USSR. Having stood against Suez War and invasion of Hungary Nepal posed itself as neutral facilitating its entry into UN. It also made Rishikesh Shah popular in the international community and he stood a good chance of being UN Secretary General reserved for Asia next year. But before the chance came Rishikesh Shah was called back by the King.

events.title: Tribhuvan Highway Inagurated
events.detail: The first motorable road known as the Tribhuvan Rajpath connecting Kathmandu with Raxaul on the Indian frontier was built under the supervision of Indian Army engineers and was opened on 11 December 1953. Although proposals dated back to the late Rana period (1945–48) construction began in 1952 under Prime Minister Matrika Prasad Koirala with Indian financial and engineering assistance. It was constructed with estimated cost of USD 1.92 million. There is also some evidence that although the Rana regime had first requested the US for help with the highway Nehru did not want the Americans involved in Nepal. Which is why the Tribhuvan Highway became an Indian military project. About 3500 Nepalis were employed on this construction in June 1954. The expenditure incurred on this project was converted into outright grants to Nepal under the Colombo Plan. The road followed a longer route via Naubise Daman Sim Bhanjyang and Bhainse instead of along Bagmati River. Matrika Koirala said that it was chosen largely for strategic and engineering reasons as it did not require many bridges. The highway revolutionized Nepal's transport and economy by replacing the week-long journey from India with a one-day trip after 1961 lowering transport costs reducing prices of essential goods and facilitating development projects in Kathmandu. However the road suffered from poor engineering monsoon damage and a longer-than-necessary alignment.

events.title: Ineffective Land Reforms
events.detail: Government brought Land and Cultivation Record Compilation Act in 1956 and continued with the Lands Act in 1957 as an effort towards land reform but it was largey ineffective as government lacked political will as well as proper tenants' records. The 1957 Act prohibited the landowners to charge rent more than 50% of the produce

events.title: NC Sixth General Convention
events.detail: Suvarna Shamsher; With B. P. Koirala's support Subarna Shumsher was elected president through the convention held in Birgunj defeating Ganesh Man Singh by a large majority (236 over 172). Bishwa Bandhu Thapa and Tulsi Giri were elected general secretary. Girija Prasad Koirala was elected to CWC for the first time. The delegates also adopted overwhelmingly the the democratic-socialim as its guiding principal.

events.title: Tanka Prasad Acharya
events.detail: After no conclusion be met from negotioation with political parties unexpectedly King announced the formation of a Cabinet consisting of four Praja Parishad members and three independents with the Praja Parishad leader Tanka Prasad Acharya as Prime Minister. Tanka Prasad Acharya (NPP) Chuda Prasad Sharma (Old NPP felow of Tanka Prasad) Gunja Man Singh (Independent formal Chief Royal Advisor) Pashupati Ghosh (Jana Congress faction of NPP Bhadrakali Mishra loyalist) Purendra Vikram Shah (Independent king's cousin) Balchandra Sharma (Nepal Democratic Party faction of NPP) Anirudha Prasad Singh (Independent)

events.title: Bakhanpur Credit Cooperative Founded
events.detail: The first cooperative of Nepal was founded on April 2, 1956, in the Chitwan district. Bakhan Singh Gurung, with the support from the Rapti Valley Development Project (RVDP), conceptualised a cooperative model to pool skills, labour and capital for mutual benefit, leading to the establishment of Bakhan Cooperative. Although the Department of Cooperatives was established in 1954, the first cooperative was launched three years later in Chitwan with 60 members.

events.title: Nepal Rastra Bank Established
events.detail: In early 1950s Indian Rupee dominated Nepali market and Nepal had no control over foreign currency holdings. Responding to these needs NRB was established under the Nepal Rastra Bank Act 1955. Nepali rupee also entered international currency market through a fixed exchange rate between Nepali rupees and Indian rupee in April 1960. Prior to it the NC and IC were traded at 100 IC for 71 to 177 NC between 1932 and 1955.

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 150.5= INR 100) 1956
events.detail: NRB announced it would supply INR at NRS 150.5 when the market rate was 156

events.title: NRB sells draft of 16.3 million INR to stabilize the rate
First Five-Year Plan
events.detail: NPR 330 million spent; ~74% came from aid; 60% only implemented; 7 PEs were established; out of targeted 1450 km only 565 km road was built; Tribhuvan Highway completed; Araniko Highway construction began; TIA improved; micro-hydro and rural electrification; Malaria eradiction; TU established; Gandak Irrigation Project; out of total development expenditures transportation and communications received 36 percent and 20 percent was allocated to agriculture along with village development and irrigation; only schools and post offices exceeded expectation

events.title: Block Development Programme Introduced
events.detail: The Block Development Programme was introduced in Nepal under the Indian Aid Mission as an administrative framework for rural development. Under this system the country was divided into approximately 150 development blocks each covering around 200 villages. Within each block Village Development Centres were established and placed under the supervision of a Block Development Officer (BDO) a generalist administrator supported by sectoral officials. The Block Development Officer coordinated and integrated development activities within the block including agriculture education health irrigation and cooperative development. This structure was designed to improve administrative efficiency by bringing multiple development sectors under a single coordinating authority at the block level. In practice the India-led Block Development Programme and the US-supported Village Development Programme operated in parallel and often complemented each other. Both approaches were eventually brought together under the broader framework of Tribhuvan Gram Bikas which functioned as an umbrella rural development strategy combining external assistance administrative restructuring and community-based development initiatives in Nepal.

events.title: Tanka Prashad's U-turn on Constituent Assembly
events.detail: By August 1956 all the political parties withdrew their supported who had earlier supported the goevrnment as an alternative to King's direct rule. Only the Communists indebted to Tanka Prasad for their newly won legal status supported the government throughout its tenure in office. Tanka Prasad Acharya and his party became fully unpopular among parties because they vouched for election of a Parliament with limited powers operating under a Constitution granted by the King stepping back from previous demand of Constituent Assembly. Except Samyukta Prajatantra Sangh of K. I. Singh all others were against it. BP Koirala even went to court for PM infringing on the King Tribhuvan's proclamation of February 18 1951 and the People's Representation Act of 1952 which had legally defined the aims of elections. The court however dismissed the petition.

events.title: Village Panchayat Act Enacted
events.detail: A comprehensive Panchayat Act was enacted in 1956 but was never implemented with any vigor and only a small number of panchayats were actually set up. Later The Nepali Congress government had projected legislation to expand the powers and functions of the panchayats and had seemed determined to press for their establishment throughout the whole of Nepal. However it was only administrative and local body comared to 1962 panchayat which was the building block of the national political system.

events.title: Sino-Nepalese Treaty of 1956
events.detail: It terminated the Treaty of Thapathali of 1856 and Nepal recognized Tibet as a part of China. Diplomatic passports and visas were introduced for travel between Nepal and the Tibet Region while accommodating traditional exemptions for border-district residents and traders. Nepali traders got explicit right to continue commercial activities in Lhasa Shigatse Gyantse and Yatung. Nepal signed a sister Economic Aid Agreement in October 1956. Through this China granted Nepal 60 million Indian rupees.

events.title: Private Forests (Nationalization) Act 1957 Inacted
events.detail: This historic legislation brought all private forests tax-exempt lands and associated wastelands under state ownership to assure their adequate protection maintenance and utilization. Then communal responsibility for forest management disappeared and communities having no stake in forest preservation and management. Consequently forests were converted into common property. But the government was unable to manage the forests effectively due to the lack of requisite infrastructure in both technical and administrative. In short at the time of forest nationalization the state was totally unable to control protect and manage the forests of the country as it lacked the necessarily institutional capacity. Besides many feudal landlords remained in control of forest resources and access to them.

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate (NPR 130.5= INR 100) 1957
events.detail: NRB announced it would supply INR at NRS 130.5 when the market rate was 136

events.title: NC First Special Convention
events.detail: BP Koirala; Meanwhile MPK's Nepal Praja Party was merged to NC. Subarna Shumsher resigned from the post of president saying BP should lead the united party before election. A conference was held in Rajbiraj Saptari with a proposal to hold the special convention which was unanimously passed. On May 23 1957 the special convention was held in Biratnagar electing BP Koirala as the president. Bishwa Bandhu Thapa and Tulsi Giri were re-elected to general secretary.

events.title: NCP's Second National Convention
events.detail: Pushpa Lal’s Policy Keshar Jung’s Leadership Support for Mahendra’s Coup; Pushpa Lal vs Keshar Jung (Dr. Keshar Jung Rayamajhi presented a document advocating party program changes while Pushpa Lal advocated for a constituent assembly and a republic.The convention adopted Pushpa Lal’s policies but elected Rayamajhi as General Secretary. After his policies were rejected Rayamajhi supported King Mahendra's coup which dismissed the elected government and established the Panchayat system calling it a "progressive step." Conversely Pushpa Lal branded the coup "military terror" insisting on resistance and struggle to maintain the Communist Party’s revolutionary character.)

events.title: Fall of Tanka Prasad Acharya
events.detail: Shanti Rakshya Swayam Sevak Sangh Kendra a nonpolitical social organization in Kathmandu valley was formed in 1951 as a public service acgency helping the government to distribute rice and other essential commodities equitably through its local branches. In June 1957 a shortage of rice caused much distress in the valley. Prices rose steadily and the public clamored for action by the Kendra to bring pressure on the government to alleviate the situation. Kendra decided to dramatize the food situation by organizing a hunger march on June 15. A procession of about twelve thousand persons shouting "Give us food or quit office" paraded through the streets of Kathmandu. On June 24 and 27 the Kendra called general strikes in Kathmandu. Food Minister Chuda Prasad Sharma talked in grandiose terms of a plan to utilize airplanes and helicopters to import 200000 maunds of rice from India and an equal amount from Burma at a cost of 10 million rupees. But it was apparent that government was incapable of effective action. Out of sheer frustration Tanka Prasad Acharya submitted a letter of conditional resignation to the King on July 5 asking either to allow me to form a homogeneous cabinet or to consider this letter as my resignation from the government. His urge for homogeneous cabinet came as his want to lay down the burden of unpopular government. But the King wasn't positive of that as it would minimize the role of independent members. He dissolved the Acharya government on July 14 and the next day called upon K. I. Singh the sworn enemy of the Nepali Congress and "the Koirala brothers" to form the next government.

events.title: Kunwar Indrajit Singh
events.detail: His choice as a candidate for the leadership of a new "national" government cannot be understood on any rational basis other than his and King Mahendra's common dislike for the Nepali Congress. The CWC of the NC Praja Parishad and Nepali National Congress adopted resolutions decrying the appointment of K. I. Singh and questioning his competence to hold the general elections successfully. The eleven-member Cabinet consisted of seven members of the Samyukta Prajatantra Sanghparty three "independents" including Laxmi Prasad Devkota as Education Minister and one member of the dissident Nepali National Congress i.e. Jiva Raj Sharma. The Samyukta Prajatantra Sangh party members in the Cabinet were without question the most incongruous collection of Ministers ever inflicted upon Nepal. None of them had any substantial influence in the country even in the areas from which they had come nor were they important even in the ruling party's hierarchy.

events.title: Election Postponed
events.detail: The election announced by the King was postponed indefinitely citing to lack of preparation from Election Comission and the Cabinet. Parties held strikes against the postponement and termed it as "black day". The failure of the King to announce a new date was the most criticized point. General Conference of the Democratic Front was organized by the Nepali Congress, Nepali National Congress, and Praja Parishad met at Birganj on October 8 which resolved to launch a country-wide Satyagraha movement on December 12. It was creating massive pressue on the KI Singh government and the King.

events.title: National Language Policy
events.detail: Initially Schools in Terai were managed by the local Nepali landlords and Indian merchants. Government was also indifferent to Terai schools mainly due to the dearth of Nepali teachers owing partly to their limited availability and partly to their unwillingness to work in the humid malarial Terai. Consequently the schools had imported a large number of Indian teachers from across the border and these teachers naturally preferred to teach in Hindi or English rather than Nepali. As the new Nepali teachers were sent to terai they attempted to make Nepali the sole medium of instruction. It divided politicians over regional lines. In this context of public agitation that the Singh government announced its language policy on October 12 1957. To qualify for government aid and recognition Terai schools were required to use Nepali as the language of instruction in the middle and high schools and to use textbooks approved by the government. Furthermore all teachers had to be Nepali citizens and were required to attain a specified degree of proficiency in Nepali by 1959. Despite protests government went forward with the policy clarifying it had no intention to supress regional dialect.

events.title: Gandak Project Controversy
events.detail: A loud controvercy began when KI Singh set up a commitee to study draft proposal from Indian government on Gandak dam. Though government was terminated abruptly by the King on November 15 before the negotiation could take shape KI Singh banned many press house which questioned government regarding the project.

events.title: King Mahendra's Direct Rule
events.detail: Announcing that he was "compelled in spite of his reluctance to conduct the administration of the affairs of the country for a few days." King too charge of the government.

events.title: Democratic Front's Satyagraha
events.detail: The Democratic Front's Satyagraha was already announced demanding for election date. Just before few days of the Satyagraha King called all political parties for a conference in a way that the Democratic Front will be in minority. The Front and non-Front parties were divided on the necessity of Satyagraha and just before 36 hours of the Satyagraha King made concluding remarks of the cinference calling the Satyagraha unnecessary and insted focus on educatinf people on democratic value and consult with Election Comission on date of election. Not wanting to disobey royal order the Fornt and non-Front parties immediately went to Election Comission. The Front jointly addressed a joint petition to King reiterating their view that elections could be held within six months and requested the King to issue a proclamation to this effect. Non-Front parties also prepared a joint report which advised the King to commence the elections on February 12 1959. Since no Royal Proclamation came The Front move forward with its Satyagraha. B. P. Koirala and others were arrested while picketing at the main gates of the Singha Durbar but were released after a few hours. Finally On December 15 King Mahendra broadcast a Royal Proclamation over Radio Nepal naming February 18 1959 as the day of general elections. The Front parties were once again divided over the issue of the purpose of the elections. On December 24 1957 the Praja Parishad executive reiterated its previous demand for elections to a Parliament while the Nepali Congress and the Nepali National Congress continued to espouse elections for a Constituent Assembly.

events.title: Last Wave of Smallpox And Eradication Campaign
events.detail: In 1958 a wave of smallpox again hit Kathmandu. A 1965 survey revealed that 16% of the Valley's total population had struggled with the virus at some point in their lives. Those were the ones the disease hadn't killed. WHO and the Nepal government launched a pilot program in 1962 in Kathmandu Valley using new freeze dried vaccine an improved version of the one Edward Jenner had devised in the 1790s but got disappointing results. After two and a half years only 30% of Valley residents were protected. WHO blamed ‘administrative problems and the religious and mundane objections of some sections of the population to vaccination’. In 1966 the program expanded countrywide with new commitment and revised procedures including better record keeping to prevent double counting. In 1971 the program started month-long mass vaccination campaigns. Each year for four straight years several thousand temporary staff vaccinated 6 million Nepalis. Between 1967 and 1975 39 million Nepalis got vaccinated or re-vaccinated. Aggressive surveillance routine house-to-house searches and containment became the game changer. But then came a setback: ‘a tidal wave’ of new cases with nearly 2000 new infections in 240 separate outbreaks. Three of every four of these cases were imports from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. To address outbreaks in Morang the Nepal smallpox program in 1975 initiated a ‘watchdog’ system a tactic recently devised in India. Staff were posted at the houses of infected people to ensure that they did not leave and that no unvaccinated person entered. Cash rewards were given to citizens and staff reporting new cases. In April 1975 Nepal saw its last case. On April 13 1977 Nepal was declared smallpox-free.

events.title: Cholera And Innovative Control Mechanism
events.detail: The 1958 cholera outbreak in Nepal was the first to be bacteriologically confirmed and internationally reported marking the start of a period of study between 1958 and 1960. The findings established that the Kathmandu Valley acted as an independent endemic cholera focus rather than solely importing cases from India with cases peaking in 1958 followed by lower-intensity transmission in 1959 and 1960. Cholera has spread to the Kathmandu Valley and also to Morang Dharan Dhankuta and Bhojpur in the east according to a report by the World Health Organization (WHO). While 1958 saw 2452 reported cases 1959 and 1960 showed a shift towards higher rates in rural outskirts alongside a for 1960 lower proportion of cases in Kathmandu. The committee formed by the Ministry of Health to control cholera concluded that cholera was spread by flies in Nepal at that time. The then Kathmandu Municipality charitable organizations and the Cholera Prevention Committee confiscated and destroyed stale food rotten fruits and fish in the market to prevent the spread of cholera. Hotels and restaurants were monitored. The government had released a budget of Rs 25000-25000 twice to control cholera. WHO had given enough anti-cholera injections to 25000 patients. At that time up to 36 patients used to come to the hospital daily. The US also provided 280000 cc of cholera vaccine and two tons of medical supplies. Since few people came to get the injections they even had to advertise it as a 'painless injection'. WHO has stated that about 66000 people out of Kathmandu's population of about 200000 have been vaccinated in two years. According to a news report published in Gorkhapatra at the time drugstores were instructed to sell medicines until night. Arrangements were made for Bhaktapur-Kathmandu buses to operate until 3 am. A campaign was launched to sprinkle bleach powder in drinking water to control cholera. Bleach powder was also sprayed on vehicles garbage dumps and excrement. The government had formed a cholera prevention committee under the chairmanship of the then Health Minister Randhir Subba. The committee decided to seize and destroy any food left open and stale in hotels. A reward was announced for the person who killed the flies. A reward of five mohars (currently 2 rupees 50 paisa) was announced for killing one mana of flies. Kathmandu Municipality had also appealed to the residents to kill flies. The municipality had stated that it would pay 50 paisa for one mana of moru (mohar rupee) to those who killed flies. Children under the age of 14 killed many flies. 80 percent of the children who killed flies reached the Kathmandu Municipality office on Naya Sadak to collect the prize. The municipality had collected and destroyed 6400 flies from various individuals. Even though the cholera outbreak had subsided the government later announced that it would award prizes to the three people who killed the most flies in the valley. The first prize was 100 rupees the second prize was 75 rupees and the third prize was 50 rupees.

events.title: Second Lalitpur Municipality Election
events.detail: The Patan municipal election was litmus test for the NC-led Democratic Front and non-Front parties. Only one avowed Front candidate won in Kathmandu and none of the five Front candidates was victorious in the Patan elections. It was clear that the Front had failed to demonstrate any overwhelming influence in Kathmandu Valley.

events.title: Third Kathmandu Municipality Election
events.detail: Municipal elections were to be held every 4 years and was held on 20 January 1958 for Kathmandu. This time, the election was contested on a party basis. According to which, Prayagraj Singh Suwal of the Nepali Congress won the post of Mayor, while Krishnalal Shrestha of the Nepal Communist Party won the post of Deputy Mayor. Elections were held in Lalitpur Municipality on January 15, 1958, in Birgunj on March 13, 1958, in Bhadrapur between February and March 1958, in Tansen between July and August 1958, in Biratnagar on November 26, 1958, and in Bhaktapur on November 8, 1958. Similarly, on October 29, 1959, Khasyauli Municipality was formed. On November 4, 1959, Rajbiraj Municipality was formed. On April 13, 1960, Ilam Municipality was formed. On May 26, 1960, Janakpur Municipality was formed. On September 5, 1960, Taulihawa Municipality was formed. On November 5, 1960, Bhojpur Khikamachha Bazaar Municipality was formed. In this way, the number of municipalities gradually increased.

events.title: Regional Transport Organisation Formed
events.detail: On January 24 1958 the governments of the United States India and Nepal signed a tripartite agreement to jointly establish a Regional Transport Organisation (RTO). The RTO was officially created on July 1 1958 to spearhead the organized long-term construction of Nepal's motorized road network. Its initial plan focused on constructing approximately 900 miles of roads within 5 years including major connections like the Tribhuvan Rajpath and the road connecting Bhairahawa to Pokhara. However ‘the organisation’s target was completely out of the realm of possibilities’ and as such the project was abandoned in 1962 after constructing ‘148 miles of jeep track…paved 24 miles of existing road graded 193 miles and laid gravel on 41 miles. The project also left behind nearly United States Dollar (USD) 1 million worth of heavy construction equipment which was to United States Agency for International Development (USAID)’s chagrin used on the historic Lhasa-Kathmandu Highway built by the Chinese ‘a project United States Operations Mission (USOM) had no desire to support’.

events.title: Royal Proclamation
events.detail: In the proclamation King proposed the early establishment of (a) a Constitution Drafting Commission in order to prepare a Constitution incorporating the idea of a bicameral Legislature (b) a nominated Advisory Assembly in the interim period before the elections and (c) a government without a Prime Minister consisting of independents as well as representatives of political parties. The Advisory Assembly was announced on March 5 but it was dissolved shortly.

events.title: Constitution Draft Committee Formed
events.detail: The Commission—headed by the chairman of the Public Service Commission Bhagawati Prasad Singh—included Hora Prasad Joshi and the general secretary Surya Prasad Upadhyaya of the Nepali Congress; Ranadhir Subba president of the Gorkha Parishad; and Ram Raj Pant the principal of the Law College. Sir Ivor Jennings who had previously advised in Sri Lankan and Malaysian constitution was an advisor in this committee. The Constitution as drafted by the Commission was first approved by the coalition Council of Ministers before it was submitted to King Mahendra for his approval.

events.title: Subarna Shamsher Rana
events.detail: Finally on May 15 King Mahendra issued a Royal Proclamation establishing a Council of Ministers under the interim chairmanship of Suvarna Shamsher. Representatives of four parties—the Nepali Congress Gorkha Parishad Nepali National Congress and Nepal Praja Parishad—and two independents were included. Unexpected elevation to the chairmanship of the Council was construed by the representatives of other parties as a recognition of a special position for the Nepali Congress implying thereby a denigration of their own status and a nullification of the mutually agreed basis of interparty equality in the Council. Press and public accepted this new political experimentation except one newspaper reflecting Nepali Congress views refused to accept the democratic façade of the Council of Ministers and described the new arrangement as an indirect form of direct rule. Suvarna Shamsher (NC) Dilli Raman Regmi (Nepali Rastriya Congress) Chandra Bhusan Pande (Praja Parishad) Purendra Vikram Shah (King Mahendra's relative) Bhupal Man Singh (King's representative) Ranadhir Subba (Gorkha Parishad) Shortly King also announched the Advisory Assembly of 62 representatives from only six parties—the Nepali Congress Gorkha Parishad Praja Parishad Nepali National Congress Samyukta Prajatantra Sangh and Communist party. However its first meeting could not be held until two or three months before the elections.

events.title: Nepal Airlines Corporation Founded
events.detail: Nepal Airlines Corporation was officially founded on July 1, 1958, through the enactment of the Nepal Airlines Corporation Act. Originally named Royal Nepal Airlines Corporation (RNAC), it began its operations on July 3, 1958, with just 97 personnel and a single Douglas DC-3 Dakota aircraft. The Government of Nepal created the airline to establish aviation sovereignty, as all domestic flights were previously managed by Indian companies. Currently Nepal Airlines has 2 Airbus A330-200, 2 Airbus A320-200, and 2 De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter in operation.

events.title: Preparations for The First General Election
events.detail: Chairman Suvarna Shamsher allocated sizable funds for election expenses as early as August 1958. Ranadhir Subba who held the Law and Parliamentary Affairs portfolio moved swiftly in appointing election officers for all the constituencies. Mock elections were held and publicity campaigns were held by Election Comission. The opposition parties except the Communist Party grew increasingly concerned that the elections might actually be held this time a development that was unlikely to prove advantageous to them. They demanded that the proper criteria for citizenship be determined before elections were held. But nothing came of this. The problem however came from the Advisory Assembly where independent candidate Surya Bahadur Thapa won over his nearest opponent Hora Prasad Joshi of the Nepali Congress by a thirteen-vote margin. A political resolution was soon brought by the D. S. Pariyar on December 10 the one-time president of the Parallel Nepali Congress which asked for postponement of the election until the Constitution is published as the Royal Proclamation had said the election be held under new Constitution. The resolution was passed but King Mahendra prorogued the Assembly on December 20 "in order to facilitate the participation of the members in the general elections". In support of the Advisory Assembly resolution recommending postponement of elections some thirty-odd social cultural and political organizations presented a joint petition to the King on December 16 who had no mass support. The support grew to 42 organations but they were not taken seriously.

events.title: Political Parties Before Election
events.detail: Nepali Congress: Between 5th and 6th general convantion NC went through a substantial revitalization. On one side it was constantly pressing the government and on other side negotiating with the King to gain voice in government. By 6th convention NC got ideological clarity which helped to pose it as the ideology driven party compared to its rivals which constantly purged into intra-party power-struggle. Unique of all it was a pluralist party representing diverse socio ethnic and economic elements in both membership and leadership level. It was the only party that was functioning with codified rules and procedures (Communist were the next). BP was made party president through special convention. Matrika had also rejoined the party. In 1957 NC leaders toured all sections of the country and in innumerable public meetings stressed the historical factors underlying King Tribhuvan's proclamation on elections for a Constituent Assembly while criticizing the government. However later on February 6 party accepted Mahendra's Proclamation to hold parliament election instead of Constituent Assmebly citing that if they did not go into election the retrogressive reactionary elements (like KI Singh) will remain powerful and remaining democracy will come to end. So BP argued that being dissatisfied with the proclamation they had to be pragmatic to go to the election to at least protect and institutionalize the achievent of the revolution. After BP's arrival the democratic socialist election manifesto was prepared and advertized. Gorkha Parishad: Lead by Bharat Shamsher and Mrigendra Rana that had Rana support and background. It was reorgamized Gorkha Dal that veiled its militant qualities with the cloak of Gorkha nationalism and a commitment to parliamentary democracy. One of the parties after NC that was well-organized and had a national presence. Though its influence was largely confined to the hill areas and particularly to the area immediately around Kathmandu Valley. It drew its base from the Kshatriya caste and from hill ethnic communities such as the Magars Gurungs Limbus and Rais. Brahmans and the Terai communities were virtually unrepresented. Nepal Communist Party: On April 1956 the ban on Communist parties was lifted by Tanka Prasad Acharya administration after which the party came to public leaving its underground activity. There was a clear division between moderate Keshar Jang Rayamajhi who argued party should accept monarchy and move forward with progressive agenda and Pushpa Lal Shrestha who argued party should fight against all feudal elements including the monarch. The party went to election with this divided lines. However it was one of the parties after NC that good organization and strict candidate screening mostly representing students lower-middle-class merchants and urbanized peasants. Though like the Gorkha Parishad they were also restricted territorially having active centers of party strength only in Kathmandu Valley two or three districts in the Terai and a few places in the hills. Rastriya Praja Party: After the death of Tribhuvan MPK's party virtually total eclipse of the once powerful M. P. Koirala. His party disintegrated rapidly and passed quietly into limbo as most of its leaders joined NC. Praja Parishad: Following differences with the Nepali Congress Bhadrakali Mishra and Tanka Prasad Acharya had split from the party and reactivated the Nepal Praja Parishad. After dissolution of the second MPK's government the most opportunists --Balchandra Sharma (prev. RPP) Tanka Prasad Acharya (PP-NC-PP) and Bhadrakali Mishra(prev. NC-Jana Congress)-- combined their factions under the Praja Parishad label. Later in 1958 the party again split into parallel lines Nepal Praja Parishad (Acharya) and the Nepal Praja Parishad (Mishra) going into election with two separate names. Samyukta Prajatantra Sangh: KI Singh formed this after his return from China. He was a was a first-rate demagogue appealing people from his blunt and rugged manners rather than ideology. It was significantly different from most other parties in that its leadership was mostly non-Brahmanic in origin and that the top-ranking persons in the party echelon came from areas other than Kathmandu. KI Singh stood for full fledge monarchy with a parliament. He started politics being anti-Indian in 1951 turning anti-China later after his arriaval from China.

events.title: Kanti Highway Completed
events.detail: The 92 km Kanti Highway (Tikabhairav(Lalitpur)-Hetauda Road) was originally established and initiated for construction in 1954 by King Mahendra and completed in 1959. The highway functions as a crucial alternative route connecting the Kathmandu Valley to Hetauda.

events.title: Nepal-India Telecommunications Project
events.detail: In 1959 a Nepal-India Telecommunications project began as part of the same Regional Transportation Organization (RTO) tripartite agreement between the two countries and the US with USAID contributing USD 2.9 million to install a 1000-line telephone system in Kathmandu. International facilities were routed through Delhi and Calcutta while India provided housing facilities for US-provided transceivers. Subsequently US assistance was also vital towards establishing an internal radio communications network made up of 57 stations with seven area stations ‘each with five to nine satellites… A remotecontrol receiver and building were erected in Kathmandu and over 100 operators and maintenance personnel were trained. A telecommunications department was set up in 1959 and renamed to the Telecommunications Development Board in 1969.

events.title: Constitution of the Kingdom of Nepal
events.detail: Constitution generally followed the format and in some cases even the language of the 1950 Indian Constitution. Fundamental rights were restored from previous constitution.The Crown was established as the source of all legislative executive and judicial authority. At best it amounted to the adoption of a token democratic exterior for the future governments; at worst it amounted to a calculated measure to create the illusion of political democracy under an essentially authoritarian system. Sovereignty: In the Preamble it was clearly stated that the Constitution was granted as an "exercise of the sovereign powers and prerogatives vesting in US (royal family) in accordance with the tradition and custom of our country and which devolved on Us from Our august and respected forefathers." It also stated "the executive power of Nepal is vested in His Majesty extends to the execution and maintenance of this constitution and the laws of Nepal and shall be exercised by him either directly or through ministers". Parliament: In ensured bicameral parliament with Senate (Maha Sabha 36 members 6yrs tenure with one-third retiring with every two years) and the House of Representatives (Pratinidhi Sabha 109 members 5yrs tenure). King and the Parliament: Despite a bicameral parliament the king continued to hold important powers such as the prerogative to appoint half of the members of the Senate while other half were elected by PR method. The King was empowered to reject on his own discretion the Prime Minister's recommendation that the Parliament either be summoned or dissolved (Art. 26.2). This provision negated the basic principle of the Cabinet type of government and reduced the position of the Prime Minister to that of an ordinary civil servant. The house could not introduce any money bill without the consent of the King and could pass no law without the formal assent of the King who could withhold refuse or postpone his assent at his discretion and without any explanation. The King also reserved to himself wide discretionary powers to suspend either or both of the houses of the Parliament at any time he deemed necessary (Art. 56.1). The Constitution also insured the personal inviolability of the King by specifically debarring the Parliament from discussing his "private revenues" (Art. 44.4) and "the conduct of His Majesty and his successors" King and DIscretionary Power: All powers relating to matters not provided in the Constitution or covered by existing laws were stipulated to be the residuary powers of the King (Art. 68). The King was also assured the power to grant pardons reprieves and respites and to remit suspend or commute any sentence passed by any court tribunal or authority established by law. King and The Government: The Council of State consisting of Ministers Speakers and royal apointees was used to counterbalance PM. The King could dismiss a PM if after consulting the Council of State he was satisfied that the PM had lost the confidence of the Parliament or "persisted in acting contrary to the provisions of this constitution" (Art. 13.5d). This created dyarchical form of government with two loci of power. King and The Army: The supreme command of the army was vested in him as part of his discretionary powers and he alone was empowered "to raise and maintain armed forces; to grant commissions in such forces; to appoint Commanders in Chief and to determine their powers duties and remunerations" (Art. 64.164.2). It was laid down explicitly that "no bill or amendment relating to the armed forces shall be introduced in either House of Parliament without the recommendations of His Majesty" (Art.64.3). Government: British model of government. A Cabinet led by the Prime Minister and consisting of not more than fourteen ministers was envisioned. Ministers were individually or collectively responsible to the King for their actions and held their office at his pleasure. PM was required to select at least two Ministers from the Upper House. Judiciary: The King reserved the right to appoint the Chief Justice and other judges at his discretion and similarly reserved the right to dismiss them for "misbehavior or incapacity" on the recommendation of a specially constituted Royal Tribunal (Art.57.1 57.4b). The Constitution also provided for the establishment of such statutory bodies and offices as the Public Service Commission the Constituency Delimitation Commission the Election Commission and the Auditor-General. Members of these bodies were direct appointees of the King and as such were responsible to him alone for their actions.
