2015 General Election Result's Major Highlight
events.detail: BP's Last Minute Candidacy Cancellation: BP's nomination papers for Ramechhap North and Morang had different details about him. In the Morang nomination, the address was 'Koirala Niwas, Biratnagar', while in Constituency No. 13, it was 'Nagpokhari Naxal, Kathmandu'. If other details were also different, the candidatures of both constituencies could have been cancelled. That is why two party workers, Manahari Baral and Hom Bahadur, were sent from Kathmandu to Ramechhap overnight with BP's luggage and the candidacy was withdrawn. Gorkha Council candidate Bishnu Prasad Upreti won by a landslide in the constituency where there was no Congress candidate after BP left. Surya Prasad Upadhyay Defeated: Surya Prasad Upadhyay had contested from two places – Constituency No. 5, Kathmandu and Constituency No. 14, Ramechhap – and had lost in both the constituencies. Not only Congress General Secretary Upadhyay but also the presidents of two other parties were defeated from Constituency No. 5, Kathmandu. Nepal Praja Parishad President Tanka Prasad Acharya and Prajatantrik Mahasabha's Ranganath Sharma were defeated from here. Brahmashamsher was the candidate from Gorkha Parishad in that area. However, he later withdrew his candidacy. After withdrawing his candidacy, Brahmashamsher joined the Nepali Congress and was made a member of the Mahasabha. Even then, Surya Prasad could not win the election. Meanwhile, in Constituency No. 14, Ramechhap, Surya Prasad was defeated by Gorkha Council candidate Beni Bahadur Karki. Beni Bahadur Karki's father was killed by the Mukti Sena of the Nepali Congress during the 2007 revolution. His father was an army captain, and Mohan Shamsher had sent troops to Birgunj under his leadership to suppress the Mukti Sena's rebellion. However, he was killed by the Mukti Sena's bullets. Beni Bahadur joined the Khukuri Dal to avenge that. From there, he supported Bharat Shamsher and became a high-level leader of the party when the Gorkha Parishad was established, which later merged in NC after coup. The same Beni Bahadur was made the Speaker of the National Assembly by the Congress in 1991. Surya Prasad, who lost in two seats, was appointed Home Minister by BP after nominating him in Mahasabha. Krishna Prasad Bhattarai Defeated: Krishna Prasad Bhattarai, was a candidate from Constituency No. 104, Gorkha North. Jagat Nepal has mentioned in his book First Parliament that the main reason for his defeat was alcohol consumption. Two or three porters used to carry alcohol for him in a tumlet. Since he did not accept caste, even if he was the son of a Brahmin, he would sit with everyone in the family and eat food without changing his dhoti. That is why the Brahmin and Chhetri members of the Congress got angry and did not go to vote. According to BP Koirala, Gorkha was a new place for Bhattarai and he did not know the workers there. A storm hit on the day of voting. Bhattarai was defeated by a small number of votes as not many people turned up to vote. Bishwanath Subedi of the Gorkha Council, who defeated Bhattarai, was very ill. He could only campaign on his own. Gorkha Council leaders Bharat Shamsher, Shubha Shamsher Thapa and others had reached Gorkha on horseback to campaign for him. Carrying medicines and other supplies, they also performed minor treatments to impress the people. A group led by Congress leader Rajeshwar Devkota had even attempted to attack the team to prevent them from campaigning for the Gorkha Council. Rajeshwar Devkota himself was also injured in the conflict. Even after the defeat, the Congress nominated Bhattarai as the Speaker of the first Parliament. At that time, there was a provision that even a person who was not an MP could be made the Speaker. All Party Chairmans Lost: Chairman of the Nepal Rashtrabadi Gorkha Parishad party, Randhir Subba, was defeated in Dhankuta Election Constituency Number 26. The President of the Terai Congress, Vedanand Jha, in Siraha Constituency Number 39; the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Nepal, Keshar Jung Rayamajhi, in Palpa-93; the Chairman of Nepal Prajatantrik Mahasabha, Rangnath Sharma, in Kathmandu-5; the then President of the Nepali Rastriya Congress, Dilli Raman Regmi, in Kathmandu-2; the Chairman of the Nepal Praja Parishad (Mishra group), Bhadrakali Mishra, in Election Constituency Number 45; and the Chairman of the Nepal Praja Parishad (Acharya group), Tanka Prasad Acharya, were also defeated in Kathmandu-5. Defeat of KI SIngh: Dr K.I. Singh, the then Chairman of the Samyukta Prajatantra Party, in Doti South Constituency Number 71. His party had won five seats. However, KI Singh, couldn't not accept his defeat. Along with Tanka Prasad Acharya, and Rangnath Sharma, he submitted a joint signature on a statement to the King to instigate a fair investigation. King ahd no choice but to ask them to settle the dispute through relevant acts and rules. However, KI Singh was not satisfied with King's answer. He filed a case in the Supreme Court claiming the election was rigged. To fight the case on his behalf, Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India, Nirmal Chandra Chatterjee, had to arrive in Kathmandu. He was even a candidate from the Hindu Mahasabha in the first parliamentary election of India from the Hooghly election constituency of South Bengal. He is the father of the former Speaker of the Parliament of India, Somnath Chatterjee. Attorney General Shambhu Prasad Gyawali argued on behalf of the government. After the division bench of the then Acting Chief Justice Bhagwati Prasad Singh and Justice Min Bahadur Thapa determined on November 13, 1959, that the claim of the petitioner Dr K.I. Singh, could not be reached through law and evidence, this case was settled. Ganesh Man's Grudge: Ganesh Man was a celebrity figure ever since his daring jail break. Contesting from Kathmandu-1, he mistakenly believed that his name alone would guarantee an electoral win. However, when the election results were made public, Ganesh Man felt as if he had fallen from a cliff. He was given tough competition by the founder of the Communist Party of Nepal, Pushpa Lal Shrestha. Ganesh Man, who was irritated by this result, labeled the people of Kathmandu as ‘sheep.’ Saying that he won by only 3,138 votes against Pushpa Lal, he threatened never to stand for election thereafter. Tilak Kayastha, who was involved in Ganesh Man’s publicity during the first election, recalled, “Ganesh Man’s perspective was that he had suffered imprisonment while fighting for the people’s fundamental rights and stood firm against cruel rulers. He believed the people should have rewarded him with a landslide victory; his dissatisfaction stemmed from that.” It was a striking coincidence that after the first election, he never faced another electoral battle.

events.title: Policies and Programs of NC Government
events.detail: Economic Development: Subarna Shumsher emphasized the government's preference for labor- intensive projects on a short-term basis while at the same time carrying out some capital-intensive long-term projects. Government focused in mobilization of internal resources for devlopement. At that time 78 per cent of the development budget was contributed by foreign aid and revenue only made up just 2-3 per cent of the national income. For that purpose he introduced the first income and property taxation program in the history of Nepal. He then announced taxes on Birta land urban property foreign investments trade profits watertaps and radio receivers. The taxes were very modest as they were estimated to bring in only 25 lakhs rupees in additional revenue. In the second budget reviewing past fiscal year he noted that 53% of the allocations of the Development budget would be spent and that about 81% of the allocations for education and 56% for health were likely to be expended. In his estimates for the year 1960/61 the Finance Minister proposed an expenditure of some 2.5 crore rupees on the Development budget compared to previous 1.4 crore. Government also intended to float government bonds to the value of Rs. 2 crore at 5.5 % interest which would mature after five years to finance devlopment. Administrative Reorganization: Previous governments frequently replaced officials often on political grounds which created insecurity and weakened administrative effectiveness. To address this problem the government reorganized the Central Secretariat and introduced a probation system for senior officials. Government employees and administrators were screened and evaluated before permanent appointments were made. The government also created the position of District Development Officers to supervise development projects. Salaries of government employees were increased and specialized branches of technical services such as engineering health and education were established with clear hierarchical structures. Parliamentary Functioning: Although the Nepali Congress held a strong majority in the House of Representatives parliamentary proceedings generally followed democratic norms and procedures. Members of opposition parties were given opportunities to criticize government policies and participate in discussions. Debates were conducted openly and parliamentary rights and privileges were respected.Given Nepal's low literacy rate and limited experience with parliamentary institutions the relatively smooth functioning of Parliament was seen as a significant achievement and demonstrated the possibility of democratic governance in Nepal. Law and Order: In Mahottari district Hindu–Muslim riots broke out due to religious tensions involving disputes over a mosque and alleged beef imports resulting in deaths and destruction of property. In Dang district clashes occurred between peasants and landlords reflecting long-standing economic inequalities. Gorkha's Karmabir Mahamandal incident was the biggest of all. Bajhang Episode: Government was determiend to abolish semi-autonomous Rajya states in western Nepal. Resistance emerged from the ruling family of Bajhang particularly from Om Jang Shah son of Bajhang chief and his supporters who opposed the government's attempts to remove their authority. They arrested the district judge and destroyed goods and papers belonging to the central government. A few days later his followers seized several Forest Department employees and they allegedly established a parallel administration and challenged central government authority. In response the government dispatched officials and security forces to suppress the movement. Armed confrontations followed and the leaders eventually fled to India and appealed to King Mahendra. Foreign Policy: Nepal adopted non-alignment. It also emphasized Nepal's right to make independent decisions regarding both domestic and foreign affairs and consistently defended national sovereignty whenever external pressures appeared. During the NC government the most of border issue with China was solved and a trade treay was signed with India. In the middle of September BP addressed the fifteenth General Assembly meeting on September 29 laying the strongest emphasis on Nepal's historical independence and its full faith in the United Nations as the custodian of its integrity and sovereignty. Nepal was the first country in South Asia to formally recognize Israel establishing full diplomatic and bilateral relations with Israel on June 1 1960. Diplomatic relations between Nepal and Pakistan were also established during the NC government.

events.title: The Opposition
events.detail: Since opposition parties were so weak inside parliament they took strategy of mostly using direct public agitation against government. National Democratic Front: The Tanka Prasad faction of Praja Parishad Samyukta Prajatantra Sangh and Prajatantrik Mahasabha formed the National Democratic Front as early as June 1 1959 to arouse public opposition. It just had five membeers in the parliament. The Front made many corruption allegations and was against Gandak Treaty calling out NC to be pawn of Indian imperialism. They also criticised Treaty of Trade and Transit with India calling that it gave India monopoly in Nepal. When Mustang issue came over they asked for resignation of NC government for giving away Gandak to India and Mustang to China. Gorkha Parishad: It was the main opposition party in the parliament and Bharat Shumsher was recognized the leader of opposition. It limited most of its opposition in the parliament. It was mostly India-leaning though previously anti-India. It charged China for incursions into Nepali territory in the north and demanded Nepal's absolute authority over Everest. In overall Gorkha Parishad contributed to development of parilamentary democracy and left the streets for Communists and the National Democratic Front. Both Mrigendra and Bharat Shumsher ahd very shart analytical skills to question government in the parliament but they failed to rally the public. Nepal Communist Party: Most ideologically consistent opposition. They utilized the NC government's determination to provide fullest possible civil liberties opening opposition fronts both in parliament and in public. While Gorkha Parishad pressed on Chinese invasion the Communists stressed on threat from India. They opposed import of vegetable (Dalda) ghee even organizing large protests on September 1 claiming that it would affect domestic production. In June 1960 the government caved against public pressure and reimposed ban on import of Dalda. They held public demonstration against Gandak on February 13 while on issue of China they argued that it would be inconceivable that there could be threst from China. On Mt. Everest issue many protests were held in Kathmandu by Gorkha Parishad Democratic Front and ruling NC itself but Communists just called for settlement of debate through historical facts and not through emotional nationalism. Some 18 social organization pro-Everest rally two days after which protest Communists staged a protest over Gandak Treaty instead. Ironically on Gorkha case they stood up with the feudals who were against the land reform. Largely their opposition stood against NC regardless of ideology. They were the most visible opposition to the government at the time. Nominated Members of Senate: King nominated half of the senate members. He included two NC leaders often in conflict with BP three ex-Congress who had turned sharp NC critique and eighteen others. Though it had limited power it was very active in criticizing the NC government. They even passed a resolution raised by a Communist senator charging government of corruption and calling for investigation. Also were fierce critique of the Gandak Treaty. Jana Hit Sangh: Organization formed in April 1960 solely to fight government's taxation policies and land reform. It was entirely based in Kathmandu and led by middle-class merchants and landowners. They were the ones who staged protests in all three cities of the valley just two weeks before the coup calling for dismissal of NC government. NC And Intra-Party Opposition: BP was able to unify party on his leadership. Only few dissident voices from MPK Tulsi Giri and Bhihwabandu Thapa were there which were not prominent. MPK was even supporting the National Democratic Front. He even wrote articles calling King to intervene from country turning into single-party monopoly and urgent need for opposition. The Diciplinary Committee criticized his article without any actions but later MPK himself left the party. Tulsi Giri resigned from his Ministerial position at the end fof August without good explanation. Despite lots of opposition NC still emerged victorious in by-election and municipal election. In 1960 by-election it won two out of three seats while it emerged the largest party in municipal election. However the popularity might have reduced a little by the Gorkha Case. Ad-hoc Opposition Groups: The ad-hoc opposition were the landlords and merchants who faced new taxation and land reforms. Students were one of the strongest opposition of the government especially in Kathmandu though over time they had turned into appendages of political parties. However over nationalist issues students were united whether in opposing Gandak Treaty or Mt. Everest issue. At the time Congress also organized its own Youth wing called Nepal Tarun Dal and helped it become a driver of socialistic movement. Opposition criticized governemnt mainly regarding budget allocation and "Congressization" of administrative machinery. And whenever the opposition ran out of issues it would fall back on allegation of "corrupt conduct" by Ministers. The corruption was actually reduced partly due to fear from opposition and partly due to the realization of facing 1964 election for political mandate.

events.title: Nehru Visited Nepal
events.detail: Just two weeks after the installation of the Nepali Congress Cabinet Prime Minister Nehru of India paid a three-day official visit to Kathmandu.BP and Nehru affirmed an "identity of views" of the two countries whose policies both in the international and in the domestic sphere were "animated by similar ideals and objectives."

events.title: Tribhuvan University Inagurated
events.detail: Nepal National Education Commission was formed to formulate a new national education system which suggested to establish a Nepal National University. The commission had recommended that the university be established in Sheetal Niwas. Later King Tribhuvan's two wives Kananti Rajya Lakshmi and Ishwari Rajya Lakshmi jointly announced the establishment of Tribhuvan University. It was announced that they would chair the commission themselves. The members of the commission included the then Prince Himalaya Prince Basundhara the King's private secretary Sardar Hansman Singh Khadganar Singh Rana Director of the Education Department Sharada Prasad Upadhyap Mir Subba Bhairav ​​Bahadur Pradhan and Laxmi Prasad Devkota. Laxmi Prasad Devkota was in charge of finding location for the university and Kirtipur was chose. Both queens had donated 375 ropanis of land in Lalitpur which later occupied the Institute of Engineering (IOE) under TU. On the occasion of the 52nd birth anniversary of the late King Tribhuvan the foundation stone of the building was laid at Tanglatar Kirtipur on Jun 25 1959. Some time after the establishment of the university it was mentioned that an engineering school would be established. After the establishment of that school nursing and dentistry were also included in the plan. The plan mentioned that 12 lakh rupees would be spent to start the university's programs. Tribhuvan University Act was promulgated establishing it as a self-governing and corporate institution with perpetual succession. Patna University in India used to conduct the intermediate and undergraduate examinations for Tribhuvan University. The MA examination was started by Tribhuvan University itself. In 1960 the results of IA ISC ICOM BA BSC and BCOM were made public by Tribhuvan University. From 1961 all examinations were conducted by Tribhuvan University itself. Till then there were 35 Nepalese and 20 Indian professors in the college. After the New Eduaction Plan of 1971 all the government colleges of Nepal became the affiliate college of TU.

events.title: Enacted the Birta Abolition Act in 1959
events.detail: It transformed Birta lands into "Raikar" lands. For the Nepali Congress party this law was the key frontal attack on Nepal's "feudal" economy.

events.title: Gandak Treaty
events.detail: India construct Nepal Gandak Western Canal (to irrigate an area of 8700 ha. land in Nepal); Western Gandak Canal and Main Eastern Canal; India to construct 15MW power plant in MWC and Nepal was entitled 10MW but current production capacity is between 3MW to 4 MW only; Nepal retains full sovereignty and territorial control. It was estimated at more than 500 million Indian rupees

events.title: Pokhara Municipality Established
events.detail: The city then had as many as 5,000 people. When the municipality was initially established with 13 wards, a proper local election infrastructure had not yet been set up for Pokhara. Its boundary area in east was from the foot of Kahu through Kahun Kholo to Dhunge Sanghu and Kazi Pokhari. In the west it extended from Pardi Dam to the other bank of Fewa, and from the foot of Banpale's nose, along the edge of Bulaudi Dam, along the foot of Dharapani and foot of Dhunge Khola Markeni Hill to the Firke Kulo's Dam. In the north it extended from Firke Kula Dam to the hill leading to Byasi's Khirrapokhari Kaski and along the edge of Miruwa, along the edge of Dhungekhani, the old Tundikhel, along Kali Khola and Seti Dobhan. And, in the west it extended from Kazi Pokhari to Chor Sanghu and directly to West Pardi Dam. To manage the city's transition and early administrative growth, the BP Koirala government handpicked social worker Shiva Bahadur Thapa to serve as the chief administrator/mayor.

events.title: Nepal's Dependency on Aid
events.detail: The average aid to GDP ratio of a mere 2% in 1960s to around 10% by the 1990s. Till mid-1960s Nepal was entirely dependent on foreign aid to carry out all of its development projects.

events.title: US Aid's Priority Changes in Nepal
events.detail: Aid received by Nepal also underwent significant shifts in donors’ approach and interest areas as seen by the US’ withdrawal from road infrastructure in the 1960s and a shift towards governance agriculture health services and malaria eradication and grassroots development from thereon. One of the reasons for this was also the imposition of the autocratic Panchayat system by King Mahendra which resulted in aid and projects being diverted towards politically expedient areas. ‘With USAID withdrawal of funds for panchayat grants and increasing domination of the Panchayat system USAID reduced administrative support for the [Panchayat Development] program and lost interest in the ineffective policy dialogue with HMG. Although the US remained Nepal’s largest donor until the mid-1960s its rapprochement with Communist China in the late 1960s and its continued involvement in the Vietnam War resulted in the US viewing Nepal as inessential in its global contest against the Soviet regime. ‘Washington’s relative contribution declined from 40% of Nepal’s total aid during 1962-65 to 23% during 1970-75 and further to about 12% during 1976-85.

events.title: Balaju Industrial Estate Established
events.detail: Balaju Industrial Area was Nepal's first industrial estate established in 1960 through a joint effort between the government of Nepal and the United States government. Spanning over 670 ropanis of land in Kathmandu it functions as a centralized hub providing essential infrastructure like land roads electricity and drainage for various manufacturing and production industries. The Balaju Industrial Estate houses approximately 134 to 141 industries including DDC Nebico Biscuits etc.

events.title: Nepal Christian Fellowship Founded
events.detail: As scattered house fellowships emerged, leaders recognized the urgent need for structural cohesion, spiritual defense, and collective leadership. The Nepal Christian Fellowship (NCF) was formed in 1960 to serve as a singular network for these isolated groups. In 1992, the organization officially dropped "Christian" and added "Churches" to its moniker, becoming the National Churches Fellowship of Nepal (NCFN). This changed its operating dynamic from a loose network of individuals into an official, structured corporate council representing hundreds of indigenous denominations.

events.title: BP's first visit to China
events.detail: Chinese claimed Mt. Everest; BP koirala protested; revealed in parliament it just before Zhou Enlai's Nepal visit in April. Zhou Enlai told Koirala Chinese aid did not match the Indian aid amount because ‘That may not be good for you or for us . . . India may become wary if we give you too much assistance . . . the international community would take it that we are trying to compete with India’.

events.title: Nepal-China Boundary Agreement
events.detail: Recognised China's sovereignty over Tibet; Nepal transferred 1836 sq km of land to China while China transferred 2139 sq km to Nepal resulting in a net gain of 303 sq km for Nepal; though the treaty was signed BP Koirala was surprised when Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai claimed that Mount Everest belonged entirely to China presenting historical maps showing the peak inside Chinese territory. BP koirala strongly protested then but kept it private untill Zhou Enlai's Nepal visit. Later in 1962 agreement was signed to share Everest.

events.title: Nepal's Exchange Rate was Fixed 1960
events.detail: NPR 160= INR 100

events.title: Kings Trip to Japan US and Canada
events.detail: King Mahendra accompanied by a large personal and official retinue including Deputy Prime Minister Suvarna Shamsher visisted Japan (April 18-15). Then his entourage flew for US where he addressed the US Congress on April 28. At the time Rishikesh Shah was the Nepali Ambassador to the United States. King Mahendra began his state visit to Canada on May 25. In a press conference he said "Wherever the communists are not banned but are allowed to work openly they have made slow progress". After completing his official visits King Mahendra left for Nepal on June 16 with visits to Lisbon Paris Frankfurt Vienna Tehran Kabul Srinagar and New Delhi on the way and arrived in Kathmandu on July 28.

events.title: Zhou Enlai's Nepal Visit
events.detail: It was part of China's effort to strengthen Sino-Asian-African solidarity promote the Panchasheel of Bangdung Conference and counter both Western imperialism and Soviet influence. He visited six Asian and ten African nations in early 1960s. Nepal selected Pokhara as the meeting place likely to avoid protests in Kathmandu over Everest issue. But due to safety concern over Nepal's aircraft it was asked to make a test flight. The aircraft actually broke down upon landing in Pokhara. In the end Nepal had to borrow a small plane from the Indian Air Force to transport Zhou and a limited number of delegates to Pokhara. On the evening of April 28 back in Kathmandu Zhou Enlai and B.P. Koirala signed the historic “Treaty of Peace and Friendship between China and Nepal” and formally exchanged ratification documents concerning the boundary agreement. Regarding the Mt. Everest issue Zhow said in a press conference that China accepted the Map given by Nepal and according to the Map southern slope belongs to Nepal and northern slope to China. And they accepted that the peak belonged to Nepal. Shortly after the trip Zhou recognized the need for linguistically trained Chinese officials in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Hence a group of recent high school graduates were dispatched to study Nepali in Tibet under his instruction. Among them was Zeng Xuyong who would eventually become the only fluent in Nepali language Chinese ambassador to Nepal and would have to navigate the chaos after the Royal Massacre before he concluded his time in Nepal.

events.title: Sino-Nepalese Treaty of Peace and Friendship
events.detail: Signed in Kathmandu by Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai and Nepalese Prime Minister B.P. Koirala. Both nations formally recognized and pledged to respect each other’s independence sovereignty and territorial integrity.

events.title: NC Seventh General Convention
events.detail: BP Koirala; The general convention held in Kathmandu elected BP Koirala as the president for the second time. BP(5973 votes) won against a token candidacy of Bhudeo Rai (865 votes). Shreebhadra Sharma and Tripurbar Singh Pradhan were elected as General Secretary.

events.title: Clash at Kora La Pass of the Mustang
events.detail: Chinese troops opened fire on Nepali border guards killing one and ten were taken prisoner. BP vocally opposed it and Zhou Enlai issued a letter condemning the incident. Immediately the prisoners were released and compensation to the dead man's family was paid. This time again Communists were conciliatory towards China praising Zhou Enlai's letter.

events.title: BP's Israel Trip
events.detail: After the establishment of the diplomatic relationship between Israel and Nepal on June 1st 1960 BP Koirala met Prime Minister of Israel David Ben Gurion in Tel Aviv and spoke at the Weizmann Institute of Science. The State of Israel opened its Embassy in Kathmandu in March 1961. His visit officially formalized full diplomatic ties between Nepal and Israel making Nepal the first South Asian country to do so.

events.title: Treaty of Trade and Transit with India
events.detail: Recognition of Nepal's Tariff Autonomy: Nepal gained greater flexibility to pursue an independent industrial and tariff policy. Export Promotion: Allowed Nepal to provide incentives for domestic industries and exports. Control of Re-exports: Measures introduced to prevent foreign goods from entering India through Nepal to exploit tariff differences. Excise Refund System: Indian excise duties collected on exports to Nepal were refunded/transferred to Nepal under establishing the Duty Refund Procedure (DRP) using AR1 form.

events.title: BP in US Attending UN General Assembly
events.detail:
BP spoke in UN General assembely and had sideline talk with President Eisenhower. Themes of BP's UNGA Address:

1. Non-alignment: He does not define non-alignment as neutrality. Instead he says that we do not align beforehand. He argues that every issue should be judged independently. Instead of automatically calling America is always right or USSR is always right he says that we judge every issue individually. That is intellectually sophisticated. He asserts for moral independence saying that we do not want anyone to tell us how to think. He is not only rejecting military domination but also rejects ideological domination propaganda and intellectual dependence. In his point of view political independence means nothing without freedom of judgment. He also talks about how small states have comparative advantages in foreign policy. Large states have alliances military commitments and ideological obligations. Small states have fewer commitments. Therefore they can think more objectively. This is almost a comparative advantage theory of diplomacy. He never claims small countries are morally superior. He carefully says: We merely have fewer commitments. That intellectual humility strengthens his argument. He even gives evidences of Nepal'snon-alignment. Nepal supported criticism of Anglo-French-Israeli Suez intervention. While India abstained Nepal formally denounced the Soviet armed intervention in Hungary. Nepal took a neutral stance during the 1958 Lebanon crisis and favored direct UN deployment over unilateral Western military interventions. When the UN established the United Nations Observation Group in Lebanon (⁠UNOGIL) Nepal eagerly volunteered. Five Nepalese military observers were dispatched to Beirut in 1958 marking the historical birth of Nepal's ⁠UN Peacekeeping contributions. Nepal strictly backed impartial UN operations during the 1960 Congo Crisis to safeguard the newly independent nation's territorial integrity against foreign mercenarism and domestic secession. Nepal strongly endorsed the mandates of the United Nations Operation in the Congo (⁠ONUC).

2. Defense of the United Nations: BP does not merely praise the UN. He wants it transformed into something much stronger. He proposes stronger UN global peace force international development authority greater administrative capacity and more economic coordination. This resembles early ideas of global governance. He sees the UN as evolving toward a stronger international institution rather than remaining merely a forum for sovereign states. This is genuine strategic autonomy.

3. Support for Decolonization and China: He supports Algeria independence African independence PRC representation Mongolia and Congo's territorial integrity. He frames every issue as subject of self-determination rather than Cold War ideology. It is consistent with democratic socialism and anti-colonial internationalism. In 1960 most Western countries refused to recognize the PRC at the UN. BP argued that the UN cannot be universal while excluding 630 million people. This is one of the speech's strongest examples of realism rather than ideological alignment.

4. Democracy and Socialism: He argues that real peace requires development poverty reduction and technological transfer rather than only military balance. Political liberty alone cannot function in a vacuum. Economic progress is equally necessary. He boasts that Nepal has adopted liberal values preserved through free elections. According to him Nepal chooses democracy but that does not require joining the Western bloc. He separates political system from foreign policy alignment.

5. Idealism: The main weakness of BP Koirala’s speech is its idealism. It places too much faith in the moral power of small states and the ability of the United Nations to overcome great-power rivalry. Proposals such as a stronger UN and a global peace force were visionary but difficult to achieve given the realities of Cold War politics national interests and the dominance of major powers.

events.title: King's Trip to London
events.detail: On October 17 the King and the Queen accompanied by a retinue including Deputy Prime Minister Suvarna Shamsher arrived in London to begin a three-day state visit the first ever made there by a Nepali monarch. Having completed the state visit King Mahendra stayed on for an additional two weeks inspecting educational establishments and industrial plants throughout the United Kingdom. He returned to Kathmandu on November 9. During his absence the police firing in Gorkha had occurred resulting in the reported loss of seven lives.

events.title: Gorkha and West No. 1 Unrest
events.detail: A new party called Karmabir Mahamandal was formed by Yogi Naraharinath which tried to register with the Election Commission six days before the candidate nomination deadline. But the EC refused. Karmabir Mahamandal appealed to the palace. King Mahendra issued a royal command instructing the EC to register the party. But the EC still declined and Karmabir Mahamandal could not contest the polls. Yogi Naraharinath was a staunch opponent of the parliamentary system and was in favor of Hindu nationalism and direct monarchy. The state-led land reform of NC government threatened lands held by religious trusts (Guthi and Birta grants given to temples and monasteries). As a nationalist yogi he viewed Koirala’s secular-leaning democratic policies and land redistribution as a dangerous "socialist" or "communist" encroachment on religious autonomy. He urged: “Do not pay taxes to the government. Do not hand over forests to it. We need to destroy this government. I am a close confidant of the king” He used to tell people and show them a letter from the palace as he tried to foment unrest in the name of Karmabir Mahamandal. He traveled to places like Gorkha weaponizing his status as a holy man to rally local populations against the land tax and property nationalization laws enacted by the Nepali Congres. On 25 October 1960 his disciples mounted an attack on the headquarters of Gorkha district. Their plan was to occupy the town and capture the chief officer. Security personnel retaliated and in the ensuring combat seven people lost their lives and many others were wounded. Yogi was arrested in the north-western district of Jumla four days after the Gorkha incident. After the coup King released him and he became a key ideological architect for King Mahendra's new Panchayat system crafting the intellectual framework that justified absolute royal rule by fusing the concept of Nepali nationalism with Hindu monarchy.He was also granted a permanent base at the sacred Gorakhnath Maṭha in Mrigasthali (Pashupatinath area)

events.title: Tenth Anniversary of 1950 Revolution
events.detail: The Nepali Congress government decided to commemorate the occasion by inaugurating development projects all over Nepal estimated to cost more than 10 crore rupees. King took part in some of inaguration programs where he got chance to taunt the governemnt "responsible persons should renounce their selfish interests and work honestly for the welfare of all or else they will be regarded as having fulfilled their selfish interests with the blood of brave persons."

events.title: King Mahendra’s Royal Coup
events.detail: Context: The Indian Army Chief General Thimayya arrived in Kathmandu on December 8 1960 for a one-week official visit. Suvarna Shamsher left for Calcutta on December 12 for personal reasons. The much-publicized Nepali Tarun Dal Conference attended by a number of delegates from foreign countries began its session on the morning of December 15. By evening of that fateful day all the members of the Nepali Congress Cabinet that were in Kathmandu had been arrested and King Mahendra had sounded the death knell of parliamentary democracy in a broadcast to the country over Radio Nepal. BP Koirala along with Speaker and other Ministers and Assistant Ministers were arrested and kept in Singhadurbar prison amid tight security. The government released some leaders after three months and transferred Prime Minister BP Koirala ministers Ganeshman Singh, Surya Prasad Upadhyaya, Ram Narayan Mishra, and Prem Raj Angdembe Speaker Krishna Prasad Bhattarai and assistance ministers Dibansingh Rai, Yogendraman Sherchan, and Jaman Singh Gurung among others to Sundarijal prison. Girija Prasad Koirala and other party leaders were kept in Nakkhu Jail. Royal Proclamation: King alleged NC government in his proclamation that it worked solely to advance party interest it attempted to paralyze administration encouraged corruption incapable of maintaining law and order and encouraged anti-national elements. He even went on alleging parliamentary system as climsy Western imposition incompatible with Nepal's tradition and history. Considerations of King: He was likely dissatisfied with his minor role in new governmental structure. He may have been suspecious that NC leaders were plotting eventual abolition of monarchy given NC leaders criticizing the constitution and opposition excessively warning King. He was also afraid of Gorkha Parishad being a weak opposition and close to NC. Support Groups of Coup: Most important support came from the landlords and merchants who were strongly opposed to NC government's land and taxation policy. Another was orthodox Hindus who were against NC's secular stance such as their refusal to apply caste provisions that Rana regime legalized. Given NC's alleged "pro-India" image "anti-India and pro-China" many Communists some students and young intellectuals were in the side of the King. The beureaucracy especially the royal palace secreteriat was in favor of King who had lost majority of their power and influence after the installation of parliamentary institutions. And the most important of all was the support from the army. A number of army officers were appointed to high positions in the civil administration immediately after coup. Similarly many opposition and dissident NC leaders who found building party bottom-up tiring and didn't have votor base sided with the King such as Dilli Raman Regmi, Tanka Prasad Acharya, Bhadrakali Mishra and Keshar Jung Rayamajhi. Outside Conditions: At the time there was a general pattern where democratically elected governments in new democracies and newly independent countries removed by coup. For example: Pakistan (1958): PM Firoz Khan Noon and president Iskander Mirza by General Ayub Khan; Turkey (1960): PM Adnan Menderes was replaced by General Cemal Gürsel; DRC (1960): President Lumumba was replaced by PM Joseph Iléo immpediately and later Mobutu Sese Seko seized power with coup; Korea (1961): PM Chang Myon was replaced by General Park Chung Hee; Burma (1962): President U Nu was replaced by General Ne Win; Ghana (1966): President Kwame Nkrumah was replaced by General Joseph Arthur Ankrah; Nigeria (1966): President Nnamdi Azikiwe was replaced by General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi. Indonesia (1967): President Suharto replaced by General Suharto. However Nepal's case was unique in two manners that unlike others coup was not primarily carried by the military and it did not establish any new leader after the coup it only consolidated the power of traditional King.

events.title: King Mahendra's Direct Rule
events.detail: Along with the proclamation he announced the formation of a new Council of Ministers with himself as chairman. Interestingly it included only Nepali Congress members or "independents". An unofficial ad hoc committee consisting of four high officials of the Central Secretariat was appointed shortly after the coup to consider institutional innovations. The committee was instructed to survey political institutions in Yugoslavia Egypt Pakistan and Indonesia to determine whether recent experiences in these countries might be instructive in the establishment of a "Nepali" political system. Approximately a year later another committee was appointed to draft a new Constitution. Before constitution was promulgated three separate but interdependent institutions had been created to provide the framework of the new political system: the four-tier panchayat (village district zonal and national) and class organization systems which were non-party mass organization and a National Guidance Ministry to supervise the entire system. Dr. Tulsi Giri (Ex-Congress) -- Foreign Affairs; Defence; Transport and Communications; Electricity and Irrigation; Palace Affairs Bishwabandhu Thapa (Ex-Congress)-- Home and Local Self-Government Rishikesh Saha (Ex-Nepali Rastriya Congress) -- Planning; Economic Affairs; Finance Surya Bahadur Thapa (Independent) -- Agriculture; Forests; Industry and Commerce Aniruddha Prasad Singh (Independent) -- Education; Health; Law and Justice; Parliamentary Affairs Four Assistant Ministers—Nageshwar Prasad Singh (Ex-Congress) Khagendra Jang Gurung Kazi Man Limbu and Bhuwan Lai Pradhan—were also appointed.

events.title: Indian Chinese And American Reaction to Coup
events.detail: India: The Indian press and political leaders issued immediate and unanimous denunciation of the coup. Nehru labeled allegations against the Nepali Congress as "vague charges" and characterized the coup as " a complete reversal of democratic process." Under the Koirala government Nehru commented "for the first time Nepal had some order of Government which was trying its best to improve things." India however didn't distance the King by signing four agreements of aid totaling 1.32 crores Indian rupees in April 1961 and continuing discussions on Gandak project. King also balanced foreign policy by having his mouthpieces in the cabinet. For instance Tulsi Giri potrayed himself as pro-Indian at beginning and Bishwabandhu Thapa as anti-India. Later Tulsi Giri turned anti-India and pro-China stance while Rishikesh Shah was soft towards India. It helped King to arouse anti-India sentiments at time to stigmatize NC as puppets of a foreign power. China: China maintained a discreet silence on the royal coup. Later Peking provided 1 Crore Indian rupees of aid and Rs. 2.5 Crore worth of commodities required for Chinese aid projects. Nepal-China Joint Boundary Commission was also underway and dismissal of BP didn't interefere its proceeding. Later in October 1961 the Sino-nepal Boundary Treaty was signed to settle dispute over Mt. Everest and other 11 areas. America: US made its disapproval known throufh diplomatic channels while public comment was extremely muted. It recounted that BP Koirala government had made strides towards social and economic reforms which was stalled by the political change.

events.title: Student Organization Post-Coup
events.detail: Nepal Chhatra Sangh was functioning under NC while Nepal Students' Federation(detailed info not available online) was under NCP. With the Royal take-over both of them found themselves missionless but the succeeding years proved to be comparatively favourable to their functioning. By 1962 a large number of student leaders of the pre-1960 vintage joined the Tribhuvan University and started working on their old political lines. Tribhuvan University Students’ Union (TUSU) was established in 1961. Navaraj Subedi (pro-Establishment) became the first president of TUSU winning over Tirtharam Dangol (pro-NC) while Daman Nath Dhungana(pro-NC) became the vice-president. The TUSU soon became a launching pad for the political activities of students. In May 1963 the agitation launched by the TUSU to protestagainst the expulsion of certain students from the University turned into a movementto demand the institution of an independent Students’ Union in every education alinstitution. The Government showed concern as the demand for autonomous unions clashed with the principle of National Guidance. Regardless various groups in the student community identified themselves by their overt and covert activities emerging as pro-Congress pro-Communist and pro-Establishment. Meanwhile there arose pro-China and pro-Soviet factions in the Communist party. The student organization also faced division leading to (pro-China) student group forming an organization called the Akhil Nepal Rashtra-vadi Svatantra Vidyarthi Union which managed to win 1963-64 TUSU election. Later in 1964-65 the NC-backed students; wrested the TUSU from the hands of communists. In May 1966 presumably by way of an answer to the ominous rise in the hostile political activities of student groups in the country the Government sponsored an organization called the Nepal Students’ Organization. A number of politically motivated student groups refused to join the officialorganization. This made it easy for pro-Moscow student leaders to infiltrate anddominate the Students’ Organization. The government held power to appoint the Secretary and the Treasurer but the popularly elected President and members largely protested against the regime. In April 1967 the Government dissolved this Nepal Students’ Organization.

events.title: Betrayal to BP and NC
events.detail:
Many NC leadres sided with the King taking important positions in Panchayat system First NC Cabinet Ministers: Bishwabandhu Thapa (Became first chairman of the Rastriya Panchayat) Parshu Narayan Chaudhary (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat; Chairperson of Royal Council) Bhadrakali Mishra (Chairperson of the Raj Parishad, 1991) Lalit Chand (Member of 1962 Rastriya Panchayat; Also became the Chairperson in 1968) Kashi Nath Gautam (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat without party's approval)

Other Senior Leaders: Shreebhadra Sharma Khanal (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat) Balchandra Sharma (first Vice-Chancellor of the Royal Nepal Academy in 1957; ambassador to France) Kedar Man Vyathit (Vice-Chancellor of the Royal Nepal Academy in 1969; Minister of Transport and Communications(1962); Home Minister (1979)) Rudra Prasad Giri (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat without party's approval) Bakhan Singh Gurung (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat without party's approval) Bhagwat Prasad Yadav (Member of 1981 Rastriya Panchayat without party's approval) Nageshwar Prasad Singh (Assistant Minister of Interim Mahendra Cabinet)

events.title: Political Rivalry Among Royalists and Internal Opposition
events.detail: KI SIngh: He was the most unstable of all. At first he welcomed banning of political parties later he demanded restoration of parliamentary system. In April 1963 he decided to launch a countrywide satyagraha demanding to lift ban of political parties and restore parliament. On 2 April King nominated him Chairman of the Council of State presumably to neutralize him from conducting opposition. However on 8 April when he saw that his rank was much below the Chairman of the Council of Ministers (Tulshi Giri) he demanded for himself a rank higher than the Chairman of the Council of Ministers claiming that the Council of State was a body higher than the Council of Ministers under the present constitutional provisions. Singh regarded Giri to be much inferior to him in political stature. When his stand was rejected by the King on 10 April Singh disdainfully refused the office maintaining that he had not been consulted by the King before making the offer. After his pressure tactics failed he once again declared that he would launch the satyagraha in March 1964 to get his demands fulfilled. On the eve of the satyagraha hes was arrested and was sentenced for 2 years of jail by special tribunal. Singh was acquitted on 14 June by Supreme Court and the satyagraha was never launched. Tanka Prasad Acharya: Since he was not given important portfolio in the post-coup government they proposed the King to form "country-wide nonpolitical organization on a democratic basis to counter anti-nationalists" however King rejected it. The proponents of this proposal were political actors like Dr. KI Singh Dilli Raman Regmi Tanka Prasad Acharya and Ranga Nath Sharma who had become déclassé after the 1960 take-over and were largely ignored by the public. The "Decembrists" : The most conspicuous individual opposition would be that of the triumvirate of the Decembrists Rishikesh Shah Tulsi Giri and Bishwabandhu Thapa that is the dramatis personae of the royal take-over effected in December 1960. Rishikesh Shah: The most vocal of them having the distinction of being the first and so far alone to remain in opposition was Rishikesh Shah. He stood for liberalization of the system; unrestricted exercise of intellectual and political freedoms; opening of the National Panchayat for the public; and broadening of the scope of the present election system for the National Panchayat. Despite his radical-seeming posture he was an aristocrat who struggled to connect with the masses. Tulsi Giri: Tulsi Giri's opposition was often directed at specific government policies or other leaders such as Surya Bahadur Thapa and served as a strategy to force the King to rehabilitate him in the power hierarchy. In June 1965 he challenged the continued detention of political prisoners (including B.P. Koirala) to corner the King despite having defended their detention while he was Chairman of the Council of Ministers just months earlier. His oppositional stance was perceived as opportunistic and he eventually returned to the establishment as a "zealot royalist" after failing to extract concessions. Bishwabandhu Thapa: Thapa was initially a tireless ideologue of the King's "all-encompassing" royal leadership. As his political fortunes dwindled he began to voice opposition to the partyless nature of the system he helped create even demanding the restoration of political parties. By 1966 he argued that without political parties the administration would drift toward dictatorship. Like Giri his oppositional activities were viewed as a ruse to regain relevance; he eventually returned to the regime becoming the Chairman of the King's "Back to the Village" campaign. Student and Peasant Organization: Hira Lai Bhandari who was member of banned left-wing Kisan Sangathan became central committee member of government-controlled Peasants' Organization. In one of its meetings held in Kathmandu in August 1963 he criticized the administration for incompetence graft nepotism and denial of justice. The panchayat loyalists within the organization called Bhandari's speech to be inconsistent with the policy of the organization and that disciplinary action would be taken against him. Summons were issued against Bhandari and was kept under detention. He was released in in October to be re-arrested soon after. Of the government-controlled Class Organizations those for peasants and students were often critical of the Government but their leaders were appeased in various ways. Ever recalcitrant as it appeared to be the Students' Organization was finally dissolved by the amended Constitution in 1967.

events.title: Civil Administration During Panchayat
events.detail: King Mahendra laid off employees about five months after overthrowing the elected government in a military coup. In 2018, 13 secretaries were removed at once. Many old employees, both gazetted and ungazetted, were dismissed. Among those removed from office in this reorganization was Yog Prasad Upadhyay, who later became a leader of the Nepali Congress and Home Minister. Another person removed from office was Krishna Prasad Ghimire, who was later appointed Attorney General. Governor of NRB, Himalaya Shumsher Jabra was also removed. During the reign of King Mahendra, there was a growing trend of inducting people from within the family or loyalists into government positions in the name of political appointments and development employees, and later making them permanent through the normal process through the Public Service Commission. It seems that an attempt was made to maintain the Panchayat system through the administration by making political appointments in the names of Zonal Administrators, Land Reform Officers, Panchayat Guidance Officers, etc. The king tried to run the bureaucracy. The government ministers were only nominal. Even the ministers were afraid of the secretaries who had good relations with the palace secretaries. PM Marichman had launched a 'complaint program'. After he got many complaints about a female land revenue officer he wrote to the king to remove her. But, he couldn't remove her as she was a distant relative of the palace. Those who recited poems in the king's riding camp were promoted by decree (Hukum Prabhagi). From allowing a Spanish-speaking person to enter the Foreign Service directly, to numerous other actions that went against the merit system, the decree was issued. Employees were repeatedly dismissed through pamphlets (parchs/notice) without giving them chance for formal inquiry. Later, after the Administrative Reforms Commission chaired by Bhesh Bahadur Thapa suggested stopping political appointments, political appointments to other positions except for the Zonal Commissioner were stopped. The pamphlet system existed until the beginning of the restoration of the multi-party system. The worst example of dismissal from the party on political grounds can be said to have been after the referendum. In 2037 BS, many employees were stripped of their positions on charges of supporting multi-party politics. In a center in Siraha, after the panchayat did not get a single vote, all the employees assigned there were dismissed. Action was also taken against the CDO. Moreover, even the Prime Minister could not make any major changes in the administration. The government could not do anything without the approval of the Chief District Officer or the Saruwa Durbar. The country was ruled by a dual system of government, i.e., a system of government run from two places (diarchy). Expressing dissatisfaction with this, former Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa had to go to jail for saying, "There is a dual regime in Nepal, one from Singha Durbar, the other from Narayanhiti Durbar." The CDO and Zonal Officers used their power to win the government candidates in the Panchayat elections. The people's representatives who were elected with the help of the administration could not even oppose the wrongdoings of the administrators. Land reform officers and Panchayat guidance officers had become permanent secretaries of important ministries and had reached the position of influencing the administration of Nepal. When promotions were made by decree, great injustice was done to those who were on the verge of promotion. Even the Public Service Commission was disrespected in these promotions and promotions. Even the Public Service Commission was informed after the removal through a pamphlet.

events.title: Education Data 1961
events.detail: By 1961 there were 400 primary schools 156 secondary schools and 33 higher secondary schools.

events.title: Nepal's Excessive Reliance in Foreign Assistance
events.detail: In 1961 Nepal’s internal revenue was USD 12.3 million; however its regular budget expenditure was USD 14.1 million while its development expenditure was USD 9.9 million. This shortfall in meeting budgetary targets meant Nepal had to continuously rely on foreign assistance as a way to meet its infrastructure goals i.e. 46.7% budget relied on foreign aid. Further aid reliance did not contribute towards Nepal’s economic growth during the Panchayat years with Nepal’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth between 1965-89 averaging only 0.6 percent.

events.title: Forest Act 1961 Inacted
events.detail: The Forest Act sought to restore government administration registration demarcation and control over national forests. It also defined the duties of the DoF listed forest offences and prescribed penalties as well. This acts also made provisions for handing over forest resources to the newly formed Panchyat which had far reaching consequences for local control of resources. The Act had four different types of forests. Panchayat Forests: Any part of government forests of Nepal which had been kept barren or contained only stumps that could be handed over by HMG/N to the care of the village Panchyats for the welfare of the village community on the prescribed terms and conditions. Panchayat Protected Forests: Any part of government forest of Nepal which could be handed over to the Panchayat for protection and management purposes. Religious Forests: A part of govt. forest located in any religious spot could be handed over to any religious institution for protection and management purposes. Contract Forests: Any patch of government forest which had neither trees nor sporadic trees could be handed over by HMG/N on contract basis to any individual or institution for the protection of forest products and their consumption but ownership of the forest land would remain with the government and control could be resumed whenever the government deemed it necessary. But the Act had only little impact on those forest areas that is distant from Kathmandu and inaccessible areas where local people continued to use the forests for subsistence needs regarded of their legal status and forest legislation. Similarly the government passed the Forest Protection Act-1967 that provided the forestry official judicial power. Ideologically until early 1970s the legal regime relating to forestry in Nepal was normally based on the Indian Forest Act-1927. It however had little impact on forest protection in the Hills where local people continued to use the forests for their needs despite their legal status.)

events.title: East-West Highway Construction Began
events.detail: Earlier the highway connecting the east-west region was only limited to postal highways during the Rana period. However this highway was not a fully paved or black-topped road. It was only limited to the Rapti river in the west and did not include the western districts of Banke Bardiya Kailali and Kanchanpur which were famously known as Naya Muluk. Nepalese were compelled to travel via Indian territory while visiting from one district to another district be it in Chitwan or Naya Muluk due to the dense forested region as well as north-south sans bridges. It was precisely to end this dependence on India that King Mahendra initiated the idea for an east-west highway. Due to lack of enough budget it was constructed with economic and technical assistance from various countries. King Mahendra had initially requested India to build this highway. However when India refused they sought the help of the Soviet Union. India was also attracted after the road from Dhalkebar to Pathalaiya was built by Soviet Union. In 1959 Soviet engineers conducted the very first geographic surveys for the proposed route. The highway was initially regarded as ‘not economically justified’ by USAID who refused to fund the estimated USD 70 million project. In 1961 King Mahendra officially inaugurated the construction of the highway. China offered to build a 100-mile stretch but geopolitical pressure from India forces Nepal to hand that segment over to New Delhi.

events.title: King's Royal Proclamation
events.detail: "As political parties may prove obstacles to the task of creating a favorable climate for this new movement of national reconstruction we have by this proclamation declared illegal and banned for the present all the existing political parties and class organizations affiliated with such parties... Since panchayats are the basis of democracy and a democratic system imposed from above has proved unsuitable . . . we have now to build democracy gradually layer by layer from the bottom upward. It is our aim to associate the people in the administration at all levels and to develop village district and municipal panchayats."

events.title: NC's Activity in Exile and Party Mergers
events.detail: A convention was held mid-january by approximately 150 political workers from the central Terai district of Birgunj who met in Raxaul (Bihar). Shortly thereafter several hundred Nepali Congress leaders and workers held an emergency secret convention in Patna. In that convention many leaders from other parties also joined the Nepali Congress. Among those who joined were Surendra Prasad Upadhyay (Chief Whip of the Nepal Rashtrabadi Gorkha Parishad in the dissolved parliament) Bhadrakali Mishra (President of the Nepal Praja Parishad—Mishra faction) Kashi Prasad Srivastava (General Secretary of the Sanyukta Prajatantra Party Nepal) and Ramjanam Tiwari (General Secretary of the Tarai Congress). Shortly thereafter, Bhadrakali Mishra was also appointed the General Secretary of the NC. The resolutions publicly adopted by the convention were comparatively mild in tone merely petitioning the King to reconvene Parliament and release political prisoners.

events.title: Subarna Shumsher Made Acting President of NC
events.detail: A conference was held in Patna that made Subarna Shumsher the Acting President of NC to coordinate party activities in exile.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip's First Nepal Trip
events.detail: Queen Elizabeth’s 1961 visit to Nepal was touch and go since it happened barely a year after King Mahendra’s coup in which he dissolved Nepal’s first democratically elected parliament, imprisoned Prime Minister B P Koirala and his cabinet, and ruled as an absolute monarch. The royal visit was seen by some as an endorsement of the coup, but this was during the height of the Cold War and tensions were also rising between India and China. The West regarded an assertive monarchy in Nepal as a stabilising factor in a volatile region, and for King Mahendra himself it was proof of international endorsement of his move. Carrying on the tradition of Nepal’s Rana rulers, the British royalty in 1961 was taken on a tiger hunt in Chitwan. The government went to extreme lengths to beautify Kathmandu and give it a modern look. What is today Kantipath in front of The Royal Hotel and the Tripureswar roads were widened by cutting down a row of jacaranda to impress the British visitors. Pretend street lights that did not work were erected along the way. The Royal Hotel’s Russian owner Boris Lissanevitch catered for the state banquet for the Queen hosted by King Mahendra at Singha Darbar.The next day, Edmund Hillary was knighted at a function at the British Embassy in Lazimpat. Queen Elizabeth had to cut a brown, green and white cake supposed to represent Mt Everest with two tiny marzipan figures representing Hillary and Tenzing on the summit.

events.title: Administrative Reorganization
events.detail: Government reorganized the traditional 32 districts into 75 districts 14 administrative zones to streamline local governance. Districts were led by Chief District Officers (CDOs) representing the bureaucracy of central government. It was responsible for administration security revenue collection and implementation of government policies. Zones were led by Zonal Commissioner (Anchaladhish) whose task was to supervise districts coordinate CDOs maintain law and order monitor Panchayat implementation and report to Kathmandu. In 1965 all the Bada Hakims were removed and their responsibility was transfered to the Zonal Commissioners.

events.title: Surya Prasad Upadhyaya Released
events.detail: All warrants for arrest issued on political grounds since the December coup were canceled and Surya Prasad Upadhyaya was released from prison. Later he was nominated the member of Council of State though he rejected reportedly because of their unhappiness at not having been included on the Standing Committee.

events.title: Nepal joins International Monetary Fund
events.detail: IMF

events.title: Gorkha Parishad Merges with Nepali Congress
events.detail: Bharat Shumsher who was arrested along with other leaders was released after three months by issuing statement of support to Panchayat. However when he later got chance to travel abroad he visited the Rome session of the Socialist International and then went to India. In India he denounced the royal regime in Nepal and pledged cooperation with the Nepali Congress to overthrow it. A month later he announced the merger of the party with the Nepali Congress. After the joining of Bharat Shumsher by Feb 1962 the raids were better planned were carried out on a larger and more ambitious scale and at times seemed to be genuinely revolutionary in character.

events.title: King Mahendra's Participation in NAM Conference and Pakistan Visit
events.detail: In September 1961 King Mahendra participated in conference of the heads of nonaligned states at Belgrade where he emphasized emphasized "non-intervention and non-interference in the internal affairs of nations." . Leaving Belgrade the King visited Pakistan for the first time.

events.title: King Mahendra's China Visit
events.detail: King went on a 17-day state visit to China and Outer Mongolia. Sino-Nepal Boundary Treaty was signed by the King during the visit which drew the alignment at the trijunctures in conformity with the watershed principles as suggested by India. New Delhi officially welcomed the boundary agreement and suggested that the application of the same principles to the Sino-Indian dispute would facilitate a solution. On the last day of his visit suddenly China presented draft on Kathmandu-Tibet Road Agreement i.e. Araniko Highway which was not raised by either side before. To avoid political fallout Tulsi Giri signed the agreement rather than King Mahendra. The King intentionally omitted his name anticipating that the highly controversial document would trigger severe diplomatic backlash from India. China made it covertly clear that if King Mahendra did not agree to build the road it would back out of or stall the highly anticipated border treaty. Having been badly outmaneuvered for once the King was in no position to resist the pressure. China wanted to urgently sign this road agreement because Tibet was facing New Delhi's 1960 ban on trade in strategic goods citing the border conflict while the existing routes to Tibet from China were harsh and faced disturbance from Khampa rebels. Therefore using Nepal's route it could quickly and cheaply import surplus rice manufactured goods and essential supplies like petrol. Nehru registered his dissatisfaction in the Parliament over the agreement. Comforting India and West's concern over the agreement King at the inauguration of the india-built Pardi Dam in Pokhara in November 1961 famously said that “Communism won’t come here in a taxi.” Later Nepal itself imposed a limited ban on the exportation of strategic goods—including iron products cement petrol kerosene and coal—to Tibet on December 6 1961. Five months later Nepal agreed to extend the ban to include Indian-produced goods imported into Nepal. This left a wide divergence in the two governments' trade policies however as goods imported into Nepal from third countries could still be transhipped to Tibet if they were not on the banned list. The survey works undertook in early 1962 proposing two routes over Rashuwagadhi and Tatopani. Though Rashuwagadhi route was 20km shorter Nepal opted with Tatopani route likely hoping to prolong the construction period as much as possible.

events.title: Tulsi Giri vs Rishikesh Shah
events.detail: Concerning NC prisoners Rishikesh Shah was in favor of releasing the prisoners if they agreed to cooperate with the new regime while Tulsi Giri was not in that line. In foreigh relation too Rishikesh Shah was moderate towards both India and China while Tulsi Giri was fierce towards India and leaned towards China.

events.title: Sino-Nepal Boundary Treaty
events.detail: King Mahendra of Nepal and Chairman Liu Shaoqi of China signed treaty delimiting and mapping the 1414 kilometer border between the two countries resolving all outstanding territorial disputes. The treaty drew the border directly across the peak of Mount Everest dividing the summit between the two nations.

events.title: NC Begins Its Second Armed Struggle
events.detail: After the conference in Patna Nepali congress had two factions. The moderates led by Subarna Shumsher had a goal of convincing King on release of prisoners and restoration of the Parliament. The radicals were led by Bharat Shumdher who believed in full-scale armed revolt aimed at deposition of the King and if possible abolistion of monarchy. As King was against lifting ban of political parties talks failed eventually. The moderates and the radicals came to agreement that it would be wise to revolt in few strongholds and capture those forcing King to come in negotiation. For this purpose Nepal was divided into Eastern Central and Western regions. Responsibilities were assigned to Keshav Prasad Koirala Nona Koirala Girija (following his release) CK Prasai and Bhawani Bikram Limbu in the East; and to Beni Bahadur Karki, Shashi Shamsher, Saroj Prasad Koirala, Rameshwar Babu, Tej Bahadur Amatya, Bakhan Singh Gurung, and Sheikh Idris among others in the Central region. In the West responsibilities were entrusted to Diwakar Sharma, Ganesh Kumar Sharma, Kashi Prasad Srivastava, Kashi Nath Gautam, and Achyut Raj Regmi among others. Camps for military training were subsequently established at ten locations across India spanning from east to west. These camps were set up in Naxalbari, Forbesganj, Darbhanga, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Balrampur, Tanakpur, Pithoragarh, and Jhulaghat. Guerrilla training and the stockpiling of weapons began at these sites. Gandhian Pacifist Faction: A faction within party stood agaisnt the armed struggle and decided to remain in Nepal struggline with quiet defiance, and underground networks to keep the democratic spirit alive. Those leaders were, Surya Prasad Upadhyaya, Mahendra Narayan Nidhi, Ramhari Joshi, etc.

events.title: Relation With India Deteriorated
events.detail: While India had reservation regarding road agreemnt with China Nepal was constantly pressuring India to take legal action over political refugees. After the Janakpur Bomb Incident Nepal King Mahendra stated on February 6 that India had been asked "to surrender these people" but New Delhi replied that this would be illegal so long as they had not violated Indian laws. In a curious tactical by-play on January 31 a spokesman of the Nepali Foreign Ministry announced that "unidentified aircraft" were dropping arms to Tibetian rebels in the Mustang area. The Nepali army was incapable of handling the well-armed Khampas on its own he blandly declared and if the Chinese should feel threatened by the rebels and should demand the right to send troops into Nepal to bring the Tibetians under control there was little Kathmandu could do but comply with the request. India immediately fearing Chinese troops to come to Nepal offered its help to come to Nepal's assistance. The issue was dropped later only after Nepal denied the accuracy of the original statement by their own official.

events.title: Communist Party of Nepal (Burma) Formed
events.detail: The party emerged from a split in the Communist Party of Nepal (Rayamajhi Group) in 1962 representing the pro-Soviet sector of the party. The third congress stated that the Soviet Union was the international centre of socialism and condemned the positions of China. The congress called for a peaceful political struggle in Nepal and condemned the idea of armed struggle as 'adventurism'. The congress branded the rival CPN of Tulsi Lal Amatya and Pushpa Lal Shrestha as 'extremist'.

events.title: King Mahendra's Assasination Attempt
events.detail: While King was in his eastern Terai tour in Janakpur a 21-years old young NC cadre Durgananda Jha threw a bomb to his motorcade. King was not injured and he continued with his tour as if nothing had happened. Jha soon went into exile in India but did not think it right to be in exile when 59 people were arrested and beaten up in the name of the bomb incident while he was preparing for various movements and therefore returned to Nepal. He was detained at Parbaha Railway Station as soon as he returned and put in Central Jail in Sundhara Kathmandu. He was hanged in February 1964. Few NC-inspired uprisings began in the September of 1961 which government ignored calling it "dacoit" (bandit) gang. When the attacks continued and became more obviously political in character such as Janakpur Bomb incident the government completely reversed its position calling it "anti-national" and starting killing.

events.title: Bharatpur Capture Incident
events.detail: On February 8 at exactly 12 o'clock in the night the Mukti Sena reached Bharatpur for capture. The Bharatpur administration easily surrendered the Gaindagasti camp the Rapti Dun Project office and the Jhuwani police station. But not more than 48 hours of the capture the Army sent from Kathmandu recaptured the Mukti Sena while it was celebrating its victory in a field near the Deuti Khola in Bharatpur. The army captured 11 members of the Mukti Sena. Three people were shot and killed there. The others were dragged from there and taken to the Tikauli Jungle and brutally killed except Jagat Prakash Jung as he was from royal family. However Jagat Prakash did not surrender. He was then returned to Chitwan and his limbs were gradually cut off his body without limbs was thrown into a pit and beheaded. Then his head was brought to the palace as proof of the murder. On Feb 10 a shootout between Royal Army and Mukti Sena was reported in the Chitwan Guest House killing more NC revolutionaries. Some were taken to Narayani riverside near Pulchowk and buried and rest were buried in the Guest House Ground. In total approximately 34-85 people were killed. 18 people identified so far are: 1 Hari Prasad Gurung 2) Jagat Prakashjang Shah 3) Laldhwaj Gurung 4) Saravsingh Gurung 5) Shamsherbahadur Gurung 6) Tekbahadur Gurung 7) Hastabir Gurung 8) Bharat Gurung 9) Khembahadur Gurung 10) Imansingh Gurung 11) Buddhasinh Rana 12) Khambasingh Tamang 13) Singhbahadur Tamang 14) Chechchhu Tamang 15) Tulbahadur Tamang 16) Panchu Gurung 17) Rambahadur Tamang 18) Ashbahadur Lama; Those made to disappear during that movement: 1) Sriharsha Khanal 2) Baikuntha Adhikari 3) Khadagsingh Gurung 4) Tekbahadur Gurung 5) Babulal Thing Tamang 6) Deubahadur Tamang 7) Dhwajbahadur Golay Tamang 8) Bhuvan Lama 9) Rambilas Yadav 10) Baldev Yadav 11) Bhola Sah Kanu 12) Suleman Miya 13) Chandrabahadur Praja 14) Bhimbahadur Praja 15) Buddhiman Tamang. Among the dead, Hari Prasad Gurung of Lwang Ghalel was the same person under whom Hari Chowk is named. In April 2 the government issued a statement announcing the confiscation of the assets of 30 individuals including Nepali Congress leaders Subarna Shamsher, Bharat Shamsher, Keshav Raj Pindali, Nara Bahadur Thapa, Shashi Shamsher, Yog Prasad Upadhyay, Bhadrakali Mishra, Saroj Prasad Koirala, and Dwarika Devi Thakurani. Many party cadres deployed across the country began to be arrested. Some even lost their lives in clashes with the police and the Royal Army.)

events.title: Sajha Yatayat Founded
events.detail: ⁠Sajha Yatayat was founded on March 16, 1962, as a cooperative public transport organization in Nepal. It was created to provide cheap, safe, and reliable public bus services for the Kathmandu Valley, and was established under the Cooperatives Act of 1959 with majority government support and a founding chairman named Bishwabandhu Thapa. It started its operation in July 16, 1962, running its first fleet of Tata Mercedes-Benz buses in Kathmandu. Since 2016 Sajha Yatayat has expanded its network and provides long haul bus service to Baglung, Gorkha, Birgunj and Lumbini.

events.title: Constitution Drafting Committee Announced
events.detail: King announched Rishikesh Shah as the head of the drafting committee. An Intellectual's Conference of 139 delegates was called in June to deliberate on the various problems confronting the country impartially and decide a path forward. Rishikesh Shah lauded the delegates vowing that government will reform itself in regards to the criticisms and while Tulsi Giri commented that no such discussions were made in the cabinet.

events.title: CPN's Third National Convention and Split (Pro-Russia or Pro-China? The CPN Splits )
events.detail: Dr. Keshar Jung Rayamajhi who had majority i.e. 11 of 17 in the CWC drifted to the right by supporting the King’s actions contravening decisions made at the secret Darbhanga Plenum demanding the reconvening of the dissolved Parliament. In response an Inter-Zone Coordination Committee was formed in August 1961 chaired by Tulsilal Amatya. Amatya coordinated with Pushpa Lal in India and attempted to unite him with the imprisoned Manmohan Adhikari. Following the committee's decision the CPN held its Third General Convention in Varanasi India. This convention adopted Amatya's program of 'National Democracy' and elected him as General Secretary. In the aftermath of the convention a global ideological schism between pro-Soviet and pro-Chinese communist lines permeated the party. As the debate intensified leaders took opposing sides: Tulsilal (pro-Soviet) published 'Which Way?' and Pushpa Lal (pro-China) responded with 'The Main Path'. Amatya favoured the idea of national democracy, whereas Pushpa Lal advocated the line of people's democracy. The internal conflict culminated in 1968 when Pushpa Lal held a separate third national conference of Maoist contingent in Gorakhpur India. The party then split into the Communist Party of Nepal (Amatya), Communist Party of Nepal (Rayamjhi), and Communist Party of Nepal (Pushpa Lal). In 1971 when the East Pakistan crisis erupted China backed Pakistan but Pushpa Lal chose to support the India-backed liberation of Bangladesh. Because his geopolitical actions aligned with India rather than Beijing the true pro-China hardliners within his own party (like Narayan Man Bijukchhe) rebelled against him accusing Pushpa Lal of being a fake Maoist.

events.title: Nehru-Mahendra Meeting Unsuccessful
events.detail: Through the meeting King Mahendra wanted assurance from Nehru that it wouldn't allow NC to carry out its activity from India. However Nehru sticked with his old line proposing solution based on compromise between King and the NC which was of course rejected by the King. Later in a press conference Nehru told that Indian soil could not be used to mount raids on Nepal but that "peaceful agitation" by Nepali exiles "can be carried on here." In case of the road agreement Mahendra concluded that it was too late for Nepal to go back.

events.title: Cabinet Reshuffle
