events.detail: Approximately 3 weeks after the tussle between Shah and Giri King introduced drastic changes in cabinet portfolios and even expanded the size. Under the new allocation Tulsi Giri was given the more prestigious title of Vice-Chairman of the Council but was divested of the important Foreign and Home Ministries. Rishikesh Shah became Foreign Minister but lost the Finance and Economic Planning portfolio. Bishwabandhu Thapa was given back the Home Ministry and Surya Bahadur Thapa now inherited the Finance and Economic Affairs portfolio. Several new Ministers and Assistant Ministers were added. Tulsi Giri --Vice-Chairman Rishikesh Shah Bishwabandhu Thapa Surya Bahadur Thapa Aniruddha Prasad Singh Lalit Chand -- New (Ex-NC leader of Kailali-Kanchanpur) Nageshwar Prasad Singh Bhuwan Lai Pradhan Kirtinidhi Bishta Vedananda Jha --New (President of NC splinter Terai Congress from Brigunj) Giri Prasad Budathoki Khadga Bahadur Singh Kaji Man Kandangawa Shailendra Kumar Upadhyaya -- New (Leader of Communist Party connected to Keshar Jang Rayamajhi) Prem Bahadur Shakya

events.title: Second Three-Year Plan
events.detail: NPR 600 million; ~62% from aid; ~89% execution rate; 12 PEs established; 920 km of roads built against a 1,600 km target; Trishuli and Panauti Hydroelectric Projects initiated; Kathmandu-Hetauda ropeway upgraded; Biratnagar airport expanded; 16,000 hectares of additional land irrigated; Cooperative Bank established; Rapti Valley development project scaled up; National Education System foundational work; over 1,200 new primary schools opened; major land reform program (Land Reform Act 2021 BS) introduced; industrial corridors formalized; transport and communications absorbed roughly 39% of total expenditure; industry and commerce received 14%; social services received about 13%; high implementation success compared to the First Plan; successfully bridged severe data and baseline statistical gaps.

events.title: Second Failed Attempt to Improve Relation With India
events.detail: Quiet diplomat Rishikesh Shah was brought to the Foreign Ministry to improve relation with India to keep Nepali Congress leaders in India under strict supervision and if feasible to arrange their repatriation to Nepal. On September 4 Rishikesh Shah flew to New Delhi and had talks with Nehru but he couldn't succeed. Nehru told journalists that India could not prohibit Nepali refugees from expressing their views in India peacefully and advised King Mahendra to improve the situation by conducting "friendly negotiations" with the rebels. As the plan failed on September 22 Rishikesh Shah and Aniruddha Prasad Singh were relieved from their position. Tulsi Giri once again took over the Foreign Ministry and his close ally Bishwabandhu Thapa inherited Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Ministry.

events.title: India Imposes Undeclared Blockade
events.detail: To escalate its support of the Nepali rebels India imposed an unofficial and undeclared economic blockade of Nepal in late September. A number of minor incidents on the border were used to rationalize a total interruption of trade rela- tions between the two countries. For several days the flow of essential commodities into Nepal was halted although no formal ban was placed on their exportation. Kathmandu's vehement almost hysterical response to this new tactic was a reflection of its vulnerability to such pressure. King Mahendra was placed in a situation in which he would have had to make major concessions to the Indians and the Nepali Congress for alternative sources of supplies were not available. However to King's rescue came the Sino-Indian War that dramatically soared his bargaining power.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.detail: Khrushchev placed the covertly built medium- and intermediate-range ballistic nuclear missile sites in Cuba to deter future American invasions of Cuba (following the failed 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion). To balance out U.S. nuclear missiles stationed near the USSR in Turkey and Italy. President Kennedy ordered a naval "quarantine" to stop Soviet ships on October 22. On October 27 U.S. forces dropped non-lethal depth charges to force a Soviet submarine to surface unaware it carried a nuclear torpedo. A nuclear launch was narrowly avoided because Soviet officer Vasili Arkhipov refused to authorize it. On October 28 1962 Kennedy and Khrushchev reached a secret compromise that successfully averted a global war. While USSR dismantled its nuclear weapon sites in Cuba US publicly promised never to invade Cuba. Mao criticized Khrushchev on two main fronts of "Adventurism" and "Capitulationism". First Mao believed putting nuclear missiles in Cuba in the first place was a reckless poorly planned gamble. Second he argued that Khrushchev had "kowtowed" or surrendered to American imperialism. Mao famously mocked Khrushchev's retreat by stating that the Soviet leadership had transitioned from "adventurism to capitulationism". He used this event domestically to launch propaganda campaigns proving that China—not the USSR—was the true leader of the global communist revolution.

events.title: Nepal-Pakistan Trade and Transit Treaty
events.detail: The Trade and Transit Treaty was signed providing for mutual most-favored-nation treatment. This was viewed in Kathmandu as a major contribution to the economic diversification program as a counter to Indian blockade. However the development of that trade depended upon Indian cooperation in making transport and travel facilities available and this has been the subject for discussion between New Delhi and Kathmandu on several occasions since 1963. India insisted upon the imposition of service charges that were estimated to amount to only Rs. 15000 per year but a compromise settlement was accepted three months later. Soon 1965 Indo-Pakistani war brought that trade to halt.

events.title: Sino-Indian War of 1962
events.detail: China attacked primarily over disputed Himalayan territories in Aksai Chin and across the McMahon Line. Triggered by shifting border policies and India granting asylum to the Dalai Lama the war resulted in a decisive military victory for China's People's Liberation Army. New Delhi hastened to make fundamental changes in its Nepal policy. The unofficial economic blockade was lifted and trade began to flow across the border again. It came to King Mahendra as an opportunity to achieve his motive with India. Consequently Nepali Congress resistance movement was suspended in November and then terminated in December by Subarna Shamsher reportedly on the advice of the Indian government. Later when Nehru wrote letter to King requesting India Army stay temporarily in an open area in Kalapani and it was allowed. However even after the end of war the Army stayed there and King never came to that issue. After capturing key strategic positions China declared a unilateral ceasefire and maintained de facto control over Aksai Chin establishing the Line of Actual Control.

events.title: NC's Armed Struggle Terminated
events.detail: When at the request of India the NC announced the suspension of the armed movement it divided the party into two camps. Bharat Shamsher Saroj Prasad Koirala Keshav Prasad Koirala Padma Shankar Adhikari Bal Bahadur Rai Tej Bahadur Amatya etc. were in favor of continuing the armed movement within the country. Parshu Narayan Chaudhary Vasudev Risal Ganesh Kumar Sharma Achyut Raj Regmi Bhadrakali Mishra Kashinath Gautam Jagannath Acharya etc. were in favor of the suspension. Surbarna Shamsher mentioned the India-China war as the main reason for suspending the armed movement. It was approved by the NC meeting held in Calcutta.

events.title: Constitution of Nepal 1962
events.detail: It was a rather odd but the constitution turned out to be ingenious combination of certain features of the "National Guidance" system in Egypt and Indonesia i.e. strong central leadership controlling political participation the "Basic Democracy" system in Pakistan i.e. citizens vote for local representatives only the "Class Organization" system in Egypt and Yugoslavia i.e. people organized into groups (workers farmers youth etc.) and the panchayat system in operation in several Indian states. Added onto this basic structure were the Raj Sabha ("Council of State") and the Daudahas ("Tour Commissions") more perceptibly "Nepali" in origin and inspiration. The Panchayat: The system had four main levels arranged from local to national all with tenure of 6 years. The Panchayat Ministry had full power to dismiss all of them if needed. The Village (Gaun) Panchayat was divided into 9 wards, each with 9 members and one Pradhan Pancha and one Upa-pradhan Pancha elected by village council consisting of all Nepali citizens 21 years of age or older. In this election, the ward members of the village panchayat were elected by show of hands or by consensus. While the elected ward members only got to vote for Pradhan Pancha and the Upa-Pradhan Pancha using ballot papers untill Third Ammendment (1980). However, there was no provision for stamping. Arrangements were made to put a check mark in front of the name of the Pradhan Pancha and Upa Pradhan Pancha of one's choice. However, the tenure of the members was determined to be 2, 4, and 6 years through a system of drawing lots. The council was tasked hold two annual meetings—a winter meeting to discuss and approve the village budget as formulated by the panchayat and a summer meeting to discuss development programs. The village panchayat was responsible of local development (roads water schools) dispute resolution and basic administration. Members as well as Pradhan/Upa-Pradhan Pancha had a 6-year term. Once elecetd Pradhan/Upa-Pradhan Pancha held position for 6 years regardless of their membership tenure. Elections were staggered every two years for one-third of the seats, meaning local councils were in a state of perpetual election and rotation. The Town (Nagar) Panchayat (any town exceeding 10000 population; 14 town in 1962 which reached 33 in 1990) was equivalent of municipality with 9 elected members and up to one-fourth members nominated by government. They would then elect one eacy District President/Vice-President (Zilla Sabhapati/Upa-Sabhapati). Moreover the budget prepared by the nagar panchayat required the approval of the central authorities. Had same structure and tenure as Gaun Panchayat. The District (Zilla) Panchayat was established in 75 districts each with district assemblies consisting of one member from each village panchayat and one third of the membership of each town panchayat within the district area. It had two primary functions: to hold at least two meetings each year and to elect the District Panchayat Committee and District President (Zilla Sabhapati). The district assemblies elected 11-member Panchayat Committee which serve as the executive body in each district. The panchayat which must meet at least once a month functions primarily as the expediter of development projects undertaken within the district but it also supervises the activities and budgets of the village and town panchayats under its jurisdiction giving directives to them if necessary. It has limited taxing and fee-collecting powers and is entitled to a maximum of 10 per cent of the income of the primary panchayat units. Members had 6-year term with staggered voting every 2 years for one-thir members. Zilla Sabhapati also had 6 year tenure. Zone (Anchal) Panchayat was established in the new administrative units called zones, introduced by this constitution. The 14 zones were designed for police administration, security, tax collection, and centralized royal oversight. Zone assembly consisting of all the members of the District Panchayat which would elect the 11-member Zone Panchayat members and one each Chairman and Vice-Chairman. For each zone, a Zonal Commissioner (Anchaladhish) was appointed by the King, who was a singular bureaucrat/strongman replacing the Bada Hakim. He held all the weapons, police authority, and judicial vetoes. The Zonal Panchayat could discuss regional development, sports, culture, or local transport. However, any resolution they passed had to be approved by the Anchaladhish. Both Anchal Panchayat and Anchaladhish had 6-year term. Anchal Panchayat had rotational voting. The National (Rastriya) Panchayat would be the apex body and the legislature of the Kingdom of Nepal with total of 121 members however which no power to elect or remove the PM. Total of 90 members were elected by the Zonal assemblies in total. The state-controlled mass organizations elected members as follows: Peasants’ Organisation → 4; Youth Organisation → 4; Women’s Organisation → 3; Ex-Servicemen’s Organisation → 2; Workers’ Organisation → 2. University graduates formed a separate electoral group electing 4 members. Lastly the King nominated 16 members. Members served a 5-year term, but because they were elected indirectly by Zonal Assemblies, their seats were highly unstable. If their grassroots village or district tenure expired during those 5 years due to the staggered cycle, they automatically lost their seat in the national parliament. Class Organizations: It envisioned mass organizations for peasants laborers women students young persons children and former servicemen as an alternative to political parties. It had four-tier structure similar to the panchayat. The primary class committees where those in each village or town panchayat area elected directly by all the members of each class within the jurisdiction of the panchayat. Every primary unit delegates one member to a district council which elects a five-man District Executive Committee from among its membership and in turn this committee elects a zonal committee. The president and fourteen of the eighteen members of the Central Committee are elected by a National Convention composed of the members of the district and zonal committees of the class organizations. The secretary and treasurer of the Central Committee are appointed by the central government and the president nominates two other members. The members of the zonal committees elect the fifteen representatives of the class organizations in the National Panchayat. These organizations enjoyed monopoly in the political sphere while any other parallel organizations were banned. However the class organizations were instructed that they cannot participate in panchayat elections as a group. Most of the attention of the leadership was directed toward internal struggles rather than real issues. Guidance System: A new Ministry of National Guidance was announced in 1961 with responsibility of establishment of the panchayats and class organization and to limit panchayat and class organization from encroaching their hierarchial responsibilities. Vishwabandhu Thapa was the minister. District Guidance Officers were appointed to each of the seventy-five Development Districts to carry out the duties of the Ministry on this level. Furthermore a joint district and zonal Guidance Committees and a National Guidance Council was formed to advice government on better coordination. Later the ministry was dissolved transfering responsibilities to Panchayat Ministry. Raj Sabha and Daudahas: Raj Sabha had two primary functions: to supervise succession to the throne or the establishment of a regency in the event of the King's death or incapacity and to serve as a consultative body when the King and the National Panchayat are not in agreement on proposed legislation. The Daudahas or Tour Commissions were appointed by King Mahendra in 14 zones consisting of a chairman representatives of the military and judiciary and a secretary in February 1961 each of which toured a section of the country and then submitted a report to the palace. The Commissions also were granted special judicial powers equal in substance to those of the Zilla Adalats. National Identity: For the first time in constitution Nepal was declared a monarchical Hindu State and Nepali was declared the national language.

events.title: Mahendra's Nationalism
events.detail: King Mahendra promoted a centralized state-led model of Nepali nationalism aimed at strengthening national unity and consolidating the Panchayat system. The monarchy was projected as the symbol and guardian of the nation while national identity was increasingly defined around common state symbols and cultural traits. The Panchayat regime promoted the ideas later summarized as “Ek Desh Ek Bhasa Ek Bhesh” (One Nation One Language One Dress) by emphasizing Nepali as the national language Daura Suruwal as the national dress and Nepal as a Hindu Kingdom. Hindu Kingdom and Nepali as national language was instituted through 1962 Constitution while Daura Suruwal was established by making it mandatory for all civil servants. This nationalism was further institutionalized through state media cultural organizations bureaucracy and especially the education system. In 1961 under the tutelage of King Mahendra His Majesty’s Government founded Ratna Recording Sansthan which paired with Radio Nepal to press records of Nepali national music. Songs like "Rato Ra Chandra Surya" "Baneko Chha Paharale" "Gauchha Geet Nepali" "Nepali Hami Rahaula Kaha" etc. were recorded during that period and widely played in Radio Nepal and school assemblies. King Mahendra himself wrote under pen name M.B.B. Shah and popularized patroitic songs like "Ma Mare Pani Mero Desh Bachi Rahos" and "Nepal Mero Timilai" through Radio Nepal. During the 1950s Gurung Sherpa Tamang and Newari songs were also represented in Radio Nepal's folk songs but from 1965 the Radio Nepal broadcasts have been predominantly Nepali. Cultural institutions like Rastriya Naachghar Pragya Pratisthan etc. became mediums to promote Panchayat ideology by censoring dissent funding pro-palace art and systematically spreading the state-backed propoganda.

events.title: Patan Industrial Estate Established
events.detail: The Patan Industrial Estate was founded in 1963 with infrastructure assistance from India. India has assisted in the establishment of four industrial estates: Patan Dharan Nepalgunj and Rajbiraj. It covers a total land area of 293 ropani and houses about 112 industries. It specializes primarily in cottage industries including wood carving metal crafts copper statues woolen carpets and textiles.

events.title: Air Connectivity Expansion
events.detail: Between 1952 and 1963 five domestic airfields in Pokhara Simra Biratnagar Bhairahawa and Janakpur were built with Indian assistance.

events.title: First Rastriya Panchayat Election
events.detail: To elect Rastriya Panchayat; 125 members; 16 appointed by the King 90 elected by Zonal Assemblies 15 elected by class organizations and 4 elected by the graduates constituency. Previously affiliated to Nepali Congress 20-25%; Communists 15%; other parties 20% won the election. Every member of the Rastriya Panchayat was elected to a fixed four-year term. A 1968 amendment to the constitution added staggered terms for members elected by zonal assemblies, so that one-third of the members were elected every two years.

events.title: Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement
events.detail: Following India's defeat in the 1962 Sino-Indian War Pakistan saw a unique opportunity to align with Beijing to balance India's military dominance in South Asia. Pakistan felt betrayed by its Western allies specifically the United States and the United Kingdom who began supplying heavy military aid to India during the 1962 war without resolving the Kashmir dispute. By signing a formal international treaty with China Pakistan gained implicit Chinese recognition of its administrative control over Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir region of Jammu and Kashmir while giving away Shaksgam Valley. India claimed that Pakistan had no legal authority to negotiate or cede territory in Kashmir. During the Cold War Pakistan was part of the US built global military alliances SEATO (Southeast Asia Treaty Organization) and CENTO (Central Treaty Organization) to contain communism. However by signing the treaty with Communist China Pakistan completely broke rank with Washington. This move deeply angered the U.S. leading President John F. Kennedy to suspend financial aid and cancel scheduled state visits with Pakistani leaders. When President Richard Nixon took office in 1969 he harbored a strong personal dislike for Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and a warm long-standing relationship with Pakistani military dictator Yahya Khan. By the late 1960s China and the Soviet Union had become bitter enemies even fighting border skirmishes. Nixon saw a historic opportunity to exploit this split by opening diplomatic relations with China thereby isolating the USSR. In July 1971 Pakistan successfully facilitated Henry Kissinger’s secret historic flight from Islamabad to Beijing. This monumental diplomatic breakthrough paved the way for Nixon’s 1972 visit to China.

events.title: NC And King Further Apart
events.detail: Kathmandu special court sentenced Subarna Shamsher and several colleagues in absentia to life imprisonment on the charge of having instigated the transportation of explosive materials to Nepal for subversive purposes. It was result of failing negotiation effort between NC and King and a reconciliation between New Delhi and Kathmandu reached after Sino-India War. The obvious inadequacies of the Congress's revolutionary capacity combined with its tendency to depend upon Indian influence at Kathmandu for support of its cause were not well-conceived tactics if the object was to induce the King to agree to a compromise.

events.title: Tulsi Giri (1st Term)
events.detail: Before the inauguration of the National Panchayat King Mahendra announced the new cabinet promoting Tulsi Giri to the chairman of the Council of Ministers. King kept with himself the Defence Ministry and refered calling Tulsi Giri as Chairman of the Council of Ministers insted of the PM. It is also evident from the congratulatory messages comming to Tulsi Giri from the Foreign Ministers rather than the Prime Ministers of various countries. Because of the elimination of Bishwabandhu Thapa and Rishikesh Shah Dr. Giri was now the only Minister with anything resembling a national reputation. The only other figure of any significance in the Council was the Finance Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa who was the Minister in whom the King seemed to repose the most confidence and through whom he acted on occasion. His reputation is that of a careful hard-working administrator lacking the brilliance and flare of a Tulsi Giri no doubt but conforming better perhaps to the King's political pattern. Most evident of all was every Minister or Assistant Minister who had been advocating a moderate domestic and foreign policy towards NC or India was excluded. Tulsi Giri --Chairman (Janakpur zone) Surya Bahadur Thapa -- Vice-chairman (Nominated) Bhuwan Lai Pradhan (Nominated) Nageshwar Prasad Singh (Graduate's Constituency) Kirtinidhi Bishta (Bagmati Zone) Vedananda Jha (Sagarmatha ZOne Khadga Bahadur Singh (Seti Zone) Assistant Ministers: Shailendra K. Upadhyaya (Youth Organization) Giri Prasad Budathoki (Former Servicemen Organization) Pushkar Nath Upraity (Peasant's Organization) Nagendra Prasad Rijal (Koshi Zone) Kedar Man "Vyathit" (Nominated) Rajeshwar Devkota (Gandaki Zone) Shamsher Bahadur Tumbahamfe (Nominated)

events.title: Agricultural Reorganization Act of 2019
events.detail: The Act was initially piloted as a program in selected gram panchayats within the Jhapa Palpa and Chitwan districts government surveyed landholdings identified the actual farmers fixed fair rent rates and provided modern administrative procedures to pave path for broader land reforms in 2021. The rent couldn't exceed 50% of the produce. In Kathmandu Valley and Inner Terai rates were fixed based on the land grading such as Abal (First Grade) Doyam (Second Grade) Sim (Third Grade) and Chahar (Fourth Grade) which was way lower than 50% of the produce.

events.title: Rise and Fall of Tulsi Giri
events.detail: The King visited India Israel and Kenya between August 27 and October 11; Tulsi Giri accompanied the King to India and Israel and then set out on a tour of his own to the United States France West Germany the United Kingdom Switzerland Denmark Sweden and the Soviet Union. His tour was a tremendous personal success as far as Nepal was concerned as he met President Kennedy in Washington Prime Minister Pompidou in Paris President Luebke in Bonn and Premier Khrushchev in the Soviet Union—tangible evidence that Nepal had achieved a respectable position in the international community. This success came as a curse to Giri as King unexpectedly nominated Rishikesh Shah as chairman of the Standing Committee of the Council of State on December 9. On December 27 King Mahendra announced that he had accepted Tulsi Giri's resignation for what were described as reasons of health. It was common knowledge that he had resigned at the King's request and not on his own initiative. Similar fate was met by Bishwabandhu Thapa when he bacame stronger being Minister of National Guidance the ministry was disolved in April and he was excluded from new cabinet.

events.title: India-Nepal Trade and Transit Talks
events.detail: Following 1963 Nepal sought to mitigate its economic dependence on India by pushing for trade diversification and improved transit rights through Indian territory often utilizing UNCTAD conferences to advocate for landlocked nations. Despite bilateral tensions over India's non-ratification of the 1964 Geneva convention regarding transit rights India made concessions including abolishing the burdensome bond system (traders had to pay bond/collateral amount unless goods are successfully transported) for Nepali goods in 1963. In 1964 India agreed to provide unrestricted transit facilities for goods being shipped from one part of Nepal to another via India. In December 1966 New Delhi exempted Nepali goods in transit through India from Indian laws and also agreed to provide a "separate and self-contained space" for Nepali cargo at Calcutta port. In 1968 India agreed to provide lump sum payment equivalent to the additional duties (other tha excise too) that india imposed on its manufacturers. In 1968 New Delhi decided to impost surcharge on importers of Nepali manufactured goods with local raw materials to equal Indian excise duty. Nepal protested and India later agreed to impose 80% of the excise on Indian goods. Another problem was with importation into India the Nepali manufactured good utilizing raw materials from third country likely because India feared of its businessman investing in such industries in Nepal as restrictions were less and foreign exchange was readily available. Upon India's concern Nepal reluctantly accepted to restrict number of industries dependent upon imports from third countries to 1967-68 level.

events.title: Salt Trading Corporation Limited Established
events.detail: Salt Trading Corporation (STC) Limited is one of Nepal's largest business organizations, established on September 13, 1963, as the country's first successful Public-Private Partnership (PPP). The private sector holds 79% of ownership while government owns 21%. It was originally launched to import and distribute iodized common salt from India since Nepal does not produce its own salt. Over time it has diversified into trading of sugar, wheat, oil, rice, other grains, tea, LP gas, paper, coal and tyres for vehicles.

events.title: Hetauda Industrial Estate Established
events.detail: The Hetauda Industrial Estate was founded in 1963 with assistance from USA. It is situated at the critical junction of the Tribhuvan Highway and the Mahendra Highway it acts as a central logistics corridor linking Kathmandu Narayanghat and the major trade gateway of Birgunj. The estate spans a substantial area of 3228 ropanis and is the largest industrial estate of Nepal. It is equipped with a dedicated Waste Water Treatment Plant developed with Danish assistance to process liquid waste before it hits local waterways. There are 146 industries and establishments currently operating in the Hetauda Industrial Estate.

events.title: Surya Bahadur Thapa (1st Term)
events.detail: Thapa was seen as an appropriate candidate for the position of Chairman because he was the Minister in whom the King reposed the fullest confidence and was like King's yes-man without ambitions. One thing was clear that Ministers with political backgrounds had been removed from the Council which now consisted almost entirely of "independents" with a long record of pro-royalist antiparty activity. Surya Bahadur Thapa -- Chairman; Finance Minister; Palace Affairs and General Administration Khadga Bahadur Singh -- Land Reform Shailendra Kumar Upadhyaya -- Panchayat Affairs All the Assistant Ministers were raised to ministerial rank.

events.title: Terai Resettlement Projects
events.detail: Background: Following the success of malaria eradication government started resettlement projects with the objective of accommodating the natural calamity and disaster victims and landless peasants as well as controlling spontaneous migration by channeling new arrivals into organized settlements. Moreover there was a need for expanding the programme in order to resettle the domiciled Nepalese returning from India and Burma following the enactment of the Burmese Citizenship Act in 1964. Execution: Preliminary surveys of the Tarai were carried out with the help of an 'Israeli technician in 1962. The Nepal Punarvas (Resettlement) Company was established in 1964. The provision of land at a nominal price and also the provision of such social and economic services as a health post schools drinking water roads agriculture extension services a postal unit a police post cooperative services and credit facilities all within the project area served to encourage hill people to purchase plots of land in the resettlement project. In 1969 the government established a separate Resettlement Department within the Ministry of Food and Agriculture to organize the resettlement programme on a national scale. The already existing Nepal Resettlement Company was put under the Department. The Department was also involved in small projects of a political character in which most of the resettlers were political victims and persons nominated through royal order. In 1973 the government came up with a plan and programme relating to resettlement and control of haphazard growth of settlements; its main aims were the rehabilitation of natural disaster victims and landless families and the regulation of resettlement of forest encroachers. When the programme was introduced. the Resettlement Department was brought under the Ministry of Forestry; however this Ministry's responsibility ended as soon as the land was cleared of forest and agriculture began. Outcome: As of 1980 eight resettlement programs were implemenetd in Nawalparasi Banke Bardia Kailali Kanchanpur Sarlahi and Jhapa districts of Terai. More than 45000 households had been resettled under the program. The Resettlement Company had settled 13133 households on 22687 ha of land while the Resettlement Department has resettled 32230 households on 27802 ha of land. Negative Consequences: However the programme has been able neither to redistribute the target groups that is poor landless peasants nor to solve the problem of heavy pressure of population in the hills. No programmes were implemented to detect hill areas with the excessive pressure of population on cultivated land and hence spontaneous migration overshadowed planned resettlement. Similary the objective of conserving the natural vegetation of catchment areas has never been implemented leading to rampant forest encroachment. Despite formal distribution of 77700 ha of land for resettlement in the period between 1964-1974 an additional 237600 ha of forests were encroached upon during the same period. The extent of deforestation during the half century (1927-77) was estimated at nearly 60%. The population increase in the Tarai region the same period was over 163%. By 1980 the forest coverage in the Tarai (19%) was far below the critical minimum (33%) required to maintain an ecological balance. For instance serious destructrion of Tarai forests has occurred in the Bhabar region. its forests used to serve as a check for the fast flowing hill rivers entering the Tarai. Thus the destruction of forests in this part of the Tarai has resulted not only in floods in the Tarai plains in the south but also in the drying up of streams rivulets and springs. Since 1981 the government completely stopped land settlement in new projects as well as in old projects where land distribution was not completed.

events.title: Bonus Voucher Scheme
events.detail: In 1964, Nepal introduced Bonus Voucher Scheme designed to encourage exports and earn scarce foreign currency. Under the scheme, the exporter could effectively retain 90% of the foreign exchange earnings through a special voucher mechanism, rather than surrendering almost all foreign currency to the state. With these incentives, factories were set up along the Indian border to process imported stainless steel and synthetic fabrics and then re-export them. The finished products went either to a third country, thus earning the foreign currency bonus, or into India, where, thanks to the low cost of the raw material and tax concessions offered by the Nepalese government, they could be priced lower than similar items from Indian factories. As a result, Nepal’s synthetic fabric output expanded in five years from 5700 to 2,305,000 yards per year. However, India reacted harshly and in 1969 seized as contraband 6 million rupees’ worth of fabric and stainless steel. Acrimonious negotiations pegged the amount that Nepal was allowed to export to the 1967–8 level and eventually most of the factories closed.

events.title: Defence Diversification Effort
events.detail: India had been fulfilling Nepal's military needs specified in the letters of exchange to the 1950 treaty. After 1962 Sino-Indian border war India was not able to fulfill Nepal's request due to its own needs. When discussions were held with India it was sympathetic but was in no position to offer tangible assistance. Americans and the British were approached in the fall of 1963. Indians first suggested that the aid be channeled through their own military assistance program but this was unacceptable to Kathmandu. New Delhi finally accepted the Nepali position and in 1964 military assistance valued at $4 million equally divided between the United States and the United Kingdom was provided to Nepal. A secret Defence Agreement was reached between the two governments in January 1965 which effectively gave India a monopoly over Nepal's military imports. In mid-1965 Nepal submitted to the United States and the United Kingdom a second shopping list amounting to approximately $3 million. As neither of these governments wanted to supersede New Delhi's responsibilities in this respect they advised Nepal to seek its requirements from India first. In 1967 Nepal came to an agreement with India and obtained most of the desired military equipment from India. Indian army technical personnel were stationed at checkposts and other strategic locations along the Nepal-Tibet border until 1970 and an Indian Military Liaison Group continued to function at Nepali army headquarters in Kathmandu a decade after the formal withdrawal of the Indian Advisory Military Group. In 1969 only Nepal requested the withdrawal of the Indian technical personnel on the northern border. Meanwhile discussions were underway the "secret" January 1965 arms agreement was disclosed in Indian press causing humilation of Nepal's Government. In reaction Nepali PM Kritinidhi Bista wrote to India "and as far as Nepal is concerned the agreement no longer exists." and called for the withdrawal of the Indian army technical personnel and the Indian Military Liaison Group. Though India agreed to withdraw its military mission by the end of 1970 the 1965 arms assistance agreement still appears to be operative on a de facto basis.

events.title: Nepal Issued First Government Bond
events.detail: The government of Nepal floated its first 6% per annum Development Bond of NPR 13.1 million with a five-year maturity on February 12, 1964, issued through Nepal Rastra Bank to raise funds for developmental expenditures. However the 91-day Treasury Bills (NPR 7 million) under the Public Debt Act was issued earlier in 1962.

events.title: Tulsi Giri (2nd Term)
events.detail: Panchayat System - Partyless

events.title: Tulsi Giri Restored
events.detail: Most plausible but unverified King Mahendra had decided to seek an accommodation with the Nepali Congress including the release of all political prisoners and that Tulsi Giri's dismissal was a necessary prerequisite in view of the Nepali Congress' antipathy to him. Reportedly Surya Prasad Upadhyaya was sent to India to meet NC leaders but the discussions failed over NC's rejection to accpet party-less Panchayat System. Having failed in this Tulsi Giri was restored.

events.title: Nepal Citizenship Act 2020
events.detail: It radically reversed the open-door policies of the 1952 Act to promote "Nepaliness". It completely eliminated the citizenship by birth. Citizenship by Descent: Granted to individuals whose fathers were citizens of Nepal at the time of the child's birth; to every minor who is found within the Kingdom of Nepal and the whereabouts of whose parents are not known shall until the father of that minor is traced be deemed to be a citizen of Nepal by descent. Naturalized Citizenship: Given to any foreign woman married to a male Nepali citizen; to any foreign national living in nepal for at least 15 years and can speak and write Nepali; to child born from naturalized citizen that can speak and write Nepali. Honorary Citizenship: A special status that could be granted by the government to prominent foreign nationals who rendered exceptional contributions to Nepal and would be equal to naturalized citizenship.

events.title: Ammendment to Gandak Agreement
events.detail: head regulator of the Don Branch Canal to be operated by Government of Nepal; provision of requirement of separate agreements between Government of Nepal and Government of India for the trans-valley use of Gandak waters in the months of February to April was introduced

events.title: Nepal-China Trade Agreement
events.detail: 30 km border corridor established; Residents could move and trade within 30 km inside Nepal and Tibet; Traditional barter trade remained permitted and Tax exemptions existed.

events.title: Cabinet Reshuffle
events.detail: Bishwabandhu Thapa resigned as chairman of the National Panchayat and he was as vice-chairman of the Council and as Minister of Home and Panchayat Affairs. But after only forty-seven days in office he resigned without proper explanation. On January 26 1965 Tulsi Giri resigned as well for what he described as differences of opinion. The most plausible explanation is the Thapa and Giri's dissatisfaction over eroded power of the Cabinet and King's direct supervision.

events.title: Land Act of 2021
events.detail: Objectives: It had twofold objectives: 1. Grant the cutivators enough rights to their land or share of production in rented land 2. Divert capital and manpower from agriculture to non-agrucultural sector. It abolished the Jimidari System secured tenancy rights against arbitrary eviction Introduced land ceiling and provision of paying compensation while confiscation of excess land allowed for a dual-ownership model where landlords and tenants i.e. mohi shared rights to the same land. It also made compulsary provision to in-kind saving deposited to village-level commitee. The collecetd money was used to finance agricultural credit and industrial entreprises. It was discontinued in 1969 due to misappropriation of funds. Land Ceiling: The land ceiling was as follows: 18.4 ha/360 ropani in Terai and Inner Terai; 3.1 ha/70 ropani in Kathmandu valley and 4.9 ha/96 ropani in Hill. Restriction: Land was restricted to be sold to foreigners. Outcome: Due to lack of proper land records or cadastral survey resulted in anticipatory measures by landlords who redistributed excess lands among their families and relatives registered themselves as cultivators by evicting tenants and alienated excess land through sale. The government could not therefore recover the excess lands above the illiowable ceiling as anticipated and total excess area turned out to be very low only 62672 ha which was not sufficient to solve the problem of landless peasants. Moreover it is not known exactly what happened to this excess land. Of the total estimated land to be acquired after land ceiling enforcement only 7 % was actually realised. Section 12 of the original 1964 Act the government carved out legal exceptions. It granted exemption to land owned by the Government of Nepal cooperative societies medical institutions educational institutions or specified industrial enterprises like Giribandu Tea Estate needing land for factory operations.

events.title: Hippe Movement
events.detail: The hippie movement started in the mid-1960s in the United States heavily driven by college-aged youths rebelling against the Vietnam War draft corporate materialism and rigid traditional values. The Anti-War Protests sparked intense resistance among youth. Later writers and poets from the 1950s paved the way by questioning consumer culture and exploring alternative lifestyles. The 1967 Summer of Love gathering in San Francisco's Haight-Ashbury district popularized communal living psychedelic rock music and free love globally. During the late 1960s and early 1970s tens of thousands of young Westerners packed into inexpensive vans shared taxis and iconic long-distance buses (like the "Magic Bus"). They traveled from European hubs like London and Amsterdam driving through Turkey Iran Afghanistan and Pakistan to reach India and Nepal. It quickly turned isolated Himalayan country into a global counterculture capital. The key reasons were legal cannabis sold in government-licensed shops across Kathmandu extreme affordability rich Buddhist and Hindu spiritual heritage meditation practices and the Himalayas offering alternative to Western religion. The absolute heart of this movement was Jhochhen Tole a street right off Kathmandu’s historic Durbar Square. Renamed "Freak Street" by locals it quickly filled with budget pie shops (selling hash-infused sweets) vibrant cafes cheap guest houses and smoke shops. In 1971 legendary Indian filmmaker Dev Anand arrived in Kathmandu to shoot his iconic movie Hare Rama Hare Krishna. The plot directly mirrored the city's reality: a young Westernized girl falling into the Kathmandu drug culture. The movie’s hit song ⁠"Dum Maro Dum" became an overnight global sensation. It immortalized Kathmandu's hippie scene on celluloid and brought a massive new wave of regional tourists from India. Realizing that the hippie crowd spent very little money the government secretly began planning a pivot toward high-spending mountain trekkers and luxury travelers. The golden era of the Hippie Trail collapsed in the late 1970s. The official definitive end of the legal hippie era in Nepal occurred on July 16 1973. On this exact day under heavy diplomatic and financial pressure from the U.S. Nixon administration's "War on Drugs" the Government of Nepal revoked the commercial licenses of all 22 official cannabis shops buyers and cafes operating on Freak Street and around Kathmandu. Shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution and the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan permanently closed the overland driving routes making travel too dangerous. This movement switched Nepal from a rich-only playground to an affordable mass tourism opening cheap family guesthouses and mountain tea houses. It also revived local appreciation for ancient heritage because foreigners valued it.

events.title: Panauti Hydropower Plant Built
events.detail: It is 2.4 MW run-of-the-river plant on the Roshi Khola River in Kavre District which was constructed with assistance from the Soviet Union. It was highly significant for expanding industrial power supply outside of Kathmandu. It is still operational.

events.title: Bansbari Leather Shoe Factory Established
events.detail: The Bansbari Leather Shoe Factory was founded in 1965 with financial and technical assistance from the government of China. The factory could not compete with cheap imported shoes and after remaining sick for ages was finally privatized in 1992.

events.title: Surya Bahadur Thapa (2nd Term)
events.detail: Panchayat System - Partyless

events.title: All Nepal National Free Students Union (ANNFSU) Formed
events.detail: The pro-China faction of Nepal Students' Federation went on to form the ANNFSU. It did however remain as a united organization in spite of various splits within the radical communists.

events.title: Third Five-Year Plan
events.detail: NPR 1.7 billion spent; ~60% came from foreign aid; 14 PEs established; major focus on decentralization and Panchayat-based local development; ~12.5 MW added against ~19 MW planned in hydropower—about 66% achieved; Kathmandu–Birgunj 66 kV transmission line completed; rural roads expanded; Dharan–Dhankuta transmission begun; out of a massive 2,200 km target, ~1,120 km of roads were constructed; East-West Highway (Mahendra Highway) construction formally kicked off; Trishuli Hydroelectric Project completed (Phase I); Sunkoshi Hydro project began; TU expanded departments; National Malaria Eradication Campaign achieved near-total coverage in Terai; family planning programs launched nationwide; institutionalized Panchayat involvement in planning and local resource mobilization; social services like health and education expanded through local units but data sparse; goals for private sector also outlined for the first time; transport and communication remained dominant at 41%; agriculture and village development received 22%; industry and power took 20%; first plan formulated under a long-term 20-year economic vision; transportation targets met expectations, but food grain production lagged due to monsoon dependency.

events.title: India-Pakistan war of 1965
events.detail: Pakistan secretly sent disguised troops into Indian-administered Kashmir to spark an anti-India rebellion. Local Kashmiris did not revolt; they alerted Indian authorities instead. India counter-attacked by crossing the international border toward Lahore turning it into a full-scale war. It featured the largest tank battles since World War II. The U.S. had previously supplied billions of dollars in advanced weaponry to Pakistan and smaller amounts to India under strict agreements. These terms stated the weapons could only be used for defensive purposes or to counter the regional spread of Communism. When both nations used these weapons against each other instead the U.S. cut off the supply to enforce its policies. New Delhi felt that the U.S. policy was deeply unfair. Pakistan had launched the covert invasion (Operation Gibraltar) yet the U.S. punished both nations equally. India viewed the embargo as a betrayal that ignored Pakistan’s unprovoked aggression. This pushed India to align closer with the Soviet Union. The United Nations brokered a ceasefire on September 23 1965 as both sides ran low on supplies. In January 1966 the Soviet Union mediated a peace deal. Both nations agreed to withdraw to their pre-war borders.

events.title: Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited Founded
events.detail: It is the largest and fully government-owned "A" class commercial bank in Nepal founded in January 1966 under the special Rastriya Banijya Bank Act. It was founded with aim of expanding banking service to rural areas and eliminating IC dominance in Nepal. Nepal Bank Limited was not fully state owned because of which the private partners were reluctant to expand operation to low-profit rural areas and also unwilling to holding large reserves of volatile Nepali fiat currency. Therefore RBBL was built to deliver the goals of expanding financial access and eliminating the dual currency system. Furthermore it also gave government unhindered control over a commercial bank to execute its periodic Five-Year Development Plans, distribute subsidized credit, and manage the national treasury without corporate friction or shareholder pushback.

events.title: Ammendment to Sino-Nepalese Treaty of 1956
events.detail: It ammend 1956 treaty which specified that border residents have to use designated routes and register with authorities. Porters needed official certificates. Its main objective was to eliminate the role of the private Nepali trader in Tibet and to replace the traditional trade structure between Nepal and Tibet with direct state-to-state trading. The number of Nepalis in Tibet declined from about 5000 in the early 1960's to a few hundred by 1968.

events.title: Gandaki Boarding School Established
events.detail: Gandaki Boarding School in Pokhara, Nepal, was established as a boys-only school on June 11, 1966, through the joint initiative of three primary groups: the United Mission to Nepal (UMN), the Shining Hospital (now the International Nepal Fellowship), and the local community (including local figures like Laxya Bahadur Gurung and Bhupi Sherchan). Represented by figures like Jonathan Lindell and Howard Barclay, UMN provided major funding, planning, and subsequent construction of the physical infrastructure. The school had a tentative beginning. All buildings were of mud and bamboo structure with thatched roofs. There were 45 boarders, 16 day students and teaching staff of 5 led by the first Principal, Mrs Martha Mukhia. In 1981, it was handed over to local Nepali management as part of UMN's initial localization policy. In 1985 it changed itself to an English medium school and renamed to Gandaki Boarding School. In the same year it adopetd co-education by enrolling girls and was Recognized as the "Regional School" by the Government of Nepal. In 1988 it gained a nationwide fame after Rajendra Gurung stood in SLC board first. Until 1991, courses were available from Grade 4 to Grade 10. Then it started offering 10+2 system under the Higher Secondary Education Board. In 1999 Gandaki College of Engineering and Sciences (GCES) was opened. In 2004 GBS was awarded Birendra Vidhya National shield for SLC results with 4 boards, 66 distinctions, 100% first division among 113 candidates.

events.title: Symbolic Nationalism Meets Economic Reality: Nepal’s 1966 Currency Revaluation
events.detail: A nationlist image was at centre of Mahendra's regime as the continuation of which Nepal wanted to nationalize Nepali rupee. The Indian rupee was the chief medium of exchange in the Terai and much of the hill area. In 1961 the Nepali govrnment launched a long-range campaign aimed at making Nepali currency the only legal tender in the country. The campaign continued till mid-1966 unless it met with sudden devaluation of IC. In 1966 after India devalued the rupee by 36.5% Nepal refused to follow and instead sharply revalued the Nepali rupee by 57% to assert economic independence (Before devaluation 160 NC = 100 IC; After revaluation 101.60 NC = 100 IC). It soon became apparent however that this brave but foolish act had been motivated more by political than economic considerations. In one stroke for instance the value of Indian and U.S. foreign aid6 was reduced by approximately forty-five percent. The trade structure between India and Nepal was also thrown into disarray with the result that the prices of most imported commodities rose rapidly. By the end of the year the Nepali government had recognized its mistake and returned to pre-criis exchange rate.

events.title: Koshi Treaty Revised
events.detail: Caluse added saying leased by HMG to the Union for a period of 199 years; GoI will pay compensation annually at the tare of Rs. 5 NC per Nepali Bigha for all lands that have been acquired so far for the Kosi Project; Nepal could use water for irrigation; Nepal gave land for Koshi Western Canal in excahnge of Kuneli to Fattehpur road and power supply from Kataya powerhouse to Rajbiraj; easternembankment of the Kosi River collapsed at Kusaha in 2008 causing Bihar flood

events.title: Girija Prasad Koirala Released
events.detail: Girija Prasad Koirala Released from jail in 1967. After his release he made rigorous efforts for the release of his brother BP Koirala. The Chinese induced unrest in Kathmandu and “Great Cultural Revolution” in China had created a public mood in favour of democratic leaders. In 1968 Krishna Prasad Bhattarai was shifted to Nakkhu Jail from Sundarijail while Assistant Ministers Dibansingh Rai and Yogendra Man Sherchan were released. This gave hope to Girija and he intensified his talks with the Government and the King. Finally in 1968 BP Koirala was released from prison and he stayed in self-exile in Banaras India until December 1976.

events.title: Ratna Highway Completed
events.detail: The 113 km Ratna Highway (Nepalgunj-Kohalpur-Birendranagar Road) was opened in between 1957 and 1967 which went through subsequent blacktopping and reconstruction in late 1990s. After new classification of highways Ratna Highway is now categorized as Karnali Highway.

events.title: First Ammendment to 1962 Panchayat Constitution
events.detail: "Party-less" in Preamble: In the 1967 First Amendment, when King Mahendra officially inserted the phrase "Partyless Democratic Panchayat System" into the constitutional preamble, it legally changed the definition of "public good" and "national security." Because the partyless system was now hardcoded as the permanent, unalterable nature of the state, any speech, publication, or assembly that criticized the Panchayat system or advocated for political parties automatically became a constitutional offense. Direct Control of Anchaldish: Royal-appointed Zonal Commissioner was placed directly above the elected Zonal Panchayat. The Commissioner was given sweeping legal authority to overrule, bypass, or completely suspend the decisions of local elected politicians.

events.title: Araniko Highway Completed And Increased Communist Influence
events.detail: The 112km long highway which was to follow the traditional trans-Himalayan trade route posed significant engineering challenges and was estimated to cost USD 9.8 million. It was built by Chinese engineers and technicians and completed in 1967. The Chinese had sent teams to build the highway since 1963. In 1964 there was a discovery that arm cache was reportedly brought in Nepal from Tibet along with construction equipment though government didn't take any action. In 1967 the activities of the Chinese technicians working at the road-building sites began to alarm the Nepali government. The press reported that they were distributing Chinese revolutionary literature and Mao badges to construction laborers. They were also showing films promoting Chinese socialism. These ‘gullible’ Nepali workers it was claimed were forced to salute Mao’s portrait and chant slogans praising him before they received their wages. Nepali Government being disturbed by Mao button it started putting Mahendra button as symbol of nationalistic sentiment and potraying Mao's button as anti-national. In 1968 there were reports that Chinese personell seized and maltreated Indian and Nepali journalist and a Western photographer in Chinese-aided Sunkoshi Hydropower Project. This was a common occurance reported in Chinese project sites. A breaking point arrived on June 17 1967 when approximately 200 Chinese officials and project technicians along with Ambassador gathered at Kathmandu airport to welcome two of "Mao's Warriros" who were expelled from India for spying. The crowd was dissapointed when those two were not in the flight from Delhi. They started shouting anti-India and pro-cultural slogans. Given India's objection Nepal expressed dissatisfaction with this event to the ambassador. Another incident happened in late June 1967 in a mela to celebrate King's birthday. The Chinese stall was attacked by Nepalese students objecting large Mao's potrait without accompnying King's photo. After being dispersed by police the protesrors vandalized a zeep at Chinese embassy and a Chinese aided library. Soon follower charged exchanged between China and Nepal. This increasing popularity of Mao's Communism and King's discomfort to it is seen as the reason for Back to Village Program i.e. Gaun Farka Aviyan.

events.title: Rastriya Beema Sansthan Founded
events.detail: In 1967 Nepal Government founded Rastriya Beema Sansthan with a capital of one crore, which was at that time only functioning the non-life insurance business in Nepal. The 'Rastriya Beema Sansthan Act 2025' was introduced on the same day the next year for the ongoing operations of its business. Rastriya Beema Sansthan set up the life insurance industry as well in Nepal in 1972. In 1984, long before the split, this single entity decided to sell a small piece of its non-life equity (12.25%) to the general public to raise money. Those shares were listed on the stock market. Following regulatory shifts driven by the Insurance Act of 1992, single entities were barred from operating dual portfolios. The non-life portfolio split off into a separate entity called ⁠Rastriya Beema Company Limited (RBCL) only in June 2014. Meanwhile, the original body operates exclusively as a life insurer under its new identity, ⁠Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company Limited. RBCL is publicly traded on NEPSE with 87.75 owned collectively by the Government of Nepal, the Ministry of Finance, Nepal Bank Limited, and the Employees Provident Fund. Meanwhile, Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company Limited is fully government-owned life insurance enterprise in the country.

events.title: Back To Village National Campaign aka Gaun Farka Rastriya Abhiyan
events.detail: King Mahendra became increasingly concerned about Panchayat system as it lacked deeper public acceptance and political legitimacy despite existing for several years. In October 1967 he asked National Panchayat to discuss alternatives but it unanimously declared that the Panchayat system was “nirbikalpa”. In one side he was seeing Panchayat lacking support while in other side Mao's communisim was influencing rural peasants. Therefore he came up with second strategy of implementing Mao's Red Guards-like mass-mobilization model in Nepal to spread Panchayat ideology and connect the system directly with ordinary people. He even went as far as to discuss one-party system influenced by the Chinese communist model with Surya Bahadur Thapa. However Thapa discouraged such idea and in proposal of panchayat-turned ex-communist leader Kamal Raj Regmi, King finally came up with a royal socio-economic directive called Back-to-the-Village National Campaign (Gaun Farka Rashtriya Abhiyan) designed to spread Panchayat values and strengthen the system at the grassroots level. Influenced partly by China's mass mobilization methods but framed around development rather than revolutionary destruction officials politicians and civil servants were required to go to villages at least 7 days per year on own expense engaging in labor contribution (shramdan) teaching road construction irrigation work tree planting and rural development activities. The campaign initially generated enthusiasm and helped redirect urban elites toward rural areas. Like Mao's Little Red Book attractive pamphlets/booklets carrying King Mahendra's photograph on the cover were printed and distributed widely in villages. Though initially successfull King Birendra later weaponized it as a political tool.

events.title: Rastrabadi Swatantra Bidyarthi Mandal Founded
events.detail: King Mahendra established the Bidyarthi Mandal to suppress the student movement by instigating confrontations. Padam Thakurathi was its founding president. The organization was operated by the then Zonal Commissioners. Its members would assault—and even kill—students and others who were organized and campaigning for democracy. At that time the term ‘Mandale’ became synonymous with terror. Kamal Thapa Deepak Bohara and Rajendra Lingden rose through the politics of the Bidyarthi Mandal. The Bidyarthi Mandal was officially dismantled on May 21 1979

events.title: Agriculture Development Bank Established
events.detail: ADBL was established in January 1968 under the ADBN Act, 1967 as a successor to the Cooperative Bank in Nepal. The Cooperative Bank was a specialized financial institution established by the Nepalese government in 1963 to pool resources and provide loans to early rural savings groups and farmers. The bank was legally restricted to providing credit lines and loan facilities strictly to registered cooperative societies, meaning it could not issue loans directly to individual, independent farmers. The bank was legally restricted to providing credit lines and loan facilities strictly to registered cooperative societies, meaning it could not issue loans directly to individual, independent farmers. Its assets and operations were absorbed to form the Agricultural Development Bank of Nepal (ADBN) in 1968, which was given a much broader mandate to finance individual farmers, large corporate farming bodies, and rural industries alike. It later incorporated as a public limited company in 2005 and operates as an "A-class" commercial financial institution with 51% government ownership.

events.title: BP Koirala and Ganesh Man SIngh Released
events.detail: On May 15 1968 Subarna Shumsher issued a statement offering "loyal cooperation" (भक्तिपूर्ण सहयोग) to the King and accepting the King's leadership under the Constitution. While supporting current constitution he said that he is enthusiastic of King considering necessary ammendment to the constution in future. This statement in BP's assessment gave meaning of an unconditional surrender to King and his system. After his release BP made a statement supporting Subarna's statement in a corrective tone. In the statement he said he supports the statement of Subarna in the capacity of a democrat and close friend. He also added that he offers "loyal cooperation" to King given his belief in democratic principles and his intention to make nepal strong united and progressive. On the following day King Mahendra granted pardon to 23 leading Nepali Congress exiles living in India including Subarna Shamsher. Ganesh Man Singh also issued a similar statement within few days. Krishna Prasad Bhattarai however remained jailed for refusing to issue the statement of support to Subarna Shumsher's earlier statement. He believed that supporting that statment would be betrayal to the cause. KPB was a man of religious ideals which might have influenced his decision. His grandfather had gone to Benaras in retinue of exiled Queen Rajya Laxmi who was responsible for Kot and Bhandarkhal Parva. By the time Kishun ji went to school the patronage of the queen was over and the family had to earn by performing priestly chores. Kishun ji was also drawn to it through his family line.

events.title: BP Koirala Treatment and Travel
events.detail: BP Koirala had applied for a Nepalese passport immediately after his release. He had to immediately go India for his treatment so PM Surya Bahadur Thapa had told him that his passport will be sent to him in Bombay within three days. However despite reminding about his application for a year and half government just kept assuring him. And finally one day Nepal’s Foreign Minister claimed that BP had not applied for a Nepali passport. India: BP Koirala was admitted to All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) and again wrote to the Government of Nepal. He also wrote to the Crown Prince Birendra who was then the chairman of the Regency Council in the absence of the King who was away. The Crown Prince’s secretary sent him a letter informing that his request for a passport “has been rejected.” Only then BP approached the Government of India for necessary travel documents to go abroad for treatment. The Indian government had hoped that the Government of Nepal themselves would have issued a passport to Koirala. Since it did not do so India “orally informed Nepal on 17 August 1970 to have issued an identity certificate on humanitarian grounds.” The King took India’s issuing of identity card as an act of hostility. Koirala’s family showed to the British High Commission in New Delhi a certificate from a reputable Indian surgeon which stated that treatment was not available in India and that he needed to go to France Germany or Britain. His sponsors were the Socialist International (SI). Personalities like Harold Wilson Willy Brandt and other prominent leaders were associated with the SI and it did not look appropriate to ignore SI’s request for a permit for Koirala on humanitarian grounds for medical treatment. MP Tom Driberg and Labour Party’s General Secretary on 21 August 1970 also wrote to Foreign Secretary raising the issue of delay in granting permit to Koirala. BP was then told to approach the British Embassy in Europe for seeking permission to visit London. BP mentioned that they delebrately delayed it likely because King Mahendra was also visiting Britain at that time. They tried to avoid BP's visa to be seen as disrespect to the King. Germany: BP then decided to go to Germany given he was travelling on invitation of Socialist International (SI) and Social Democratic Party (SPD) was in governemnt. Though he was stopped at first in the airport his socialist friends in German government helped his get an seven-day visa. The SPD arranged for his hotel and he was well taken care. He found Germans to be more formal and indifferent to BP's cause. Again he started looking for visa to other countries but all of them were reluctant as all had good relation with Nepal Government. Sweden: Then SI contacted all the leaders in different countries and finally leaders from Swedish Social Democratic Party asked BP to come without visa. After reaching Sweden he got visa for another 7 days. Both Germans and Swedish leaders told him that they cannot help him with arms if India doesn't support you and if India supports you there is no need of our help. BP found they didn't have much interest in Nepal as it didn't offer them with immediate benefits compared to Africa which didn't even have any socialist leaders. He was little dissapointed with the socialists there. He found the socialists to be wary of their image than any substantial actions on ideological basis. Denmark: Then from there he went to Denmark where he met with Anker Jørgensen of Social Democrats Party who later became Foreign Minister and Prime Minister of Denmark. Anker was sympathetic of BP but he wasn't in the governement at that time. He took BP to the parliament and held discussions in its parliamentary party. Then BP left for Belgium where he stayed for a month. UK: Finally from Belgium Embassy of UK BP was issued a travel permit for a one-month stay in London after King left. There he met his socialist and family friends. Nepal’s Ambassador in London showed grave concerns at a joint press release issued on 7 October 1970 by the Socialist International and Labour Party saying “BP is in Britain at the invitation of the Labour Party and the Socialist International. He attended the Labour Party Conference at Blackpool (September 28- October 2) and has had talks with leading representatives of the Labour Party. Mr. Koirala would welcome questions from the press.” The publication of a statement about Koirala’s presence in London and his willingness to take questions from the press caused “heavy palpitation in the hearts of the Nepalese.” There were phrases in it like reference to the King’s having carried out a ‘military coup’ when he dismissed Koirala to which Nepalese Embassy took strong exception and promptly issued a press release to counter it justifying the King’s move. It could clearly be seen that King was unhappy about hosting BP and giving political platforms abroad. In a press conference in London BP went on to even formally mention for the first time that "we should resort to arms to bring democracy to Nepal." The Nepali government became alert after this was published with importance in local newspapers. The grudge of King could be seen in new German Ambassador to Nepal Dr. Hans Ulrich's delay in presenting his credentials. BP left London on 9 October for India. In his entire trip most supportive of all was the Secretary General of Socialist International Hans Janitschek.

events.title: Sino-Soviet Border Conflict
events.detail: Mao rejected Khrushchev’s 1956 denunciation of Stalin as a betrayal of Marxism. While Nikita Khrushchev pursued a policy of "peaceful coexistence" to avoid nuclear conflict Mao demanded aggressive anti-imperialism. Likewise Soviets prioritized urban workers; Maoism relied on rural peasants. Mao refused to let China remain a junior partner to the Soviet Union. He launched the bombardment of the offshore islands (Kinmen and Matsu) in August 1958 without notifying Moscow in advance. This deeply frustrated Soviet leadership. As the United States hinted at the potential use of tactical nuclear weapons to defend the islands Khrushchev actively distanced the USSR from Chinese nuclear brinkmanship. Khrushchev even withdrew all Soviet advisors and economic assistance from China. Mao condemned Moscow for backing down to the United States during 1962 Cuban Crisis. Following an ideological split disputes over imperial-era boundaries surfaced in 1969 after Chinese troops ambushed Soviet guards on the Ussuri River sparking heavy artillery and tank counter-attacks. Fighting later spread west to Xinjiang resulting in heavy Chinese casualties. Fearing a Soviet invasion Mao Zedong later opened diplomatic ties with Washington leading to China's admission to UN and Nixon's 1972 China visit.

events.title: Harisiddhi Brick and Tiles Factory Opened
events.detail: The factory was originally established in 1969 with financial and technical assistance from China as a state-owned public enterprise. Around 700 ropanies of lands of local Newars was acquired at the rate of NRs. 1500 per ropani for the establishment of the factory. The company was later privatized in 1992 with its ownership and vast prime land package (spanning approximately 50 acres) acquired by Sundar Lal Bhawanani and Narsingh Bahadur Shrestha. While traditional full-scale brick manufacturing operations at the massive original site slowed down significantly over the years due to urbanization local environmental challenges and property disputes the brand still maintains market presence.

events.title: Kirti Nidhi Bista (1st Term)
events.detail: Bista’s mother was a daughter of the Badagurujyu (royal priest) which helped him to build relations with the monarch. Within a few months of the establishment of the Panchayat system he resigned as general secretary of the Nepali Rastriya Congress and welcomed King Mahendra’s action.

events.title: Dairy Development Corporation (DDC) Was Founded
events.detail: A team led by Swiss cheese expert Werner Schultes established the first Yak cheese production in Langtang in 1952 and a milk collection and processing center at Tusal village in Kavre. It got financial support of New Zealand and the technical support of Switzerland under the leadership of the World Food and Agriculture Organization. A Dairy Development Commission was formed by the government in 1955. The commission was converted into the dairy development board in 1962 and this board created the Dairy Development Corporation in July 1969 under the Corporation Act 1964 (2021 BS).

events.title: Education Data 1970
events.detail: By 1970 there were 7256 primary schools 1065 secondary schools and 49 higher secondary schools.

events.title: Nepal Oil Corporation Ltd. Established
events.detail: NOC established on January 29, 1970, under the Company Act of 1964. The government formed it to import, store, and distribute petroleum products across the country. Nepal and India signed their first formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in 1974. This agreement established IOC as the sole supplier of refined petroleum products to Nepal, offering stable transit pathways and structured credit terms to assist NOC's early growth. Because Nepal lacks its own refineries, India allows NOC to buy crude oil from third-party global markets and utilize Indian refineries to process it.

events.title: Krishna Prasad Bhattarai Released
events.detail: After BP Koirala and Ganesh Man SIngh left for Nepal preparing for armed struggle Kisunji not only opposed the decision but also accused him of making a big mistake by missing a good opportunity to develop the movement from within the country. After seeing his analysis and criticism of BP King became positive to release hima and finally on Mar 27 1970 he was released. Upon release too Kishunji followed his own political conscience by declining to be part of any of the two political lines prevailing within Nepali Congress at that time. BP had called for armed struggle to overthrow the Panchayat autocracy while Subarna Shumsher was pursuing the line of negotiation and persuasion with the monarch. He distanced himself from both the lines. He believed negotiation with the king would lead nowhere while any type of armed struggle would make the party externally dependent. He believed in the Gandhian method of nonviolent satyagraha. In fact it was this very political line which Nepali Congress ultimately adopted much later eventually culminating in the overthrowing of the Panchayat rule in 1990. Within 3 weeks of his release he inagurated the first convention of Nepal Student Union NSU.

events.title: Kirti Nidhi Bista's Forced Resignation Over Indian Military Checkpost
events.detail: Afer becoming PM Bista assigned the then foreign secretary Yadunath Khanal to prepare a proposal to withdraw Indian troops from the 17 border checkposts. He got the proposal approved directly by the king without taking it to the Cabinet for Panchayat Council for fear it could be rejected. The king’s green signal was all he needed to implement his plan. The move was received with strong reservations by New Delhi which even compelled King Mahendra to sack him on April 13 1970. Later Bilateral talks were held afterwards while anti-Indian sentements was soaring. Araniko Highway was successfully constructed linking Kathmandu directly to Tibet which treatened India's open-border trade monopoly with Nepal. Further pusing nepal towards China seemed counterproductive. Finally India removed its troops from all the 17 checkposts. Once the last Indian troops left Nepali soil in late 1970 the primary source of friction was gone. Mahendra reinstated Bista as the head of government in April 1971. However the millitary base at Kalapani still remains till today.

events.detail: Panchayat System - Partyless; acting

events.title: Nepal Bidyarthi Sangh (NSU) Founded
events.detail: The Nepal Bidyarthi Sangh evolved as the successor of Nepal Chhatra Sangh in the post-coup period. It started organizing itself by opening ad hoc committees first at the zonal level and eventually at the district level. It had two main objectives- to counter the move made by the pro-China group and to disseminate its own ideology. By 1969 it had 51 branches in different districts of the country. On 20 April 1970 it held its first nation-wide conference electing Bipin Koirala as its first President. Marshall Julum Shakya and Sher Bahadur Deuba were among the founders. The Government regarded the conference as dangerous to the systemdispersed the conference put 22 student leaders under arrest and sentenced them to imprisonment for 5 months and 13 days under the National Guidance Act. The Supreme Court however upheld the holding of the conference andacquitted the student leaders. In 1971 the NSU grew more militant and made a bold attemptto mobilize all politically conscious students in its favour. It also held its second conference in September at Narayanghat Chitwan. About 300 students participated in the conference. This conference was significant in the sense that never before in the history of the Nepalese student movement had a national student meeting of this size and importance been held outside the capital city of Kathmandu. It elecetd Sher Bahadu Deuba as its president and passed its 20 page documet called Ne. Bi. Sa. : Kina ra Kasari? In 1972 it formed Action Committee consisting of three representatives each from the pro-Peking pro-Moscow and NSU to launch mvement against the New Education System. By the end of 1972 student activism started declining due to most politically radical student leaders leaving the University many joining Government jobs and factions among the party leaders.

events.title: Fourth Five-Year Plan
events.detail: NPR 3.35 billion; ~49% from foreign aid; ~93% implemented; 11 PEs established; over 1,300 km of roads built; Prithvi Highway completed; Arniko Highway completed; Tribhuvan International Airport runway extended to handle jets; focused on rural development agriculture and decentralization; regional development concept introduced; 25% of total outlay allocated to agriculture and irrigation; 31% to transportation and communication; rural development programs like the Integrated Hill Development Project launched; 15 MW hydropower added (Kulekhani planning started); several district roads built; expansion of rural health posts and primary schools; large-scale fertilizer and seed distribution programs began; self-reliance emphasized but import substitution efforts were limited; industry and employment targets largely unmet; highly successful in physical infrastructure integration across regions; heavily suffered from institutional inflation and rising administration costs.

events.title: Rastriya Panchayat Graduate Constituency Election
events.detail: Four "Graduates' Constituency" seats were the hot topic of the election. While all other members of this legislative body were elected indirectly by small electorates-ranging from 50 to 150 voters. For the Graduates' Constituency seats however approximately 10000 Nepalis with either Bachelor's or Shastri (Sanskrit) degrees are franchised and this electorate includes a large proportion of the educated and politically conscious elite in the country. Of the 22 candidates for the four Graduates' seats 17 agreed to run on a common platform that advocated several major changes in the existing political system: (1) that elections to the national legislature be direct and based on the principle of universal adult suffrage; (2) that the Prime Minister be appointed by the King on the recommendation of the legislature; (3) that all restrictions on fundamental rights be removed; and (4) that the sessions of the legislature be made open to the public. PM Bista denounced the 17 candidates as opponents of the Panchayat system and sought to mobilize the electorate against them through the government-controlled press and radio and by a circular to all government employees instructing them to support his own 4-man panel of candidates. Bista suffered an embarrassing setback as his candidates were roundly defeated and all of the successful candidates had run on the 4-point "opposition" platform. Ramraja Prasad Singh Dr. Prakash Chandra Lohani Ratna Prasad Kharel and Krishna Prasad Bhandari were the winners.
